This game has set a new bar for what remakes should try and achieve!
The story revolves around both Leon and Claire as they try and venture though what remains of Raccoon city and discover what has cause this major zombie outbreak. The characters are really great with the voice acting being perfect for each character, while there may be some lines that feel off when delivered, for the most part this game has a great script. The story itself  unravel in a consistent flow and feels perfectly paced out which is really impressive. It manages to balance everything from the action, to the emotional interactions between characters, to the information that the characters learn in the story and it all feels natural. 
The setting of Raccoon City is really impressive with locations such as the RPD being this grand, historical police station, to the sewers feeling congested and murky to the NEST feeling like a top secret, never to be discovered testing centre located under the feet of every Raccoon resident. Each area feels like its own character and keeps the game from becoming stale at any point through the runtime. 
Visually, this game is just gorgeous with everything that the player is able to see feel jaw dropping due to the graphics. This was one of the few games that i would just move my camera to observe and appreciate the surroundings that i have been put in. The list of things that this game makes look good is endless and is genuinely such an impressive performance from a graphical standpoint. From the environments to the characters and creatures themselves, each element just feels right for this type of game and is just elevated by how graphically impressive this game is. 
Sound and audio are just as amazing as the graphics with the soundtrack adding to the overall tension of the experience and the audio just adds to the immersion. With each gun shot, door opening and zombie either moaning and crunching, this game amplifies each aspect of the horror genre.
In terms of gameplay, while it may be the mechanics you may have come to know from the series, RE 2 has smoothed them out and they feel amazing to use. You will be using weapons to fend off the undead with pistols, shotguns etc and the feel of using them feel great. The inventory is also a pretty great mechanic as you will have to manage what to bring with you or what to either discard or store in the chest and can make for some great decisions and increase the intensity of the game. The item usage of the game is really great as you can do things such as examine them in case they might hide something that can aid you on your journey, combining items in order to make either ammo or meds and just simply using them to help with some of the puzzles in the game. The enemies are great while it might not be a large roster of the different types of the undead, what Capcom use here is enough for the game to be intense and keep players on their feet. Finally the boss battles that you encounter and the inclusion of the Tyrant aka "Mr X" are a great addition to the game and add pressure to the players circumstances. 
Overall, Resident Evil 2 is a fantastic remake of an already loved cult classic and i would recommend to both fans of the original or new comers to experience on of the best survival horror games of this generation.

Setting
The game is set in Raccoon City in September 1998, two months after the events of Resident Evil. Most of the citizens have been turned into mindless zombies, due to an outbreak of a viral bioweapon known as the T-virus, manufactured by Umbrella Corporation.[3][4] The game begins at a gas station outside of the city, where rookie police officer Leon S. Kennedy (Nick Apostolides) meets college student Claire Redfield (Stephanie Panisello), who is looking for her brother Chris.

After being separated following a car accident, Leon and Claire agree to meet up at the city's police department. The building is infested by zombies, and other monsters, including the "Tyrant",[b] who is dispatched to hunt down and kill any survivors. The creatures and various obstacles prevent Leon and Claire from actually reuniting as they are forced to find a way to escape the city. Leon and Claire will arrive at the station at different times depending on the scenario.

Leon scenario
In the machinery, Leon is ambushed by a horrifically mutated Umbrella researcher Dr. William Birkin (Terence J. Rotolo), but survives the encounter and drives the monster away.

In the police station parking garage, Leon is saved from an infected dog by FBI agent, Ada Wong (Jolene Andersen). They find reporter Ben Bertolucci in the holding cells; imprisoned by corrupt Police Chief Brian Irons (Sid Carton) for investigating Umbrella. As Ben tries to convince Leon to release him, the Tyrant kills Ben. While attempting to escape the police station, Leon is intercepted by the Tyrant but is again saved by Ada. After an encounter with gun shop owner Robert Kendo and his infected daughter Emma, Leon pledges to help Ada retrieve a G-virus sample to prove Umbrella's corruption.

In the sewers, Annette Birkin ambushes the pair and shoots at Ada; Leon takes the bullet and passes out. Ada pursues Annette but is knocked into a trash compactor. Leon rescues her, and they descend to NEST via cable car, where Ada kisses Leon.

Ada, injured, requests that Leon obtain the G-virus sample. In Birkin's lab, Leon obtains a sample but is attacked by a now much more deadly William. Annette tries to kill him, but is mortally wounded. Leon defeats William and tends to Annette, who claims that Ada is a mercenary and will sell the virus to the highest bidder.

Leon confronts Ada as the lab's self-destruct protocol begins, where she admits to being a mercenary. Ada demands the G-virus sample from Leon at gunpoint, but Annette shoots Ada before succumbing to her injuries. Ada falls off the bridge, but Leon catches her, letting the virus sample fall into the abyss. Leon loses his grip and Ada seemingly falls to her death.

As Leon attempts to escape the lab, he is ambushed by the Tyrant, now transformed into the larger and more powerful Super Tyrant, and engages it in a final battle. Ada, having survived the fall, tosses a rocket launcher to him, which Leon uses to finally destroy the Super Tyrant. Leon boards the evacuation train, discovering Claire and Sherry already aboard.

Claire scenario
In the Machinery, Claire encounters Sherry Birkin (Eliza Pryor), a young girl being pursued by the mutated William Birkin. In the police station parking garage, Irons abducts Sherry, and locks her in an abandoned orphanage. Claire soon receives a call from Irons to trade Sherry for a pendant she had dropped during the abduction, threatening to kill the little girl if Claire does not comply. Reluctantly, Claire agrees to do so.

Sherry tries to escape on her own, but is soon cornered by Irons. Before Irons can harm her, William returns and implants Irons with a G-embryo. When Claire arrives to save Sherry, a larva bursts out of Irons' chest and kills him. As Claire and Sherry attempt to leave, the Tyrant arrives and chases the pair into an elevator, but is killed by William. The creature then tries to attack Claire and Sherry as it mutates, but accidentally causes the elevator to fall into the sewers. Claire is knocked unconscious, and Sherry is forced to abandon her to escape.

Claire is found by Annette (Karen Strassman), Sherry's mother, who reveals that the creature after Sherry is William, her husband and Sherry's father. The Birkins developed the G-virus for Umbrella; however, William planned to sell it to the U.S. military. Umbrella sent its paramilitary force to confiscate his work, leading to William being fatally shot. To avoid death, William had injected himself with the G-virus. As William takes his revenge on the Umbrella soldiers, sewer rats infected by shattered vials of the T-virus carry their infection to Raccoon City. Now a mindless mutating beast, the G-virus drives William to infect Sherry, as she is the closest genetic match to William and thus the most suitable host to spread the infection.

Claire finds Sherry trapped in a trash compactor by Annette. Upon reaching her, however, Sherry falls ill. Annette realizes William has already infected Sherry and has Claire bring her to an Umbrella lab called NEST, where a vaccine is stored. Once there, Claire uses Sherry's pendant to unlock the vaccine, but William attacks after mutating again. Claire sends Annette to administer the vaccine while she fights William. After seemingly killing him, Claire reunites with Annette, who has managed to cure Sherry before dying from internal injuries. Sherry tearfully bids her mother goodbye. As the facility enacts a self-destruct protocol, Claire and Sherry make their way to an evacuation train. William returns yet again, now mutated into a much larger monster, and Claire defeats him just as the train prepares to leave. Upon boarding, Claire discovers Leon there as well.

Ending
After Leon, Claire, and Sherry reunite, William attacks the train, having mutated into a gigantic horrifying mass of fangs and flesh. Leon and Claire are almost killed in the fight, but manage to uncouple the carriage occupied by William. The carriage falls behind and is consumed by the exploding lab, destroying William once and for all. As the three survivors finally escape Raccoon City, they vow to continue the fight against Umbrella.

in a similar way to when Resident EviI 2 debuted on the Playstation 1, I admit was skeptical when first started playing the game. The first time Resident Evil 2 debuted I was 18 years old and had been playing the first game in the series faithfully since it early release on the Playstation. In fact the first RE game for PS1 was the game on the Playstation I played the most in my teenage years. So at age 18, I wasnt thrilled right away when I picked up the original RE2, only to find that some of my favorite elements of the slower moving haunted house style game, had been adapted into a much larger, and more action oriented sequel. However, as I played it, I soon found that a lot of the things I loved about the first game, were still in it lurking below skin deep. Metaphorically in the way that the police station is actually an old museum before it was converted with many secrets to unravel. Those elements helped me get over the game being moved out of the evil mansion. In a similar open minded way i tried to give this reboot a chance. Not entirely disappointed but some things did make me feel kind of sad. I was a teen when Claire was a teen. At 42 now but somehow Claire is remodeled the same age lol so what now am I supposed to feel like a dirty old man? l also notice this RE2 still takes place in the same year. Call it chronology confusion I guess, but i also liked some of that nostalgia. We still see glass monitors and Sony Wega style televisions as we explore the police stations beveled walls. In fact on a personal note regarding nostalgia, the very TV set i played the first RE games on, still sits faithfully beside my 2019 Bravia oled tv. I have kept it working to this very day and hooked up to my og xbox. Sadly the PS1 and Saturn i had from then got traded off a long time back but I still play Silent Hill 2 once in awhile. Some of the reminiscing was fun but the repetition eventually left me feeling bored and usually then i found sth else to do. Fortunately the game has some replay value but not as much as one might hope for given the mass amount of packaging releases of RE2 usually come wrapped with. In regards simply to the rebooted game itself the graphics are pretty (i was playing at 60 frames 4k on an oled set with an rtx 2080 super) and the levels remain well designed. I think mostly thanks to major graphical improvements the reboot game did a much better job of getting the player involved and fleshing out the story overall. I got a much greater sense of really being there. The side stories and extras are also very good. In both versions i played RE2 i preferred playing it alone and at night with the lights off for pure effect. I will say the overall atmosphere and level of presentation is far superior in the newer game. A few of the jump scares got me and i laughed each time. Maybe just because i wanted them to, whereas when i was younger,  i might have just gotten annoyed because i was just a "little too cool for that kind of thing". By this age i just want to be entertained for my buck yeh any cheap thrill if i can make it work and this game basically paid its bills for me. I cant say for certain that you will have the same magic but i thought it was alright playing it all alone at night her on the oled with my desktop etc. without spoilers. There were some key differences between versions of course. I liked the scenes with Mr. X were especially nerve wracking. As well as zombie improvements to mechanics, the action isnt broken every time you merely walk into a door. It really causes the overall feeling to flow MUCH better. So that was what i found made the game overall a better experience, at least for those willing to let it test their nerves for awhile. The second level of enjoyment i got came from the puzzles themselves. As an adult i admit i found they were a little too easy. Easy enough that i put them together without turning to a guide for help. Heck even the 3 digit padlocks and statues were cracked quite easily as an adult without the guide. The only time i read for help was for the safe codes but not complaining about it because i like when it is at least possible to get most of a game (or all of it) by faithfully looking for clues that should be in the game itself, and not in the latest issue of you get the idea.. its a really good game all on its own but it is a reboot from sth else. I found it was a big enough improvement and had enough new surprises and elements to make it worth the time. Just maybe for those who are really hooked on the original or cannot find enough new about it to qualify going over it again, or maybe those who just plain dont want to relive the nostalgia..then there will be people who want to gripe. but for me it was solid entertaining and i would and do recommend it.

All that being said, pretty solid title that I would fully recommend

[h1][b]An honest opinion[/b][/h1] 

AH yes, [b]R[/b]esident [b]E[/b]vil 2. A game now overwhelmingly beloved by old and new fans. This game, not only proved that remakes can be fantastic but also that Capcom knows that it is better to make money with a good game. RE2 gave me something I never knew I need.

[h1]The Original[/h1]
Sadly, I was not alive when the original was published, however, only 10 years later I could enjoy... watching someone playing the game. I'll be honest, I was not only fascinated but also a little scared, YES I was scared, let me alone. Until then, I was playing Pokemon, I was young so I couldn't enjoy other great games like Fallout 3 or Left 4 Dead... yet. And there I was, watching something new to me. A game with zombies, weapons and one of my early video game crushes...Claire Redfield, but it shall not be about here in this review... not only. Almost 5 years later I was allowed to play the game. I had so much fun... fun dying a lot... fun running out of ammo... fun dealing with motion sickness...FUN. I know, it sounds a little sarcastic doesn't it, however, I mean it. All of them are things which were new to me, until then I have played relative "easy" games which were kinda straight forward. I loved it, it was my start into another video game world and I couldn't have be more happy about that. 

[h1]The announcement[/h1]
When Capcom announced that they are going to work on a remake of the game I was so grateful for, that they would take the old game and will give it an amazing new look, you think that, that was the best day of my life, yeah, I wished.

Until now, remakes are considered a curse to the video game industry. So many remakes and a lot of them are considered the worst games in history. And it doesn't stop there. Movie remakes were getting more common now, but all remakes fail to give us the satisfaction that the old movies gave us. I was worried when Capcom announced a remake of Resident Evil 2.

[h1][b]R[/b]esident [b]E[/b]vil 2[/h1]
I have to be honest here, it took me nearly 6 months after the release to get some time to play the game. I watched people playing it and read some reviews. The reviews were fantastic. All the people who played it had genuinely fun and loved the game. I heard some criticism, but they were not overwhelmingly. And when I started the game, I was hooked for at least a couple of days. 

[h1]Characters - Claire[/h1]

[b]Claire Redfield[/b]
Let's start with her, I'm sorry I gotta do this. As you all have read before Claire was one of my video game crushes but let's talk about Claire and how she changed things pretty early on. In video games and movies Girls were either annoying or just there for the guy. Sometimes you crushed on them, that is totally fine, they were there for crushing on them. Claire is not like THE OTHER GIRLS tho. She is mostly independent, the only thing what she had in mind coming to the city, was looking for her brother. She wanted to know if he is okay and safe... she was a sister. And that makes her different to other girl characters who show no or little fear and could battle anything at any time. She had a reason to be there, she always had a reason to fight and continue the journey. At the start, it is her brother, and then it continues with her being an older sister for Sherry. Claire never gave me the vibes that she was scared... confused certainly but never scared. She was prepared to take this world on. She did rely on Leon for a couple of minutes yeah, but sure everyone would. That is normal in a world were you could die at any point and there is a cop with a weapon, I sure would have relied on Leon. However, that is not for long. Both have their own story to tell, and there is little interactions between them. Claire has no problems to depend on herself and that makes her a great female heroin in this world. 

[b]Leon S. Kennedy[/b]
There is not much to say. Leon is an amazing character and I like him and his interaction and story with Ada Wong are great. I wished there is a little more in his story arc but you can't have everything I guess. I enjoyed playing his side of the story but it felt like something was missing. I can't explain it and I won't. Let's agree Leon is Leon and Leon is a cool character.

[b]Ada and Sherry[/b]
I like their short playable times. But I can't really say much about them without going to far into lore and story. So I will move on. 

[b]Mr X[/b]
I love this guy. I don't know what it is about him, but while being in the police office I never felt save. Not only because of the Zombies and Lickers. But also this guy could appear at any time. It was stressful. His looks are great, I love his hat and the fact that is an achievement to shoot it down. Great guy, just wished he wouldn't try to kill me, I might have talked about the weather or something. 

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
Had anyone else the feeling that it was a game, I mean a real game for gamers. Okay, let me explain. Nowadays it is common to make everything close to real life. That it looks like the real world and feels like the real world. Whereas it is true that RE2 and also the newer games look real which is an amazing thing in a survivor horror, it certainly doesn't move the characters in a real way. It feels very game like, like in the old days. Movement is weird, how you scope and shoot is totally different to most shooters and it is amazing. Because in most shooters you have enough ammo to battle an army. Here you miss one shot and you cry because you might die because of that mistake, and it very easy to miss a shot. The game certainly doesn't make it easy for you. But what I like is, it isn't easy but not impossible like other titles. Don't get me wrong, I love titles impossible to beat, but RE was never such a game and I am soo glad that it isn't. Because you can emerge in this world easier and you have time to think what to do next and how much supply do I have now. Do I need to explore more to get some more supplies or have I enough for the next stage. 

[b]Boss battles[/b]
I kind dislike the boss battles, especially the final boss in Claire's arc. It feels weirdly easy and nothing special. Even on hard difficulty it doesn't feel like a boss. More like an annoying mutant with too much HP. But we all know Capcom has changed that in Village, which is amazing and I hope they continue like that. 

[b]Graphics[/b]
Can we talk about how amazing and atmospheric this game is. I know in some stages it looks a little 'washy'? yeah, just weird. But overall? this game looks and feels so atmospheric, it just feels like the world is going down, that you need every single supply you can find to survive and then the dark corridors of the police station with all sorts of dangers, the sewers with this ugly mutations and then the Umbrella Corp. facilities. All of them bring another feeling with them and the atmosphere is just incredible well done and never stops during playing.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
RE2 Remake is just one of the best remakes in video game history, in my opinion. I did play it fist on a console and a couple days ago I decided to play it on PC again. It wasn't a mistake and I would do it again. The sad reality is that remakes getting worse and worse because of money and missing love for the franchise. I am glad that RE2 is an amazing game and Capcom did a great job with it. Props to the team who worked on it, you gave me something I never knew I needed.

This was it for me, I hope you have an amazing day. 

Cheers

An absolutely brilliant example of how to remake a game: improve QOL, add modern gameplay elements that don't detract from the original, and above all preserve the core essence of the original game. This was clearly made by a team that understood extremely well what the whole vibe of RE2 was and knew how to preserve it while making the game actually fun to boot. 

The over-the-shoulder camera brings together two eras of game design perfectly: the original cinematic tension of the first RE games, and the modern dominance of souls-like third-person action. This and other modernizations greatly enhance playability without touching the basic gameplay that makes original RE games so fun: explore a huge mansion, collect items to solve puzzles, manage your inventory, and dodge spooky monsters. Understanding that the game is actually kind of easy with all the modern additions, there are a few tricks to make players feel unsafe: Mr. X can go many more places now! Your knives will break! The zombies lunge WAY more easily now (but can still be dodged)!

All these elements had me intensely strategizing from within a saferoom: "to get this item, I need to make sure I have this weapon...I know a licker will block my way here, so I'll take the long way through the library on the 2nd floor to get to that room...if Mr. X shows up I know I can run to this safe location instead..." and when a game is that engrossing, you can't help but love it.

Right off the bat, I want to say that this is a well done game and if you have the money and are a fan of the Resident Evil franchise but wish that the game regained it's grit after what 7 did, I would HIGHLY recommend this game. It's a talented remake and CAPCOM is able to revitalize the puzzle solving, ammo conserving gameplay that the original 3 games had (along with updating the graphics to the pitch perfect RE: ENGINE). The puzzles in this game are a nice follow up to 7, the intricate escape room type of sequence to the story also carries over from 7 and the tight gripping action sequences are able to not become overly ridiculous or make me say "WTF" in confusion. 

However, on to the cons, I do think the replay ability of the story does suffer once you know the puzzles of the game (however, I appreciate what the 2nd run feature attempted to do despite that also becoming a game of "Do you remember this sequence?) Along with this, I believe the Lost Survivors DLC was not needed at all and is just quite frustrating and forgettable. I see CAPCOM's vision for wanting to have a more fast-paced part to the game to keep things interesting but I believe that CAPCOM could have expanded on these DLC's instead of making them run and guns. Take, for example, the Bedroom VHS from 7, you could easily make a mini escape room situation for the Runaway scenario. Or, you could have one Run and Gun (personally I think "No Time to Mourn" is the best of these) and change the rest. HOWEVER, I will say that the No Way Out scenario was actually quite enjoyable and challenging, turning the game into a Call of Duty Zombies survival with MUCH higher challenge. it should NOT be locked behind completing the other scenarios first though!

All in all, Resident Evil 2 has my support and many others for it being well-crafted and able to bring the series back to basics. It was also able to carry the streak of good games set after Resident Evil 7's release by reintroducing the 3rd person camera while making the story AND gameplay feel meaningful again.

Minor spoilers follow, but nothing that gives away the ending or anything crucial to the plot/storyline. More gameplay/mechanic focused than anything.

.......Still here? Good.

This game is great. Period. Only downside is that, to me at least, the story felt a bit short. Still, they were remarkably faithful to the OG RE2, and getting to play through as both Claire and Leon was a blast. Sherry was even a better Ashley than Ashley, since there were no escort missions and you didn't have to worry about crucial NPC's dying from stupidity (if you know, you know).

In true RE style, this game handsomely rewards you for keeping a close eye on your inventory, feeds the hoarding addiction we all have in these kinds of games, and encourages crafting your ammo just as much as picking it up. You have a very limited carry-capacity, far slimmer than older RE games, but you can gradually expand it by picking up additional carry pouches to expand your inventory bit by bit. Still, even after collecting every one of them, you don't have much room, so you can't exactly carry around your entire arsenal at once. You have to pick and choose, usually based on what ammo you have for which weapons.

Speaking of ammo: enemies don't magically drop it after being killed, like they'd eaten a perfectly good box of 9mm rounds and were just waiting for you to split them open like a pinata and pick them up. You have to either find it or craft it, so ammo starts scarce and stays scarce. Enemies, in this vein, will need to be dispatched quickly and efficiently if you hope to keep a decent amount of ammo in your inventory, as some enemies are bullet sponges if you're not "hitting their weak points for massive damage". Because of all of this, making sure you know how to kite enemies is going to be very, very important to your survival, and you will default be getting your cardio in regardless.

Enemies-wise, some bosses are pretty easy to kill, others are decidedly less-so. G's hitbox on his attacks is a bit annoying, especially in the crane level, but otherwise no bosses felt impossible to defeat. Even basic zombies don't feel like they can be casually dismissed, as unless you use a rather powerful weapon, they take multiple headshots to down. Pretty sure that was done for gameplay sake, since one-tapping 85% of the game's enemies would make it boring rather fast if they stuck to the lore rigidly and made headshots insta-kills on regular zombies.

Unlike in RE4, you don't have an unbreakable knife that you can use to cheese regular enemies for ammo and lols. Instead you can pick up knives throughout the levels, each of them has a durability bar that degrades with use, and once that bar is depleted, the knife breaks and it's gone for good. Knives, coupled with grenades, are your Get-Out-Of-Grapple-Free card, and are meant to be used primarily as a last resort to avoid being bitten/harmed if an enemy gets ahold of you.

Herbs make a pleasant return, only that our boy Yellow Herb got swapped out for the new kid on the block, Blue Herb. Red and Green stick around, though. In that vein, the health system was tweaked a little: instead of showing your typical health bar, you have health status displays instead. Green means good, Yellow means Injured, Red means you need to crush those plants into powder and shove them down your throat before you die. Various mixtures of the 3 different types will produce different hybrid powders, but it's usually best to wait until you can mix all three for the best overall healing combination.

Overall, this game is a solid and faithful remake of RE2, and I cannot recommend it enough for fans of the OG franchise. Only downside is that I wish the game itself were longer, because it was fun as hell. 9.5/10

Not really to sure what compelled me to write a review but for some reason I feel like it.

First off, despite what my playtime says I have fully completed the game on the ps4 before so I have full experience with it. The only new thing here is a mouse and a keyboard. Second if you're expecting me to compare it to the original well no. I have played the original before thanks to my dad owning a bunch of ps1 disc but there were a couple of problems. First off we only had a ps2 but no ps1 memory card meaning no matter how far I got I couldn't save, and two I just in general sucked back then, I got used to the tank controls just fine, it was navigating and fighting enemies that annoyed me, so yeah didn't spend a lot of time on it.

It wasn't until giving resident evil 4 on the gamecube a chance that I fully got in to the series and I decided to start collecting them, with that said.

The game is a third person shooter/action horror. You navigate the police department from the original solving puzzles and shooting anything that attacks you, well if you can. the controls on both ps4 controller and mouse and keyboard work perfectly fine in fact aiming with a mouse is even better then aiming with a controller. No disrespect to ps4 mind you though when it comes to shooters I'd like something more then a joystick for aiming.

The zombies here are a pain to deal with, it can take awhile before they stay down for good, though let me tell yah there was nothing more satisfying then splitting there head in half with a critical shot. Lickers are a pain but only if you make them, there completely blind meaning as long as you aren't running around like an idiot you can get by them just fine. Zombie dogs are agile and a pain, don't feel like there's anything else to say. those sewer monsters are a major pain if you aren't ready or can't hit there weakpoints precisely, though now that I'm using a mouse I feel like it might not be so bad here. Those plant zombies in the underground section are tough but only if you don't have fire weapons prepared like the flamethrower. The bosses I honestly enjoyed there challenging but if you now what you're doing you can beat them.

The game is broken up in to two play throughs scenario a and scenario b, technically 4 but I'll get to that. Leon and Claire both function similar to each other though they both get different weapons. Leon gets a shotgun while Claire gets a uzi, Leon gets a flamethrower while Claire gets a grenade launcher with different ammo. Depending on who you pick for scenario a, scenario b will have a tougher time not just with some puzzles but encountering some enemies much earlier, especially a certain one I'll get to in a little.

There are also two other characters you play as in the game for short segments Ada and Sherry. Ada is similar to Leon but she also has a tool for hacking which is pretty simple to figure out and do, Sherry however is a tense stealth section avoiding the corrupt police chief. They don't last for very long so if you don't like there segments don't worry.

Leon and Claire regardless of what scenario there in deal with some thing, For Claire it's the mutated William Berking as a final boss and For Leon MOTHERFU***NG MR X. OK Mr x is an invincible enemy who you encounter a couple of hours depending on you're playtime in scenario a. In scenario b he's already in the police station when you get there though he only shows up after collecting a certain item. This guy is relentless and he actually scared me when I could here his footsteps while traveling. For Claire you encounter him for a while, but once her and Sherry escape in the elevator he's supposedly killed by William and you never see him after that. Leon's campaign however he is relentless hunting him down everywhere even in the underground facility where he manages to punches through security glass.

Thanks to the scenario system it's fun to reply with either character in either scenario but there's also bonus content like the survivors. you play as other people in the game to help them escape the outbreak all having something unique. One might be dealing with poisonous zombies which put's the blue hearbs to use, one might deal with armored zombies etc. I't helps add more replayability when it comes to earning a higher score and even unlocking more stuff to play with. 

The graphics look great gore details are really nice and the voice acting is nice to. Characters actually have emotion to them now and there are some heart wrenching moments. One thing I definitely remember from the original was the gunshop owner who quickly gets eaten. He's back here and he now has a daughter and without spoiling much I hope, it's sad what's implied.

So yeah with all that said if you're just looking to play a good resident evil game or grew up with the newer ones like me. Resident evil 2 remake is a good time. Also about the free thing my grandma got me this game off my wishlist for Christmas, she's awesome like that.

I'm a first timer to the series, but was aware of the major characters and rough story beats via cultural osmosis. Consider me a convert after playing this - I loved it.

I played Claire for my first run, and Leon for my second. I found Claire's character and story more compelling, but I still enjoyed Leon's run a lot. "Because game" contradictions aside, I liked how they ran parallel and only together told the full story, but still worked as their own thing. The combined ending really iced the cake. All of the voice actors do a pretty good job at bringing their characters to life in a way that made me care.

The gameplay felt fun but intense, and seems to be balanced to the point where you often feel like you're only just scraping by - appropriate for the survival horror genre. Some of the scares were extremely effective, especially when health and ammo were low. I preferred Claire's weapon set to Leon's, but that's apples and oranges, I suppose. The puzzles are generally simple, but still felt fun and rewarding. Even though the game has a more-or-less linear sequence, the layout of the RPD and other areas do add a sense of player freedom, as you learn and traverse them at your own pace. Although, that pace definitely hastens when there's a Tyrant on your trail. I'm not exactly a speedrunner by any measure, as I have the tendency to get very immersed in environments and atmosphere when playing. Although, I can certainly see why this game would be popular with speedrunners.

Graphically, the game looks fantastic. A few minor instances of blurry textures and delayed pop-in aside, the character models and environments shine, and the lighting is always extremely atmospheric. My current PC would have been a few years behind the "standard" back when this released, but due to a really well-done graphics settings menu, which includes estimations of processing load and memory load, I was able to customise things in a way that ran smoothly, but still looked great.

So yeah, wholehearted recommendation for this one! I'm excited to continue my foray into the series after this.

This right here is what a remake should be, not a "texture upgrade" that only exists to remove the original game off of steam. This game nails everything for me, it even got me interested in the other Resident Evil games.
       It's pro time, everything this game does well is about to be put on full display. The game is around 6-7 hours if you want it done asap, and about an hour more if you explore. This combined with the ability to do a "2nd run" and play as two different characters creates a ton of replay value. The story is also fantastic on it's own or as a part of a larger whole, nothing said is too difficult to comprehend even if you haven't played the other games before this. The atmosphere is amazing taking only a few moments to immerse yourself into this world. I can't in good faith allow a review to reach the light of day without mentioning the big man himself, Mr. X. This big bastard leads to the most terrifying and fun hour of the game, everything that works about Re2make rears its head here. Every step made here could lead you into the fist of one pissed off tyrant, nothing bad to say about it, truly perfect. my final positive is a huge thing for this type of game, and that's consumables. Using ammo and healing are both important mechanics that you'll use often, so finding the right balance between giving the player too much ammo and not giving them enough is very important. This point can be made either way based on personal experience, for example a veteran of the earlier games may want to conserve as much ammo as possible, this would give them an unbalanced experience as they would posses 100s of bullets and next to no heals. On the flip side a newer player may want to kill every zombie they come across and end up not having enough for the bosses. For me however this was no issue, I always had enough bullets to get out of a sticky situation or deal with a boss enemy, no more no less.
        While sucking this games ♥♥♥♥ sounds like a good time unfortunately we have to talk about the games downsides, of which there are very few. Each campaign has a section in which you switch who you play as for a quick segment, this is nothing new as I soon found out. The Leon switch is pretty painless and a nice change to get familiar to the new area. The Claire change however is a 20 minute waste of time, equipped with bare bones stealth mechanics and slow ass gameplay this section does nothing but waste time and give GDQ a good time to read donations. Most puzzles in the game boil down into the simple formula of explore area, find where key items need to go, find the key items, place them accordingly. This formula personally is fine and an excellent gameplay loop to satisfy me, some however find it boring and not as interesting as puzzles in the earlier games so I thought it was worth a mention.
       Well here we are at the end. No need to wait anymore, I don't give a ♥♥♥♥ if this game is on sale for the price of a penny or an organ, You buy the game. P.S. [h1]~The Good~[/h1]

 Resident Evil 2 Remake is absolutely wonderful in so many ways. This game has managed to scare me and put me on edge so many times...I haven't felt that way with a horror game in years. They took the base of Resident Evil 2 and expanded on it in a natural and great way. The story split up was a genius idea, seeing as they removed some scenes from the original. 

[b]~Leon Portion~[/b]
 
*[u]Character[/u]: Walking into the remastered Main Hall as up scaled Leon was a trip. Walking around those old locations in the RE Engine as our lovable police recruit in general felt so unreal. Speaking of Leon, his character is very faithful and is handled wonderfully. Leon is so hopeful and determined throughout the game, encouraging himself and others. Leon's voice actor was also incredible and did an amazing job portraying him. Everything about Leon is great in this game...I mean it's Leon! You can't mess up Leon...[b]imlookingatyouwelcometoracooncity.[b] 

*[u]Story (spoilers)[/u]: [spoiler]Exploring Raccoon City Police Department and seeing the unsettling and eerie atmosphere was so much fun. There's so many fun dynamics. The claustrophobic corridors (the Lickers and Mr.X taking advantage of this the most.), the ever growing darkness and ominous lighting, and the hopeless feeling as you see your own officers die/turned in front of you. It's all so great. It also helps that Leon is a "Rookie" as rookies are usually confused enough as is, which also transfers to the player. Its fun to see. The puzzles were fun (for the most part) and the boss fights were fun to play. Leon's arsenal felt a little lackluster if you're not a collectable go getter but hey, that's mostly the players fault. [/spoiler]

[b]~Claire Portion~[/b] 

*[u]Character[/u]: About the same as Leon tbh. Both were amazingly and faithfully portrayed. Claire's voice actor did a stellar job. 10/10. 

*[u]Story (spoilers)[/u]: [spoiler]I absolutely adore the fact that Claire is basically retracing Leon's steps in a new way (since it's basically new game+ and a mini DLC had a baby). You're doing pretty much the same but with a different and cooler arsenal (you get a grenade launcher and a big iron on your hip, what more could you ask for???). Get the three medallions. The underground is where things really changed, Sherry joins you! I won't touch more into this. You gotta play it yourself but the dynamic between them, albeit short, is great. (You have to do this for the true ending anyway.)[/spoiler]

~[b]RE2 in general[/b]~

RE2 Remake improved RE2 a lot in terms of gameplay. It's fun, engaging, and immersive. The third person perspective is a great addition compared to the angled view of the original. Gone are the days of stair climbing and door opening loading screens! You can traverse freely through them here! The RE Engine is beautiful and compliments the game amazingly in visuals and optimization. The characters are amazing and the changes made from the original are great fun to explore. The content is great too. it'll take about 20 hours across both characters to beat all missions and tasks. 33 hours if you want to 100% the game. (Capcom have even added the original sounds from RE2 and "Ghost survivors" all for free! Thanks Capcom!) The zombies are designed so well and behave very realistically. From their animations, throwing their weight around, to even just breaking through windows is all very well made and makes for some of the most realistic zombies in gaming history. 

[h1]~The Bad~[/h1]
(Light Spoilers)

[spoiler]CQC in this game sucks. There's no way around it. Ammo is scarce (which I like because it adds to that hopeless feel) and sometimes the best way to handle a zombie encounter is to just avoid the fine lad all together but the way grabbing works, sometimes what you think is a miss isn't because hitboxes and now they grab you and you're forced to use a save item or take the bite. I know that it makes the situation more hopeless and makes the zombies scarier to face but it tends to get annoying when it happens a ton of times...especially when Mr.X is trying to give it to ya. God forbid you find 3 zombies in a corridor, you're forced to either kill them, take a bite and use invincibility frames, or use a save item (which becomes quite valuable in hardcore). Sometimes zombies will turn around with lighting speed to grab you as well, which seems entirely unfair. (They fixed CQC somewhat in RE3 Remake with the dodge mechanic). The G-Adults suffer from grab syndrome as well. Sometimes they grab you right after being stunned from a grab and all I could do was roll my eyes. Another thing that sucked is that, maybe I personally missed something, but slow walking on PC is impossible. You'd have to hook up a controller to be undetectable to Lickers. You can still stealth past Lickers but they'll pick up on you as you fast walk by. More of a minor annoyance then a major criticism.[/spoiler]

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]

[b]This game is 100% worth your time.[/b] Capcom did a fantastic job of bringing back all the best parts of the classic Resident Evil 2 and making them look, sound, and play like a 2019 game. If you’re of the mind that the series had lost its way for a while there, this game is very much a return to form. Exploring the dilapidated ruins of Raccoon City is a thrill. So why not give it a try? After all, it is your first day rookie. ;)

This is a masterpiece of the survival horror genre and an incredible remake. The atmosphere is second to none, with god-tier audio design and stunning visuals that work together to create a constant state of dread and tension. It's one of the most immersive horror games I've ever played.

A quick disclaimer: I'm currently binging the RE series and have grown tired of bullet-sponge enemies. I like to full clear games I like, so to make my first run more enjoyable, I used a one-shot headshot mod. My experience is based on that. Even so, the game perfectly balances its quiet, tense moments with thrilling combat. The scripted zombie spawns are perfectly timed, always managing to catch you off guard just when you start to relax. And of course, there's the constant, terrifying pressure of being stalked by Mr. X.

On harder difficulties you will be quite likely forced to play as usual in older RE games. Kite enemies.... hope you don't run out of ammo, if do, take your knife out and pray... and avoid killing stuff if you can. 

The story and characters are great, and I especially loved Claire in this—and yes, the great modding scene certainly helped. I still chuckle at the awkward fence scene with Leon, which felt like a perfect teen romance with my schoolgirl outfit mod.

I'm giving it an 8/10 mainly because, for me, it was a "great one-time-wonder" but didn't have that addictive quality I'd need for a higher score. It's a superb, near-perfect horror experience that everyone should play.

As for DLC, you don't need any of it. If you're thinking about the all-item unlock, I'd strongly advise against it for a first run. Save it for subsequent playthroughs if you just want to marathon for the remaining unlocks.

RE2 is an absolutely phenomenal remake, one which is bolstered by the developer's renewed sense of confidence and a newfound sense of direction. Capcom has fully come to grips with what the series should look like in this day and age, and the end result is pure survival horror, retooled and retweaked for a modern audience. The Godfather of survival horror is back.

[h1]Game Impressions[/h1]

[b]+ Fun puzzles:[/b] basically, the entire game is a continuous puzzle. Go there, find that, progress to next area. But not once in ~8h do they feel repetitive. All elements play into it nicely and mechanics such as crafting are not overly complex for what their purpose ultimately is.
[b]+ Ammo conservation:[/b] you always have just enough to scrape by, which alters the way you approach a zombie encounter. It's always on your mind that the amount of bullets you can find in the game is finite but the zombie hordes are not.
[b]+ Environment:[/b] many secrets are not automatically logged in your journal. You need to keep an eye on different pieces of environment (e.g.: locker code written on a whiteboard). Also, reinforcing the barricaded windows in the police station has a visible effect (i.e.: less zombies appear on those corridors).
[b]+ Graphical detail:[/b] game looks flawless; simple as that. The player's model has different textures / shares applied depending on the environment he's been in. The uniform can get wet, covered in mud, etc.
[b]+ Map:[/b] extremely clear and intuitive to navigate. Highlights individual areas in different colors when you finished looting them.
[b]+ Replayability:[/b] the two characters have intertwining stories, meeting different characters, having access to unique areas and information, etc. This, however, constitutes a small part of the playthrough, 90% of the gameplay loop being identical. Although I can't be bothered to replay the entire game for some cut-scenes right after finishing it once, after watching a compilation for the other character on YouTube, I am inclined to say that Claire's is the better story arc.

[b]- Lack of prompts (sometime):[/b] referring strictly to the transition from the first level to the second. You may be unprepared to move on but the game doesn't require an ACK before rolling the cut-scene. Well enough, you get to return later and finish exploring.
[b]- Mr. X:[/b] the best and worst part of the game. While succeeding in maintaining a certain level of tension after most of the building is secured and you get comfortable, encounters with him quickly become tedious. Most likely, they will end with you running away in one of the arbitrary safe zones and waiting for him to wander away. This is extremely time consuming and the alternative (i.e.: running around until you lose him) is not viable for reasons that will become apparent 1-2h into the game. Moreover, his positioning can sometimes be bugged. For example, there is a room where the only way to progress is through a tight window near the ceiling. Just looking at him, it is obvious that he can't follow through it and you think you may be safe. Alas, one of Mr. X's many talents is [i]teleportation[/i], apparently.
[b]- Minor sound issues:[/b] in the boiler room, you can't hear the rain when the camera (not the character model) is inside the building, even if the door is wide open. Also, there are some issues with echoing footsteps in areas where there shouldn't be any.
[b]- Voice acting:[/b] ok for the most part but at times it's too exaggerated (even though the dialogue is supposed to be a tad cheesy), or not in tone with the recently ended cut-scene.
[b]- Item interaction:[/b] without an always-on crosshair, you need to fumble about until the interact icon appears for certain items. Normally this is just a minor annoyance but sometimes you end up failing to pick up a story item in a critical situation, leading you to waste precious resources returning after it when you discover that it's not in your inventory after all.
[b]- Inventory space:[/b] even though you can (greatly) increase it over the duration of the game, it almost always is too constricting. To me, this limitation seems to have no utility whatsoever, except for forcing the player to run to and fro the storage box, least wanting to discard possibly valuable consumables.
[b]- Final boss battle:[/b] without giving anything away (plot-wise), I find it very annoying that they took one of the worst parts of the game (movement) and made that the main mechanic for the fight.

Resident Evil 2 Remake and Resident Evil Remake are my favorite Resident Evil games. It’s tough to separate the two for me. REmake represents the pinnacle of what the original trilogy was: fixed camera angles, beautifully detailed 2D backgrounds and 3D character models, memorable level design, a mix of true horror and shlocky action, restricted inventory space, puzzle solving, and tough combat with a limited arsenal. RE2R picks up on everything REmake accomplished aside from the fixed camera angles and 2D backgrounds. The fixed camera angles are replaced with a more modern 3rd person view and the world is now rendered fully in 3D without compromising on any detail thanks to modern hardware. So, while I’ll miss the original’s fixed camera angles and 2D backgrounds, the only detail lost is those choice camera angles that either hid information intentionally from the player or were just stunningly beautiful.

The visuals of RE2R are truly spectacular. The Racoon City Police Department in particular is such a memorable location. Whoever had the idea of the setting to be a police department setup inside an old art museum was a genius. The location is dripping with character. Each room has sort of three layers of personality, an old museum underneath, a police department set inside, and a zombie outbreak on top. This layering gives weight and a history to the location that the player can feel as they move through the halls. It also helps that the connection between the player and the protagonists Leon and Claire is as strong as ever. The in-game models of Leon and Claire are rendered in great detail and all their animations are realistic and responsive. I love the lengths the developers took to add small details to the character animations, such as pinning the flashlight between the neck and shoulder when reloading a gun. All in all, the visual presentation of RE2R is stunning and one of the reasons I’ll keep coming back to it.

In terms of gameplay, RE2R does not deviate far from REmake outside of the perspective shift. Hardcore difficulty in particular has that REmake feel with its ink ribbon/typewriter save system and more restrictive inventory size. I’d recommend hardcore to most people, especially those looking for a classic Resident Evil experience. Inventory management has always been the real puzzle in Resident Evil games and that is back in RE2R along with plenty of in-world puzzles. No real brain busters but plenty that make you think for a bit. The pace of combat is also similar to REmake with each zombie posing a threat, especially early on. Leon and Claire aren’t exactly gunslingers and have to take their time to aim their weapon. Zombies are slow, but they’re odd cadence and erratic movement mean they’re not the easiest targets. Even when you do connect on a shot, Zombies and other enemies do not drop easily. Often it will feel like you have to put a whole, precious clip into a lone zombie. This coupled with limited ammunition means picking your battles is important.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is not ground-breaking, but it does accomplish being a faithful remake. RE2R sticks to the strengths of the original Resident Evil trilogy while presenting itself as a beautifully detailed 3rd person survival horror game.

[b]TL;DR[/b] Masterpiece of a survival horror game and should serve as an example of the best of the best in its genre.

[h1]Disclaimer[/h1]
Am Resident Evil fanboy.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
There is nothing to say about the graphics other than they are phenomenal. The RE Engine continues to impress and this game is no exception. Maxed out the game is just unreal (if you can handle it). Another thing worth mentioning is the game runs incredibly well while still looking great, so that's always a good thing.

An unusual omission of Ray-Tracing though.

[h1]Sound[/h1]
Sound design is phenomenal creating an amazing sense of atmosphere and dread. I have nothing bad to say about it. The groans of the creatures are haunting, the sounds of the weapons satisfying and the ambient noise absolutely suitable too. Voice lines are cheesy but nothing I don't expect from Resident Evil.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The police department is absolutely the strongest part of the game and it gets a bit weaker towards the end, but the change in pace is a great build up to the finale.

Loved the exploratory game-play and scarcity of ammo making the zombies in the first half of the game a real threat and an obstacle to overcome instead of something you point and click at to kill (although I do enjoy Resident Evil 6 for the opposite reason as well). When Mr X comes into the picture it adds a new layer of learning the outlay of the police station to effectively avoid him and complete whatever task you're trying to do. This does result in a ton of back-tracking as you revisit areas while take the long way around again and again to avoid him, but it did not sour the experience for me. Boss fights can be a bit eh, and sometimes just feel like the only reason they are there is to drain some of your resources you've been saving up (ammo, healing, grenades, etc).

The alternate campaign with the other protagonist (whoever of Leon and Claire you did not pick for your first playthrough) has new sections to explore, but does also retread a lot of the areas you visited previously. You have some new weapons and pathways to use to keep it fresh, but it could be frustrating for some.

While I am fine with Ethan's first person perspective in RE7 and Village, I am also glad to see Capcom is not done with third person camera angles.

[h1]Story[/h1]
As a remake of one of the classics most people will already be aware of the story of this game, but for the sake of completeness: it follows what has come to be the standard Resident Evil formula by these days (and was actually the standard formula when the original came out). You come into some kind of nightmare full of creatures returned from beyond the grave, or turned from living humans and you unravel the mystery and hope to stop the bad guy.

I like the way it plays out, even if the twists are obvious based on my knowledge from other games in the series.

I love all the characters!

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I did not play the original so I can't speak for its faithfulness to it, but Capcom have created an amazing game in its own right with the remake. I can recommend it for full price and if you get it on sale it's a steal. It's not the longest game, but long enough to make it worth the price - plus a few bonus modes when the main game is done.

If someone wants an easy point of entry into Resident Evil, Resident Evil 2 Remake is one of the best places to start. It balances survival horror and action extremely well, and after revisiting it on PC and pushing into higher difficulty runs, I appreciated its design even more than I did the first time.

The story is fairly straightforward, but the presentation carries it. The writing, performances, and atmosphere do a lot of the heavy lifting, and the small cast is memorable enough that the game stays engaging without needing anything especially complex. More than anything, the game succeeds at making each new area feel tense, dangerous, and worth pushing through.

Gameplay is where it really stands out. The best way I can describe it is that it feels like a survival horror escape room built around resource management, puzzle-solving, and constant pressure. Every item you find feels important, and every decision matters a little more because the game keeps enough danger around you to make simple progress feel rewarding. That balance between tension, planning, and payoff is what makes the game so satisfying.

Replayability is also one of its biggest strengths. Playing as Leon and Claire gives you enough variation to make repeat runs worthwhile, and the ranking system, unlockables, and extra modes give the game a lot of lasting value beyond a single playthrough. Officially, the remake supports separate Leon and Claire campaigns and includes extra modes from the original game, which lines up well with your point about it rewarding repeat runs.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is survival horror at its best and one of Capcom’s strongest remakes. It respects the original while modernizing it in a way that feels polished, tense, and highly replayable. I have easily revisited many times, and I still consider it one of the best modern Resident Evil games.

I want to love Resident Evil 2 Remake more than I actually do...

That's not to say that I dislike this game, far from it. Out of all of the games from this REvival period (that I have played), RE2 Remake is probably the best of the bunch. It's a real top quality game and one of the few truly good triple A horror games from the 2010s, trailing behind Dead Space 2 and The Evil Within 2. There's an evident passion and love for the source material, and that reverence pours through with just how meticulously crafted this game is. What I am saying is that Resident Evil 2 REmake is really, really good... but I feel like it just didn't click with me like I would have wanted.

I'll admit, I'm biased to the classic game this spawned from. In fact, the classic Resident Evil 2 from 1998 is my personal favorite game of all time. Is it objectively perfect, no, but it vibes with me like no other game. It's classic RE at it's most refined. As Simon Pegg in Spaced put it "It's a subtle blend of lateral thinking and extreme violence". ♥♥♥♥'s good basically, and there was no doubt that I was extremely excited when the E3 2018 reveal trailer dropped and I got to see my favorite twunk cop, trenchcoat daddy, and Claire in HD on the stunningly beautiful RE Engine. It was the first game I pre-ordered since L.A. Noire in 2011.

There was a vocal minority of Survival Horror Boomers that were upset by the game not being done in the style of the original (e.g. tank controls and fixed camera angles). I am not one of those people. I love classic survival horror games, from the popular series like Resident Evil, Silent Hill and Fatal Frame, to the more obscure and offbeat like Koudelka, Illbleed and D2. I've been around the block, and I generally know my stuff when it comes to these sorts of games. That being said, the time when that sort of horror game was at the forefront of the tripple A landscape is over, and has been for about 20 years now. For Capcom to spend millions of dollars on making a game in a niche style to appeal to the rather small niche of folks who deem themselves as "TRUE SURVIVAL HORROR FANS" is honestly kinda stupid.

These folks wanted a remake in the way of the classic REmake from 2002, but aside from impracticalities of that pipe dream that I listed above, REmake was born out of an ideal of fleshing out the original game. The original Resident Evil is what feels like a half finished painting, you can tell that there was probably a lot more that Shinji Mikami wanted to do with it but just couldn't at the time due to financial or technical difficulties, or even just lack of experience. People forget that REmake came out only six years after the original hit store shelves in 1996, and it wasn't because that style of survival horror went out of style (though it would in just three years), but because the game had been superseded by it's follow-ups in just about every way. So with the advent of more powerful tech and with a lot more experience under his belt, REmake was Mikami's chance to finish that painting.

In that same sense, RE2 went through a similar process all before the original came out. As most know, RE2 was an almost completely different game (dubbed RE1.5 by the fans) and development was rocky. The team behind 1.5 was not happy with their work, and it was basically almost complete before they scrapped it and made the RE2 we know today using all the experience they gained from the last project, keeping what worked and scrapping what didn't. Unlike RE1, the painting was finished by the time RE2 was released in 1998. So the question was never about tweaking and filling in the gaps of the original game, but rather adaptation.

And I think that's where a lot of my problems are, with the adaptation (or translation) of elements from the original work. I feel that in the bid to make the game more palatable to modern audiences, a fair bit of the charm was lost, and in some cases, I just think they kinda went overboard and disrupted the flow of the original.

Regarding the former point, the lack of real music in the game is a bit disappointing. Sure, one can just switch on the classic music switch (that's behind payed DLC), but it doesn't always mesh well with this new game. The original remake had both new tracks and redone old tracks to fit the tone, and they didn't do that here save for one of the boss fights iirc. It's become a trend in horror games to have most of the music be diegetic and forgo a proper OST for most of the game, and that's a shame, cause Resident Evil has some really iconic music over the years. I mean, it was iconic enough for them to slap the original OST in the game, so why not make a soundtrack that actually compliments the game? They've done it before.

The re-created police station is pretty neat and the level of fidelity is astounding, but I'd be lying if I said the areas really stood out like they did in the original, save for a small few like the lobby, Chief Irons' room and the central lab area. They kinda just fade into the background as largely dark, gray, indistinct hallways whereas the original game had them all be visually unique.

The lack of a proper A/B scenario here is just sad. They have a halfhearted attempt here to do that, but now you have some real story consistency issues that are somehow more baffling than the originals. You characters that get killed by a boss, only to show up in another character's scenario, to get killed by the same boss... again. It's like the worst fusion of RE1's separate-but-both-canon scenarios and RE2's A/B scenarios. It's just really dumb.

As for the latter criticism, they made three big tweaks to the game that I'm really not the biggest fan of, those being Mr. X, the side character bits and the sewer.

I'll be the first to admit, I just kinda hate pursuer characters. I don't really find them scary, rather I find them to be just kinda annoying, especially when they are unkillable. They turn the game into a hide-n-seek simulator, much like Clock Tower or Amnesia, which is not fun (to me). And when you do down Mr. X, there really isn't any reward like with Nemesis or even Mr. X in the original. No ammo or weapon upgrades, you just get him to stay down for like, 20 seconds or so, and it's almost never worth the ammo to do so.

Secondly, the side character portions where you play as Ada or Sherry were never great in RE2, they were just a box puzzle and ammo collection snippet that only last like, 5 minutes each. ESPECIALLY on hardcore mode. Ada's is not great, but it at least it doesn't drag things to a halt like Sherry's section. 

On the subject of dragging, the sewer is just bad. They extended it to be a somewhat sizable area rather than just a transitional place where you grab two medals and ♥♥♥♥ off on the tram to the lab. It just keeps going for ages, and the mini-boss they turned into a regular enemy here sucks to fight against. This area is my least favorite in the original, but it's quick. Here, it's both bad and longer than it needs to be. Once again, it's mildly bearable in the first run through, but sucks on repeats, and that's been a real problem with most of the REvival games, where the first playthrough is prioritized, and each playthrough afterwords is diminished due to long set pieces that drag ass (like RE7 intro and 8's village raid and House Beneviento).

I've dragged the game hard in this review, but I do wanna say that I do really enjoy most of this game and respect the work put into it, but there's just too many things keeping me from loving it like I wanted to when I saw that reveal trailer at E3 2018, which is a damn shame.

Having never had the opportunity to play the original RE:2, I was so happy when the remake was announced. I've now played it on Xbox, PS and the superior version, PC.

Story - Enjoyable story for what is an already well established staple story of the survival horror genre. Great characters and brilliantly voice acted. This being said, I would have wanted more variety in the B scenarios as this is something that was noticeablely flawed to me. I liked the idea of having 2 different runs for both characters however for me, it was poorly executed. There are barely any differences between Leon and Claire other than different bosses, weapons and slight route changes which just isn't enough in my opinion.

Gameplay - Veteran fans of this series remember the fixed camera and tank controls but what I love about what they've done here is the mix RE:4 and old school inventory management. Nothing revolutionary but why change a winning formula. Unlocking infinite ammo weapons behind S rank and S+ rank was a great idea, gaining interest from people who otherwise don't enjoy the 'hardcore' difficulties to at-least give it a try. I generally play games on hard difficulty but with games like RE, I typically go with normal due to the fact that i'm not amazing at survival horror games. However, with hardcore I felt the right amount of challenge without it becoming unfair and annoying which unfortunately alot of devs seem to confuse the 2, it was however done brilliantly here. Mr X was also extremely well done, getting chased through rooms that you haven't already cleared is nerve-racking.

Graphics - Game looks stunning, as is everything that's put through the RE engine. The character models and detailing of the environment are also brilliant.

Audio - The audio was spot on, very good work, especially with the zombie screeches however I feel like the guns could have done with a bit more oomph. Also being able to get the original RE menu sounds and soundtrack was a nice addition.

DLC - Nothing harmful here, just some nice cosmetic items and cool guns (Excluding the infinite ammo instant unlocks...)

Game modes - Whilst I appreciate the efforts put in, I really wasn't a fan of the Ghost Survivor runs. 

Overall, RE: 2 remake is a fantastic game and sits at the top of my list for all time favourites. Whilst my RE journey began with RE: 5, this is the game that has since got me playing the originals.

*SPOILER-FREE REVIEW*

Resident Evil 2 Remake is a master-class in survival horror with how it integrates unsettling ambiance with its realistic graphics and sound design along with survival horror mechanics such as inventory management, and its constant introduction of new threats as you get familiar with the game's mechanics.

Pros:
-Straightforward map system where items/locked doors/puzzles you've missed will be shown on the map 
-Cool locations with realistic graphics and immersive atmosphere with the lighting and sound design
-Satisfying route progression to do with obtaining a key item for a lock that you found at a location you left a few hours back but you then end up finding a hidden route back to that location 
-Never a dull moment even when there's backtracking since they keep introducing new threats as you familiarize yourself with the map 
-Besides the zombies, they have other unique enemies, and there'll be hints as to how to deal with them best which'll have you strategize on conserving specific types of ammunition or completely evading them
-Inventory management will make you strategize on what items to prioritize on bringing and makes for a thrilling experience if you have full inventory slots when you have to get that 1 key item to progress through the game especially if backtracking will be a pain
-Interesting "combine" mechanic to make different types of ammo and health items that will have you think on what combinations will work best with your playstyle 

Cons:
-Wasn't too satisfied with the Boss fights when it just involves running around a limited area and shooting their obvious vital points
-With there being 2 playable characters Claire & Leon, there's a 2nd run option where you play as e.g. Leon after you beat Claire's route and vice versa. Considering how they're part of the same story with different roles in the game, the amount of similarities there were with their routes broke the immersion that Claire had actually went through all that you've gone through during your first run. Examples include Leon solving the same puzzle as Claire when Claire had long left that certain location which required said puzzle to be solved, beating the exact same boss, and plot points that completely disregarded certain events from Claire's first run

All in all the cons are just small problems I had with the game, and the the pros farrrr outweigh the bad! So glad I got to play this masterpiece of a survival horror game, HIGHLY RECOMMENDED😆😆😆

This is how you do a remake!! Game looks amazing, and has good controls. My only nitpick is the lack of interaction between Leon and Claire during the game and a proper B senario. Overall they did an amazing job on this remake (unlike re3) and I would definitely recommend to any survival horror fan.

It's okay for a single run through, I would say it's a strong rent game. Play it once then never touch it again, it's the best way to get the most positive experience out of it. I did enjoy my first run through with both characters, minus some petty gripes it was a fun experience, the crows feet only emerged once I started replaying for extras.

Hitboxes can be wildly inaccurate to some characters bodies, expect to get hit or grabbed from 2 meters away by bigger enemies. Movement, especially turning circles, feels sluggish at crucial times, very similar to GTA IV or RDR1. Control overall feels rather spastic, again with the aforementioned turning circles you'll frequently end up swivelling into furniture or getting stuck on the corner of desks, bearing in mind this game has no dodge mechanic so quick turns are the only real course for evasion, and it feels very cheap to have Leon or Claire essentially walk towards an enemy when you try to move back because the turning circles are so wide at times. The main problem for me though is how RNG heavy the game can be with challenge runs, zombies sometimes take as many as 25 pistol shots to the head to kill on hardcore difficulty, emphasis on the 'sometimes', because other times they only take 15, or 10, or 5, or even 1 if you luck out with an instant critical. That just ruins so much of the sense of achievement for me. Not only does it feel somewhat condescending for the game to essentially hand you an easy victory at random with an instakill, but it invalids the effort you put in to conserve resources when a single enemy can drain them all just because you rolled a 1 with damage. Who cares if you skillfully navigated an entire section of the map without firing a bullet, because now this one zombie in your way that you can't get past without killing is going to tank 20 bullets to the leg and refuse to fall over or stagger for you to move past. This kind of thing consistently ruined all repeat playthroughs I did whilst achievement hunting, and as far as I remember not a single run ended up being fun, nor satisfying to beat.

I also think most of the elements in this game that people praise so much really take away from replay value. Mr X was fun the first time, not scary because his goofy face and inspector gadget cosplay always makes me chuckle, but he added a cool tension to the game (for the brief period where he organically roams after you at least), but my god is he the most tedious, boring, uninteresting thing on repeat runs, he's essentially just a timer mechanic in a funny hat. Coupled with the RNG of bullet damage and enemy AI, it really weighed on my will to live as I stand on the other side of a library door, listening to him repeatedly try the door that's blocked from the other side as my S rank time slowly slips away because I need to get in there to progress with the damn game.

Extra modes are at best underwhelming. They're completely detached from the main game, just little time trial runs through insanely dense populations of enemies, with the exception of the final ghost survivor mode which is a kinda wave defense thing, different but plays ultimately the same, aka trial and error praying to RNJesus and once you beat it a single time never looking back or wanting to bother with it ever again. It's a shame they didn't do anything like Separate Ways, or Assignment Ada, something more substantial and in line with the core game, not just action arcadey speedrun modes that most people will play once and never touch again.

Personally I think the lions share of the value of this game is meant to be in the replays, getting S ranks, EX weapons, challenge/achievement runs etc, and that's why I don't think I can give it a thumbs up. My initial scenario A and B runs took 5.5 and 4.5 hours respectively, but all achievements totalled me about 50 hours, so roughly speaking that's only about 20% of my experience was positive, and I think I can safely say I regret spending the time getting those extra achievements, I just let my love of the RE franchise convince me it was worth it. I wish I could enjoy this game as much as everyone else does, but it just doesn't work for me, too many fundamental flaws in the fine details make it nothing but tedium to keep playing after the first run.

Oh, and you get a negative review on principle for locking the OG soundtrack and unlockable costumes behind paywalls, for shame.
