This is a review from a newcomer to the series, if you're looking for the PoV of an OG fan coming back to a remake this won't be for you.

The review is based on mostly Hardcore difficulty playthroughs aside from my first one in Standard.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The game manages to instil a sense of dread on you from the first step into Racoon City to the last. A blind playthrough will have you wondering whats on the other side of the door every time you advance in the game.
This may seem like the ambience section but it's important to mention this point before praising this gem! The zombies feel like a real threat despite their sluggish pace, the guns feel great to fire and reward proper marksmanship, the puzzles are interesting yet brief landing on that sweet spot between challenging and annoying, the resource management is fun and well adjusted for the different difficulties heavily rewarding the mastery of efficient routes and properly countering the encountered enemies.

[h1]Ambience[/h1]
I will avoid spoilers by only addressing the police station as a whole since its heavily advertised and visible on the preview images of this page but this does apply for the entire game.
Every single room I entered felt hand crafted and (un)lived in having a story to tell from how it was to what went wrong.
The edge you feel exploring new territory and the relief of reaching a safe room is only heightened by the amazing graphics and soundtrack putting games in 2021 to shame. Overall an incredibly pleasant experience.

[h1]Story[/h1]
I don't want to dive too much into it to avoid spoilers but it's an interesting plot as you uncover more and more about this living nightmare. Theres plenty of documents to collect to deepen the lore but it's a great experience even while ignoring those.
Theres a total of 4 main stories, 2 for each main character divided between 1st and 2nd run which complement each other lore wise.
I recommend playing both the first and second playthrough as different characters for the full experience.
Theres an additional story unlocked once you complete the 2nd run that is worth the playthrough the rest of the Ghost Survivor stories are "what ifs" that explore how characters that are only mentioned or briefly seen could have tackled the apocalypse following a more arcade/speedrun format without much story, they're worth the play for the challenge/fun but add nothing to the actual plot.

[h1]Length[/h1]
This will be subjective depending on how well you adjust to the game I suppose, I personally completed my first playthrough (Claire) in around 4/5 hours but know of people that took much longer. Once you master the game you can complete it between 1 and 2 hours. Don't be fooled by these single digit numbers however there is much replay value if you enjoy the grind to master the game.

[h1]Quality/Bugs[/h1]
I had 0 bugs (at least that I've noticed) during my entire playtime. I can't speak for how the game was or wasn't but right now its what most strive to be, extremely polished and smooth performance wise.

[h1]Price[/h1]
I bought the game while it had a small discount but I still recommend it at whichever price point you find it at trully worth your money. As far as the DLC goes it seems to be cosmetics only and the infinite ammo unlocks if those interest you by all means buy them but I'd stay away from the infinite ammo weapons as these will ruin the experience for you, only time I recommend them is while achievement hunting (you do get them for completing some of them however).

[h1]Closing thoughts[/h1]
I have been a fan of the zombie genre for a long time but always avoided the Resident Evil games due never really being recommended them by friends or just seeing thoughts on later entries that weren't exactly welcomed.
I am super glad I decided to see it for myself, a real masterpiece that created yet another fan of this amazing series.
As of writing this review I just finished getting 100% achievements and getting ready to start a playthrough of Resident Evil 3 while eagerly awaiting the 8th entry. Don't be skeptical of trying this gem you owe it to yourself if it interests you in the slightest.

[b]+ Visuals: [/b]Played the game at 80% and, ignoring some awkward reflections here and there, the game looks awesome.

[h1] Overall Opinion [/h1]
I did not play much of the original Resident Evil 2 and I remember even less about it. To my surprise, Capcom has managed to produce a delightfully modernised and captivating remake that is likely to appeal to many fans of the genre, even if this is your first entry into the RE series.

To be candid, I have little interest in many of the entries from the Resident Evil franchise, especially those that overemphasise the action portions of the game to the point of comicality. However, this RE2 Remake seems to tick many of the boxes when it comes to finding a healthy balance between fun and engaging gameplay, and adequate storytelling.

[h1] Story [/h1]
I think the term "adequate" is appropriate here as the game is definitely not without its narrative quirks and somewhat cliché sequence of events, however, the characters are substantive enough to deliver a story with enough integrity for you to see it through to the end without an unbearably bitter aftertaste. I am also somewhat lenient towards the story's writing as I understand the developers' desire to remain relatively faithful to the original work. That being said, the game is far from breaking free of the superfluous stereotyping that plagues much of the industry, viz. weak story arcs and two-dimensional side characters.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]
The puzzles are engaging enough without being overly taxing or precarious that it would otherwise steal from the game's entertainment during the more tense parts of the story. The standard zombies in the game are appropriately formidable as to always feel dangerous to the player without being too arduous to deal with during casual gameplay; only becoming "bullet sponges" during a Hardcore difficulty playthrough. The variety of enemies that you will encounter is likewise balanced such as to keep the gameplay interesting while simultaneously not overburdening you with having to remember an excessive amount of strategies to counter each one. The special enemies and bosses in the game still inspire anxiety even beyond the first playthrough yet always feel beatable so long as you are deliberate with how you use your ammunition and consumables.

[h1] Different Story & Extra Modes [/h1]
The game feels well fleshed out and ample in length. The main story takes place along 1 of 2 plotlines that run somewhat concurrently to one another: story A (the default game) and story B (the second run).

Story A is the first experience by default and is better paced to set the mood and scene of the game while gradually introducing the player to the various mechanics. Story A can be played as either Leon or Claire and remains mostly the same between the 2 with the exception of some unique differences in the side characters and ending boss encounters.

Story B becomes available by completing story A (as either Leon or Claire) and puts the player more immediately into the action (as a result, the story arc feels much weaker). The puzzles and obstacles remain largely the same as in story A but with just enough differences to keep you on your toes for the entire playthrough. Story B can also be played as either Leon or Claire (again, each with their own unique differences) and with subtle changes to make it arguably a little harder than story A.

Completing story B will net you the so-called "true" ending of the game, as described by the developers.

Additionally, there are a number of extra modes that deviate from the main story of Leon and Claire. It was genuinely interesting to explore these "what might have been" scenarios for the different side characters. In doing so, the characters themselves feel less superficial and in turn help to portray the dystopian setting of Raccoon City a little better.

[h1] Length [/h1]
The average and unfamiliar player can perhaps expect to spend about 6-8 hours on their story A playthrough (completing everything), about 4-6 hours on their story B playthrough (completing everything), and another few hours attempting the various extra modes/challenges.

These extra modes are largely independent of the main story arc and offer shorter, arcade-style challenges to complete.

[h1] State [/h1]
Much to my amazement, during my 40+ hours of gameplay thus far, I am yet to encounter any bugs or issues with the game in any of the different game modes. To Capcom's advantage, the game had already been released for over 2 years when I first purchased it.

Resident Evil 2 Remake, unlike the Resident Evil 3 Remake, takes original content and expands upon it. The game is quite simply a masterpiece. It maintains a creepy atmosphere, and brings back the true survival horror experience. Ammo is scarce and the zombies are more threatening than ever. The common complaints people have towards the game are solved by a simple "git gud", but I will list them anyway. Also the Resident Evil Engine is gorgeous and they made it clear they have abandoned the horrid fixed camera angles and the outdated tank controls.

Common Complaint 1: "The zombies are too tanky."
-While this is true it serves a gamplay purpose, that being it has tight corridors and few zombies compared to re4 and re5 where you can get swarmed. This makes the game scarier because zombies are to be feared and not be some bullet fodder.

Common Complaint 2: T-00 (Mr. X)
Mr. X is first seen as scary and rightfully so. His A.I. is quite advanced and can find you faster depending on how much noise you make. People then argue after many playthroughs he becomes annoying but just like the zombies he serves a gameplay purpose. After the player gets over the initial fear of the police station atmosphere and zombies, a new tension is added, a pursuer. This constant pressure from the Tyrant will keep players on their toes and this is a good thing for horror.

Common Complaint 3: "Ammo is too scarce."
Most Modern fans of the series started with Resident Evil 4; Resident Evil 4 is excellent, but it spoon-feeds the player ammo and herbs which as a result, destroys the survival horror experience. RE2 Remake sticks to the roots of the original and it catches the newer fans off guard.

The pros of the game far outweigh the cons: excellent controls on PC (Which is rare for PC RE games), simple but effective story, good puzzles, great exploration, and the spawn of infamous Redfield lineage meme. The game is polished and made with love and I hope Capcom keeps this trend for the upcoming RE8 and the RE4 Remake.

So, I'm kinda split down the middle with this one. On one hand, the game is an excellent survival horror title if I look at it stand-alone. On the other, if I compare it to the game it's a remake of... I can't say that I prefer this version. Basically, all the content cut from the original, plus some goofy decisions when it comes to balance, make it hard for me to call this the 'definitive edition'. At the same time, this is far more playable thanks to updates to controls and the like. So, what do I mean by 'goofy'? Well, blue herbs, for instance, are barely used in this version. All of the enemies, besides one, that can poison you AT ALL have been removed. What else? Dynamic difficulty. It just doesn't belong in any survival horror title, since resource management is a KEY part of what makes the game qualify as such. The doors are goofy... Sometimes zombies can't get in places for... reasons. And finally, Mr. X is much less scary here. I felt over-exposed to him, where he became more of an annoyance than a worry. (This is all in addition to the extra scenarios being pointless in the remake.)

I guess my point is, this is just another game from Capcom that feels a bit rushed out the door. They have a good start here, a REALLY good one at that. Just... if they'd actually remade the WHOLE game, I wouldn't be left feeling like this is still inferior to the original in so many ways.

Anyway, I'd still say that it's probably worth your $40... or just play the ps1 version, up to you.

Resident Evil 2 is an official remake of the game with the same name released in 1998. The remake version utilizes over-the-shoulder view like most third-person games nowadays, rather than the fixed camera view in the original. In this game you play as Leon and Claire, 2 survivors of the zombie outbreak. While both characters have their own story modes, honestly it feels more like a "what if" scenario, since both campaigns use the same maps and similar puzzles, with only some unique areas and meeting different NPCs being the difference. However, to unlock the true, extended ending you need to play as both characters, one in New Game (Scenario A) and the other in 2nd Run (Scenario B).

While this game might seem like a linear, third-person horror shooter, for me it's more like a puzzle game with survival horror elements. While some parts of the game are linear (usually the "transition" areas), the main story just consists of 3 large, open areas, where you must solve a puzzle to progress. The puzzles in A and B have minor differences, but mostly the same. It's not like, Evil Within for example, which is a linear shooter. The story for one character's campaign is quite short, and doable in 2-3 hours if you're already familiar. It is also not recommended to try killing all zombies, as they are quite hard to kill even with a headshot, and in the end you're just wasting ammo. If they're knocked down, you can just run past them. 

There is also a free DLC included, named The Ghost Survivors. It consists of 5 short, linear missions where you play as dead NPCs encountered during the main story in an alternate scenario. There are no puzzles here, just lots of enemies to fight and avoid. 3 of them can be played in an easier difficulty, while the other 2 only has one difficulty option and are both really difficult. If you like survival horror shooters, you'll like Resident Evil 2. Just keep in mind that you need to manage your inventory and ammo.

TL;DR: A great game with a decent story and excellent puzzles.

Pros:
-Gameplay: Very fun. Gunplay feels very responsive and I enjoyed the difficulty in killing Zombies. Like in the first game every kill has to be judged by necessity. Do I really need to use my bullets to clear this corridor or am I just better off dodging each time? 
-Puzzles: The first games puzzles varied greatly in quality in my opinion but this games puzzles all work well with not too much "adventure game logic". Some puzzles require backtracking but in a way that makes sense (In my opinion). Also tons of extra mini puzzles with there answers often hidden in the environment to solve that all work really well.
-Atmosphere: The game oozes a spooky atmosphere (though toned down from the 1st game). Zombies slow turn towards you as they realize your presence, the loud footsteps of a pursuing monster, the creaking of floor boards alerting you that you are no longer alone the game uses everything in it's power to drag you into Racoon City and (IMO) succeeds greatly at it.
- Graphics: Graphics are fantastic. Even at lower settings the game looks great.
-Music: Excellent. Sets the tone very well and varies greatly throughout each level,

Neutral:
-Writing: I liked the writing but it is VERY campy. If you like that type of stuff you'll love it if not then this games story probably wont be for you. The voice actors do a good job with what there given but a lot of lines are very cheesy. Personally I enjoyed that aspect of the game but understand that others might not.

Cons:
- Bosses: If I was to have one minor nitpick with this game it would be that the bosses weren't very fun in my opinion. There built up well but I felt gameplay wise they weren't great. 

Conclusion:
A high recommend for those looking for a Spooky game or a game with a great atmosphere.

TLRD:Having never played the original RE2, I went into this with no expectations about how the remake should or should't be. So with that said, I really enjoyed this remake. 

The game runs excellent and is highly optimized-- can run at 120 fps with almost max settings on a GTX1080ti. The RE engine is excellent imo. 

The game-play itself is very well refined, especially when compared to RE4, 5, and 6. The controls feel good, and nothing seems awkward or too difficult to learn. My only complaint about the controls is the lack of a dodge mechanic given how slow the player moves compared to a couple of the bosses. However, Capcom added a dodge in RE3 Remake, so I suppose they listened to people who had the same complaint.

The story is good, but nothing super amazing. The characters are likable and the voice acting was well done in both English and Japanese dub. As stated earlier, I cannot compare the Remake's story to the original's because I have never played it, but I think some people said there may be a couple of minor areas that were redone to accommodate the new engine and play-style. My biggest gripe is that the game feels relatively short compared to other games in the franchise like 4-6. I went into my first playthrough completely blind and took my time to explore and loot everything to my heart's content and still managed to finish the entire run in about 8 or 9 hours. Then, on subsequent runs, I have even managed to get consistent times as low as 1.5 hours without even really trying to speed run or anything. With that said, the replayability is fantastic, as is with just about every Resident Evil game (yes, I'm looking at you RE4 with like 100 playthroughs logged and counting.... lol that game was my childhood).

The atmosphere of the game is downright perfect. Capcom did an excellent job captivating what it would be like to be inside of a zombie apocalypse. Ammo is scarce, nothing ever works in your favor, and you can NEVER trust a body-- Rule #2 double tap. Being a fan of horror movies, haunted houses, and spooky shi t in general, this game is so relaxing(?) for me to play because of how amazing and enjoyable the creepy, ominous atmosphere is. The game is straight up eerie. And don't get me started on Mr.X.... You don't know the meaning of anxiety until you hear 400lbs footsteps clopping on the ground getting louder and louder (and faster and faster) as you frantically look 360 degrees trying to find the source. It's too good.

Resident Evil 2: Remake Review


So many memories, so many great experiences…, and they are all back!

Please note that this Review may contain spoilers from the Original game 

Some key points that this Remaster offers:

1.	Complete Remake of the original
2.	New areas
3.	New Weapons
4.	New Gameplay Mechanics

Remake:

They remade the whole game from the ground up. Every little detail is new and made to represent current gen. Character models, monster designs, buildings and objects look absolutely incredible.

If you played the original and then this one, it experience is unforgeable. The same great places with one hell of a makeover… Beautiful lighting effects, reflections that enhances the beauty and horror of the situation you find yourself in. Putting the entirety of it into words does not do it justice… The beauty present in the RE2 Remake is absolutely incredible, and it is present in all aspects of the game.  It fits in perfectly with the survival horror game that brought nightmares to our game times way back then… Seeing it again in this remade version brought so much back… 

For returning players, you are in for one fantastic nostalgia trip. New player will experience a beautiful and masterful survival horror game. They updated the game mechanics as well. We no longer have Tank controls; Similar to RE7 we now have an over the shoulder view and we can move about as we aim and defend ourselves. Adding to the mechanics are sub weapons, we have the use of grenades and a combat knife. The combat knife has a durability bar and as it gets used it withers down and eventually breaks. 

The soundtrack is different, which is to be expected. Albeit it doesn’t have that eerie feel to it like the original did, the remade one does wonders for its own game. The game portrays a stunning survival horror game. There is ample atmosphere to keep you on your toes clenching your teeth, and before you realize it a zombie is on top of you…, if you’re lucky that is. There are other things running amok here as well.

Locations in the game didn’t just receive a visual remake, they also got expanded. You can expect new areas in some locations whilst others were just enlarged when compared to their original sizes. There are so much more to this remake, you will have to play it to fully take this incredible experience in.

Don’t forget the additional content we enjoyed back then… Some of them made their way here as well, along with some new ones… Once you beat the game you will start unlocking additional modes that you can partake in.

MGR Gaming’s Conclusions:

Looking back at what I wrote, it does not feel like I did this game justice. They did incredible work with this Remake, that is for sure. There are a few notables that was a let-down… They removed some of the monsters we faced in the original which did suck to be honest… here I was sneaking through sewers just waiting for them to pounce on me, yet they never showed… The game does make up for it with numerous regular Zombies that can be found pretty much everywhere.
Several other changes were made to the game. Some small and others a tad larger, however, without spoiling them, I personally think it enhanced the experience as a whole, whilst offering some new variables in the remake. However, most importantly, they fit in perfectly with the lore of where Resident Evil is now.

Just like the original, the remake offers incredible replay value. Not only to beat your campaign scores by going faster and faster…, there are several new game modes that you can try out, each of them designed to give you some serious challenges. Let me tell you know, as hard as they are they are incredible fun to play.

With the updated mechanics and removal of the Tank controls it can go both ways. There is some veteran RE players that love those controls to this very day. I myself am one of them. Back then it was an acceptable combat and control mechanics, which happened to fit in perfectly with what Resident Evil was all about. 

They tried to maintain it over the years slightly changing and improving it as time went by. It did change the nature of the series to a more action shooter based game, but RE 2: remake does not follow. Just like RE7 the game is a full on Horror Survival experience. This is not Gears of War, or any other shooter game, it was never made to compete with games like that and not should it be compared to them. The new combat mechanics works pretty well in my opinion. We have freedom of movement; we have sub weapons which essentially acts as a counter attack as well.

I recently replayed RE 4 again and the first game I picked up after it was this one. And to be honest, it felt like a breeze getting into the handling and control mechanics of the game. Sure, enough this game has its own challenges, but for me, the new mechanics enhanced the overall experience at the cost of immersion. Something I can understand for this day and age.

I took the RE2: Remake as a sequel to the RE games, not a comparison to other games because Resident Evil has never been about that. It is here that they excelled once again delivering us a fantastic experience. If you are a RE fan you are in for a world of fun.

Hey everyone! I beat RE2 on Standard around a year ago (Leon A and Claire B) and recently decided to go back to it. Originally my plan was simply to beat the game on Hardcore with both... aaand I ended up going for S+ Hardcore and getting all achievements. Whoops. No seriously, I adore this game!

-I love the interconnected design. It's most visible in RPD, but sewers and NEST have it too to an extent. You need to visit some locations more then once, but what might've been frustrating in a linear design feels like a huge playground in the locations that open up and connect back on themselves. It's also one of the biggest boosts to replayability in my opinion, having multiple options makes planning out your route more interesting.

-I love the game encouraging disabling and avoiding enemies over killing them. The toughness of zombies combined with the relative scarcity of ammo means killing everyone is impractical, and it's better to just shoot to stun and run/shoot off legs in many situations, and kill sparingly.

-The fact you can shoot off legs. And arms for that matter, though I feel like the head or the legs is always a better target. Stun and a chance at significantly lowering the threat of a zombie? Yes please!

-Mr. X is great. The pursuit feels quite organic, adds good tension to the game, and goes back to the interconnectivity thing. If you know your way around RPD he doesn't feel as bad since there's usually a way or two to go around him and still get to your destination, and he encourages remembering it and thinking of plans B on the fly.

-The limited inventory (especially on Hardcore) adds into route planning. Can you really afford to pick this up? You'll need two slots for that gear later. Maybe leave it for later? Will there be a later? At least for me it also encouraged skimming out on healing to save on inventory, which I feel like helped me get better.

-And since we're on topic of routing: The ranks. I appreciate the game giving me a goal to strive towards beyond just "beat the game" and I know I personally wouldn't bother trying to beat the game quickly if it didn't give me an idea of what it considers a good time. Striving to achieve S+ allowed me to discover and appreciate just how interesting and well designed the previously mentioned mechanics are.

I could probably go for longer, but I feel like this is enough for now. I just really felt the need to share my love for this game and how it doubles down on replayability.

As a huge fan of the series since its debut, I was really looking forward to this remake of one of my favorite PS1 games. I know im the minority here when I say this, but RE2 Remake is kinda overrated and not all that great. RE Revelations 1 and 2 are far better than this game. 

Good Stuff:
+Game looks gorgeous. 
+Updated map is fantastic- it shows the names of the rooms, what rooms youve been in, save points, item boxes, what items are left to collect in each room (provided you visited the room first), along with what kind of key youll need for the doors, etc so you no longer have to painstakingly keep track of which room is which like the original. Also, when you get everything in the room (if there are items) it will turn from red to blue on the map. Very handy!
+Those "loading door" screens are gone. I always hated those. Loading altogether is very minimal and fast too .
+HDR shines in this game- way better than RE7 imo. 
+I like how they added a feature where you can find boards lying around to patch up windows so zombies cant come in, (although its quickly abandoned later on). 
+Controls are miles better than the old tank style and those irritating static camera angles are finally gone. Wish they would do that with the first REmake.

Bad Stuff:
-Zombies take 4,5,6 headshots (or more) to kill them. Its very inconsistent throughout the game and gets annoying fast. I played on Normal. 
-They added sub weapons to assist you if you get grabbed by a zombie but no melee attack at all. If you dont have a sub-weapon available (knife, grenade or flash grenade), when you get grabbed by a zombie your character just stands there and takes damage. There's no way to push them off you either which is just ridiculous. And if your sub weapon is a knife the only way to get it back is to waste ammo and kill the zombie or find another one. The knife will also eventually break too...thats a high quality knife right there. Imagine if your gun broke if you shot too many bullets in this game...maybe theyre saving that for the RE4 remake though, (i really hope not). 
-Zombies will have this incredible intuition where once you get close they spin around and have this enormous reach to grab you, causing damage (unless you have a sub weapon, but see above). And once they see you they dont ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ stop, they just keep coming after you- even if youre far away and out of sight. Your character doesnt run very fast either.
-Having to backtrack alllllll the way around an area, go up and down stairways just trying to get on the other side of the room I was originally in...just like in the original game. Especially if you get a new story item like a key or something, new zombies will suddenly appear in areas youve already cleared (even if you used the previously mentioned boards to keep them out too), just like the original which feels very artificial now. 
-While I did like the new map, they decided to remove the glimmer of keys and items in game...WHY?!? So you basically have to sweep the room waiting for a button prompt to pop up, or alternatively- checking the map to see if its red or blue. The map also takes up only half the screen with the other side blank for some reason. Thankfully though you can move it around and zoom in and out. But still...utilize the whole screen ffs!
-Voice acting isnt all that great. A lot of the dialogue is really, really bad too. (I know RE is B-movie fare, but I was expecting a lot more for a modern AAA remake of a classic.)
-Ada Wong went from mysterious in the PS1 version to a boring cookie-cutter version in the remake. 
-Leon's character model looks way too similar to the blonde kid from the Backstreet Boys...hairstyle and all. I guess Capcom Want It That Way. 
-The "Original Version Soundtrack Swap" is a cool addition but is paid dlc that I think shouldve been included from the start. No eerie save room music like the original here, hell- even the title screen announcer isnt there like every. other. game. (unless you buy the dlc then he shows up). Its amusing that Capcom gave away the character models from the original game for free but the music? Pay up. 

Now its been over twenty years since Ive played the original RE2 and since then games and my preferences have changed of course. But when more modern games like Dead Space 1 and 2, Evil Within 1 and 2 and the fantastic but overlooked/underrated RE Revelations games do survival horror in its own way which i think is much better it makes this game seem like it wants to [i] look [/i] modern but for the most part- stay in the past.

RE2 Remake the best remake on the market. A grand statement when there are so many out there, but it improves upon the original in nearly every meaningful way.  It ticks all the right boxes for nostalgia, including some goofy old game modes post-ending, while still adding enough new elements to transform those old tank controls into a pretty damn good 3rd person shooter in its own right.    While i can't sing this game's praises enough to fans of the original, newcomers should be warned that the game is fairly short.  This is made slightly more tolerable due to a high replay value from presenting the main scenario with 4, albeit mostly minor, variations.  Another potential con, although most long-term fans of the series at this point would probably rate it as a positive, is that the story and presentation here can dip into absurd and campy territory.   The writing and acting are all leaps and bounds above the original, and there are genuine moments in the story where these elements start to shine, but more often than not you find yourself snapped back to the reality that you're playing through the plot of a 90s horror game as your character makes an absurd quip and readies a weapon to deal with whatever many-eyed monstrosity lumbered into the middle of the scene.
I was apprehensive when Capcom showed the first reveal trailer for this, but in the end i can't recommend it enough.

This game is a slow burning horror nightmare. What makes it so terrifying is that every point in the game where you feel slightly more comfortable in the atmosphere and engaging with enemies, the game introduces a new variable to slam you back into instability. Being kept on your toes while still feeling like you're gaining a better understanding of the flow of the game is such a key element in horror games. Most horror games usually strip your abilities down to nought, which has the player just avoiding enemies the whole time. Basically a running simulator. Games like this that come to mind are Alien Isolation, Slender the Arrival, and Amnesia. While these are great horror experiences, it's not as exciting as your goal is really just to sneak for 4 hours of game time. I think an engaging horror game should give the player little victories. It changes a 1 dimensional horror game into an experience that draws more feeling from the player. For that reason, RE2 is fun and terrifying.

[h1]One of the best remakes out there[/h1]

After a very decent Resident Evil 7, CAPCOM decided that it was the turn for one of the most cherished games of the franchise to have a remake. Does RE2 2019 stand up to its name? Absolutely.

RE2 2019 recycles some key elements from RE7, like the menus, probably the graphics engine and in general all the non-gameplay elements. What it does best is the remake of the original RE2. The story is more or less the same, but new mechanics lead to a very fluent gameplay. The characters and the core story of the game is very well developed, so both lovers from the original and newcomers will enjoy this title. It presents interesting enemies and trademarks not only for the franchise but in general for the Survival Horror genre, like the Mutated Dogs or the frightening Lickers. The puzzles, the tension… everything works very good in this title, specially the first time that you complete it (you will have then the option to complete another time the game, but with a different character… it is not very different, but this adds a few more hours to the game, which is always good).

All and all this is a very good game, one of those that, when you play it, you will be thinking: “this game is so good”. Worth it for the full price, and highly recommended if you find it for a good price on sales.

This game is phenomenal on so many levels, especially as a remake, so I'll try my best to briefly discuss each awesome aspect of the game despite me haven't getting 100% on it.

[b] The gameplay: 9/10 [/b]

The gameplay is amazing! There is a versatile amount of guns to utilize alongside other weapons, but the ammo and grenades are limited and achieve a great balance. People do complain about how zombies sponge up a lot of bullets, and I do agree, but honestly I think it adds to the challenge which I like. Speaking of zombies, there are so many types, and the bosses are insane! My favorite out of all of these, however, is Mr. X. He constantly follows you around throughout the game, which adds for tension all throughout and legit terrifies you.

[b] The story/characters: 8/10 [/b]

I enjoyed the story within this game, but have a particular problem with it. Leon's and Claire's routes intersect in many areas, which kinda ♥♥♥♥♥ up the story, never mind the fact that the game's story is, albeit slightly, changed from the original RE2. Regardless, there are many strong points about them that make up for it. For one, there is an insane amount of documents spread about the game that adds to the lore. Sure, some of y'all don't care, but I think they are intriguing. Another more important point is the amount of characters in the story. They are all great and have distinct personalities, hell some even hit home with you on an emotional beat which makes the story much more engaging. The best part is that you get to play a lot of them at one point or another, which varies the gameplay and adds their perspectives of the story.

[b] The graphics design/art/performance: 10/10 [/b]

When I saw the trailer, I thought "hmm, this game looks darn good." But damn did I underestimate the power of RE: Engine.  Not only does this game look spectacular, it runs solid if you got a decent build. Some settings you can turn down without noticing a difference, like the lighting from high to medium, and still get significant fps boost if you need it. Back to graphics, textures are crisp, character designs and models are so crisp they're basically real, fire and water effects look awesome, and the settings... OH MY GAWD. For a town, you get to see so much of it, and it all looks beautiful. I can't do it justice with words.

I also want to dedicate some attention to the attention to detail. Some of it goes hand in hand with gameplay, but there is a lot of detail here: your character will pat themself dry when coming inside from rain, they put their hands up to block heat from the sun, shadows are sharp and move with your flashlight, your character legit always has their finger off the trigger for safety. Even the barrel inside of a gun is spiraled to mimic real life guns. So much more, but this little stuff goes a long way to making a game believable, and breathtaking.

[b] Sound/Music/Voices: 9.5/10 [/b]

I love the soundtrack in this game and the sound effects too. The sound effects add a lot to the world you are in, the music is great, and the voice actor nailed their lines all across the board. They sound like actual humans and suit their characters. Backtracking on sound effects, they also add a lot to the horror and tension, whether it's the heavy footsteps of Mr. X closing in or the shaking of fences to indicate zombies nearby. The music, although being great, is not frequent, but that allows for the true silence and horror of the game to prevail.

Overall: 9.5/10

-Keeps relatively well to the source material
-Mr. X will keep you on your toes in the sections he is in
-A lot of replayability

Resident Evil 2 Remake might just be the greatest horror game ever made. Capcom masterfully reimagines the 1998 classic, delivering a perfect blend of survival horror, compelling puzzles, and heart-pounding atmosphere that sets a new standard for the genre.

The combat is brilliantly executed, with every encounter feeling tense and impactful. Ammunition and resources are scarce, forcing you to think strategically about when to fight and when to run. The enemies are terrifying, especially the relentless Mr. X, whose pursuit adds an unparalleled layer of dread as he stalks you through the game. Every bullet fired feels meaningful, and every encounter leaves you on edge.

The puzzles are well-designed—challenging but fair. They strike the perfect balance of making you feel clever when you solve them without ever crossing into frustrating territory. The integration of these puzzles into the environment is seamless, and the way they guide you through the labyrinthine police station is nothing short of brilliant.

And speaking of the police station: the atmosphere is jaw-droppingly good. The dark, rain-soaked halls, flickering lights, and eerie sound design create a sense of tension that never lets up. The environment itself feels like a character, with every creak, shadow, and distant groan contributing to the game’s oppressive sense of fear. Seriously though, who decided to turn a museum into a police station? It’s a bizarre choice, but it somehow works perfectly within the game’s world.

The visuals are stunning, and the RE Engine delivers some of the best lighting, textures, and animations seen in any game. Combined with the top-tier sound design and immersive storytelling, Resident Evil 2 Remake is as much a feast for the senses as it is for your nerves.

Whether you’re a long-time fan of the series or a newcomer, this is a must-play. It’s an unforgettable experience that shows why Resident Evil remains the king of survival horror.

Remakes are complicated.

I’m not instinctively interested in them, primarily because I’ll usually gravitate towards the original game. There’s just an element of the original article that’s more compelling, right? In spite of the antiquated looks or cumbersome control schemes, I’d prefer to engage directly with the game as it was first conceived.

Games don't diminish with time, even as technological progress widens the gap. We don't need to always be yanking the past into the present with its classics (beyond strictly commercial reasons, I guess).

One of the defining features of the remake, graphics quality, has never acted as an impediment to immersion for me. Indeed, there’s been occasions where the visual makeover acts as a counteragent to that immersion. In such cases I find myself [i]less[/i] absorbed in a game’s setting, not more.

But I understand that for newer players, the original appearance is the impediment, so I’m glad the remake is there to serve them.

It has other purposes, though, and I think one such remake exemplifies them in every respect. That game is [i]Resident Evil: Remake[/i] (2002).

It’s the perfect [i]Resi[/i] game in so many ways, radically improving the original whilst remaining true to its essential essence. If you put [i]Resident Evil[/i] and [i]Resident Evil: Remake[/i] in front of me, I’d opt to play the latter—a rare circumstance for me. It’s distinguished by the fact that their creator, Shinji Mikami, oversaw both titles.

2019’s [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] is not [i]Resident Evil: Remake[/i], which is to say it does not surpass its 1998 progenitor... But it comes very close. And that is wild, because the 1998 version is one of the best games ever made.

In a major shift, [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] switches out the fixed camera for an over-the-shoulder third person perspective. That doesn’t mean that the journey through Raccoon City’s police department is closer to [i]Resident Evil 4[/i] than [i]2[/i], though.

This remake is a genuinely frightening game, in which the radically updated visuals bring the zombie-infested police station new (un)life. The stunning use of light and grunge work to its advantage. It doesn’t have the same ambient strengths as the original, which didn’t much need the dark to elicit fear, but that’s okay—what it lacks in originality it more than makes up for in efficacy.

This is a gorgeous game that works as a startling piece of video game horror.

Its most successful feature is Mr. X. He was strictly a scripted terror in the original game, but here he roams the police station in search of you. What an incredibly brilliant piece of design his presence is, too. He changes the way in which you approach navigation, requiring you to listen closely to the environment so as to avoid a costly encounter should he prove too close.

It’s astounding to me that the follow-up, [i]Resident Evil 3[/i] (2020), dropped the ball so badly in expanding this concept to Nemesis himself. Instead of being an evolution on the roaming terror of Mr. X, Nemesis was reduced to a series of uninspired boss fights. But then the [i]Resident Evil[/i] series has often taken one step forward, two steps back (see [i]Resident Evil 4[/i] and [i]5[/i]).

I think this game drops in quality a bit once you leave the police station, which I’d argue wasn’t necessarily the case before. But that might just be because high-tech laboratories are less interesting (and more predictable!) settings.

With this [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] we also see the shift from earnest, so-bad-it’s-good writing to the slick-but-mediocre writing that started in [i]Resident Evil 7[/i]. It’s very much like watching a competent but substandard horror, where the characters are dull, the writing boring, and the performances predictable.

I’m not going to argue [i]Resident Evil[/i] should be more like it “used to be”, because the writing was terrible. But you can’t deny it had an identity of its own. Does [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] (2019) have such an identity, despite largely staying true to the original? I don’t think it does, at least not as a piece of narrative, and that’s kind of weird. Like I said, though…

...remakes are complicated.

This one works best if you set aside the original. They are two different experiences. Here you have a high quality journey all of its own that compliments its past, rather than seek to usurp it. It can't really [i]be[/i] the original and nor should it, instead setting out to adapt the concept for modern audiences.

And why not, right? Again, it's without its own singular brilliance in that modernity has rendered its narrative content bland, but I'm willing to forgive that when it plays this damn well.

I won't pick [i]Resident Evil 2[/i] (2019) over 1998's masterpiece, but I remind myself that I don't have to. I'll visit this rendition of Raccoon City for its visceral horror, its sinister Mr. X, and its refinement of style, both in play as well as appearance.

If only all remakes were this good. I might find myself enjoying more of them.

This is my first Resident Evil game. I played through the demo and decided to pick up the full game. RE2 does a fantastic job of building up atmosphere. The setting is the world's most convoluted police station, and it's full to the brim with flickering lights, flooded corridors, hastily blocked off passages, and all manner of corpses and viscera. It really feels like you're walking into the apocalypse 28 days later in a fully immersive and beautifully rendered world. But what really sets the tone and puts you into the headspace of the characters is the sound design. The banging on doors and windows letting you know you're about to have company, the snarls and growls of zombies as they notice you or when what you thought was a corpse sits back up, and of course, the thundering footsteps of Mr. X reminding you that you're still being hunted by something unkillable. With the visual and the aural working in tandem with the gameplay, RE2 is able to build tension like no other and scare the bejeezus out of you.

The level design is full of blocked paths and shortcuts, so that as you explore, the map twists back on itself like the bowels of an ouroboros. During the first part of the game, I thought it was just a cool choice taking inspiration from a metroidvania, but I realized its purpose as soon as Mr. X showed up. He's the minotaur you're stuck in the maze with. You'll be almost to where you're trying to go and his looming figure will force you turn around and reevaluate. There's always another path, but it's rarely as empty as you last left it, so often you'll run out of the frying pan and into the fire. 

A lot of survival horror games will drop you in a terrifying world full of monsters, but you're so armed to the teeth that you never feel the full tension of that setting. RE2 is the opposite. Limited inventory space and limited ammunition keep you from ever feeling that safety. Every enemy will take bullet after bullet and keep on coming with undeterred relentlessness. Figuring out what to bring to a fight becomes almost as important as the actual aiming and positioning during the fight, and there's always room for the unexpected. If there is any problem I have with this gameplay loop, it is that they take the hardiness of the standard zombies a bit too far. I understand if the lickers or the sewer mutants eat up half your ammo, but I feel like the guns should do a bit more against your rank-and-file zombies. I mean hell, they end up coming back after a while anyway, why not let me put them down a little easier?

The real weakness of the game is in its characters. The campiness of the dialogue and cutscenes feels at odds with the serious tone of the setting and gameplay. If you weren't hovering intimately over their shoulders and if the game wasn't so immersive, it would be hard to care about anything going on. That said, RE2 does a great job of making Claire and Leon feel distinct in their gameplay through their arsenals. My strategies approaching enemies and bosses completely changed between my first and second run. That difference was part of the reason I was able to go right into a 2nd run without feeling fatigued. Another reason is that the game very cleverly plays on your expectations and changes things up just enough to make exploring the same space feel new. 

If you're a fan of survival horror, Resident Evil 2 is a must-play.

This entire review is going to sound like me declaring my eternal love of all things Resident Evil, but ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ do I [i]LOVE[/i] Resident Evil games! [i](Except you RE Zero, you’re the worst}[/i]. I remember buying Resident Evil 2 for Playstation as a thrilled teen on my 13th birthday. Not only had the game just launched, but it’s one of the most anticipated games of my entire life at that point. I had been following the game as much as I could through Gaming Magazines. I called all around town to find a copy, and it was the first M rated game I purchased with my own money. Almost exactly one year earlier I had rented It’s predecessor, Resident Evil, and it had awakened something new in me. I didn’t know I was a horror [b]fan[/b] before playing this game. “It changed my life forever” might sound a little dramatic, but honestly, it did.

The Resident Evil 2 I'm reviewing here isn’t that game of course, not technically. It’s the 2019 remake. Let’s be honest though, this remake is exactly how my 13 year old nerd brain saw it back in 98’. When I first played this remake I was lost in it. Other than some additional content for this version, it is almost exactly what I remember from 20+ years ago, just ultra polished and modern. So if that’s something that interests you and you haven’t purchased this yet, then YES, this is a faithful remake that will send you stumbling through time; back to the glorious 5th generation of gaming. Man, can you imagine if games were this good looking back then? 

[h1] I hope I don’t have to write a report on this. [/h1]
[i]- Leon Kennedy; Ringer of bells and breaker of clock towers! [/i]

There are literal monsters roaming the streets of Raccoon City and the one thing this dude doesn’t want to write a report about is the damn Bell breaking. What a goof-ass.

[h1] Story [/h1]

Resident Evil 2: Remake [i](referred to as RE2 from this point on) [/i] tells the origin story of long running franchise hero Leon Kennedy, and Chris’ [i]from the first game[/i] sister, Claire Redfield. The game begins at a gas station right outside Racoon City in September of 1998, only a couple months after the events of the first game. Leon and Claire meet and head toward the city, spoilers ensue and they are seperated and discover the entire city has been overrun by, you guessed it, ZOMBIES! You can choose to either play as Leon or Claire, but other than some minor plot points, the game plays out pretty much the same. You head through the police station, built inside an old Museum. You head to the sewers and eventually a super secret, way bigger than probably possible, underground Umbrella lab [i](Evil Corporation and creator of this mess)[/i], because [i]of course.[/i] The whole way you are learning about what’s happening, who’s responsible, and meeting other neat characters like Ada Wong and the Berkin family. If you haven’t played RE2 yet, I want to avoid saying much else about the story, but, if you’re a fan of Monsters (not just zombies), Cheesy Dialogue, Over-the-top heroics, and super creepy Police Chiefs, then you’ll absolutely love the stories told here.

[h1] Gameplay/Performance [/h1]

Gone are the days of the old school RE games. No more TANK CONTROLS. No more FIXED CAMERA angles. No more INK RIBBONS [i]All the typewriters now have ink available already![/i]. RE2 takes the gameplay brought forward with RE4 and perfects the 3rd person action that the games had been doing from 2005 until RE7 in 2017. So, if you’re coming from Resident Evil 7 as your first RE game, and I know there are some of you, then this game is a 3rd person shooter. There is no way to switch to first person. This is a plus for me, as I really enjoy this style of game, but I also understand some people really don’t, and that’s okay. 

This RE2 is, in all the ways that matter, a modern Survival Horror game. Slick graphics, intuitive gameplay, top notch narrative, deadly creatures, and a wonderfully designed layout that is honestly a joy to navigate. It gives you enough ammo to get by while never feeling overpowered. It gives you enough healing items to stay alive, but never feel safe. About the only convention it breaks is it’s accessibility of the “save” function. There is a typewriter to save at, like every 20 feet or so in this game. I think on my first playthrough, just enjoying the game at my own pace, exploring every nook, I had 52 saves. Back are the unlimited ammo unlocks by doing things like beating the game on hardcore mode, or completing a run using no health items or no saves. Beat the game in less than 3.5 hours and that sweet unlimited Rocket Launcher is all yours! This game also has one of my favorite things ever… a “Noir” mode, where the entire game is in Black and White, if you throw on one of the optional costumes for the characters.

For a first timer, expect this game to take about 5-7 hours per character. There is a bonus secret ending if you play each character's “B” campaign, which is the same campaign started from a later point, with shuffled puzzles and item locations. This is the one thing keeping this game from a 10/10 in all honesty. Well, that and the zombies that can take 12 headshots and not die… Anyway, I did not enjoy having to play this extra campaign stuff. This seemed like artificial gameplay tacked on to make the game seem like it had more content than it does. This isn’t needed because this game has a ton of extra stuff to do! Give me the real ending when I beat both normal campaigns, and just more neat bonus unlocks if I go through the “B” stuff.

[h1] “What the hell is up with you?” [/h1]
[i] - Claire Redfield; after shooting a zombie in the face 13 times and it keeps getting up [/i]

This game ran flawlessly from start to finish. I had no crashes in 25 or so hours. I ran across 0 bugs that I could notice, with the exception of one alive zombie falling on a dead zombie’s corpse and the corpse launched across the library at lightning speed. A chuckle moment, if anything. Silly video games, amirite? Capcom has packed this thing FULL of visual options to tinker with. If you have a very particular way you like things to be, sure thing you’ll be able to do it with the video, audio, and graphics options this game offers. It even includes a little meter showing which options affect what and how much of your video ram is being used. It’s excellent, Go nuts!
[h1] Summary [/h1]

In my opinion one of the best horror games ever made. Capcom really outdid themselves with this remake.

[b]Overall Score: 9/10 [/b]
[b]Why Buy?[/b] You’re a fan of horror and want to play one of the best.
[b]Should avoid if:[/b] You don’t like being able to fight back and want to just hide in a locker, or if you just want zombies, ‘cause in this game [i]THERE BE MONSTERS![/i]

Thanks for reading [i](if you did)[/i] and please let me know if you found this review helpful at all! Also, go check out my RE0 and RE1 reviews! I’m playing through all of the RE games in chronological order in anticipation of Village!

Changed to positive review due to CAPCOM creating a beta dx11 version of the game (which works with windows 7 64 bit)
I managed to significantly improve the 5-15 second freezing bug. I was believe it or not, trying to solve this bug for the last 2 years. Anyways, it turns out the DRAM, CPU, nvidia driver and game are fighting with each other regarding Vsync and textures. So here's the solution to stop them fighting:
1- In nvidia control panel Set vsync OFF or even better Adaptive (Half refresh rate)  (NOT application controlled)
 and set texture to QUALITY or HIGH QUALITY
2- In game set Refresh rate to 60
3- In game set Frame rate to: variable
4- In game set Vsync to ON (crazy but it worked for me)
5- Graphics settings choose a pre-set (Recommended or Max) and do NOT modify (except as a last resort)
6- A sign that you have been sorted is the logos fps jumps from single digit fps to double digit (uptp 80fps!).
Hope this helps if you have Win7 and nvidia card
7- If the above haven't worked go to the BIOS:
a- increase the DRAM voltage especially if you have an old system (helps RAM to sustain speed otherwise system freezes during intensive level loading). e.g increased mine from 1.95 to 1.975 (check manufacturer max volt and don't exceed)
b- increase the CPU voltage slightly e.g mine increased from 1.2250 to 1.2500 (in case your CPU is under-volted it will increase performance) - this helped me a lot
c- disable CPU virtualisation, disable all CPU powersaving/media functions
8- disable any GPU overclocking resident program. eg GPU Tweak II etc.
9- Fire up one of your other favourite games which have no freezing issues (in my case T7). You will be surprised that your favourite game that you thought never freezes does actually freeze periodically depending on the above settings. Check this game (T7) from time to time. It helped me diagnose the freezing issue for Re2. I later found that my GPU clocking program had to be turned off as well as CoreTemp.
10- change your desktop resolution to match that of the game
11- Install reshad.exe mod
12- try steam offline mode
13- disconnect from internet and disable antivirus 
14- some people reported that disconnecting unused USB devices helped.

OLD Review:
PROS
Graphics, voice acting top notch 10/10
Story 9/10
Sound effects, music 8.5/10
Action 7/10
Shooting satisfaction 5/10 (trying to headshot wobbling enemies, as weapons are upgraded so too are the enemies) 


CONS
All the cons stem from the dreaded very low frame rate affliction, let me explain:
1. The game is ENGRAINED with single-room HDD loading system as this was the method for the original resident evil series. therefore the game almost freezes when moving between rooms or areas as it intensively accesses your drive (unless you have installed the game on a top notch m.2 or nvme storage device). It prefers to frequently load in small batches.  It simply doesn't know to load the adjacent rooms/areas on your ram like SOTR which takes ages loading multiple areas but overall better loading experience.
2. When turning down the graphics, the game wrongly assumes you want to transfer graphics processing to the CPU which is a killer for older systems with new graphics (old phenom, 8gb ram, GTX 1070 8g). Turning DOWN all graphics gave me 1-2 fps (YES all graphics turned DOWN made the game slower). This nearly drove me nuts until I defaulted to recommended graphics (high) by mistake and lo and behold I could run the game at 30-40 fps again.
3. If you are fighting enemies between areas, game slows down as it tries to load data from drive making beating enemies more difficult

[b]♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ [/b]: This is a MUST play - if you're a fan of the Resident Evil franchise, or if you're into the Horror genre. This game is exceptional, loaded with extra content, with high replay value & worth every cent at full price. 👌🏽

[h1]Gameplay Features[/h1]

[b]Combat[/b]: The controls are refined and polished, the shooting feels good - but more importantly it matches the survival-horror game design. You are either rewarded or punished for how you engage in combat. If you're frantic, and moving your reticle will expand causing a decrease in accuracy & overall damage output - but if you are concentrated, focused, and still your reticle will tighten increasing your accuracy & your overall damage output. This is a brilliant but subtle touch to incentivize players to control their fear, maximize their damage output, preserve ammunition, and increase their chances of survival. However, each scenario is different - knowing when to engage in combat & when to escape is just as significant. Finally, the combat sees the return of Defense Items for a Counter-Attack. If you find yourself constantly being grabbed by enemies, these Defense Items will trigger a quick counter to temporarily stun or possibly kill the enemy - giving you a brief moment to escape or continue the fight. These are clutch for preventing you from taking any additional damage.

[b]Combining[/b]: You will be able to create unique items such as Healing Items, Ammunition Types, Weapon Upgrades, Key Items, and Puzzle Pieces. Make sure to examine any items you pickup in your inventory for a closer look.

[b]Inventory & Item Management[/b]: Learning to manage your Inventory and deciding which items to carry on you is essential. Do you prioritize additional weapons and ammo? Do you favor carrying multiple healing items for an emergency? And how many slots do you keep open in your Inventory as you explore to pick up new items? Just make sure to pickup all the Extra Hip Pouches you can find! Another key component to the game is Item Management - especially considering there is a limited number of resources available to you including Healing Items & Ammo. Knowing which enemies to kill and when you truly need to heal is key to your survival.

[b]Exploration & Puzzles[/b]: You will want to move through the environment quickly, scanning & searching for Key Items to pickup as you explore. Also, your Map is color coded to let you know of any potential missed items in specific locations - Blue means you've cleared the room, Red means you've missed something. Additionally, if your character visibly sees an item but does not pick it up - your Map will mark a drawing of the specific Item and the room location for you. The puzzles in the game are incredibly rewarding to solve the more difficult they are - there are many that vary in terms of length, difficulty, and type. They will test your reading comprehension, your memory, your problem-solving skills, and some of them your overall patience (*cough* Drug Testing Lab *cough*) but they are a welcome addition and a refreshing challenge.

[h1]A Return to Evil[/h1]

If Resident Evil 7: Biohazard (2017) was a return to form for Capcom with the survival-horror roots for the Resident Evil franchise - then RESIDENT EVIL 2 / BIOHAZARD RE:2 is the formula perfected.

This game was clearly a labor of love for Capcom who managed to faitfhully recreate the 1998 classic but simultaneously managing to reimagine it for a modern audience - with new areas, creatures, puzzles, and weapons - keeping it feeling fresh and new. Capcom manages to expertly blend all the classic ingredients of a Resident Evil game with unnerving heart-pounding gameplay, terrifying monsters, challenging puzzles, visually-stunning set-pieces, and all with a AAA production - creating an experience that feels of incredible quality & polish. Also, worth noting - Capcom utilizing their latest proprietary RE Engine (originally created for Resident Evil 7: Biohazard) the devs use a gorgeous photorealistic style for character models, and a brutal disgusting 'wet gore' effect for the zombies and monsters to display the physical damage you deal on them. This technology creates a visually stunning showcase here - with exquisite detail. (If only there was a photo mode, it would be perfect to display how incredible the RE Engine is).

Just to comment quickly, Capcom managed to do some incredible worldbuilding in this offering - from the level of details in the surroundings, environmental storytelling, and the characters that help really build the world. One of my favorite aspects of the remake is the brilliant writing & performances in the game - giving the characters an extra added layer of detail, nuance, and humanity that was missing in the original. Notable mentions include Annette Birkin, Marvin Branagh, and Kendo - who get a surprising amount of depth here and feel far more fleshed out and grounded - especially for tertiary characters. Personally, I found Leon's arc throughout the game to be the most interesting - as you witness his growth & change...with that tragic revelation at the end.

And now the final point I'll touch on is replayability. There is something inherent about the structure and design of a Resident Evil title that gives them an incredible amount of replay value. Whether you're replaying the campaign for another run to collect hidden items, files, or secrets - or - you're replaying the campaign for another run to improve your performance, rank, or time after learning Key Item Locations or managing your Inventory better. Plus you're encouraged to make a Second Run playthrough to complete the full story of both characters Claire & Leon with the return of the A & B classic story mode. This feature gives each separate character unique storylines, characters, key items, rooms, set locations, weapons, and even enemies. Additionally, there is a ton of extra content here - including five Bonus Game Modes (my personal favorite being 'Flan' from the hilarious The Tofu Survivor Mode). There are also half a dozen new costumes (some for free, some unlockable, & some for purchase), there are harder difficulties, and plenty of Achievement Hunting for Completionists out there. All of these features make a new playthrough feel fun, fresh, engaging, and unique.

[h1] Rating: 10/10 Masterpiece [/h1]

This game is truly a masterpiece. There's a reason it was in contention for Game of the Year (2019). An absolute masterclass in game design, narrative, gameplay, character, voice-acting, writing, sound design, AI, animation, graphical presentation - and just the way all the elements seamlessly blend together so cohesively to create a uniquely terrifying & harrowing experience.

For the longest time I considered the remake of the original title Resident Evil (Gamecube 2001), now known as Resident Evil HD Remaster (2015), the definitive Resident Evil survival-horror experience. However, after finally playing this game I can say this is the new gold standard - not just for the Resident Evil franchise - for the survival horror genre as a whole.

I've been playing Resident Evil for 20 years, and this is my favorite. I played it first on PS4 pro, pre-ordered, but now that I have a PC and it was on sale, I decided to buy it again for the mods. My first playthrough was as third person claire, now I am running both Leon campaigns with the first person mod by praydog. Having a flashlight toggle and an upclose view of everything has changed the game for me. So even if you own it on console, it's worth buying again for the mods.

The game itself is utter brilliance and seems to address all the main complaints of RE4-7, and to some degree the first three games. The fixed camera angles of the old games were cool, but combat suffered in my opinion due to autoaim, meaning in replays, the scare factor is gone and it's a matter of whether you have enough distance and ammo. With RE4, 5, and 6, aiming is nice... but too nice. Simply put, those are action games with mostly smooth controls, predictable enemy movements and exploitable AI. And RE7 was pretty good, brought back classic puzzle design, revamped the horror and had an aiming system that felt good for RE. Tanky, slow, with enemy movements that made it hard to line up a headshot. My biggest complaint was that enemy variety is non-existent. 

This is where RE2 remake shines for the same reasons the original did. People were scared this was gonna be another action zombie game, but that couldn't be farther from the truth. These have to be the tankiest, most tenacious zombies ever created. Using the adaptive difficulty like RE4 did, the game tracks how well or bad you are doing. I've shot zombies point blank in the face with a shotgun, didn't even stagger the SOB just to have it bite me and bring me down from green to red. Yikes. But at some point, I'll shoot a zombie once with a handgun and blow their head to bits, and that's how RNG works in this game. I never feel comfortable in combat, and that's how it's supposed to be. Aiming is hard. Zombies sway and stumble towards you, never keeping their head still more than a second at a time. With the way the reticle stays big until you focus, trying to take rapid shots with any weapon will almost always result in wasting ammo. Couple this with the fact that unless you get a critical headshot, board all the windows, and clear every room, zombies will almost always get back up, repopulate, and be in an entirely different spot or even different rooms the next time you come through an area. The only thing that stays consistent when playing the game is item locations, everything else beyond cutscenes and certain scripted events are entirely dynamic.

Resident Evil 2 is packed with zombies, lickers, dogs, Mr. X, poisonous abominations, not so local flora, and things that just don't seem to die. The puzzles are fairly decent, nothing quite Nintendo level (I guess kids can handle harder puzzles than adults but O-k) but they're fun to figure out. The game hosts 4 different playthroughs and some extra modes, and is extremely replayable. Each playthough only takes 3-8 hours depending on your skill, and that makes replaying it all that much better in my opinion. It's very fun learning from your mistakes to improve your runs, beat the game in less time, with less mistakes, less ammo. It's just that good. Buy it.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is a masterclass in modern survival horror. Capcom brilliantly reimagines the 1998 classic with stunning visuals, immersive sound design, and refined gameplay that keeps the tension high from start to finish. The over the shoulder camera adds a new level of immediacy to the scares, while the atmosphere and pacing are top-notch.

While it's true that about half of the original content like some of the unique B-scenario elements and a few enemy types are absent or significantly reworked, the game more than makes up for it with its polished presentation and tighter narrative. The reimagining focuses on quality over quantity, streamlining the experience without losing the soul of the original. It’s a respectful update that both newcomers and longtime fans can appreciate.

Overall, Resident Evil 2 Remake is a thrilling ride that successfully honors its roots while carving out its own identity in the franchise.

So, this comes from somebody who NEVER played the original game on Playstation.

At first, the game was very promising. Nice graphics, nice atmosphere. There was a little issue with graphics (if antialiasing is turned off, wet things, like blood, rain, etc. glitched), but overall, itt looked great.

Then I got to the police station, where the game crashed to desktop. After starting the game again, it CTD'd again. Thanks to the guy in reviews, I was able to fix this via modifying the cfg file.

Then the old, consolish things from the '90s started to appear. A zombie attacks you, and you CAN'T do anything. You just sit there and wait. Okay, don't get close to zombies, got it. A bit later you get a knife and this solves, hurray. After that, you start to find a LOT of puzzle(ish) object. Actually, there are only two kind of objects you can interact with: items you can use (bullets, herbs, etc.), and puzzles. In every room, you find a locker with a combination lock. Or a door, which needs a specific key. Or a terminal, which opens lockers, but missing some buttons. I can see you need to run back and forth in the building, from one puzzle to another, while avoiding zombies. Not fun.

But the moment I gave up, was when I realized that YOU CAN'T DROP/DISMISS AN ITEM FROM YOUR INVENTORY. And you have 8 slots, and you need a slot for each of your weapons as well, so if you have a pistol and a knife, it already takes up 3 slots, as bullets also needs one slot. The solution? There is a conatiner next to each save point, and if you're out of free inventory slots. you need to run back to a save point, put some items in the container, then run back for your item which you were unable to take. Nonsense.

I'm sure it's a great remake of the original game, and if you've loved and played it back in the day, you'll like this version. But for me who doesn't have this nostalgic bond, the game mechanics just feel old. Also, I was expecting some zombie horror survival game, but the gamplay itself is more about "find the key/passcode/etc." than anything else.

The first playthrough of this game was phenomenal. It was terrifying at some points, intriguing at others. I struggled to put this game down until I finally finished my run as Leon. Then I started the 2nd run.

For those who don't know, RE2 has the option for you to play as 1 of 2 characters (Leon or Claire). Once you complete your 1st run, the 2nd run option will open up, which provides different story segments and the true ending. This second run was a slog.

While it was a lot quicker than the first one, I felt bored out of my mind at a point. Besides one different location and some of the puzzles and enemies being moved around, it just felt like a replay with barely any differences. On top of this, the stories of the 2 characters are supposed to occur simultaneously, which is frustrating as you end up completing many of the exact same tasks as you did in the 1st run. So not only is it just a repeat of the events, but there is this whole canonical confusion as to what it and what isn't.

This game was pretty fantastic. I've not played the original and am aware it was executed a lot different, but this one handles things well. It single handedly pushed me to go and check out what I was missing in the a lot of the rest of the series.

If you've played RE4, Dead Space, or a survival shooter along those lines, you'll be pretty at home here. Ammo can be a lot more sparse than the aforementioned games, especially on Claire's route, but it feels fair, if also perhaps more difficult than those games. 

Graphically, the game is stellar. If you look hard enough, you'll find spots that aren't perfect, sure, but as a whole the art is pretty damn good. It really sticks out among a lot of games of this time frame for its prowess here. Every room is incredibly detailed and speaks strongly for the care the developers put into them. 

Sound design is seriously good. Walking through the world, the game makes full use of its environment for this to really put you in your character's shoes. I really can't recommend headphones or an otherwise strong sound setup enough for this. It adds a lot to the experience.

All in all, the game is an unparalleled love letter to the game it's based on. It stands tall among the sea of "remake"s we've seen which literally amount to ports and upscales in a lot of cases. Even among games that did get proper reworkings and art updates, it definitely stands out. 

This is a must buy if you care about Resident Evil.

Forget RE5, this RE2R is the true successor to RE4. I didn't expect too much out of this remake but i am really impressed with what Capcom has made here and i can safely say that this remake is superior to the original RE2..! As a standalone game but as a remake? Not so much.

First off the game is third person! As every mainline RE should be and the gameplay is true to the original formula while being a lot more challenging. The story is still mostly the same but with a much better narrative and more fleshed out side character segments. The voice acting is mostly good except for Leon's performance doesn't always sound convincing and at times very corny. Graphics are incredible, the new character designs of Leon and Ada look like top models and are in line with their original portrayal meanwhile Claire... Claire sucks. 

I dislike her characterization, she curses all the time like a dumb millenial and doesn't feel nor look as good as she did in the original, in fact, her facial expressions looks hilariously bad. Like the developers tried way too hard to make her cute and attractive while keeping her realistic, at the same time not trying to offend anybody which ends up with her face looking all weird and plastic with botox lips. Call me nostalgic but i actually prefer Revelations 2 Claire over this one, the worst part about her (and Leon somewhat) is how she curses at enemies while your shooting them "BASTARD" "JESUS" "GOD" "GET THE F.CK AWAY" this is so distracting and out of character for her, really F.ck this Claire. Moving on. 

The physics and lighting of the RE engine are great i love the rain and fire both look very natural. The music? Well, there is no memorable music to speak off unless you buy the original OST as DLC... The exploration is the best part of the game, it's really immersive and non-linear and the map auto updates the rooms you have or haven't visited yet and also shows where items are which saves you a bunch of time from memorizing them. The main locations from the original have been expanded upon here making them bigger and less linear and with more extra items like wooden boards, gun powders, weapon upgrades, grenades which are important since you'll easily run out of ammo unlike in the original.

The zombies are the best enemy type featuring both male and female zombies each with different clothing and they're not as easy to kill as in previous games. They move quickly and do lots of damage if you're too close making it hard to steadily aim for their head, aim for their legs instead. Each shot shows permanent physical damage and you can even shoot their hats and limbs off! I also LOVE the fact that zombies stay dead on the floor (mostly) even after leaving and re-entering the area instead of immediatley rotting away like in previous games this is perhaps the first time an RE game actually does this consistently. Lickers are back and are harder than ever before, the plant monsters are also here except that they aren't actual plants rather some weird looking zombies with plants all over them and the sewer monster is not hard but more annoying to kill with less powerful weapons.

The boss fights are also mostly well done. Dr. Birkin and Tyrant (Mr X) are the main villains and they keep showing up just like in the original but are more challenging here. Some boss fights are heavily scripted like the second Birkin fight where you can only beat him a certain way and the Crocodile where you do basically nothing but run away in a cinematic cutscene like in RE 6 but to be fair, the croc has always been a lost cause even in the original, he's definitely pathetic in this remake. Tyrant is definitely more menacing here, he follows you up stairs, in doors except for save rooms and can't be temporarily killed like in the original. He is a lot of fun but can also somehow teleport to wherever you are at times which kind of breaks the immersion.

If you liked the old Resident Evil 2, I suggest to buy this REMAKE. It is not ideal but at least it is a top class remake.
