What this game does well is teaches you how to think ahead -- prioritise supplies, conserve ammo and plan an optimal path.  Everyone will have their own approach to the game, despite it largely being a rail-driven affair.   

The game strikes a good balance between tension and action.  The assortment of weapons and tools available are fun and effective at their specific tasks.  Don't worry if you're not an FPS pro -- you don't need to be, and there is optional aim assist if you want it.  The game's not so much about twitchy reflexes.  It's more about being cautious and scavenging / conserving the right ammo for the right situation.  This isn't problematic for new players, as Standard difficulty is forgiving enough in this regard, but Hardcore provides a new challenge.

It is a phenomenal remake of a phenomenal game. [b]I was gifted it by one of my friends for my birthday.[/b] If you're a fan of the original, I HIGHLY suggest starting your first playthrough in Hardcore mode. Hardcore mode disables autosaves (save for the initial autosave immediately after the opening cutscene.) Ink Ribbons are REQUIRED to save, health and ammo are more scarce, and you REALLY have to think about what to bring, who to shoot, and when to save. You also take more damage, and do less damage. As someone who played the original far more than I am willing to admit, I was pleasantly surprised by quite a few changes and surprises that game throws at you, as well as seeing some iconic locations and enemies on glorious current gen hardware. The graphics options are robust and extensive, with the game looking gorgeous on just about any setting. [b]A quick note about the "VRAM Usage" indicator: The game at MAX settings says that its using 13GB of VRAM, whereas MSI Afterburner/Rivatuner states that its only using between 5-6GB of VRAM.[/b]

I do have a few gripes about performance though:

First, as a recommendation, TURN OFF Screen Space Reflections. It give a lot of the reflective surfaces a fuzzy "white noise" effect when viewed at certain angles, especially in the Police Station. I'm not sure if the setting looks better on RTX cards, as I have a 1070Ti.

Now for my biggest gripe:

There is one glaring issue that I have yet to find a solution for: stuttering/hanging/lagging. There are times (for me at least) the game will run smooth as butter for a session, but more often than not there are instances where the game will freeze for upwards of a minute or two and the audio will continue to play. This is especially frustrating when it occurs during cutscenes, as the visuals will freeze but the cutscene audio will continue to play. When the game does unhitch, the cutscene will continue to play, albeit without sound. Luckily though, when the game does do that during regular gameplay, EVERYTHING remains as it is until it fixes itself. Meaning, there would be no cheap deaths due to it. I find it to be incredibly annoying, especially during a couple of boss fights in Leon's campaign that put you in a relatively small areas to move and fight. It will do that even if sitting on the pause menu. A quick google search brings up many forum and reddit posts complaining about this issue as well, on a wide variety of hardware. Not 100% sure if it's a hardware issue or an engine issue, as I have read reports of players with top of the line hardware (i9 9900K & 2080Ti) having similar issues that I've had. Your mileage may vary, as some have reported no issues at all. 

My Rig:
GPU: GTX 1070Ti 8GB
CPU: i5 9600K
RAM: 16GB 



[b]BOTTOM LINE: Buy it. I have adapted to the stuttering/hanging/lagging and while its annoying, it can give you a moment to gather your bearings and think about your next move if it happens in a pinch. 10/10 would recommend[/b]

The first RE remake is probably my favorite game of all time. It's definitely way up there. Naturally, I was excited to try this one. It didn't disappoint. While the quality of life improvements and general gameplay changes in the first remake were just frequent enough not to fundamentally change the original, the improvements in RE 2 definitely change the original. For the better. A REmake 1 player could jump into the PS1 title with some trouble, but not much. I feel that doing the same for RE 2 would be extremely difficult. The original RE 2 now feels like a worse version of its remake, while the original RE only feels like a different version of the remake. It's truly incredible.

Of course the story is filled with corn and the boss fights are lame, but that's just Resident Evil. It works here. The visuals, sheer horror, and gameplay make up for it. I was never creeped out with Resident Evil 2. Instead, I was filled with a primal fight or flight type fear the entire way through. I thought that was cool. 

While I still would've liked to see how RE 2 would look if it was remade with fixed camera angles, I think the choice Capcom made here was more than wise. It allowed for a radically different product that was accessible to more people, and I dig the hell out of that. This game is awesome. One of the best I've played in a while, and definitely one of the best in the entire series.

By far and away one of the most frightening games I've ever played. They give you so much agency it's overwhelming! After every session, I'm literally sweating and have my adrenaline levels up so high it takes me a while to both physically and mentally recover. Just when you think you're starting to get the hang of things, Capcom starts throwing a boatload of wrenches at you and you're back to running away and staring at your map, trying to figure out how the heck you're going to get out of THIS horrible situation. You're glad to put it down, but it eats at your mind and makes you wonder, "What's going to happen next? I just HAVE to find out!" and you're back in the saddle once more.

I thought Resident Evil 7 was scary, but this takes the cake. Well done! Deserves the acclaim it's received, no doubt.

UPDATE: After finishing the game, I have no problem recommending the experience to anybody with the slightest interest in survival-horror. 

The puzzles and the gameplay were excellent, and every single setup gave me the creeps, even when nothing came of them most of the time. It played on many of my fears, from wandering through dark corridors with flickering lights, to being forced to investigate noises you KNOW will lead to no good.

Many places were obvious setups that you'd just DREAD going through (but you always have the option to remove future threats if so inclined... and I was very inclined), and sometimes, places would be so gross and dark you'd anticipate an ambush, and nothing would come. It really messes with your psyche! It's great!

The performance/stability was the cherry on top; my rig (1080p Resolution, Ryzen 5 1600, GTX 1070, 16GB DDR4) handled high/ultra settings and I never noticed it dip below 60 FPS at any given moment. 

I did crash once after 7 hours of gameplay, but did not lose any progress whatsoever when it happened, and I never crashed again following that moment. I'm not going to hold a single harmless fault against it, as the issue could have simply been a me-problem.

It's a relatively short game, but a very wholesome experience. The fact that there's two character storylines, and two scenarios per character, means I'll definitely be spending more time here. I haven't even unlocked most of the good stuff, not to mention touched the side-stories! I bought this for $20, and I definitely got my money's worth.

I liked the game on my first playthough. Then? Then it made me angry.
If I'm honest, I do actually recommend the game, but let me explain my problem here. I enjoyed the gameplay, I think it's fun and entertaining. The environment is fine, the game looks nice at most times. The plot is a bit messy, and it's rather short. The only reason it took me a bit long is because I like exploring and I took my time to check every room of each map to find everything I could. Otherwise, it would have been over in like 5 hours. The puzzles are fun and I also liked the action. There aren't many types of enemies so I believe it can be a bit boring for some people. The zombies are bullet sponges, but I still had enough bullets on "normal" mode to kill almost every enemy so I had no problem with that. (I know, I didn't have to kill everything, but I wanted to.) Mr. X didn't bother me either. He makes the game harder, but I still had half the police station to explore when he arrived, and I explored it anyway. I don't think it's hard to get away from him, because he's slow and there are plenty of safe rooms where I could hide. I don't think he's as bad or hard to beat as I saw some people think. The characters are a bit shallow and somewhat boring. The voice acting is meh, it's nothing special. I bought this game for Leon and I'm a little bit disappointed by how... dull was he portrayed here. Other than that, the chemistry between characters didn't really work well for me, I don't think it was well made. But that's not what bothers me, because I still had plenty of fun playing it. 
So. Why did I end up being angry at this game? When you start it, you can choose between the 2 main characters, Leon and Claire. This determines how your routes will play out: the chara you picked first has route A and the other one has route B. In my case, it was Leon route A. This means I solved every puzzle, killed almost all enemies, collected everything, opened all doors/gates and saved the day with Leon. Then, there was no ending. My son Leon defeated the big bad and then suddenly: credits. Then the game told me that I can now play Claire route B and THEN I can see the true ending. Okay, I said. The game and plot let me believe that Claire was minding her own business in the meanwhile and now I can see what was she doing. So I started Claire B. The game cut the full beginning out and started at a different point... and I noticed quickly: everything was back at the start. Everything was locked, every enemy was there again, every puzzle was unsolved. Even the jump scares were the same. Even though I think in my case Claire B plot was supposed to support and add more to Leon A plot, that's not what it did. It doesn't matter who you choose at the beginning and it doesn't matter what you did in route A: you have to repeat EVERYTHING in route B that you just finished doing in route A. Every single thing, puzzles, enemies... You have to do it all over again. I don't care that they have at least different weapons and different lines to scream when they are frustrated. It makes zero sense, because it creates a complete mess of which chara did what: because they do the exact same thing. Other than that, they don't even meet, only at the start and the end, they don't communicate or see each other, when they are supposed to be in the same building at the same time. It messes up the timeline and I simply don't understand who thought it was a good idea to force the player to repeat the game TWICE for the true ending. There are some small differences: you get about 20 minutes to play with yet another character in both routes and have about 3 different cutscenes. Other than that, both Leon and Claire have their own big bad to defeat. Then, whoever had route B can defeat the TRUE big bad in the TRUE ending. Everything else is the same. I truly hate everything about this idea. Now, I have not played the original RE2 yet, so I don't know how this worked there, and it also means that I do not have nostalgia to say it is perfect and flawless, because it is true to the original and whatnot. I think this is ridiculous and tedious. I simply don't see why couldn't they write different plot or make different puzzles or at least create new maps (except a very small one) for route B. The game introducing 2 different characters with different routes makes you think you can finish the game in many ways, but no. The choice is an illusion. 
I didn't really want to give this game a negative review... It's not like I didn't enjoy the game or don't think it's good. It is good, it is fun (maybe too short for the full price) and I do recommend to play route A with whoever you like... But be prepared for this nonsense. I was about to give it a positive review, but when I realized that I am now forced to complete the same damned story again for the true ending which is basically just 10 minutes plus, I simply decided to rage quit route B. I will mostly likely finish it anyway, but this completely ruined it for me. I can't give a positive review, because creating a game this way is simply lazy, stupid and unimaginative.
Update: Finished route B (a lot quicker since I already knew where to go and what to do...). My opinion didn't change. There were small differences, but it's basically the same plot twice and this creates serious problems with the timeline. It's simply a mess like this.

Going through your first run of this remake is an incredible experience. I'm an OG Resi fan, having played Resident Evil 2 when it first came out in the late 90s. It was perhaps my favourite Resident Evil for years, so I had a hard time imagining Capcom could possibly do the game justice. Even more so when I heard this is a reimagining that doesn't even have fixed camera angles anymore. I was wrong. Capcom has done the original game justice alright. They released an intense, visually beautiful and mechanically sound modern survival horror game that sets new standards.

I'm not going to say the game is perfect. It's not. A glaring flaw for instance, at least once you play it long enough, is the limited nature of the B scenario. For those that don't know, the game has two protagonists, if you pick one to start with, that's called a scenario A, once finished you can play with the other character as a scenario B, supposedly showing what the other character was doing all this time.  In the original game the B scenarios felt a lot more complementary to their A counterparts. And also Claire A/Leon B, ie the canonical route, was different to Leon A/Claire B. Here the routes are virtually identical. Even the differences between scenario A and B are very limited. Basically a different prologue/epilogue and item placing.

But even if the game lacks the replayability of the original, it matters little. As mentioned earlier, the first run through this game is absolutely fantastic and worth playing. I recommend this game to all fans of the Resident Evil series and survival horror. It is a must. If you don't have the patience to go through all the repetitive routes, I recommend Claire A/Leon B. Even though it is not really the canonical one anymore, since the continuity is problematic and the other route is basically the same. The character interactions still feel more right.

I like the way they design the game so far. I'm bit disappointed with the endgame (tunnels, sewers and laboratory). I would definitively recommend it for those who like RE series. (Usually I never write reviews about games I've bought.)

When I was 13, I begged my dad to get me that ♥♥♥♥♥♥ ZombiU game. I think I played it for maybe 30 minutes. I turned it off, and never played it again. "It was too scary!" I was a dumb kid terrified of a video game. 

A few years ago I had my first experience with a Resident Evil game, that being a Resident Evil 4 port for the Xbox One I think I found in a bargain bin. Played it for a couple hours, and turned it off. I thought it was boring, and that the Resident Evil franchise was overrated. I won't lie, I was overly critical at the time, because about a year later, I got all the boys together, and we sat in front of the TV and we played Resident Evil 7 in the middle of the night, and I ADORED it. It was gritty, it was unnerving... and it was TERRIFYING, but I HAD to see it through.

Now, a couple weeks ago, as you probably know, the Resident Evil 3 remake was released to somewhat mixed results. I heard it was short, but it was overall enjoyable. As tempted as I was to buy it, I instead decided against it, because I saw this game, marked down to $20. I had heard how great it was, primarily from the legendary "Moist Meter", and because it's probably the best looking game I've ever seen. 

I bought it, downloaded it, and about an hour into Leon's campaign, I was hooked. The story, the gritty atmosphere, the gore, the terror, Mr. X... Just a little bit ago, I finished Claire's path, saw what is considered to be the "True" ending, and couldn't help but feel that infamous "Post-Game Depression".

Now, how is someone like myself going to grade a game like this. Someone who never was a big fan of the survival horror genre, who is sick of seeing anything and everything zombie related a decade after the trend died; Someone who isn't even a fan of the series...

(I realize I'm getting really overly dramatic for a review of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ video game, but bear with me)

... You love it. You love everything about it.

You love the story, you love the cinematics, the scenery, the characters, the weapons, the seemingly impossible to kill enemies.

You love the chills you get seeing a Licker for the first time. You love the badassory you feel putting together an inventory of devastating weapons. You love the terror you feel every time you hear the Tyrant's footsteps echoing throughout the police station.

You love Resident Evil 2

The Tyrant is the sole reason i never got to finish this game in the first place so finally blowing him to smithereens was the most satisfying ending and I was extremely happy with the outcome of the ending.

I still have yet to play the Bonus Content but as a gameplay standpoint this game excels in making you feel so claustraphobic and alone in this large police station. Being constantly on the move and away from Mr. X feels like survival with each encounter you have with him. The ammo economy also makes you feel like you need to ration out your ammo, making sure youre always prepared for the next fight. let me set a scenario for you: youre faced with a zombie in a room, do you either A: use some of the ammo on his head to hopefully get a critical hit or maybe you think itll knocked em out for good. Or B: do you shoot off their legs to slow em down and dodge them the next time you need to enter the room for an objective. id personally choose B, because youre just spending less ammo to hopefully save some for the next fight. These choices are the difference between you and chances of survival because there is absolutely no way youre going to kill everything, you may not even have to return to a certain area, meaning you dont need to spend ammo whatsoever. 

I think that with a mindset like this, you can traverse through this game flawlessly. Rationing ammo is the most important thing in this game, and with the right movement as well, you can slip past anything at anytime. Just know when to run and when to shoot. I overall recommend this game, its a fantastic remake with a great story and gameplay loop. I really hope they can remake RE5 and 6 because we all know how those games went down... but good job Capcom, i sincerely hope RE9 is good as well, maybe introduce Leon again since we havent seen him in a while?

[h1] The best hits mixtape [/h1]
When Resident Evil 2 Remake was first announced it immediately drew the attention of the gaming world. After breathing new life into the franchise with RE 7, Capcom once again chose to go big. Instead of a mere HD Remaster, a treatment which [url=https://steamcommunity.com/profiles/76561198010155821/recommended/304240/]the first RE had already seen[/url], the studio chose to remake the game from scratch. The result is a critically acclaimed blockbuster of a game. When examined more closely, RE 2 Remake turns out to be a patchwork of all the best ideas the franchise have had during its over 20 years-long run. It’s a narcissistic self-tribute, made with deliberate attention and care necessary to sew all the pieces together into a smooth, coherent whole. The result is something much bigger than the mere sum of its parts. Let’s try and examine each one of them below.

[b] Fear of the unknown [/b]
As RE 7 already made evident, the “REach for the moon” engine is capable of rendering stunning visuals. It was only improved upon for the RE 2 Remake release and the game is simply beautiful in its dour, dim colour palette. Especially the cutscenes can be breathtaking, which also provides a perfect tool for delivering a personal character-centred narrative. Cinematic intrusions are used scarcely, not to break the immersion and instead highlight the characters and emphasise the atmosphere. The effect is powerful enough for the first third of RE 2 to be genuinely scary. Which is an astounding success for a game drawing foremost from zombie flicks. 
[url] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2059618899 [/url]
During the very first zombie encounter, the player is already made painfully aware that they are woefully unprepared to face the danger head-on. Search for the answers that takes you to Racoon city makes it blatant that things had spiralled out of control. As you take your first steps into the poorly-lit interiors of Racoon City’s Police Department, search becomes a struggle for survival, as it gets scary to take a simple peek behind the corner. The game perfectly plays off the early fear of the unknown to get the player fully invested into the fate of their chosen protagonist. By the time you get accustomed to the game enough to grow bolder, those early horror moments will have you hooked in proper. 

[b]Run or gun[/b]
In RE 4 Capcom introduced a then-new, more action-oriented approach to gameplay. Facilitated mostly through “over the shoulder’ camera perspective, the game was filled with intense close- quarters firefights. The studio seemingly enjoyed the formula so much that (for better or worse) two more games followed this direction, never quite achieving the success that RE 4 had. RE 2 remake revisits this idea and makes it reach its full potential once more. Every fight in the game requires the player to carefully balance between running and shooting. The player is required to be fully immobile in order to reach the best accuracy but staying in one place for too long is an easy way to get overrun. Naturally, every shot counts as ammunition is always low and most enemies tear a third of your health in one bite. The shoulder-camera perspective also fits best for the portrayal of a zombie horde coming from all sides. Once you see outstretched hands missing your back by a hair’s breadth, you will know what I mean.
[url] https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2059619651 [/url]
However clunky, for the franchise standards, RE 2 remake has probably the most fluent third-person shooting the series has seen yet. The choice of weapons isn’t exactly wide, albeit Claire and Leon have a separate arsenal to further diversify the gameplay between the two. Once you get a hang of the movement, adapt to the zombies’ jerky shambling and learn that nothing quite stays dead in Racoon city, the game at large stops being scary. Instead, the game exudes pressure by introducing an unstoppable force – Mr X, a humanoid behemoth that will remove any false sense of security from the equation. The entry of the Tyrant serves as a turning point, at which RE 2 shifts its focus onto more action and releases a wider variety of series’ trademark grotesque monsters. 

[b]Custom strongbox parts[/b]
Feeling of being perpetually hounded never quite stops in RE 2. That said, there are multiple calmer sequences allowing the player to catch a breath. Many of those moments are spent solving puzzles, the second thing series is best-known for. The puzzles are often weird and entirely irrational, they require you to think but are easy enough as to not stall you for too long. They manage to take the player’s mind off things, relax and just barely let their guard down so that the next punch can sink in properly. A punch likely delivered by a  3-meter tall miscreant with eyes in all the wrong places. Part of each puzzle is finding the proper place to use the key items and managing inventory. RE 2 remake still has some backtracking and requires a little equipment-tetris, though as far as the quality of life goes, it is the most welcoming Resident Evil up to date. The items fit into equipment on their own stacking and combining nicely and many game sections “shut off” the player as to make getting lost more difficult. Much like in mansion from the first RE, RE 2 remake has he player run in circles throughout the police department, gradually gaining entry to further and further rooms. Puzzles overall successfully provide diversity to the gameplay, so that it never gets dull throughout the campaign.

[b]Eat the flowerpot[/b]
Alas, this is why I consider Resident Evil 2 remake a best hits tape - mixing quirky puzzles, RE 4 combat, RE 7 visuals and narrative and having all those grafted to RE 2, the best-received of the first three games, serving as a foundation.  Having said all that, the game does bring new toys to the table too. Foremost RE 2 commits to making the most of the series’ dual protagonist formula. Claire and Leon have their respective subplot. You even get to play a segment as secondary characters, all so that the complete story can only be witnessed by playing the game twice. The game goes to great lengths to get the player to run it the second time, a little too far for my taste. You see, the ending is “cut” on the first playthrough and the player is informed that they have to play as the other protagonist to get the full picture. This rather cheap trick is probably my biggest complaint, as the game already has a prefect replayability, complete even with “2nd run” campaign variant, giving the seasoned players a head start into the game. 

This is but a tiny dent in otherwise spectacular game. RE 2 does require you to suspend disbelief a lot to truly get invested into it. Yet, that quirky aspect of the game is so integral to the franchise identity that I wouldn’t have it any other way. So naturally, if I come across an ornamental office plant, I will shove it flowerpot-first into my face. It was green, there is no way it won’t be good for your health.

Resident Evil 2 is an absolutely brilliant game. It can be easily recommended to all survival-horror fans, as this is the franchise that has shaped its sub-genre. Make no mistake, it’s a Resident Evil game and the survival part does eventually overtake the horror. Luckily, the title doesn’t let go without setting the tone properly first. Long story short, if you were to choose a single game from the franchise, RE 2 is your best bet. Especially that while playing it you will experience, in a sense, the legacy of the entire series. All neatly compacted into a 15 hours-long (assuming both runs) gourmet survival-horror package. Grab your flashlight and make each one of these shots count.

I grew up when the original was one of the biggest titles to hit the Playstation 1, and I knew it was inevitable for me pick this one up. The quarantine seem a fated time to do so -- pardon my weak attempt in dark humor. While Control sits on top of my 2019 game  list, this walk down zombie infested memory lane did not disappoint. In fact, I can say that this particular gem sets the bar on remakes. (Sad that I've had glimpses of disappointing feedback for the remake of RE3) 

Objectively, modern graphics capability and full voice acting contributes a lot to this. But the narrative direction and the tweaks in mechanics make the game brand new. It's a nice entry point to the series for younger players who haven't gotten into the universe - despite people having mixed feelings with the take on RE3, I think the ball will just keep rolling from this one. I can't recall being stalked by Mr. X in the original as much, and I don't remember the Licker being that swole and relentless when triggered. I can't recall if boarding windows was a thing before, I think it wasn't and I feel that small touch brings in some weight to the refreshed experience. The zombies are sponges -- that in itself is worth mentioning. 

But the best, the best thing I have to say is that I am happy the did away with the friggin' door animation in some way. Although unlocking with keys or cutters is still a thing, stuff can jump you from the other side if you're being careless. Don't want to sound simple-minded here but that was a big thing for me. Zombie encounters from the original RE3 don't count those are slightly scripted. 

It's a love affair REkindled, hands down.

[h1]A masterpiece of an experience [/h1]

Having never had the opportunity to delve into the Resident Evil franchise before, I had very little idea of what to expect from this game. I certainly did not expect this game to be taking up a spot on my "all time greatest" list. RE2 is first and foremost an incredible experience, one masterfully conveyed through the medium of videogames rather than a game in the traditional sense. In many ways RE2 is not "fun". It's difficult, frustrating and often terrifying, while also being extremely fulfilling, empowering and exciting. Indeed, if you go through this game without experiencing all of the above, you've missed out!

What do I mean by that? 

Well RE2's gameplay mechanics revolve around player [b]disempowerment[/b]. If you've played zombie games before, you'll know that zombies are slow, stupid and go down easily. In the opening sequence of this game however, you'll send 5 - 10 perfect shots into a zombies head and he'll crumple to the floor, only to rebelliously stand up again. And as you watch your ammo slowly disappear you'll understand that these zombies are not to be taken so lightly.

But soon you'll learn how to deal with them, luring them to areas in order to simply avoid them, or strategically deciding which zombies to cull in commonly traversed areas. You'll begin to feel more powerful and in control organically, without the game ever dialing up your damage output or health.

And then the game will throw all your fast movement stratagems out the window when it introduces lickers to you, making you once again feel powerless. And again, wholly organically, you'll learn to deal with this new threat and your confidence will rise, only for the cycle to repeat later on.

This gameplay loop is infinitely rewarding, so much more than finding a gun that does slightly more damage or upping the anti purely by giving enemies more health. Like I said, it's frustrating and will cause moments of genuine terror, and you'll probably quit the game in a huff, only to come back 30 minutes later when you realise how much you miss the satisfaction of learning to best your opponents. 

And that is what I mean by, "it's an experience". This game will force you to be brave, just like your characters who are completely out of their depth... and it shows! Mr X being the epitome of this mantra, but this I shall leave for you to discover on your own.

And what about the rest of the game?

So much effort and attention to detail has gone into crafting this experience. The graphics are gorgeous and moody. The audio is sublime, it's wonderfully subtle, leaving you feeling constantly on edge without the need for a dramatic orchestra to convey terror. And when the score ramps up (especially for the "final" bossfight"... just wow!), you feel the intensity of the situation perfectly.

The storyline is engaging (having never experienced this franchise before). The supporting characters add monumental amounts of depth to the experience, and they all grow as people which is incredibly satisfying.

I could go on and on about how flawless most aspects of this game are. In fact, if you remain unconvinced I must recommend a video by "RagnaRox" on youtube about this game, he explains far more proficiently than I why this games' organic progression and atmosphere are inordinately fantastic! - [url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=BhFTKiM_13w]The video[/url]

So in order to terminate this soliloquy: I cannot wait to dive back into this game and experience the story from Leon's perspective in a couple of days, and I'm certain I shall be revisiting this game many times in the future.

It's absolutely fantastic, but don't take my word for it, the 97% positive rating at the time of writing speaks for itself.

TL;DR Game is great but it has some aspects that might turn you away.
I was someone who never played the original Resident Evil games. However I did play the first Resident Evil's Remaster. I wrote a review on it, but long story short I did not think it was fun in any way. So if you felt the same way I did, let me tell you that you'll love this game. I've never been big on horror games. I've loved horror movies and stories but horror games always intimidated me. Recently, Resident Evil has helped me get into the genre with it's confusing and intimidating, yet somehow oddly pleasing learning curve. Unlike the first game, this one pulls out all the stops the original had due to technical limits and has transformed the tank-controlled low-poly Resident Evil 2 into the polished survival horror masterpiece that is this game. It really is a remake in the sense that it takes a game that has aged poorly and fixes it up to be on-par with modern standards, while not tainting the original values of survival horror that the original had. Personally I'm happy they didn't tag on "remastered" onto the name, because this is truly not a remaster. It's a remake in every sense of the word and deserves to be known by itself, and not as a similar sister game to the original.
If you've read this far, I'd like to warn you that the game isn't exactly for everyone. If you enjoy games where you can take your time to explore the environment, then I do not recommend this at all. 

SLIGHT SPOILERS AHEAD
For a good part of the game, the iconic Tyrant (better known by the semi-official name Mr. X) will be tracking you down. He's not simply a boss encounter or a story detail. He's an active threat to you. You will feel fear at every turn, and your heart will sink upon hearing the loud crashing of his boots against the creaky wood as you approach your destination. You will be only a room away from your goal and you can bet he's likely to be in that very room. If he's not, you might want to watch your back. However, while truly terrifying, even as someone who enjoyed him being in the game, he is really REALLY annoying in that he can essentially trap you. You're only safe in a few areas, and as time goes on he'll simply begin pacing outside the door. There's horror games, and then there's games that place you under constant horrific pressure at every moment. If you're not someone who can deal with an active threat, then I don't recommend you buy this. Otherwise, I'd say this is a perfect game for people who like horror, and even those who don't.

This is the newest RE game that stays true to the series' roots while implementing modern game play mechanics. It has the perfect balance of survival horror and action, whereas the other games in the series lean more in one direction or the other.

It's very late to give review for this game, but there will never be late to play this game. If you're a resident evil 2 fans, get this game, if you're a resident evil games fans in general, get this game, if you're just a survival horror games fans, and not familiar with RE2 or RE games, get this, you can still and sure you will enjoy the game.
Plus and minus:
-It's a RE2 remake, one of the best RE trilogy. Some people, even I get a bit dissappointed how some part, and enemies aren't included in the remake. Those are no spiders, crows (I personally love them), alligator boss fight turned into a chase stage (you don't really fight him), and seems the A part didn't affect much event on the B part (original game did better on it).
-Graphics are amazing man, the models are top notch, no just they look detailed and realistic, but they are damn very good looking. The zombies and the monsters, from the lowest to highest mutation, the design are really great, they are both terrifying and cool-looking. My most favourite is Birkin 3rd stage, such a badass looking boss. But you might get dissapointed with Tyrant design, I don't want to spoil, and it's not a big of a deal. But, original game did a far better job on Tyrant (the mutated MR.X).
-I don't feel any downgrade on the difficulty, other than you get infinite save on medium (should've used ink ribbon even on this mode), unless you're on hardcore, you wouldn't be worried about save limitations. Also the checkpoints, honestly, the addition of this feature reduce the tension. Enemies are terrifying man, they give you challenge, especially the lickers, you'll hope you'll never encounter one of these. So unlike the original, the building aren't lit, it's dark, and the sounds of those guys really scare the sh*t of me. the only problem is the bulllet sponge really, they took lot of damage than it should be to kill imo, it makes it just tedious. But if you get know how to shoot correctly, there shouldn't be problems (lickers are ridiculously strong).
-You'll still have a sense of scarcity in the game. They also included weapon upgrades, and it make more sense than previous games, by solving puzzles to open spacial cases. In my opinion, this is a really coll feature, heck, you can upgrade you inventory capacity (of course with some effort to find the pouches), no more tedious back and forth to inventory box.
In conclusion, they did a really good job on this, it even become one of my most favourite RE.  The improvements are really improving the experience of the game from soundtracks to sound effect, they sounds futuristic. Usually I don't really fond of modern games, because most of them get easily boring in my opinion. But this game has the excitement of classic games, that makes you wanted to play more than just once, not for achievements, but because it's just an enjoyable game. Modern game, with classic games excitement I can say.
Tips:If you have enough money to buy the bundle with the dlc, you better spend your money on that. You'll get additional costumes and classic musics and sounds. Sadly, they are too much cheapskate not to put this on the vanilla. Really, those gonna keep the excitement to keep playing the game, man. I remember you'll usually unlocked costumes from playing, not in here and this time you gotta pay for them, if not, you'll get stucked with just the remake outfit and original outfit. I honestly get tired of looking the sam costumes over and over, finishing another playthrough with different costumes is what been keeping me up to play more of playthrough, this is a big flaw imo. I have a love/hate relationship with resident evil games. I’ve played almost all of them, finished most of them, but not all of them.

What I love about resident evil is finding ways to kill zombies and monsters with limited resources. Moving from point to point and the atmosphere. I like the campy stories and the guns.

However I only started with resident evil 5, so I hated the older games like the first Remake, while I liked revelations, RE6 I couldn’t play RE 4 due to controls.

So what I’ve hated about resident evil 2 and 7 are the puzzles. Having to look for items, look for clues and figure out which goes where.  I get that solving puzzles adds to the tension when you know you have to run past zombies and other creatures to get to places but for me it’s kind of annoying.

They could have solved this issue by just showing you where to find the next item on the map, and make it an option you could turn on or off so the purists can play with it off.

With that said I recommend this game. Interesting story, good characters, satisfying gunplay, and the puzzles are bearable. Though for me it loses replay value because it makes me redo the slow annoying puzzles each time I want to play through the game.

Resident Evil 2 / Biohazard RE:2 was the first Resident Evil game I got into. Going into this 100% blind was an adventure.

Pros:
-Graphics are wonderful
-Story is great
-All Enemies are challenging 
	Even small crowds of zombies can be threatening if not dealt with properly 
	Not knowing the weaknesses to any of the creatures allows for a learning experience that can be helped if you read the documents around the map
-The Tyrant (aka: MR X.)
	Wow. Just wow. He will randomly walk around the map until he finds you and when he does your pants will always be down. The balance between running from him, dodging zombies, and completing objectives will bring you to a new level of paranoia. There is more I want to say about him but the less you know the better experience you will have.
-Difficulty 
	Assisted: Very easy, great for beginners to games in general or achievement hunting.
	Normal: Challenging for a newbie to the game. Loot is not a surplus amount but it will give you enough if you are smart with it. Enemies are a challenge when you don't know how to kill them.
	Hardcore: Hardcore! It's really hard if you don't know what to do and can still prove to be a challenge if you do. Supplies are much more scarce and you can't get as much inventory space. Enemies are pretty strong and will mess you up if you are not careful. They use a unique save system that makes you think twice about saving your game every 5 minutes.
-Replayability
	You get two different characters to play from. Each has the same roots to the main story but have different stories themselves (This is hard to explain without spoilers, trust me when I say its worth it to play through them both) My first playthrough was about 7 hours. That time will shrink the more you play. The faster you beat the game the higher rank you'll get (S, A, B) which makes it fun to return to and try to beat your past time
-DLC
	All the DLC in this game was put in for free and they are all great additions. They tell you stories of side characters from the main story. Be sure to play them all for a fun challenge. 
-Bugs
	I encountered very small bugs rarely. Game is polished nicely
-Environment
	The RPD is huge and has plenty of memorable areas that are helpful for when you are in the middle of a chase and you don't want to stop to look at the map. If you kill a zombie on a staircase it will stay there until the end of the game which allows for that sweet, sweet, immersion. Zombies will also trip over other zombies and faceplant! If you stick a knife in one of them... you guessed it! It will stay there so you can always come back for it. If you are like me and love immersing yourself into the story and gameplay, then this is for you.
-Puzzles
	The puzzles are good. Some are easy some will take you a few tries. Nothing to complain about. Nothing to write home about.


Cons:
-Voice acting
	Overall the voice acting was good, but sometimes certain lines would be super cheesy, not match the character expression, or awkwardness in general (some people would call this a pro I'm sure, maybe they had these lines in the original game, I don't know for sure.) Every time it happened for me I laughed at it and said "That was cheesy" and move on.
-The sewers
	I hated the sewers. It is my least favorite part of the game. The enemies are rediculous to fight even when you know how to fight them. It is super cramped which means you have no room to maneuver. The puzzles are challenging but a pain in the ass to do. With all of that said, I think it works really well with the game. It captivates it so well. Having no room to breathe at all but having to squeeze through the overly large monsters. Wanting to shoot them in their stupid monster faces but knowing damn well you don't have the ammo to throw around. It's a love-hate thing.

I feel this review is biased because I had so much fun with the game. I really can't think of any actual cons, things that make me what to not play the game. That's why even the cons I defend a little bit cause they really don't bother me all that much. If I think of anything I will add it to the cons but for now this is all I can come up with.

CONCLUSION

If you are one the fence about buying this game, do yourself a favor and get it. For the price of $40, it is well worth it. I got it for $20 on a half-off sale, and I must say worth every penny. If you don't like horror games (like me) then get it because you are clearly interested enough to read this long-ass review.

I would recommend it, but it's certainly not a perfect remaster.

PROS:

* Modern impressive game engine 
* Adding gunpowder to add more variation to gameplay
* More weapon upgrades
* Really impressive atmosphere
* Amazing gore system/mechanics that make the zombies better than ever
* Defensive weapons from the RE1 Remake are included
* Mr X is initially very intimidating 

CONS:
* The story has been needlessly cut and shortened in places, in very negative ways
* Both character stories are very similar in a lot of situations
* Some of the boss fights are just annoying and frustrating
* Mr X quickly just becomes very irritating and an inconvenience, rather than a constant menace
* You can't down MR X for ammo, which is a missed opportunity for adding new custom weapons or other content
* The two stories no longer make sense, with one character dying in two places at once

Ultimately it's a great version of RE2, but it's far from perfect. 
I have no idea why they cut down some of the story from RE2, to the point that both Leon and Claire's stories feel very similar at the end, and the stories don't actually make any sense timeline wise.
It's also a shame they felt the need to put Mr X in the A scenarios, because he quickly becomes an annoying inconvenience, even more so in B scenario.

This feels a bit rushed, especially the B scenarios, which felt tacked on. If they had taken their time, they could have not only kept the whole story from the original, but improved and expanded it. And perhaps added some new areas.

The Resident Evil 1 Remake is still by far the best example of how to update a Resident Evil game.

In this age of remakes Capcom finally jumped the remake train and remade Resident Evil 2 which is a real classic. I remember playing it as a kid, this was the first game of that type, it took me maybe 20 or 25 hours to complete it. Everything felt new and fresh back then for me and even without knowing english the experience was amazing. So how's the remake? Well, in short that's how remakes should be done, but it's not perfect.

There's probably no point talking about the story. Everyone already knows it. A cheesy, pretty simple but at the same time very entertaining. If there would be more cut-scenes (and I think this game lacks cut-scenes badly) it would be like one of those old cheesy action movies.

So what are the big changes? This is not a 1:1 remake with improved graphics, this is a whole new game. First thing it is now a third person game which leads to different gameplay mechanics. In the original you couldn't aim, accuracy was pure rng but when you hit that headshot it was satisfying and you were happy being able to save some bullets. Now obviously you can shoot zombies in the heads whenever you like, especially on PC with a mouse it's extremely easy. But zombies don't die from headshots here, unless you shoot them a lot of times ranging from couple of shots to ~10. But that's a good decision, wouldn't be fun killing every zombie with one shot, especially lickers. Instead developers thought of another great way to make your way through zombies – you can shoot their limbs, that requires only 2-3 shots mostly and without a leg they can't walk so it's easy to avoid them when they're crawling. And it's so satisfying to shoot off all the limbs, their arms and legs fly off. Great sight.

There's of course the good old police station to explore. Everything is different but familiar at the same time. You explore, solve some puzzles, unlock doors and shortcuts. But then mister-x shows up and starts chasing you. I really hate this. I didn't encounter him in original game, I played only A story and there's no mister-x in it. It was fun taking your time and exploring everything, now you're forced to rush through the game. There are mods which could render mister-x harmless or you could use cheats DLC to get infinite weapons and stagger him each time you run into him. Still i'd prefer to not have him in A scenario just like in the original RE2.
There are other changes and they're disappointing. One of the most scary place for me was sewers where I met spiders. There's no spiders in this game. There's also no moths, cockroaches and crows. ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crows scared me back then I almost ♥♥♥♥ my pants.
Inventory management is pretty much the same. While progressing through the game you unlock more space but I hate this stupid inventory. Why the ♥♥♥♥ a shotgun or huge pliers take same a mount of space as one key? All keys should fit into one slot. I can't stand this. 

Graphically this game looks amazing. I really love the new Capcom engine, I hope to see more games on that engine. It runs great, scales well on different PC's, could run on potato. Max graphics look stunning and it performs very well. Game runs on 90-120fps for me on 3440x1440. It's rare to see a game so well optimized.
Environments look realistic, every area is highly detailed. Lighting is good but the game has that wash out feel, don't know why.
Character models are fenomenal. Face animations are great too, watching cut-scenes is a joy. And I must admit even though i'm straight but Leon looks hot as hell, should be a joy to play as Leon for female players. On the other hand Clair is good looking too, but Ada steals the crown fro male audience.
Overall graphically this is one of the best looking game today.

Sound is pretty good but in my opinion it doesn't come close in quality to graphics. It's fine, but nothing special. Music or ambient sounds are not too scary. It lacks that scary music and sounds which adds another layer of fear to the game.

This is a good remake but I didn't feel the same as playing the original. Probably because I already knew what to expect, there wasn't any moments of surprise. But I can't really blame the game here.
It has some replayability value. Leon and Clair playthroughs are quite different, there's even some sections and locations exclusively available only on one or the other playthrough.

A good game for horror fans, don't expect anything super scary, if you haven't played the original this might leave you more impressed but even if you played it it's still good. Definitely worth getting on sale.

PROS: The gameplay in this title is on point to what you'd expect from a third person title.  Movement is fluid and crisp, shooting is precise, everything with that just feels on point.  The visuals are just as stunning.  The RE Engine really does wonders for this game, presenting the RPD in a wonderful light.  The audio is visceral on the enemies, giving each a unique cry.  The voice acting is great for emulating that experience from the original.  Some of the soundtrack even exceeds the original, such as the Super Tyrant Theme and Hunk's Theme.  Speaking of, the new gameplay revolving around Mr. X amps up the tension in the RPD, and is a welcome, terrifying addition.  The game's difficulty feels like a natural scale, raising the stakes as you progress, and providing the player with enough ammo and items to make it through, so long as the player remembers the tenants of survival horror.  The rewards and completion bonuses are a wonderful RE tradition, and allow you to take those tenants, and jettison theme right out of an infinite ammo rocket launcher.

CONS: The removal of a real, impactful A and B scenario is the real hurting point here.  Each character gets their own beats through the campaign, but with the exception of the very beginning, 2 notes, and the true final boss, the 2nd scenario really does very little to differentiate itself from the original playthrough, and feels like wasted potential.  Other than that, the new soundtrack is incredibly lacking compared to the original, with very few exceptions.  And like a fair number of Resident Evil games, the middle feels like the weakest part of the title.

ACHIEVEMENTS: There are a few challenges on this list that require some careful planning on what route is to be taken throughout the game, most of which aren't that difficult, but can add up if one doesn't pay attention.

FINAL: This is a stellar remake of a classic survival horror game, marking 2 for 2 in the Resident Evil series.  It's flaws are fairly few, and stand little against it's successes.  Without a doubt, one of the stand out titles of it's year, and one anyone with a passing interest in survival horror should give some notice to.

When Capcom announced they were going to remake Resident Evil 2; i was excited but also nervous -- Capcom's track record with the Resident Evil franchise has been up & down beforehand.

The demo for this game proved me wronged so much -- the time, care, and dedication was extremely superb. 

So what is Resident Evil 2?
You play as iconic Resident characters: Claire Redfield, the sister to Chris Redfield; and rookie officer Leon S. Kennedy. You both arrive at Raccoon City at the worst time possible, and it is up to the both of you to escape the city. Now why should YOU, yes YOU. play this game rather than the Resident Evil 3 remake - that's because of two things: massive replayability and constant looming presence -- let me explain:

(On a side note): Resident Evil 3: remake for $60 has cut content, one protagonist, no such constant looming presence just scripted events, and a linear experience. Just want to point that out 

(Now back to Resident Evil 2 remake review)

This game offers a nonstop creature that hunts you everywhere -- not to the safe rooms but when you roam around the Police station and other parts of the game that has his presence you can hear his big footsteps and no simply knocking him down will not kill him, only put him on pause for a few seconds while you get away or to a key area of the game that you need getting to. 

Secondly, is how massive the game is in terms of puzzles, backtracking (in a good way), and hell replay the game from a different perspective that offers a unique twist and turns (i won't say what however, that's for you to find out). 

And to tack the main story on you got "Ghost Survivors" which basically tells the story of three characters from the game or rather the larger Resident Evil 2 narrative it's kinda important but not really. Higher difficulties also offer a sense of being smart and not dumb. I highly recommend playing on ASSIST first before playing Standard and Hardcore. 

Overall for whatever price point this game might offer it is one of the best remakes that i ever came across, and certainly has more value than the Resident Evil 3 remake on the whole. Recommended

RE1make set one hell of a high standard. It’s the gold standard for any game remake really, offering the full experience of the original only amplified by updates like Lisa, the crimson heads, some new areas, and other surprises. There’s a shifting of fundamental elements while retaining everyone, plus more, then a number of extra game modes, gimmicky they may be. The best way of making my point: if I'm going to play RE1 now, I'm always going to play REmake. It provides everything I’d want of the original game and then some.
[Note: While that's sure as ♥♥♥♥ not what a movie remake ought to do, and not necessarily the only reason to do a game remake and makes it worthwhile, I’d say it’s almost certainly the sort of expectation people hold in mind when wishing whatever beloved game of theirs gets remade] 

When it comes to RE2make, it’s not that it does some things wrong though. It’s about the things RE2m doesn’t do at all. There's much needlessly missing that absolutely deserved enough development time/care to retain (and hopefully supplant) the original RE2. In contrast to REmake, when I play RE2m, I’m mostly just left nostalgic to go back and play RE2 for the full story and experience they abandoned in many ways.

I personally don’t characterize RE2's issues as related to leaning into RE4, though I do understand the perspective. It centers on RE2m jettisoning the original general shooting style for over-the-shoulder aim/shoot again. Some call for more, wanting the fixed camera angles (others even for tank controls), but the central killer-issue shared is that larger gameplay shift change for free-aiming that yields a different experience than the (still enjoyable) classic style of old-school/REmake/REzero games. I'm fairly alright with updating to over the shoulder, finding enough room still to yield a similar enough experience to the original (IMO anyhow) by balancing enemies and elsewhere. I’d likely have really enjoyed the classic mechanics still too, perhaps even preferred them. However, I can’t say for sure. It’s too hard to isolate a feature like that when other RE2m issues distract far more from its pursuit. 

Whatever combat complaints aside, RE2make really failed to overthrow the original in even the fundamental recreation aspect by calling quits on many elements prematurely and leaving out certain explanations/plotting events for literally no reason. IIRC, there's no context about the mayor's daughter with Chief Irons; you miss that great helicopter scene; there's X's introduction; and numerous cat & mouse interactions with other characters being seen for whatever reason then separated again  I'd trade every non-canon subpar side mode they added just for those characters to retain their rightful roles and context in the already existing story where I can only presume those things still go down the same way, but were sidelined in development in favor of doing/saying/having nothing. 

Then you've got this recreation of the police station that's great, and the lab that's beyond fantastic (especially with how they make plants real enemies this time around), yet they TOTALLY cut out the earlier city elements that made it feel... bigger, realer, like an infected city from back in the day that left RE2 feeling bigger in scope than RE2m even now. That moment when you first reach the police station and camera sweeps upward, it's epic and ominous at once. You feel contained in this place because you've got context for what's outside the place. They've added those random quasi-city segments in RE2m during the middle, but with such an odd shallowness (especially after the police station) that it’s the sort of design depth you’d get in 1998 anyway. Those parts are merely hallway connections between Area A and B rather than being (and more importantly feeling like) larger set pieces or intersections of something grander. 

That missing "get to the station" factor, those extra cut-scenes, all these things give the weight of life to the city. You feel so much more you’re there as it’s happening rather than arriving at the apocalypse that just already down. Kendo may not seem like major piece, but his struggle and the panic around him adds much texture. Putting him back in the picture, interacting with that chopper pilot, seeing the Mayor's daughter all moving around... even these brief things, create a feeling of a living city where all this other stuff is happening at the same time and you’re just not around to see it. There’s an atmosphere amplified by all those little extra Ada moments, Annette encounters, Ben mentions, Chief Irons looming (I am a big fan of his new garage scene & 3rd floor shenanigans though), Sherry scenes, and it all combines in the feeling of active, concurrent chaos. You’re showing up to the party late, but it ain't over. 

I don’t think I need to emphasis how significantly the lacking A/B and B/A modes is a MAJOR hit, though there’s more to it with the current characters runs being so damn similar anyway. You basically get Leon A, Claire A with both doing the exact same tasks/beats/puzzles/bosses, but one has a bad Ada segment and the other a bad Sherry segment. They should have at least structured it Claire A / Leon B in an interlinking way if restricting us to one-character path, so we’re actually getting a complementary story that somewhat makes sense over-layered. RE2m desperately needs that original RE2 vibe that they're BOTH in this city at the same place/time yet isolated to different areas/tasks. While Claire is fighting G, Leon is fighting X, creating the impression of a larger singular narrative coming together. Hell, in the original they'd even bump into each other at semi-regular intervals for a real sense they're progressing together instead of RE2m’s relatively random re-joining at the end "oh hey whats-your-face from way earlier!"

It’s not that RE2m is bad--especially if you've never played the original--and it certainly could've gone much worse. Nevertheless, what we did get is still MUCH LESS than what already was. It’s almost in grasp of what might have been,but that's probably a big part of what's so frustrating. They got sooooo close that goal was within grasp. And if only one or two elements goofed up, okay that might still be close enough on target. Though the real pattern here is one covering all the bases for "good enough" and calling a wrap. They don't go the extra mile the original RE2 does, let alone the extra, extra mile that REmake provided. Sure, it nailed a great gaming base adaptation (imo anyway) and some areas are in-fact the sort of wonderful re-imagining to be expected. Yet so many others weren’t that, or were outright eliminated, along with whatever other elements and characters. There’s nothing palatable about rejecting the existing double story (and inverted double story) that made RE2 so ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ beautiful in the first place in 1998. RE2make never reaches that next level. It just doesn’t, They needlessly stop short of fantastic remake that so, so, so easily could (and SHOULD) have been given a few different calls earlier and more time later. It’s like I'd said towards the start, RE2m is a remake effort that just leaves me wishing I were playing the original instead. 

Having said my piece, I'd like to mention most of this writing I'd put together before RE3make's release (though ruminated since RE2s first week). I actually started RE3m but stopped early, finding myself *needing* to finish this write-up finally. I've held huge expectations give 3's concurrent development with RE2, fewer snags during, and time after. The demo only elevated  those hopes of something that finally matched REmake's achievement. Yet, I've also heard the whispers of the types of changes that tarnished RE2m  even while going dark on game this month for fresh eyes. Anyway, my last thoughts written, I'm finally ready to move forward to discover either accomplishment or disappointment for myself.

The best entry in the series since Resident Evil 4, this remake of Resident Evil 2 goes back to a more survival-horror type of gameplay with limited inventory space, more punishing ammo management and stronger enemies. Content, level-design, plot and bestiary wise it remains faithful to the original with the exception of the last couple of areas which were overhauled quite a bit. Ghost Survivors, 4th Survivor and Tofu are also in along all the special rewards for completing the game under certain conditions.

The biggest change is on the gameplay front as the game plays with an over-the-shoulder camera with strafing while aiming rather than fixed camera angles with tank controls.

Finally after beating the hardcore scenarios for Leon and Claire, and to coincide with the release of the RESIDENT EVIL 3 remake this weekend, I'm finally putting up a review for last year's remake of the survival horror classic, RESIDENT EVIL 2.

RE2 puts you in the shoes of rookie cop Leon S. Kennedy, and college student Claire Redfield, younger sister of Chris Redfield. After bumping into each other at a local gas station, the pair makes their way to Raccoon City, unaware of the many horrors that await them.

Much like the original, the game is split up into two campaigns: for Leon and Claire, respectively. Depending on who you start with, it can lead to different interactions in the story, and in the case of a character's B Scenario (2nd Run as this game calls it), many item, enemy placements and puzzle solutions will differ from the other character's A Scenario, allowing for much replay value.

In terms of the game itself, it has a beautiful presentation style and the enemies you encounter look absolutely disgusting, thanks to the power of the RE ENGINE. There's also a lot of environmental storytelling, giving you just enough hints on what happened to the places you travel in, especially in the police station.

Characters have been given a lot of overhaul and the voice acting is pretty damn good, everyone plays their parts well, even if some moments did come of as a little cheesy, but it's what I expect from this series anyways.

The only complaint I'll level towards the game is the music, or apparent lack of. For instance, the iconic save room theme only plays once on each of the campaigns, which honestly drains the relief one felt when you entered a save room in the original, being free of the horror, but only for a while. While there are great tracks in the game's soundtrack and it is very atmospheric, there really isn't any that are a major standout to me, outside of a few of the boss battle themes.

In short, the RESIDENT EVIL 2 remake was a remake the world of survival horror fans have long awaited for since the release of the RESIDENT EVIL remake back on the Nintendo GameCube back in 2002. And it was damn well worth the wait.

I truly felt I was in Raccoon City, from a gas station where I as Claire learned of the outbreak to down into the NEST laboratories. I didn't know if I would like Resident Evil 2 before today. I've been a fan of the series from 5-7 but I never played any of the spin offs or earlier entries. The game was on a huge sale so I bite the bullet and I'm glad I did. It looks great, runs almost perfect (I sometimes have my game stutter, but rarely ever) and is fun to play. I'm about three hours into Leon's story and I can't wait to finish it and play Claire's.

Resident Evil 2 is great - but not the greatest.

Leon (a rookie cop) and Claire (sister of Chris Redfield from Resident Evil 1) arrive in Raccoon City just as a zombie outbreak is happening. Whoops.

The gameplay is fun. The zombies actually feel like threats and not just fodder, the various weapons are all useful in their own way, the different enemies are all enemies you love to hate, there are plenty of puzzles (although nothing too hard), plenty of running around not really knowing what to do (especially at the police station), a couple of (slightly mediocre) bosses, and Mr X.

Now, for most of my first playthrough I hated Mr X. Having an invincible enemy stalking you is not my idea of fun (except if you're playing Alien Isolation), however once I learned where all the key items were located and could just focus on my objective, it became very easy to avoid Mr X. Basically, even if you hate Mr X at first, just ignore him and he'll go away.

The difficulty seems just right. I only played on standard and hardcore, and as you'd expect standard was not too hard, especially since you have an infinite amount of saves and plenty of checkpoints, while hardcore on the other hand is pretty damn hard, especially on a first playthrough. I personally recommend playing the game on hardcore difficulty first, just to experience how frustrating (in a good way) the game really can be.

The bonus modes, which are missions where you have to get from point A to point B without dying with only a very limited amount of supplies, were my least favorite part of the game. You [i]can[/i] just ignore these modes if you don't think they sound like much fun, however if you want all the achievements you're going to have to get through them.

While Resident Evil 2 is in my opinion not as good as Resident Evil 1, 4 or Revelations 1 (my own personal favorite), it's still a damn fine game.

Definitely recommended.

I dont play 1st and 3rd person games much because I get motion sickness easily, but the motion sickness I got from RE2 is bearable so I recommend this game for anyone who is prone to get the symptom like me.

Use your map, board up windows, inspect EVERYTHING you pick up, conserve ammo and if you can run away instead of waste ammo then do so. These are all things I did NOT do in RE2 and I ended up having to completely start over as I could not proceed due to having no ammo or healing supplies at all. 

My experience of the RE series was a couple of hours in RE7 (started this over again now) and friends playing the originals on PS1 back in the 90's. So I pretty much came into this as a complete novice with no real idea what was going on, though it wasn't hard to get into the story and the basics of what is going on. 

Speaking of that, the story in general is kinda nonsense but where this game shines is the way it presents the story and the really well done little events that occur throughout the game. I did kinda roll my eyes at some parts but overall it is really well done with decent voice acting making it all feel very polished. 

Gameplay is generally fun and well thought out, though there is a LOT of back tracking (if you ignore the map like I did at first, you will back track even more). I actually had to walk away from the game for half an hour or so a few times as I started to feel really claustrophobic with being stuck in the same areas and having to back track so often. Puzzles are interesting and mostly pretty inventive too. 

Graphics look amazing too, I generally prefer first person and I initially didn't enjoy the over the shoulder perspective to start with. However I quickly got used to this perspective and the character models look so great it was still really immersive. Sound is also top tier with some truly creepy ambient sounds that had me taking off my headphones as at times it was sounding like noises happening just outside my door at home! 

In summary, this game is highly polished, it looks and sounds excellent and I must say I had no crashes or even general bugs you come to expect in most games. The whole thing is very well done and I would highly recommend it to anyone like me who is wanting to finally try out the RE series.

*I would like to preface this review by saying I originally played it on my PS4 and have bought it again on steam.* 

I like to think of this as more of a re-imagining rather than a remake. I know many were hoping for something along the lines of the REmake, but I like the decision made here to go over-the-shoulder. This was another big step in the right direction in bringing back Resident Evil to it's horror roots. 
Graphics and visual do amazing job to keep the atmosphere creepy and tense even when there isn't a clear threat. 
The aim/shooting mechanics are solid and feel good, but the movement can be janky at time. 
Weapon choice is your standard affair in Resident Evil, but they all feel good and the ability to upgrade them is a nice touch (shotgun is beautiful at the late stages). 
The puzzles aren't anything to write home about and could be better. You'll spend more time trying to find the items needed. Despite that, it didn't detract from my enjoyment.

If I had to choose one major complaint with this game, and the reason it's at an 8 instead of a 9, is the 2nd run scenarios. Unfortunately, compared to the original RE2, the 2nd runs were disappointing. There weren't much differences besides some item placements and the ending. Neither campaign sets paint a cohesive story as for who went where first and how things lined up. Again though, I still enjoyed running through them despite the lack of meaningful differences. 

The 4 runs, 4th survivor, Ghost Survivor, and extra challenges such as Hardcore S+ runs provide a great deal of replay value. Whether a fan of the original RE2 or a new comer to the series, this is definitely an entry you shouldn't miss out on.

Maybe the best RE in the franchise. Of course there will always be a big place in my heart for the original RE2 and especially the remake of 1, but at the end of the day RE2 remake is a much more polished version of everything i like about the older ones. 

To be clear what I like in RE is the puzzle aspect of it ; where to go first, what to pick up or ot pickup and making a plan to get out of the RPD/mansion with the least amount of backtracking and dangerous setups. After 142h of gameplay I feel like it is my favorite speedrun game as well as my favorite overall horror game.

The contenders would be Re1 remake, Visage, Amnesia, SH2 and Soma which all have their unique take on the horror genre. While Re2 doesn't have the story of SH2 or Soma, or the scares of Visage and Amnesia, one thing it has is the fear of death. So many times while perfecting my RE2 gameplay, I found myself in situation where I had to cross a corridor filled with zombies and lickers and MrX at my back. I often found myself pausing the game, take multiples breath and calming myself a little bit before entering the next door. Re2 excels at blood pumping little moments where the wrong turn can mean a quick trip back to the title screen. 

The removal of the door opening animation makes the RPD more cohesive than ever, the bullet crafting is well balanced and interesting. The addition of herb shields adds a little bit of strategy to your ressource management and MrX could be the most scary nemesis type character in any game, except maybe for the father in RE7 who does make quite an impression at first. 

I will always love the original Re2 but for me this remake just brings it to the top of the game, once again. I wish the story and voice acting was better and I wish they had the time to make the A and B scenario more cohesive and interconnected, but after all they could have completely done away with the A/B or do multiple releases which would have been worse imo. Have fun escaping the nightmare.

I have played this on PS4, completed it multiple times through and through and had to get enough hours to review this for STEAM.

While a a really great remake in some terms, I have noticed there are some flaws with this reimagining that doesn't quite live up to par to the classic. But I will focus on what makes this a rather unique and pleasant experience overall.

=The PROS of REmake2=
-The engine: Visual/Auditory-

Holy moly, does this game look and sound fantastic. The creepy shuffling of the zombies, the hisses of the lickers, the grotesque eldritch virus-induced abominations and the hulking tower that is: "The Enforcer" or as many of the fans prefer to call him: "Mr. X". While my PC isn't exactly up to snuff in terms of power, I have watched people like: "Maximilian_D00D, Vargskelethor and Uberhaxornova" to name a few with maxed out settings and it just all looks phenomenal. It even looks pretty great on consoles or medium PC settings.

The creators and individual teams working on the visual and auditory sections of this game deserve a round of applause for making a game so immersive, I actually jumped a few times when there were enemies coming out of nowhere or by the corner.
-----------

-The gameplay-

As expected for a PRO, the gameplay has an OTS (Over-The-Shoulder) camera and as such you are able to freely aim your weapon in case you need to use it, Weapons and items from the original are back  and with that Survival Horror makes a return. You need to balance out your use of ammo, weapons or items with a limited inventory space and try to navigate throughout the time you play this game. Fear not, however, as there are ways to upgrade your inventory space and you can store items safely in an item box spread around the RPD (Raccoon Police Department). Happy hunting...

In the addition to gameplay, allow me to introduce you to the characters you will play:

Leon S. Kennedy - A rookie cop that despite being sent a letter to stay away, came anyways in hopes to start his career in the RPD Police Force. I remind you this is PRE-RE4 Leon, so he isn't that badass super-government agent you came to know him as, instead you actually ARE a rookie and your skills are obvious as such, so you are limited in what you do to combat the outbreak.

Claire Redfield - A university student (according to some sources) looking for her brother Chris Redfield. A biker chick that was previously warned about the dangers of Raccoon City (as apparently crime is very rampant there). Despite her brother training her for self-defense, you are still a civilian who is limited in skill to combat the outbreak.

Note: They both have different arsenals and scenarios for you to experiment with, I wonder how you'll get an S+ ranking on the hardest difficulties?
-----------

A little mixed note here...

=The Mixed Herbs=
-Gameplay (additional notes)-

While the gameplay is smooth and very responsive, I at first was very apprehensive of OTS view for this Remake. As the first REmake had the same style as the originals, but it also had options for new players should they desire it. I still have lingering doubts with this change, but I'm not too overly sore about the decision. I do fear that with these changes, Capcom is trying their hardest to steer the originals and their legacy away for newcomers, and I hope I'm wrong about that.
-----------

=The CONS of REmake2=
-The Story-

I WOULD class this as a mixed bag for me, but I simply cannot accept the story for this Remake, if Capcom took the time to actually fix a few things like: "the glaring scenario plot holes" and "the B-scenarios being EXACTLY like their A-scenarios just in different beginnings and endings" then I would have accepted it as a PRO, but sadly they didn't do that, instead it honestly looks like the only thing that was rushed, and you could tell.

While in the original game, the B-scenarios were critically different than their A-scenarios. Claire-A and Leon-B being the canon to the original story but Leon-A and Claire-B would have a radically different ending to that of the canon ending, but in the REmake, they seemed to have scrapped it entirely and made things even more confusing. 
-----------

HOWEVER! That being said, I still recommend this game for what you're given and it is still a pleasant experience for the Resident Evil franchise and if you want to prefer this game over the original, I can't stop you.

But I do hope to encourage you to play the original in any way you can to compare what you do or don't like.

I still give this game an 8/10 since it is still a good remake, but it could use some work to make it more acceptable in terms of story and I could have given it a 9.

Hopefully R3make will live up better.
