Before you read this review, and god forbid, buy this flaming dumpster zombie, go play Resident Evil 4, Dead Rising 2, Alien Isolation, Amnesia the Dark Descent and Dead Space.  Have you played those yet?  Good, then you have no reason to play this recycled sack of zombie trash!  Resident Hellno 2 is a game where you play as a repo-man (or woman) with the world’s smallest backpack. Dealing with a 100% customer dissatisfaction rating, where your cannibal clientele’s only rebuttal is to chew your face off!
Here is 10 point rating systems for these games along with what quality embodies them best.

[list]
    [*]Resident Evil 4-9/10 (combat)
    [*]Amnesiac the Dark Descent- 9/10 (sound design)
    [*]Dead Space- 8.5/10 (level design)
    [*]Alien Isolation- 8.5/10 (survival)
    [*]Dead Rising 2- 8/10 (exploration sandbox)
    [*]Resident Evil 2- 2/10 (tedium)
[/list]

So, why does Resident Evil 2 gets a 2/10? Because every other game I mentioned does an aspect of it better while respecting your time. But the real sin is how RE2 makes exploration and combat into boring, repetitive chores!  You will never feel like a kill is satisfying, never feel accomplished when waste 90% of your ammo on a boss and never feel like your endless mcguffins get you any closer to escaping the infection.

[h1]Backtracking [/h1]
Over half your time in game is a scavenger quest where you find items and then carry them around like a survivalist kleptomaniac. It gets really old when you have to guess at the adventure-game logic behind each item. You are forced to use a walkthrough or waste about 2 hours guessing and cursing as you waste ammo and healing items. However, using walkthroughs is tedious as RE2 will lock your screen onto their game. That’s right, no matter what display setting you use, alt-tabbing is impossible without using Ctr-Alt-Del task manager! Yes RE4 does this, but game is 14 years old, where this was made “remastered” from scratch.

[h1]Inventory management [/h1]
 Unlike all other games in the past 20 years, ammo doesn’t stack instantly, maybe because the Devs love the “authentic experience” or some BS.  Your guns take up 1 slot in your inventory, and oh do you want to upgrade them? Now they take up 2 slots! This comes to a head when you have to juggle multiple kinds of ammo and have 3+ “key items” that cannot be dropped. Leon, you have a freaking police vest full of pockets, and yet a nine volt battery takes as much space as your handgun? In future (better) games all give you a separate inventory for story items, but in RE2 it stinks of lazy coding.

[h1]The enemies [/h1]
To make the enemies more threatening they sped them up and increased their resistance to bullets.  Lickers attack you instantly and stunlock you with impossible to dodge ranged attacks. Zombies lunge faster than an Olympic fencer and have a reach that stretches like Mr Fantastic. Then there’s the “zombie” dogs, these unholy mixes of dobermans, and zambonis! They never stop moving, and they skate around like they are hovering about 2 inches off the floor.  Worse yet, their choppy huge leaping animations are headache inducing.  The cherry on top is that you can’t shoot them if they get too close.  In one chapter I have been hit by them over 10 times even after I reloaded an autosave and knew EXACTLY where they are. I have even been hit multiple times AFTER I KILL THEM. Apparently, they need time to determine that they are dead even when shot in the head.

Then there’s the aspect of being “hunted”. As Leon you are hunted by Mr. X. a giant, mute, invincible, stompy man looks like Watchman’s Rorschach on steroids. You can’t interact with him and he “improves” the game like a traffic accident improves a morning commute. He will force you to camp in the safe rooms and either deviate from the most efficient routes or waste your ammo to killing enemies.

[h1]Enemy Spawns[/h1]
My final straw was when the game pulled a Licker (giant skinned red thing) out of it’s ass while running from Mr X.  Literally, with no background cues, no warning and zero chance to defend myself I open a door and a licker pops into a room and takes out half my health. I get up and put over 30 bullets into the licker and it still doesn’t die, but it kills me when I run out of ammo.  Why not run?  Because their tongues are just as fast and make you stumble so they kill you while you try to limp away.

[h1]The weapons[/h1]
What weapons?  1 shotgun, 1 handgun, 1 magnum, a laughable bad flamethrower, and some flimsy, breakable knives. The real issue is the impact of your bullets. Even when you shoot zombies in the head they STILL don’t even flinch much, and even your shotgun sometimes doesn’t kill them unless at point blank range. But why not use a knife? Well the knives are degrade like compostable tin-foil and their main use it so stick them in an enemy they will let you go.  And you only get them back when you down the enemy they are stuck in.

[h1]Sound Design[/h1] 
Dear god, these devs love noisy sound design.  Half the jumpscares in the game are from zombies that sound like someone took a blender to their vocal cords. Don’t wear headphones unless you enjoy torturing your eardrums. Worse yet, you can’t tell the lickers from the zombies and even Leon’s SHOES sound like he’s wearing steel toe boots wrapped in lead fishing weights!

[h1]Achievements[/h1] 
Here’s the real proof that this game sucks.  The achievements.  Right now there is only a 51% completion for Leon’s Campaign, and less than 40% of Clair’s story and 12.4% for the final survivor.  That means that people got so tired of the game that they didn’t even finish the 1, let alone, both parts of the main parts of the story.  I suffered through Leon’s because I love him and Ada Wong in RE 4 but I know Claire’s missions have escort quests.  Escort quests with limited ammo, no melee ability, no way to resupply AND glitchy headache-inducing enemies?  No thank you!

[h1]Conclusion [/h1]
Capcom, if this is a survival horror, don’t make your enemies into bullet sponges, it’s more frustrating than horrifying. If you want another (good) zombie game MAKE ANOTHER (good) DEAD RISING!  That was the only survival game with weapon degradation that was a feature and not an annoyance.  This stupid “my weapons are useless” BS make me wonder if this is game was just one long advertisement for real weapons. Guns with bullets that don’t tickle, grenades with actual kick and a fuse time longer than 1 second and knives that aren’t made of recycled cardboard!

Everybody has probably already heard that this game looks and sounds phenomenal so I'll skip all that. Yes, it looks  and plays (for the most part) great. 

The moment to moment game play of exploring the mansion (and other areas), picking up clues,  reading memos that fill in the backstory, solving puzzles and killing monsters is a lot of fun. The in-game map is fantastic, probably one of the best-ever maps of any game, period, and the inventory management meta game / strategy is always fun.  There were a couple quality jump scares that got me good and gave me a good jolt of adrenaline.  Playing in a dark room without distractions is a must. 

Where the fun ended for me were the boss fights, and the second half of the game that has you persistently stalked by an un-killable enemy. 

Regarding the boss fights, I found them to be frustrating, not because they were legitimately difficult, but because they aren't well designed with how the game controls. You are put into confined arenas and tasked with trying to avoid attacks that are difficult to outmaneuver, against foes that are constantly stalking after you as you awkwardly try to pop off a few shots, before having to run around them or avoid hits. If, no WHEN you get hit,  have fun watching your character do a 3-4 second animation loop of recovering EVERY TIME. Under normal circumstances, during exploration and even fighting zombies, the controls are fine, but the boss encounters expose the clunky and cumbersome nature of the controls.  

And Mr. X....You either love him or hate him. At some point in the game (I only played Leon's first run) this guy will start stalking you around the Mansion, often forcing you to stop whatever room you're exploring or puzzle you're solving to run halfway across the mansion to get him off your trail, only to backtrack all the way back to what you were trying to do. It's not fun. It's not scary. It's just annoying, especially considering that this mechanic wasn't in the original RE2. 

Finally, I experienced a higher than normal amount of the game freezing (video freeze, but audio still goes) mid-game, and about 30% of the time when I launched the game it would either load into a solid black screen and get stuck, or I would get to the start menu and hit start, and the game would freeze there. My hardware exceeds the exceeds the recommended specs, drivers were up to date and I'm playing with an xbox controller, just as I do with just about every game that's not an FPS. 

Overall, a very good game brought down by frustrating technical issues and what disappointing design decisions.

Original RE2 in my opinion is a solid 9/10, REmake 2 does a good job on it's own but overall lacks the originals atmosphere which felt actually like you were in a city run down by zombies, the alone-ness inside such a large building and the looming threat of a seemingly new terror that's waiting for you behind every important door. The tyrant constantly following you around isn't a horror mechanic, the horror is you don't know WHEN he'll appear, but with his thumping footsteps you lose that horror factor. Maybe it's just me and I've lost the ability to enjoy horror games but T-103 is not at all foreboding this time around and he is easily dodgable with a quick juke and very slow in standard difficulty. Birkin is nowhere near being scary, his original man and monster mashup scream which scared the daylight out of me is nowhere to be heard in the REmake, he looks all fleshy and moves around like a meth addict and has a cute looking eye popping out, his mutated forms are plays on the original but without the horrific slow mutations being shown onscreen that depicts the loss of Birkin's human form, he quickly turns into a generic monster boss and his voice is not at all scary. In terms of survival horror, I had in each playthrough too many items by the endgame, meaning that even IF you gun down every bloody enemy in your path throughout the entire game, you'll still have enough ammo to fight atleast another boss. Before Claire's minigun Birkin fight on hardcore, I had over 6 gunpowders, 10 acid rounds, 10 grenade rounds, 8 enhanced ammo and 5 on the SLS60, and way too many handgun ammo in the item box with 2 first aids and full shield health each. Also, the story about how the overall infection got around wasn't shown properly, only through a couple of dialogue and cassette tapes which is a low blow to the fans. It was the atmosphere and narrative that made RE2 what it was back then and if you can't get that part right then you're obviously doing something wrong. Maybe because I already played the original that's why I found the game to be inferior or maybe it was the PS1 era graphics and sound design that made it scarier.
Somethings the REmake does better is the gameplay which is really fun to play, item management, puzzles and the rng mechanic which makes every same enemy encounter different in each playthrough. Also the new survivor modes and the returning hunk / tofu modes are way better than the original, and was a treat to play. Records and collectibles offer post game content such as concept art, viewing models and infinite ammo weapons which incentivizes replayability. 

TL;DR review
Pros:
-Visuals
-Gameplay
-RNG mechanic
-Bonus game modes
-Replay value

Cons:
-Narrative
-Atmosphere
-Lack of survival horror
-Monster voice design (which is crucial in horror games)

This review was rewritten and edited on 3-29-2020.
 
     I originally gave this game a very favorable review.  After completing both Leon and Claire's 1st and 2nd runs, I am rewriting my review to reflect my new and more thorough evaluation of the game.  This is a good game, if you're a fan of Resident Evil.  However it has some serious problems.  To start, there's some problems with the weapon wheel not working when I equip certain weapons.  I don't know if this is a design choice, or if it's a bug.  Either way, it's frustrating and silly.  I know it's a small problem to complain about, however it occurs enough during my play-through's that it leaves a bad taste in my mouth for the entire play session every-time it occurs. 
     For years I have been a huge Resident Evil 2 fan, as well as a fan of the first game.  This only feels like those games in terms of it's theme and environment.  The game-play is completely different.  The biggest problem that I have with this game is the cheesy enemy AI.  I hate how the zombies lunge forward.  Sometimes they do it over a longer distance than others.  Sometimes they turn on a dime and bite you before you can run past them.  This is such an annoying feature of this game that it's my single biggest gripe with it, and it's the main reason that I won't be playing much more of it after completing the main portion of the game.  This problem clashes with other design choices in the game, such as limited ammo and healing items.  It feels like the designers didn't know if they wanted a survival-horror game or an action game.  If you want me (the player) to kill every enemy that I meet without running past it, then don't give me limited ammo and healing items.  If you would rather I (the player) attempt to maneuver my way past the enemies, then don't give them the ability to move so fast.  It's clashes in design like these, that pull me out of the experience every-time.  
     The zombies in this game take multiple shots to the head.  It baffles me.  Sometimes you can shoot a zombie with a 9mm round and it's head completely explodes.  Other times, it can take upwards of 10 rounds to the head, and still remain active.  Why do I even have to aim if it's chance based?  What is the point of a precision aiming system, with narrowing cross-hairs if ultimately the damage that I do against my most common enemy is left up to chance?  It seems that this was added after the decision to remove the static camera and pre-rendered backgrounds.  It made sense in the old Resident Evil games that you had to shoot a common zombie multiple times to kill it, because the aiming wasn't precise.  In the event that you had a shotgun, you could just aim upwards and get a head shot most of the time, if they were close enough.  This made sense for that game.  It makes no sense whatsoever for this game.
     I don't want to aim, and have to aim so precisely, only for my shots to be left up to chance in the end, even when I score a direct hit right between the eyes.  It feels frustrating and silly to play a game that has been designed this way.  It's almost like the designers created the game with the static camera and pre-rendered backgrounds in mind, and then changed it at the last minute, realized that the game would be too easy with one kill head shots in it, and then put a band-aid on the problem in the form of an RNG system for head shots and critical hits.
     In the end, the game is good, if you like Resident Evil, but it's more frustrating to play than terrifying or fun.  After completing the main game, and experiencing the story, the nostalgia has worn off, and what I'm left with is a game in which the mechanics don't match it's control scheme or theme.  If I weren't a Resident Evil fan, I would seriously not like this game.  These design choices make me not want to spend money on Resident Evil 3, especially after playing the demo and seeing the same problems in that game.  The game is held up by nostalgia, it's legacy, and the story.  As a game, and only a game, it's just not for me.  If it weren't called Resident Evil, I would have immediately written a bad review for this game, deleted it, and never played it again.  However, because it is Resident Evil, and I remember it fondly, I can deal with it.

Being a huge fan of the original Resident Evil 2, and one of the scariest games I have ever played, I was skeptical a bit about the remake. However, I loved the Resident Evil 1 remake, and how they handled it. After some friends recommending this to me I had to play it.

Well, in short, the game is amazing. I would say the closest you can get to a perfect remake, and how a remake should be made, for any game. The overall story, setting, and world is basically the same as the original. All of the same locations, and memorable moments. But the graphics are incredible, some of the best I've seen for a 3rd person shooter in general. Very high res and beautiful textures, great lighting and shadows. Character models look fantastic. New, redone cinematic's are beautiful.

The biggest changes are in the combat, and how the game plays compared to the original. Instead of the prerendered scenes and backgrounds like the original, with areas separated by loading screens and doors, this one is all made in 3d and realtime. So all of the areas are physically connected, and you can see into other areas through windows or look below. You can get around much quicker without waiting for all of the load screens. However, one downside to this, or positive, depending on how you look at it, is that enemies can now keep following you into other areas. Not all enemies will, and they cant enter every room. But it makes the game a lot more tense, and scarier. It can be more difficult though, not being able to just go into another room and know your safe for now. Personally, I like the change. It forces you to think on your feet and make quick decisions, whether they end up working or not.

As I said above, the combat is also very different. Instead of being stuck to standing still and shooting like the original, with overall terrible aiming controls. This one is like any other modern 3rd person shooter. You can move and shoot, have a crosshair and hotkeys for quick weapon changes (you can have 4 weapons slotted (guns), and 4 other types of combat weapons slotted by holding the space bar (knives, grenades, etc.)). One nice callback to the original however, and a nice tip for new players, is if you stand still and hold right click to aim, after a second the crosshair will shrink and be much smaller. When it does this your shots will do much more damage. Especially headshots. When I learned about this I started saving a lot more ammo.

Overall, Resident Evil 2 is fantastic. An amazing remake, and an amazing game on its own. With 2 campaigns to play (4 with the Part B for each one), its a lot of content for a good price. Whether you've played the original and are a huge fan, or have never played the original or any Resident Evil, this is a great game. It appeals to a variety of players, and has a nice mix of gameplay and features. Fun combat, great world and atmosphere, good mysterious story, awesome soundtrack and graphics, some light puzzle solving, and an actually scary horror game. That had me jump out of my seat on more than a few occasions. And certain parts I wont spoil are just.... wow. The scariest thing I've seen in any horror game in a long time.

A fantastic game, but mildly held back by the original. I feel as far as design goes, if you ignore all the backtracking item hunt the older games of this series is known for, this is probably one of the best designed Resident Evil games I ever played. The police station felt like a high quality Zelda dungeon, and because of that it gives this game a kind of a Metroidvania feel. It's only now after Metroidvania is now a genre and after playing quite a few you can truly understand how I can easily make the comparison.

This is level design at its finest, albeit a little slightly held back by extensive backtracking (but also oddly is part of this game's strength and charm, I'll explain further down below).

This can be a very slow paced game for beginners, so even though typically people say this game generally takes 10 hours to beat, you might take a little longer if this is the first time ever playing a classic Resident Evil of this nature. There is a huge learning curve and a lot of intentional design choices that slow down the pace of the game.

Despite me normally criticising backtracking and noting it being both a hindrance and a strength for this game, I'll elaborate my meaning. I feel backtracking is normally just bad design, but I also believe that sometimes you can break the rules and create something great if the execution is solid.

With this game, you're first brought to the police station, which is the true highlight of the game. You're first eased into the station at a very linear path to warm you up to its interior and unlock shortcuts as you go. What makes this good is that the linear path is not stupidly obvious, therefore the station gives this air of complexity (Note: I do this very same thing when I make Zelda dungeons in my fan games). It isn't long before the entire station is opened up and you're set on an elaborate journey through the chambers to find the three medallions to technically complete and explore most there is to the station. You should be very familiar with the station, especially since the clues can be a little cryptic and you'll be exploring it a bit (this is the one small downside). 

After this, you fight a boss, and do some parking lot challenges before you're brought back to the police station again to do what is technically one final puzzle, and this is where everything you learned about the station is put to the test.

Mr. X appears, and that's where the level design here shines. He travels freely throughout the entire station and is always stalking you. Here, you learn that every Zombie you killed, spared, and how much you memorised the station matters because X is relentlessly pursuing you. However, he's not as intimidating as he may first appear because his A.I. is a little dumb in my opinion, but this is not exactly a bad thing, because he does allow newcomers to adapt while still be a little intimidated by him. But once you figure out how he works, you learn that the only thing really threatening about him is the police station itself. He's slow, he's dumb, and his footprints is loud. Newcomers might get a bit freaked out about the loud footprints, but they help you more than they help him. 

This is where the genius of the level design comes into play. Everything in this police station all loops back in on itself, so it rewards smarter players to pay attention to how this place is designed. He cannot trap you in a corner if you never get yourself trapped in a corner. The worst that could happen is maybe getting caught by a zombie you might have spared or might not have killed when you thought you did.

This leads to the zombies and how I feel about them. The zombies here are tanks! Resident Evil 2 teaches you very fast that the age old advice of "aim for the head" is a really bad idea. Your main goal should be to slow down the zombies, but I won't technically be giving away strategies or spoilers here, just use your common sense. Focus on ONLY killing zombies that you feel really could be a problem with your pathing as you try to avoid X and simply ignore the rest. 

Proper pathing is the key to success in this game, because running into Zombies in narrow corridors will almost always cause you to take damage. 

As you can see, I've typed all this so far, and it's literally all about me praising the gameplay and design, that should be more than enough to consider a solid recommendation. It may be a bit old school, and newcomers will feel intimidated. Hell, even I was slightly intimidated at first being that Resident Evil 4 and 7 are the only two I've played and beaten, but while those games I feel have the stronger atmosphere, this game blows both those games out of the water in its design and delicate mix between the horror and action genre that doesn't repeat the same failings of FF5 and FF6. 

However, after the police station I feel the design starts to fall a little short because they start to push a more linear narrative design, and I am no HUGE lover of the sewer level. In fact, the sewers comes off as a bit more frustrating than fun and I simply just want to get through it. 

I get the Dark Souls 'post-Anor Londo vibes' once the police station is cleared where the game feels like it turns into a small bit of a rush job in the design quality. However, I lived through Dark Souls 'post Anor Londo', the sewers and final level are much more tolerable in comparison to Dark Souls end game. 

Now, that's enough praising the gameplay and design. I'm going to keep this brief because this has already been talked about to death, but this game is beautiful. There is a beauty to modern Capcom games I can't ignore. The atmosphere is also perfectly on point. Whatever engine Capcom has created in Resident Evil 7 continues to blow us away with both Devil May Cry 5 and this game, I'm simply blown away with how great Capcom is doing these days considering it was only not too long ago they were considered one of the worst developers out there.

I recently played Mega Man 11 on my Switch, and while the game does have flaws and is probably the least impressive of Capcom's most recent work, it is also still a game that I enjoyed playing and gets my recommendation. 

Like seriously Capcom, how did you guys get so amazing lately? 

Get this game, it'll be worth it. The story is short once you know the ropes, but that gives it great replayability and makes it a game I'll certainly want to return to more than once.

I haven't played the old Resident Evil games, only the modern seventh one, so I can't make comparisons between this and the originals. This latest iteration is a very decent experience with amazing graphics and much the same gameplay as the seventh one. In my opinion, the biggest difference between this and the seventh is that this game is more oppressing when you have to get stuff done, while the seventh is also oppressing of course, but it's more horrifying than anything else, as well as more linear game. This game is also quite linear, semi-linear I'd call it, more linear or about the same as for example Bioshock.

What you need to do is to solve why people are zombie like. To do that, you need to progress further in closed doors by opening doors and figuring pretty amusing puzzles. These puzzles aren't hard mind you, they are not for puzzle geeks at all, so don't worry about them if you are not a problem solver. The challenge in this game is in facing the infected, which appear periodically, and if you really want challenge or to go easy, there is a hardcore mode for those who like challenge and assisted mode for those who just want to know the story. I played on standard and I would recommend that to anyone new to Resident Evil.

The story part of the game is pretty good. The acting is very well done, audiovisual side is extremely good and there are no cutscenes that interrupt the gameplay in any annoying manner, so everything is good on this front. The dialogue gets sometimes slightly cheesy, but that is intentional and part of the charm. Unfortunately or not unfortunately there is 'a real ending' you get if you play the game twice. The game is actually meant to be played twice, first as either Leon or Claire (your choice), the protagonists, then as the other one. I have only played the game once with Leon, but I can already say this game was well worth the 20 euros I paid for it on one playthrough. The game is a tad short, sure, but it is very amusing from beginning to finish if the oppressive mood or occasional gross gore don't bother you. I actually wish there would be a censored option on the most nasty parts of the game for those who don't enjoy them, but I personally was completely fine with these.

The best thing to mention is that there is a free demo to try. There you can see how many graphical options and other necessary PC specific settings are implemented. Capcom has done truly commendable job on this port, so delightful! This includes fine optimization work, so if you own RX 580 level of a GPU, then you get great visuals at 60 FPS (framerate can be uncapped).

So, this game is a great experience, carefully crafted, an easy recommendation. I don't know if the next remake of the third game is going to be as good, since it looks rather cheesy to me, but this is certainly a good pick especially if you enjoyed the seventh one. This is not some legendary masterpiece by any means, just a game that most people will be happy with. To note though, I actually liked slightly more the seventh one and wish the future Resident Evil sequels to present the same horrifying atmosphere as the seventh.

Recommend, [b]BUT only on discount[/b].

[b]This is what a remake should be[/b], brings an old game up to full 2019 standard, but keeps the complete spirit of the original in tact (if not in fact improving upon it).

This brought back the nostalgia for me as well as giving me all new frights and adrenaline-filled moments. Definitely the scariest game I’ve played in a while (mainly the footsteps of ‘Tyrant’ before you figure out how to deal with him).

The [b]standard mode difficulty is perfect[/b], I constantly ran out of bullets and also died, it certainly wasn’t easy. I was a little bit offended it suggested I go to ‘assisted’ mode just because I died twice in a row, but I ignored that.

On my first playthrough (Leon) I was a little bit annoyed at just how much I had to go back to the starting Police Station after I thought I’d finally escaped it, but they’ve set the game up so there are puzzles you come across at the beginning which you can’t complete until 2/3rds of the way into the game. I guess this was a way of saving on having to make new maps, it wasn’t my favourite though.

Similarly, it’s great you have a choice of ‘stories’, but when I played as Claire using the ‘2nd Run’ feature (A mode which is specifically meant to make things more different and play as if both stories are happening simultaneously) I was unimpressed to discover [b]the stories are ~75% similar[/b]. You play the first time and Claire is caught on the other side of burnt wreckage as you and has to find a different path to police station, you’d figure when you go to play as Claire the second time around you’d follow her on that journey? Nope, it just skips everything (Including the gas station part before it) and you start at the police station. Then you do the exact same puzzles that you did as Leon, so it’s neither different nor as if the stories are happening at the same time (aka Leon already did those puzzles).
Thankfully there were at least some differences: The weapons, the starting location, having access to at least one section of the Police Station that the other doesn’t, a certain part of the city the other doesn’t have access to, the minor characters, and some differences with the bosses. This all accounts for the 25% of the story which is different.

Oh, and it’s lame that being in inventory menus etc counts towards the timer; you’re given a score at the end based on how much time you took, I was only 15 minutes away from the next highest score, that 15 minutes was probably time I spent in menus!

It was also great that they tried to make extra use of the maps by putting in ‘extra game modes’. There are 5 of them (2 must be unlocked) and they are [b]all essentially the exact same premise[/b] just on different parts of the map; that premise is “Go in a linear path to the end point with there being a tonne of zombies in the way”. Some of them give the vibe of the “Challenges” from TimeSplitters 2, of reusing existing maps for hard challenges with lots of zombies etc in your way. However even the ‘easiest’ of these mini missions is pretty hard, they should totally have a co-op mode!
Also, a lot of them feel very same-y, with you going through the same maps (Mainly the sewers) in many of them.
The 5 star difficulty one is probably the most unique, as it’s the only one that doesn’t require you to run a path to an extraction, you stay in one spot on a barely used map (The Gas Station) and have to kill waves of zombies. Most of these are so hard I’ve only played them on “Training” mode though.
It also would’ve been nice to see them use the barely-touched map of the city streets you have to go through to get to the front of the Police Station in the beginning, they could’ve easily made that one of these missions instead of yet another Sewers one.

Also something that made the experience a bit worse for me was you need to move your mouse small distances to make sure you hit the enemies in the head, but for some reason this game [b]felt really clunky trying to aim such small distances[/b], I regularly missed shots that should have been easy. I’d wonder if it was just my mouse setup but this hasn’t happened in other games I’ve been playing recently.

So overall a good game/experience, I’m glad I purchased it but it was 70% off when I got it, it would not have been good value for money at full price for me. I’ve gotten 20hrs play out of it, might be able to squeeze another hour out of it before I uninstall, but I’m not one of these perfectionists so replaying over and over trying all the difficulties and slightly different variations doesn’t interest me. I give it a [b]7.9/10[/b]

Let me start off by saying I [b]highly recommend this game[b]. The 97% positive reviews do not lie. It's great. It's scary. What more do you want?

Now that that's out of the way... ♥♥♥♥ this game. Very paradox, I know, but as always - let me explain.

This is an absolute masterpiece. As a remake of a 20+ year old game, it does everything so right. It takes the environment, the characters and the story from the original and puts it at the level of Resident Evil 7. The R.P.D. has never looked better, the atmosphere is phenomenal and you can really feel why this game was such a success, even just in the opening few minutes.
The way the lighting and ambience sets up that first zombie encounter (which is always a big thing in every RE game) is so damn captivating that it pulls you in the moment you get to control Leon/Claire for the first time. It has also gotten a graphics update including ray-tracing so that's pretty cool.

[h3]The story[/h3]
The story is neat. It's nothing too amazing, but it gets you interested in the characters and you always have a reason to keep going. You get to play two campaigns - one for Claire Redfield and one for our best boy Leon S. Kennedy, with each actually having a so called B-Scenario which changes the locations of certain progression and puzzle items. Very replayable!
The dialogue is really strangely written and acted sometimes, but that's just a small issue and you probably won't really notice during your first runs. The chemistry between the characters is very good and fun to watch.

[h3]What about the puzzles?[/h3]
The environment and puzzles are well designed and fun to explore and solve. The puzzles aren't exactly brainbusters but they're alright and they feel and look good enough to be fun. Most of them are either "combine item x and y to get item z," "remember a three digit code" or "pick up a key or tool to open the next door." The way you progress these puzzles in the R.P.D. feels very natural though and it makes exploration and backtracking worth-while. No big complaints there.

[h3]And the gameplay?[/h3]
The gameplay is where my first issue lies. I've finished this game four times a few years ago (one run with each character plus their respective B scenario) and at least four times in the past two weeks (21 hours of playtime) and I had a lot of fun, BUT... coming off of 100%ing RE3 and especially RE9, there are a few things that I have issues with. Firstly, the gunplay. It feels weak. The sound design is alright but the guns just don't feel very punchy, they don't stagger enemies enough, even with the shotgun (which feels very good otherwise) and they do seemingly random amounts of damage. Sometimes it might take three headshots with the pistol and sometimes it might take ten. Why? Who knows, honestly. This issue carries over to RE3, sadly.
My second complaint is the absence of any sort of self-defense mechanic like the dodge in RE3.
I know, I know, the og didn't have a dodge mechanic and RE3 came out after RE2 obviously, but it just feels so punishing to have enemies approach you with no consistent way of stunning them, only to then lose a big chunk of your health because the game decided that 12 handgun bullets to the face weren't enough to kill that one random zombie...

I'll tell you right now though, these two issues that I've listed were only ever problematic during my challenge runs (no health, no item box) or the bonus modes "Ghost Survivors" and "4th Survivor" which are both optional content. I had to play them for the 100% completion though and that was just not fun whatsoever. I currently have RE2, RE3 and RE9 100% and let me tell you, RE2 was the most ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ out of the three of them. Challenges that take between 5-15 minutes have to be done nearly perfectly with run-ending, unpredictable RNG concerning enemy spawns, grapples, damage/crits which can ruin runs with no way to predict or prepare for it. To protect my sanity, I haven't played the Tofu Survivor modes and I'm not going to. I'm content with beating the game 8 times plus beating all challenge modes.

All in all, I recommend giving this game a shot. It set the gold standard for what remakes should be, not just in survival horror, but in general and is still one of the best and scariest Resident Evil games to date.

+- Much gore

+- Counter knifing OP
+- Passive collectibles
+- Items don't stack in storage
+- Visible weapons, but shared holsters
+- Are the voice actors intentionally bad?
+- Somewhere between horror and action
+- Rare/lite weapon upgrades/attachments
+- OP window shutters replaced by excess boards
+- Some of the achievements are ridiculous challenges

- Hardest boss is a shipping container...

There hasn't been an AAA survival horror game that isn't just "Hide in the funny closet until they go away" for a while now so this was like a soothing lullaby telling me everything was going to be just fine. It has a ton of cool little details and features though that elevate it to being my favourite game of 2019 so let me just gush over it point by point. 

-This is divisive but I love the gore system in this game and the way the randomness encourages you to spare some enemies or just disable them in order to save ammo. Basically unless your using some of the more powerful guns getting headshot kills with a pistol can be pretty difficult and take more ammo than you might think SO instead what you can do is take off their limbs to reduce their reach and combat effectiveness and run around them instead. The gore itself looks amazing btw I love how like, when you break through their arm right? It turns into a kind of physics object and plops down and you can see the bone breaking and everything. I feel like they were almost going for a kind of Dead Space sort of thing where just shooting a zombie in the head is not always a lot of the time the best choice and you might want to focus somewhere else. It really worked for me, and forced me to kind of run a count of my resources in my head and make split second decisions on what is worth it and what isn't. 

-MR X is fantastic in this game. Now that they are not constrained by PSX hardware limits they can do all sorts of crazy ♥♥♥♥ like have him follow you through doors and appear randomly from any doorway! (he can even enter a certain save room!) He also has an awesome amount of interactibility with the enemies in the game where he will push them over or knock them out of the way while going through a hoard of them and you can even shoot his little hat off how cool is that! I love how he effects the audio design and how you can hear his ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ footsteps just pacing all over the place and it makes you want to grind your teeth in anticipation! 

-Tofu mode has been expanded beyond anything I could imagine and now you can play as and meet all of his friends! There are so many characters to collect! It is very addictive if you like going fast.

-I really like some of the takes on the classic side characters they have in this game. Kendo being a real stand out and my favourite, but big props go also to their takes on the entire Birkin family, Marvin Branagh, Hunk, and Brian Irons who they really play up how much of a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ creep he is in this game and I love it. Its actually why the Claire route is probably my favourite because the part where you play as Sherry is ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ awesome and very scary!

Essa review é feita após eu terminar duas vezes no PS4, Lado A (Claire) e Lado B (Leon), e estar mais da metade aqui na Steam (7h de jogo). Uma conclusão resumida é que o remake é de excelente qualidade e fiel ao original, trazendo adaptações que não atrapalham, mas melhora o enredo e o desfecho do roteiro. O principal problema foi a preguiça para desenvolver o Lado B. Na minha opinião, eles deviam ter explorado mais as diferenças e, ao invés de você poder escolher o personagem, ter colocado cada um deles em um dos lados da história, que imagino que o correto seja Claire A e Leon B.
Resident Evil 2 é um game clássico da década de 1990 que 20 anos depois foi totalmente refeito do zero. Há muitas adaptações e melhorias na história. Os gráficos são perfeitos e a jogabilidade incrível, inclusive a batalha contra zumbis está mais inteligente e desafiadora, sem muitas chances de dar aquele "olé" pelas costas  deles.
Prós:
+ Gráficos
+ Adaptação do enredo
+ Jogabilidade
+ Imersão: cenários incríveis e novamente sombrios (o que a franquia havia perdido)
+ Volta às origens para sobrevivência e não ação de aniquilação (que também passou a dominar a franquia).
+ Jogo de terror
+ Personagens iconicos: Claire e Leon.
+ Inteligência artificial adequada.

Contras: 
- Lado B é decepcionante, só muda uns 10 minutinhos no início do jogo.
- Pouca informações das demais franquias que afetam diretamente os cenários do RE2, como os acontecimentos do RE3. Acredito que com o desenvolvimento do RE3, eles devem mexer um pouco e adicionar patches que introduzam melhor esses elementos.
- A ambientalização na delegacia é perfeita do começo ao fim, mas à medida que você entra no esgoto e laboratório, parece que eles foram um pouco mais apressados. No entanto, ainda sim ficou muito bom.

Resident Evil is the original horror survival game, this second installment's re-imagining keeps that tradition.  I loved the ultra realistic body damage, from not being phased by regular guns to being decimated by the shotgun.  The map system is also great at taking notes but not giving away the answers.  Going along with this even items you leave behind/install (you will understand when you play) show up on the map to make sure you never misplace something or leave something behind.   If you game over there are checkpoints most of the time and regain what you used after said checkpoint.  While, not in game the modding community has really taking a shinning to this game which adds tremendous replay value.

Good/Bad Opinion: The game play switches between horror, to madly running away as your pants fall down to very, very slow exploration and story telling and while this is good and mostly well paced it can get on the nerves of some players.  The player does have control of this most of the time, but you will get thrown into the fire at points in the story with no warning.  Another thing is you will not always be given explanations or tools needed in a convenient fashion, this is partly to push you the player but can come off as more of forced back tracking.  Luckily, almost exclusively this is for bonus stuff like upgrades and extra items, but like I said upgrades.... so your going to want to do this if your not the best at the game.

The down side to this game is it has a massive learning curve and then plateaus, followed by small but quick steps, so if your a casual gamer this is going to get bumpy.  Weapons are less effective than in the original but a quarter and a mile.  Healing items and are plentiful, but your really gonna need to save them for later, so missing and getting hit are the cardinal sins.  You are forced to take damage a couple of times so make sure you have enough life. 

Although very different that the original RE 2 the game's ultra realistic aspects take center stage in bringing this horror classic to live.  If it were in VR I'm not sure anyone could handle this.  Overall, this game is totally worth it if your looking to dive and in and challenge yourself.

Resident Evil 2 is a remake of the game which was released in 1998. I never played the original version so this was a completely new experience for me.

The good

• Play as either Claire Redfield or Leon Kennedy. After you complete the game with one character, you can play a new game plus mode with the other character where the story will be slightly different, you’ll meet different NPCs and find different weapons.
• Excellent survival horror gameplay. Every enemy is legitimately dangerous if you don’t respect them, even the basic zombies. Ammo and health pickups are limited, so you have to be careful not to waste anything. Sometimes its best to avoid enemies and conserve ammo.
• Enemies include zombies, lickers, dogs, a couple of strange mutants, and multiple bosses (who, in true Resident Evil style, just won’t stay dead).
• Good weapon variety including handgun, magnum, SMG, shotgun, grenade launcher, shock rifle, flamethrower and minigun. Plus secondary weapons such as knife, flashbang and frag grenade that can be used to escape from enemies who grab you.
• Some weapons and upgrades, like weapon mods and pouches to increase inventory size, are earned by solving puzzles, which rewards you for exploring.
• Interesting locations including the Raccoon City police station, a nearby orphanage and an underground laboratory. The graphics look amazing, and the areas where the lights are out and you’re exploring with a flashlight helps to create a horror atmosphere.
• Good story and great voice acting.
• Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.
• I didn’t suffer any bugs, crashes or framerate issues.

The bad

• Inventory system is occasionally annoying because you’re not allowed to simply put an item on the floor and pick it up again later. Any item you drop is discarded forever, which means you sometimes have to go back to a storage box to free up space to pick up a quest item that needs to be used on an object 10 feet away.

The recommendation

Resident Evil 2 is an amazing game, a must play for every fan of the Resident Evil franchise, or survival horror games in general. I actually think this is my new favourite Resident Evil game.

I understand that I am one of the very few dislikes to this game, but allow me to elucidate here. 
Resident Evil 2 was hands down my favorite game of the series, let alone of all time in my personal log of nostalgic video games. Why? The atmosphere was intense, there were items hidden everywhere, there were puzzles and objects to be unlocked, and you felt pretty good about clearing out a room full of zombies. 

So why don't I like this remake? 
The simple answer is that it tries too hard. Within the first hour I was loving it; weaving through zombies in the streets in order to make it to the police station, basking in the impressive graphics, and getting a feel for the new 'Leon', who is portrayed as much more youthful than previous games. It was great, until the real game play began. You become quickly aware that the average zombie requires 8+ HEADSHOTS before they are down for good. This becomes a serious problem when you never find more than 10 bullets in any given room. This especially becomes a problem when there are 3-4 zombies in a room. This becomes and even larger problem when there is NO 'kick' or 'dodge' mechanic, meaning that if you don't have a melee weapon (none to be found short of a defensive knife early game) you are going to die, no matter what. 

The insult to injury was in passing 5 locked doors and 4 combination locks within the first few rooms, and actually needing to pick up wooden planks and fasten them to open windows - but we can't use a simple 2x4 as a melee weapon, right? 

My ending note is this:
I get challenging games, I really do. I'm a Dark Souls fanatic, XCOM fan, and a tremendous RE fan - hell, the first remake is literal perfection. This however, is garbage. All these guys had to do was remake the game, but instead they turned it into a walking simulator, because the sheer number of resources it takes to even defend yourself is more than they literally have available. Even if they simply added a dodge or kick mechanic to it, it would make a dramatic difference. 
I was so excited about this game, but now I feel robbed of my joy in the original. I simply don't understand how the remake of the first could be so on point, only to have it followed by some truly stupid concepts emulated within this one. I could try to waste my time and beat this, but it would feel like dragging my balls through broken glass, and that just isn't fun to me.

When I was little, I watched my brother play Resident Evil 2. A terrible idea, for any one of you hoping to have a trauma-free childhood. I remember the skin-crawling sensation of watching him barely dodge grasping zombies, getting ambushed around corners, and face horrid bosses with limited resources. It was the sounds that got me most, though. The wet, slopping chomp as a zombie caught hold and ripped a chunk out of your shoulder, the baleful, tortured cries that seemed a twisted call for help, it was all an introduction to a fate worse than death for a young mind. I didn't sleep well for months.

The experience was so impactful that it inspired a lifelong fascination with undead, zombies, and horror as a whole. I was never, ever able to pick up an original copy, though, even when I had the old N64 lying about ready for action. The game was a cursed, sacred thing to never be attempted else I go through sleepless nights all over again. The same went for RE3 and C:V. The entire survival horror genre was simply too much.

Fast forward to today, having completed Resident Evil 4 and 5, Outlast, and... well, I WOULD have done P.T. if certain publishers had not f***ed up, but whatever. When I heard about the RE2make, I was ecstatic.

It does not disappoint.

The textures are ghoulish and grotesque. The environments are hauntingly familiar and yet refurbished in a natural, logical manner... well, logical for a Resident Evil title wherein you are likely to need some emblem or symbol to go to the bathroom. The gameplay is solid, tight enough to be responsive but JUUUUST limited enough to make you feel helpless if things really go tits up.

Long story short, after 15 years, I get to finally experience this in earnest. I can't recommend it enough... and for those of you with little brothers, this is your chance to *screw with them for a lifetime* so they end up like ME. Take the plunge. They'll turn out alright. Probably.

Conclusion:
Are you a Resident Evil fan? Did you play Resident Evil 1 HD or non-HD and loved it? Do you like thinking in order to beat a game instead of just mindlessly shooting? If you said yes to any of these questions, buy this. You'll love it.

Following the tradition of reboots and remasters, Capcom has decided not only to update the graphics and provide quality of life improvements but has made an entirely new game based upon the original. As a result, the game feels new even though it is still, in spirit at least,l the same old RE2 we played back in the 90s. This is an incredibly scary game, but perhaps not in the way that we traditionally mean when we refer to a movie, for example. It is a kind of tense, apprehensive anxiety that is unique to a horror video game and unachievable IMO by any other medium. 

First and foremost, RE2 understands that it is the player, not the character who needs to feel afraid, and nothing scares players more than lacking ammo and health and needing to thread possibly dangerous situations (perhaps scare is too wrong a word, but tense is still a good emotion for a horror game to invoke in players and this game does so beautifully). Lest you think this is a Man of Medan/Until Dawn styled story-based game, you would be very much mistaken. This is still a survival horror game where the difference between dead and alive (therefore, defeat and victory) is a single health point, a single extra green herb, a single round of ammo. Ammo, health and inventory management is still very much the focus of the gameplay, with you perhaps deciding the zombie isn't worth killing to conserve ammo and potential health items. Gone are the tank controls of the 90s, but in its place are more frenetic enemies intent on draining that ammo and, once that’s done, draining your hit points. Gamers too used to having extra clips of ammo will definitely feel anxious when they see after a fight all they have is half a clip left, and no end to the dark hallways in sight. The puzzles are a little different from what we might remember them, but they are very much in the same tradition. We need three Macguffins, spread around the place, oops look this one is right under a boss, this one needs a key that is right under another boss, and to get this one you need this other thing that may or may not be right under a boss. Clues and hints are more available this time around, and the moment you find one key item you'll feel elated about being able to solve that puzzle you saw - then dread sinks in when you remember that was ten rooms back, and The Everloving Tyrant is right on your heels, and where did all these lickers come from? You push the door to the next room…and realise you’d rather be anywhere but here.

Second, the game looks and feels as if it were the next generation of entertainment. The graphics got a TOTAL overhaul. From the first scene onwards the game looks like an interactive movie like Man of Medan or Until Dawn. The characters themselves have new face models. I felt Claire looked a bit jarring at first, but hours in and I'm used to her new look already. Leon looks awesome, and it's about time he looks the cutie pie husbando he is. Along with graphics updates, the dialogue has also been updated to sound less 'translated' and natural - everyone sounds American, adding to the 'Straight Outta Hollywood' feel. The cinematic display of the game doesn't detract from the gameplay - it adds to it. Lickers shuffle in the shadows, the ominous signs of blood and broken glass make you tense up, and Mr. X's boots echo through the empty halls. Ambience and Immersion are very well served in this game and ratchets up the tension exponentially.

With this game CAPCOM shows us how a true remake is supposed to be. Highly recommended.

An absolute masterpiece, the zombies in this game are genuinely terrifying and pose an actual threat instead of being a minor nuisance like in other games, the graphics are stunning, although it is a horror game, the gun play is spot on as well, the game will suck you in the moment you play it and makes you want to go back for more.

To put it simply, this game is amazing. Plentiful graphics options and an in-built vram bar allow you to see how much your usage is and adjust to make the game more stable for lower end systems. Even though I run this game in the red zone I have encountered no bugs or glitches and the have maintained a steady framerate.
   
   On the gameplay end of things, this game feels like a natural evolution of the original RE2. The story and events have been shuffled around to make for better pacing (in my opinion) and the story is still the basic RE2 plot. The puzzles are mildly challenging and even more so on the 2nd Scenarios. The 3rd person perspective had me doubting the game at first, but after a while it grew on me and I think it was the right decision. Still wish they could have implemented a bonus mode or something with the original fixed camera angle. Ammo and resources are somewhat scarce, but if you play smart and don't try to kill every zombie you encounter, then you will be fine. The aiming system feels like how we had to play the original RE2 as well. You have to pace your shots and wait for your reticle to shrink, if you do, you are rewarded with more accuracy and the a higher probability of a critical hit which can put a zombie down permanently if shot in the head. 

   Now the enemies are your typical zombie shooter affair, but with the iconic enemies of RE2 to boot. Of course you have zombies which are slow, dumb, shambling enemies that can have surprising bursts of speed or gang up on you if you aren't careful. You can shoot their limbs off to make them slower or more easily taken care of. Then you have Lickers, a classic enemy that made me put down the original as a child. They are blind, but have acute hearing, and will detect you if you move faster than the basic movement speed or touch them. They hurt a lot too and are incredibly quick and can attack from a distance with their tongue if you try to run away. They are weak to fire though. Next up we have Mr. X also known as the Tyrant. He serves a roll similar to Nemesis from RE3, the Hunter from Dead Space, or the Xenomorph from Alien Isolation. He is always looking for you while he around. Luckily you have some tools to help you look out for or better yet hear him coming. His footsteps are loud. Really loud. So you can get an idea of where he his when he is searching for you. You can expend ammo and grenades to stun him for a time, but I've always found running to the nearest safe room is the best option, since he can't enter them. He is relentless and can easily kill you even on the lower difficulties. There is a brand new enemy in this game I won't spoil here, but they are pretty creepy and you will encounter them in the sewers. The giant alligator returns as a set piece. William is also a boss you fight multiple times throughout the game. There are also the Plant 43 monsters that make a return from the original RE2, but only for a short while at the very end of the game. 

   Summary: This game is a fantastic example of how remakes/remasters should be done. Right alongside others like Crash, Spyro, and Halo 2 Anniversary. If this is kind of quality we can expect going forward from Capcom, then RE3's remake will hopefully live up to the same standard. While the dlc was kind of disappointing in my opinion, it was still a fun distraction. The graphics options make this game a great benchmarking tool as well. This game gets a full recommendation from me.

The original RE3 was my most-favorite game back then. Even though I also enjoyed the original RE2, the RE3 Nemesis holds a special place as it was the game that got me into the survival horror genre. So when I heard that RE3 is getting a remake, I was super excited and decided to buy this RE2 Remake first to see how it would look like. Although I heard a lot of praises and read a lot of good reviews since RE2 R launch, I never felt the need to actually play it. But now that I have, I agree with most of the reviews and would very much recommend this game.

PROS:
- Eerily effective ambient atmosphere (mainly through lighting and sounds) to create a sense of dread and terror, especially in the earlier parts of the game
- Intuitive controls, if you have played any FPS/Third Person Shooter games in the last decade
- Very good graphics optimization, not really taxing to your system (if you don't use a high-spec PC) yet still manages to deliver great graphics. Guess it has to do with the RE Engine that they implemented since RE 7
- Great physics engine, you can try it out yourself later to a zombie (or zombies) for fun. High level of texture detail also helps in this matter
- Quite an interesting storyline, if you are not familiar with the original game. If you are, well then maybe you'll agree with I'm going to say later
- A good amount of head-scratching puzzles to give your brain a break from maiming zombies and running away from monsters, but in enough quantity not to fully distract you from the overall atmosphere
- High nostalgia factor if you played the original trilogy, with a healthy amount of changes to keep you on the edge of your seat
- Don't forget the great, great mods which up until now are still growing by a large and active community. You can get gameplay-changing mods even to more guilty-pleasure mods (if you know what I mean)

CONS:
- Terrible handling of the multiple storylines (they called it 2nd Run this time). As a fan of the original games, this is what I find jarring the most. Each new storylines that you will unlock once you completed the requirements are basically just rehash of the previous stories, with little to no fresh contents, They will even contradict or at least create plot holes within the game's established story itself. The original RE2 masterfully crafted the whole story through the multiple scenarios, and made me play through the extra scenarios to get the full story. In this remake, I felt cheated once I completed the 2nd Run scenarios. This may be different if you never played the original game. And Capcom said they won't release any story DLC for this remake, so well...
- Because of the above, replayablity factor is also hindered a bit. The achievements and extra modes maybe will keep you playing for some more, but once you beat everything they offer then you're practically done
- In addition, the main storyline itself could be finished in relatively short time
- Character facial animations most of the time feels lifeless, even in recorded cutscenes. They managed to nail it in basically every other factors related to the animation, except the facial expressions somehow

All in all, I'd still recommend to play this game, to veterans of RE series as well as casual players alike. It definitely is one of the best games of 2019.

It's not a perfect game. Don't get me wrong, I enjoyed it very much. The gameplay is really good, and it's very rare for a game to scare me, but this one did. There's a few jump scares, but it also (for me anyway) kept me in an extended state of anxiety. Resident Evil 2 Classic is one of my favorite games, and I've beaten it countless times. I thought this game would be a piece of cake for me because of that, but it's quite different, it kept me on my toes the whole time.

There are a few negatives however. For one, it's kind of short. It felt a bit dumbed down as well. It's slightly more linear than RE2 Classic. There's still plenty of things to explore, and you aren't forced onto a path too much, but it just felt smaller than RE2C.

The B scenario is almost non-existent. It's just a little different than the A scenario, but in RE2C it was totally different. The storyline is great for the most part, I enjoyed it a lot, but there's a glaring flaw that leaves you wondering what is actually canon in this game after completing the B scenario. There's no consquences for grabbing every item you find, whereas in RE2C some items/events wouldn't be in the B scenario if you picked them up earlier in your A scenario, and blockaded windows don't stay there on the B scenario if you boarded them up in the A scenario. There's barely any interaction with the other character (Leon/Claire),

Several monsters from RE2C do not make an appearance in the remake. Some of them were insignificant (crows, roaches) but I would have loved to see some giant spiders or the giant moth, or even the naked zombies or super-lickers for a harder challenge. The plant zombies that replaced the ivys in RE2C are an upgrade in my opinion, the ivys were kind of boring in my opinion.

Replay value is pretty good if you feel like trying to get an S rank and unlock things, but not everyone wants to do that. It is worth at least four playthroughs though (Leon A/B and Claire A/B)

All in all, I still think it's a great game. There's a lot that could be improved upon, but I enjoyed it very much. I'm hoping Capcom fleshes out the B scenario sometime in the future, but I'm not counting on it.

Fantastic game that brings "survival horror" back in a big way!  The gameplay is excellent, as are the graphics, and the story is so engrossing that even my mom watched through both Leon's and Claire's cutscenes put together into movie form on YouTube.  I have not really been a fan since the PS1 originals, but this game has really gotten me back into the world of Resident Evil.

That said, this is not for the more casual crowd.  For that crowd, buy Devil May Cry V (as I also did) and play it on the easiest setting.  You will feel like a God, striking down enemies in stylish fashion.  With Resident Evil 2, you will run.  You will hide.  You will sneak by.  You will catch your breath in save rooms.  You may run out of ammo and be totally helpless.  "Assisted Mode" helps out a lot, by having you regenerate a fraction of health, making aiming easier when zombie heads are bobbing, and generally making the game more bearable.  But there is a reason that it is not called "Easy Mode", because that mode doesn't exist.

My greatest criticism of this gem of a game revolves around the fact that to get all of the infinite ammo firearms, you are required to do things that a regular player like me just can't do, i.e. (for some weapons), play through the hardest difficulty in less than 2 1/2 hours while saving 3 or fewer times.  If you want to try again, you also have to load up a save, because "continue" still takes into account the time you spent before dying.  That is a slog, and no game should put infinite weapons behind a barrier so high.  (I ended up using WeMod and playing through to get the infinite weapons, and if that is the case, then this complaint drops away...but the game should not require this.  And console players cannot do this.)  For example, you should unlock one infinite gun for each character by simply completing a game without a time limit, and perhaps another gun could be unlocked even by dying when you have no ammo.  The reason is that it's the non-pro players who need more "help" and would appreciate the infinite ammo the most.  The more skilled players would likely scoff at using infinite ammo weapons, anyway.  For them, that S+ rank can be their trophy.  Also, I wish that head shots were more effective on zombies.  If you participate in game tournaments, then disregard this paragraph.  But this may be of use to some who don't.  And for those on PC, remember that there are mods and cheats (like WeMod) to help you out.  I did finish a campaign first.  And you should definitely get through the survival horror, to actually feel helpless and surrounded.  Then, after you have finished the story, you can always play again with some help.  

Even through there are some things that I believe could have been improved, there is a lot to love.  The game looks and plays great.  It is extremely engrossing.  I like the sense of accomplishment when you figure out a puzzle or solve a secret yourself.  I also like on the A playthrough that Mr. X isn't always around.  I didn't want a Resident Evil 3 experience of always being chased in Resident Evil 2.  And unlike some reviews out there, Mr. X only chases you through a small portion of the game (probably around 10%).  And that is a good percentage.  Just enough, but not too much.

I went on a few tangents, but let me get down to the brass tacks.  This game is superb.  If you are into survival horror at all, this is THE game to get.

RESIDENT EVIL 2's overall horror ambience is very well done, and some moments really made me jump. Sometimes things that you didn't expect at all happen here without a warning, which is horrifying if you are immersed in the game. A big part of the game is getting items without an explanation for them, or finding lockers or other similar things without having a use or solution for them immediately. Thus, you should always remember the rooms in which you found something that you could interact with, so that you don't have to run around the map without a clue afterwards. The game performs quite well from my experience, and has a great range of graphics settings, there are also different presets if you prefer using those. My only points of criticism are that you seem to be unable to adjust your volume ingame (unless you go into the settings menu and change the game's audio there). The best thing to do is to Alt+Tab to Steam and then adjust the volume. The other thing that I slightly disliked is that the sprinting and movement feels a bit strange at times, but that might be intentional, and isn't a big problem anyways. Overall I'd give this game a 9,5/10 and recommend it to almost anyone, no matter their skill level. The only types of person I wouldn't recommend it to are people with very low patience, people who have a problem with horror in general and children.

By far, one of the best Resident Evil games that has been released to date, and a faithful adaptation of its 1998 counterpart.  The gameplay is top-notch with excellent gun mechanics that actually make you feel the stress of trying to shoot an approaching zombie that shambles towards you ever so gradually.  Unlike the 1998 game, this game features an over-the-shoulder perspective similar to the more recent RE entries (i.e. Resident Evil 4, 5 and 6). It should also be noted that the enemies in this game take A LOT of ammo to put down, and while it's possible to fell a good portion of them in a single playthrough, for players looking to "speed-run" the game, your best bet is to simply shoot them in the leg to zip past them.

Your first playthrough of the game will probably take you about 8-10 hours, but the game requires multiple playthoughs in order to unlock the "true ending".  Whether you choose Leon or Claire for your first playthough will determine which sections of the game you will encounter, what enemies you will face, and also what weapons you will have at your disposal.  Leon's arsenal involves less initial firepower, but more ammunition, while Claire gets a grenade launcher pretty early in the game, but she'll receive less ammunition overall.  The side-characters in each character's story are also unique, with Claire coming to aid of a young girl named Sherry, while Leon works with the elusive Ada Wong.

All said, the game delivers a top-notch, bare-knuckle thrill ride that will keep your heart pounding from moment to moment,  There are few moments of respite in this game (outside of "save/safe" areas), and the knowing your way around is going to be paramount in order to get things done as efficiently as possible.  This is one of those rare gems that I think could truly earn a top score.  10/10

Is it resident evil? Yes

Is it resident evil 2? Yes

Is it exactly like resident evil 2? No

Is it difficult? It depends on your survival skill and how much you like to waste ammo shooting one zombie in the head with 3+ mags on standard mode.

Is it an action or survival? Both but slightly more so leaning towards action

Will it give your hardware a run for it's money? I have a pc that I built and is specs around the low end of high. This game eats it alive and then some, my gtx 1080 screams and the same goes with the i7 4770k. I can tell that this game was designed separately from the console version, and was specifically for a visceral environment and game play. 

Hows the audio? They offer several options from the basic speaker setup, to the 5.1 surround, to dolby atmos, to the more personal binaural headset style. The sound quality is designed to put you on the edge and at times in fear.

How's the game play? Its similar to resident evil 6 but way more refined and designed more so for corridors, mid to large foyers, and tight spaces. The traversal is exactly the same as the original resident evil 2 so expect a boatload of back tracking, puzzles, and item hunting.

How long is it? not sure at the moment. I haven't played Leon's game yet and I'm 8 hours deep in Claire's and  I'm heading back in to the parking garage to save someone.

Is there anything that you didn't like about it? Yes, Mr. X.  To me he comes off like a drunken overbearing parent, hell bent on beating you just because you are there. Keep in mind that if he hits you he will take out 2/3 of your health on standard mode. To be bluntly honest playing cat and mouse with something that can kill you in two hits, is not exactly fun. Personally I'd expect that sort of thing out of an action RPG than a survival/horror/action game. Furthermore I'm still debating on if I will play it again after Leon's game, I prefer a Insurmountable enemy than a "invincible" enemy.

Over all I think its a great game, but it does in my opinion have a few quirks that should have been ironed out before release. Well worth buying if you love the originals than the "originals" like resident evil 5 and 6.

I'll cut to the chase. This is easily a 10/10.

CONTROLS [9/10]
- Easy to grasp, first 15-20 mins is all you need to master the controls.
- Those that have played RE7 will feel right at home.
- Quick Turn (Q) does not seem to fully turn 180 degrees and leaves you instead of a vulnerable and awkward end position where you need to realign your aim.

GRAPHICS [10/10]
- RE Engine. What more can I say besides the game is horrifyingly gorgeous.
- I'm rockin a GTX 1050 4GB with 20GB RAM but still enjoyed consistent 60 FPS (given you have optimized the settings). Heaps of Youtube videos to help you with that.
- If you have a PC with awesome specs, definitely max everything up and enjoy the gory details.
- You can literally dismember zombies limb by limb. Too many amazing details of this game to mention.

SOUND [10/10]
- This game is best played with headphones. My goodness, the binaural (3D spatial) sounds on this game is absolutely terrifying. You can legit tell where all the groaning, screeching and growling noises are coming from. And do not get me started on Mr. X's footsteps. The sound design on that is PERFECT. It elevates an already tense situation and never lets up.
- The environment sounds are nothing short of amazing. It is so immersive and eerie.
- Voice acting is great. The protagonists have done well and their adlibs are great. The standouts for me were Chief Irons and Claire's "I'll get you, you f@cker!" line. I applaud the voice behind the lady zombies. No one's talking about her high-pitched screeches which is shockingly horrific when I first heard it.

MUSIC [7/10]
- Let's be honest. This can not hold a candle to the plethora of iconic themes the original RE2 has. If you want that experience, get the DLC that plays the audio from the original RE2 (This should've been free though).
- The only memorable music is Mr.X's theme when he's around. VERY memorable might I add.

GAMEPLAY [9/10]
- They have brought back survival-horror.
- Ammo is scarce. Care must be taken on when you need to fight or GTFO.
- The undead have a hard on for noise.
- Inventory management is easy.
- Puzzles can be challenging on your first playthrough. They are not easy but somehow not frustrating which is a good thing.
- Hide and seek mechanic is awesome.
- I finished both scenarios. I started with Leon, just like I did in the original RE2. I have read about people complaining there are not much differences between both scenarios. While I get what they say, it didn't really bother me. I enjoyed both scenarios specially the second one with its more satisfying ending. Can't wait to play again and start as Claire in Hardcore.


OVERALL EXPERIENCE [10/10]
- As someone who has played the original, I totally enjoyed seeing the environments and characters that are masterfully recreated in full detail. I like that it is not a 1:1 remake but more of a reimagining. For those that have not played the original RE2, don't fret. This is essentially how the original game is told with today's gaming technology.
- This is a highly tension-filled game and the reason why this formula is beloved by fans of the genre.

CLOSING THOUGHTS
- Back in 1998, I used to bug my older sister to buy me a Playstation and it's all because I saw my neighbor playing Resident Evil 2. I wanted to be able to experience playing as a pixelated cop shooting zombies. When I finally got my hands on it, it was by far the best gaming experience I have ever had. Almost 2 decades later, I am thrusted back to a city that I'm familiar with, characters that I know and love. It is like reuniting with an old friend.
- Definitely buy this solely for the experience. Turn the lights off, crank the volume up and grab some snacks. It's a really scary game so beware. It is hands-down one of the best games in 2019 and a happy (or shall I say, a welcome) return to survival horror.

[i] Plot [/i]
The game is quite different with the previous series. It brings back RE to its origin, more puzzle to solve without ignoring action as the main aspect (obviously in RE 5 & RE 6). The storyline also widely improved, not getting straight like RE 7 so the player has more option which task that could be their priority. [i] Graphic [/i]
Many CGI scenes looked incredibly realistic, the best-looked zombie I ever seen, very smooth and detailed move. Camera blending applied perfectly and the horror setting builds strongly, it deserves to win the best visual of the year.

[b] CONS [/b]

The safe room are too safe. No zombie could break the door and rushed in.

Player movement speed is relative slow, compared with the other series.

Lack of zombies, the quantity is the same in every difficulties.

Deluxe edition only adds main character appearance.
