.... at least for me personally and directly one of the ,,survival-horror,, bangers of the year.

Story:
The story corresponds to the Resident Evil 2 from 1998 and has introduced completely new cutscenes and levels besides the campaign. You start the game either with the well-known serial hero Leon S. Kennedy, or with Chris Redfield's sister Claire. Depending on who you end the game with first, you can do a so-called B-run with the other character,but its unluckily it runs not deeply into that....
As a fresh cop, Leon arrives in Raccoon City to discover that the city is overrun by undead. So he entrenches himself in the police station, where he was supposed to work as a policeman soon. There Leon is locked up and soon finds out that the police station is also haunted by undead and much worse people. Now only one thing counts: ESCAPE.
The story of Leon (and optionally Claire) is very nice and also has several exciting sections with highlights. The game builds up the tension right at the beginning and at the end you even uncover a whole conspiracy.
Also the B-Run with Claire is worth it. You explore similar areas in many parts, but the puzzles have been changed and there are other areas that you visit as Claire (for example the orphanage).

Graphic:
The graphic of Resident Evil 2 Remake looks absolutely great in direct comparison to the original. There is no fixed camera anymore, but a shoulder perspective, like Resi 5 and 6. There are a few washed-out textures, but they're barely noticeable due to the grandiose implementation of light, shadow, and the incredibly harmonious environments. The zombies didn't look better and more disgusting in any other game, especially if they've already gotten something from the player. The faces in the cutscenes look very credible and in general the game makes a very nice impression.

Gameplay:
As already mentioned above, Resident Evil 2 has developed into a good third person horror game. The gunplay is extremely pleasant and the impact on the zombies is clearly noticeable. In the levels themselves there are often several puzzles, which often seem a bit "out of place" (Who hides a secret access behind medallion puzzles in a police station?) but they were fun and tricky. And this aspect fits Resi anyway.
There are different types of enemies and some even require certain tactics to get rid of them, or even just to slow them down (yes, I mean you, Mr. X).
Resources are rare in the game, but you can find enough to make ends meet. It's often a good idea to just leave some undead and save the ammo for later.
Crafting and weapon modding is also part of the game and is a lot of fun. You can combine the different herbs and gain advantages.
The inventory is the same as in Resident Evil 7 and here I am already at my only point of criticism: All in all I could cope with the inventory size. You can also often find belt bags to expand this. But in some sections you are at the point where there was no storage box (to store items) for a long time and the inventory is simply full. Here you often have to decide what to throw away (which is permanently lost) and what to keep. It would be nicer if the "throw away" option was a "discard" function. Also due to the fact that you only have to bring some items from a point A to a point B five meters away and the characters can't hold this in their hands over this short distance.

Atmosphere:
That's insane. No other zombie game has ever created such a good end-time undead atmosphere as this one. The infected run across the corridors, everywhere it rumbles, something is behind the wall and from one point on you have a constant trudge in the whole police station. The music does the rest. It's been a while since I've been scaring myself for the last time in a game. Resident Evil 2 managed it.
Also the disgust factor by the zombies or some certain opponent types is simply perfect. No other game comes close to Resi.

Conclusion:
Resident Evil 2 Remake pretty much knocked me off my feet. Not only that it runs like butter, looks pretty good, no also the atmosphere and everything else. I bought the game spontaneously because the videos I saw shortly before the release looked really interesting. Without any expectations I experienced a huge surprise. Horror fans should definitely not miss this game!

[b]I should state that I do NOT talk about the story at all. I do however talk about gameplay mechanics and about 1 specific character.[/b]

[h1]Graphics[/h1]
This is one of the most realistic looking games I have ever played. The environments are extremely detailed, with each location having a distinct look [spoiler]e.g. the underground looks quite industrial, the NEST is a futuristic shiny white lab, the police station looks like an old museum (because it is)[/spoiler]. The human characters look absolutely amazing. Some of the best I've seen in a game before. [spoiler]Ada is the best looking character in my opinion[/spoiler]

[h1]Audio[/h1]
The sound in RE2 immersed me in the experience like no other game has, mostly due to the directional sound option. The noises that the different zombies make is creepy, the sound of the lickers' slow movements sends a shiver down my spine, and don't even get me started on the Tyrants dreaded footsteps. Some of the voice acting feels a little cheesy, but I just take it as part of the 1998 experience.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
The game requires the player to manage different materials and gear such as weapons, ammunition, healing items, and story related items. To collect everything some backtracking is required, but CAPCOM designed it in a way that you don't necessarily need to return to a location the same way you left it, so it doesn't get tedious and boring. The limited ammo means players have to pick and choose targets. Who can I safely avoid? Who do I want to kill to make return trips easier? I've had more than one occasion where I left enemies alive only to be overwhelmed later.

[h1]Good ol' Mr. X[/h1]
I love the Tyrant and hate it at the same time. No review can do justice to the amount of terror this monster instils in me. This is easily my favourite mechanic in the game. His almost never ending hunt for Human blood acts as a timer. The game lets players get used to the gameplay and layout of the map before throwing this horrific spanner in the works, requiring players to plan their route and think about how fast they can move and how quiet they can do it. Whenever his music theme starts playing I immediately start freaking the ♥♥♥♥ out.

[h1]1st and 2nd Runs[/h1]
The game has a feature where players can choose to play as either Claire Redfield or Leon S. Kennedy. Some story and item elements will differ depending on the chosen character. Then after after the game is finished, players can replay the game with the other character, with some alterations to item locations, puzzles and some story elements. I have a few issues with the logic behind this system, but I can look past it and just enjoy what has been changed.

Character and environment designs are top notch. Lots of intense moments, even further down the road when you've got yourself pretty well equipped. The basic stuff is like in any other RE game. You wander around the map unlocking new areas by finding keys or solving puzzles. Cleared rooms stay clear until certain events get triggered - then new enemies may appear in certain places. You gather weapons and modifications for them, mix herbs and create ammo from gunpowder.

Zombies are tougher than in other typical zombie games. The damage done to them isn't a set number, so you never know how many shots it will take to down one. This also becomes modified based on your gameplay, kinda like in RE7. Headshots, damage wise, are treated the same way as body shots with the addition of a chance of blowing the zombie's head off.

After finishing the game once you can do a second run with the other character to get the true ending. Other than a different starting area and a slightly shorter and modified trip through the police station, the rest of the game basically stays the same. The original had a little more to the second run than the remake has which is slightly disappointing.

There are also some additional modes, where you play as different characters but these have little to no story. They're purely about the gameplay and can be treated as challenge modes.

The game is well worth the money.

The Resident Evil 2 remake was perhaps the biggest surprise of the year, seeing as it's a remake and all that. Whether you're talking movies, tv-shows or videogames, it's not often you see a remake of something that not only manages to live up to the original, but also far surpass it. While the original is a good game in it's own right it's certainly also an aged game and one that's likely to not really go down all that well with todays gamers due to it's tank controls, fixed camera angles and dated 3D graphics.

That's where RE2: Remakes comes in and becomes not only one of the best survival horror games of the decade, but also one of the best games of the year.

RE2: Remake takes everything that was great about the original and puts a modern spin on it, and it does it really well. The tank controls are largely gone which makes both maneuvering and aiming a whole lot  easier, and with the camera now following behind the player rather than being stuck at fixed angles you feel like you're more in control of both your character and your surroundings.

One might think that having more control would make the game less scary, but Remake is plenty scary. The modern (and quite frankly exceptional) graphics makes the gameworld feel and look far scarier and creepier than the original ever could, and they help in building up an excellent atomsphere that manages to keep the player on edge while throwing in some spooks and scares here and there to frighten the player. Even when you think you've cleared an area of zombies there's this constant feel that something's gonna happen, which keeps you alert and from letting your guard down. Which is exactly what a horror game should do. 

It's not just graphics and world-building either. The sound department knew what they were doing and if you play with headphones or use some kind of surround system the sound will do a good job of keeping you on edge. Especially when you encounter a certain enemy that wanders around a lot you'll find yourself stopping to listen to try and figure out where he is and if he's coming for you. 

As you  play you'll find that you have limited resources (ammo, healing items etc.), and you have to be careful not to use up too much ammo which further lends to the great atomsphere and sense of panic and fright that you'll experience throughout the game. You end up having to think twice about finishing of a zombie or just leaving them alive so that you can save your bullets for a tougher threat. Having to keep track of your resources add another layer to the "survival-horror" part of it all, and it's a part that's completely up to you to control. If you run completely out of ammo it's your own fault and you need to plan better and think ahead so that it doesn't happen again. 

Story-wise it's pretty good. Whether you play as Leon or Claire, you find yourself in the zombie-infested Raccoon City and have to find a way out. As you play you'll meet new characters and uncover the deeper plot and the truth behind the zombies in a mixture of gameplay and cinematics. It's nothing groundbreaking or anything, but it works and it works well. It's been 10+ years since I played the original so I can't really remember how accurate the story of Remake is to the original, but I feel almost as if it doesn't matter because what you get is good and does a great job of hooking you in and wanting to see what happens next. 

To get the full story you have to do multiple playthroughs which is something that can be a drag in most games, but not here because the second playthrough will follow a different character with their own stuff happening throughout the story. The second playthrough will come with it's own boss-battles, characters and information that further explains the plot and what's been happening in Raccoon City, so there's a ton of incentive to do that second playthrough. The option to do a hardcore playthrough, which makes enemies tougher and gives you limited savefiles, can also further incentivize you to give the game another playthrough if for no other reason than to challenge yourself. 

In short, Resident Evil 2 Remake is a great game, and a contender to being the game of the year. It's polished, has very few (if any) issues, sells the survival horror well and makes for an excellent and thrilling adventure throughout the zombie-ridden Raccoon City. If you like survival horror games it's a must play, and if you just like running around shooting zombies it's a fun time as well. One might think that it would stand under the shadow of the original and not be able to rise above it, as is common for remakes, but RE 2: Remake manages to not only rise above the original but surpass it by such a long shot that it sets a completely new bar for all future Residentl Evil games. It's truly one of the greatest games of this year and might very well also be the best Resident Evil game to date.

tl;dr at the bottom
------------
First, a bit of a story.
Back in the 90's, when I was too young to be playing horror games, my parents rented Resident Evil 2 for the PlayStation 1 from Blockbuster because they loved Romero zombie films. However neither of them could figure out how to fire their pistol and kept dying to the first zombie. I then asked if I could give it a try. 
Exasperated, they handed me the controller. It took me about 20 minutes of trial and error before I managed to make it to the gunshop, relatively unscathed. 

And that was how I began playing my very first M-rated video game.

My point is the original Resident Evil 2, released way back in 1998, holds a lot of strong nostalgia for me. I adored that game so much that I collected almost every future release and even read the book adaptations at the library. I fell in love with the series and was very proud to have beaten Resident Evil 2 100%; I had beaten both A and B versions of both characters and unlocked every weapon in the game, even conquering the notorious Hunk and Tofu modes.

So I was pretty nervous with RESIDENT EVIL 2 REMAKE.
Would it do the original justice? Would it feel the same? Would it be a completely different beast altogether?
Would it respect the source?

Thankfully RESIDENT EVIL 2 *does* respect its source material, and actually manages to greatly improve upon it.

Despite the perspective shifting from old school tank controls to a third person action camera the remake still FEELS like original Resident Evil 2, dripping with suspense and terror lined with an oppressive and dark atmosphere. There's a heavy sense of realism despite the over-the-top plot and crazy action elements, yet it avoids the problems of its predecessors; the action is certainly a spectacle, but doesn't detract from its survival horror core. You still feel like you're fighting for your life, and barely winning (even on the easier difficulties).

RESIDENT EVIL 2 still follows the same basic plot beats of the original, but rearranges and even reinterprets a lot of elements. I saw a lot of familiar characters, but found them to be very fresh with brand new performances and even updated motivations and dialogue. Rooms, key locations, and enemy behaviours have all slightly changed, not so much that they're unrecognizable but enough that nothing feels copy-pasted...for the most part.
Having played the original up and down, front to back and sideways, I actually recognized a few setups for a surprise scare. I'm not saying it's a bad thing to reuse iconic scares from the original, but personally I found they sucked a little of the tension out for me. Don't get me wrong, there are plenty of original scares in the remake, but it was very weird being the bravest one of my friends to play this game (especially since I'm a massive scaredy cat when it comes to horror games).

I guess this isn't really a game review, and more of a love letter to Capcom for not screwing up this remake. They honestly didn't need to develop RESIDENT EVIL 2 REMAKE, but I'm sure glad they did. They could have made the original an HD port and released it quickly, but this game feels like genuine passion and care was put in by the dev team. 
An excellent reinterpretation and the closest thing to a perfect survival horror game I've played in a long long time.

Please pick up this game, you won't regret it.

+Beautifully captures feelings of terror, tension, and suspense of not only the original Resident Evil 2 but old school survival horror games without falling victim to negative tropes

+Still feels like original Resident Evil, but won't leave newcomers hanging

After over a decade of unrequited requests from fans, Capcom has finally answered our calls and delivered an amazing remake that both captures what made the original great, while also feeling fresh at the same time. Much like its predecessor, REmake2 is a finely crafted survival horror experience with an emphasis on resource management and puzzle solving (also of course the genre's infamous backtracking). Unlike its predecessor, however, is a return of the third person over the shoulder perspective as seen from the series' installments over the past decade; which in this case blends well with the classic formula by making the enemies tougher to put down, especially the zombies. All in all, this remake does the original justice by being one of the new best in the series, and is a great place for new players to enter the world of survival horror for the first time.

I wanted to make sure I played the original before making my final review of this game. After playing through a decent portion of the original RE2 on the playstation 1 I have my final thoughts.

Pros:
The game is a spitting image of the original game with only 1 real major difference (that I noticed) and the rest being minor enemies being removed or visual changes.
The game looks horrible, in the best sense of the word. every dirty blood soaked room feels like its been looked over personally many times by a designer to ensure it looks as good as possible and builds the atmosphere as it should.
Enemy design is out of this world, with new technology rendering old favorite designs such as William Birkin's mutated body shambling down halls screaming out at you becoming more grotesque each time you see him.
The story holds up fantastically today showing everyone that Resident Evil doesn't have to cover up bad storytelling with explosions and giant worm Weskers to be good.
A wide selection of voiced languages including (English, Spanish, German, Japanese, and more).
The availability of using the original sounds and music to get even closer to the original game.
Includes even more bonus content than the original which includes (HUNK and TOFU) from the original but also includes several new stories exclusive to this game.

Cons:
The original soundtrack and sounds are locked behind dlc which i feel they should be free.
Sometimes it can be difficult to tell how damaged enemies are (less of a problem in bosses where there are changes to show their damage).

Final Score:
5/5 (Get this game)

This is the game that made me understand why people seem to dislike RE6 so much when I've always thought it's perfectly serviceable if a bit too generic. RE2 proves to me that it is entirely possible to have a modern third person action shooter (without all of RE4 and RE5's jankiness) and still create a horror game atmosphere, through strategic placement of critical items (you're always short on ammo, but rarely truly out of them, making ammo conservation important but not a total frustration if you're methodical and conservative enough), great way to integrate shooter mechanics without making it too action-feeling (you have to stand still for a second or so before your aim is stable enough to make a good shot, but you can move while aiming, if you so choose), and good use of Mr. X (OK I'll admit he is very annoying when you are trying to get some puzzle solving done, especially when you get hounded into running into a Licker hallway, but that's kind of the point isn't it?).

I wanted to write a short review just for the Steam Award thing ,turns out I have a lot to say about this game xD 

Resident evil 2 is an almost faithful recreation/re-imagining of the classic game of the same name that came out way back in 1998. You don't need to play the first one to get what's going on . For the few things it gets wrong about the classic it does many many things right, It is the the new standard in survival horror games that other developers should stride to achieve. 

It features two playable protagonists Claire & Leon on their intersecting quests to escape the dying Raccoon city due to the T-Virus outbreak. Claire's writing excels while sticking close to her character in the original game. A grounded and a relatable character motivation and actions. However, Leon's stumbles a bit in the typical videogame/movie be the hero , do the right thing clichés. Both things can be said about several other characters in the game that were rewritten to be more interesting or more cliches that I won't spoil here. 

Luckily,  The game play is were Resident evil 2 shines. The game is played from the third person perspective which angered lot of fans but having played the game ,this was the right decision. You control both Leon and Claire to escape the city by solving puzzles and defeating enemies while managing your short and few resources of ammo and health items. The game also includes several bosses and re-occurring ones that you will have to content with. *massive foot step sounds*  

The very detailed horrific & grotesque hallways of the police station where the game first takes place is a marvel to behold. Capcom did a terrifyingly great job in revamping the game to bring it to the modern age. Never before I have seen such detailed zombie facial animation , movement & reaction to each of your shots. Even limbs can be severed so realistically it's pretty impressive. That goes for all other enemies in the game which also I won't be going in details in fear of spoilers.   

Capcom has been doing a great job lately. I really love and appreciate everyone who contributed to greenlight & develop this game with so much obvious love and care as this is one of my favorite childhood games. Also , Capcom released a sequel to Devil may Cry which also received similar love and care. Clearly, Capcom has listened to it's fans.

Story: 7/10 (some of the character motivations weren't really believable)
Gameplay : 9/10 (Can't really see anything bad with it except the lack of a free camera mode which is me just nitpickin)
Graphics : 10/10
Sound: 10/10 
Replayability : 8/10 ( you got four campaigns for the main story, some plot holes when comparing them which is why I took away some points , several unlockable mini stories)

Rating overall : 9/10

Resident Evil 2 is a great return to the Survival Horror genre and back to its original root where the game can be terrifying when you have to manage your inventory space with very limited ammo you have. Not only that is that every room you enter, you're never safe as zombies are everywhere and they won't hesitate to swarm you if you're not careful in your surroundings. You'll also face other mutations that can be deadlier than the usual zombies. What makes this game so good is that it is a remake to the second Resident Evil game, which is regarding as the best in the whole franchise. Not only this game looks insanely good, but also captures the essence of the original game, which hardcore fans will easily recognize iconic moments based from it.

Gameplay wise, it plays like the newer Resident Evil games in a Third person perspective and no tank control, which thank goodness they didn't stick with that. Certain weapons have their pros and cons and are very useful in certain situations so it's best to not use up all the ammo on one zombie. You might want to save it later for much bigger battles. The safe room also makes a return and it pretty much functions the same, where you store items and save your game. The save system is unlimited unless you play it in Hardcore Mode, which makes you use the classic Ink Ribbons to save your game.

The stoyline is identical to the original game, but the only different is that the cutscenes look really good in the new RE Engine and some slight changes in the Remake. But I think Capcom nailed the overall atmosphere and sound design of the game as like I said, this game will keep your guard up as the zombies are terrifying and could pop out anywhere and anytime.  

The biggest question is that... Is this a good Resident Evil game? Oh hell yeah! I highly recommend you get this game, even if you're not a Resident Evil fan or have never played the game before, this is a good start in getting into the Resident Evil Franchise as well as the Survival Horror genre. Let's cross fingers that Capcom makes a Resident Evil 3 Remake and perhaps Dino Crisis in the near future.

A re-imagining of the original game from 1998, Resident Evil 2 is a survival horror game that focuses on the stories of Leon Scott Kennedy and Claire Redfield as they escape a viral outbreak in Raccoon City.

I believe CAPCOM poured a lot of love into this remake, and it shows. Graphics are crisp and look fantastic, with a lot of options for customization. Sound design is very good. Considering they no longer had fixed camera angles to hide threats that may be around corners, they had to rely on other ways to scare the player such as the horrific zombie screams and other enemy noises, or fainter ambient sounds in the distance.

There are 2 main scenarios to play, each with their own objectives and character interactions. Play as Leon, the rookie cop arriving to Raccoon City for his first day on the job, or Claire, a college student looking for her brother, Chris, who was a member of the special tactics and rescue team for the Raccoon City Police. Meeting by chance near the beginning, they are separated and each must fight through the viral outbreak to escape the city. In addition to the main scenarios, there are also secondary scenarios, 1 for each character, that will change certain elements of the game including some item placements, puzzle solutions, and enemy placements, and are required to see the true ending. Exploration is rewarded with more backstory and extra resources such as ammuntion, healing items, and stronger weapons. For a greater challenge, there are hardcore difficulties which will further increase enemy threat and change some enemy placements, as well as decreased ammo and item pickups, making you be much more conservative about which enemies to deal with and which to leave alone. Even the basic zombie enemies can be a threat if they're given the chance.

For replay value, the game has unlockables to obtain by finishing the scenarios with a fast time and good rank, such as extra costumes for the main characters, infinite ammuntion weapons, and artwork from the game's development. There are also numerous mods for the game, including item randomizers which can further add replay value even to the most experienced player. There are a few short extra modes, which tell "what if" stories of some more minor side characters of the story.

Fantastic contemporary rendition of a 90s classic. Absolute must play for old schoolers and newcomers alike.

My sole complaint is that implementing elements of the original's B scenarios into the remake's A scenarios was a mistake. From a story point of view, there's little reason to replay the game with another character because A & B for either character now feels exactly the same.

[b]The good:[/b] An exceptional and bold remake that respects and builds upon the legacy of Resident Evil 2. Enemies - even standard zombies - are dangerous. The atmosphere is frightening, gloriously rendered, and claustrophobic. The sounds, visceral and nerve-wracking, complete the experience. Blood and gore are plentiful, but never gratuitous. 

The difficulty, especially on hardcore, is high: this is refreshing, given how AAA games in general have been relentlessly dumbed-down. You must control your nerves while destroying or avoiding vicious monsters; ammunition is limited and scattered. If it's all too much; the casual, easy mode lessens the strain.

The characters and dialogue are much-improved on the original, yet the signature RE cheesiness is rightly preserved. The protagonists, villains and other characters feel human, and the tone of the story is mature when compared to previous RE games with outsized evildoers and action sequences. The scenes contain actors in motion-capture rendering; they're studio-shot and intricate, facial emotions and all. Aided by this production, the tragedy of Raccoon City carries a horrific sheen of believability.

Unlockable minigames and items, plus completionist tasks lengthen the game's life. In all, there's 20 to 30 hours of top quality gameplay here. Now that RE:2R is regularly on sale, it's brilliant value. A decent PC is required to display the game in its fullest, scariest glory, but settings can be customized. Longtime fans will be pleased by various Easter eggs and nods to series lore; time was taken, the game released with very few bugs, and its patches mostly added extra material.

[b]The bad:[/b] The B scenarios could have been structured better to accord with the continuity of the A scenarios, but nothing is perfect. Saying this feels close to nitpicking, given how superb the game is overall.

[b]Summary:[/b] The reaction to RE2:Remake consisted of near-universal praise and gratitude for what is a dramatic display of form. Now we abide, hoping that lightning strikes twice; that Capcom produce a heart-thumping, tentacled RE3 remake equal in caliber to this superb piece of entertainment.

[b]Advice for new players:[/b] Play in total darkness wearing headphones, and choose hardcore difficulty. Try not to consult guides, tab out or break the immersion; the satisfaction from completing this game using your own wit and grit is palpable. After all...

[i]"This is war...survival's your responsibility."[/i]

This game is fantastic - a surprise knockout, and a true return to form from games developer Capcom. Between this, Devil May Cry 5, and Mega Man 11, it's been high times for fans like me.

However, you don't have to be a long-standing fan to enjoy this one. The Resident Evil 2 remake stands on its own, offering a well-executed fusion of solid old-school mechanics and modern sensibilities. While it doesn't *replace* the original PS1/DC/N64/Every-other-platform-ever Resident Evil 2, it's a fine, fine game in its own right. It deftly undoes the faults embedded by RE4 and the games that followed it. Gone are the horrible writing, characters, and cut-rate anime storytelling. There's some cheese here, sure, but the only time I cringed the entire game was after seeing what a shotgun does to a zombie's torso point-blank.

Speaking of that, there's much visceral satisfaction to be had here. Combat is suspenseful, punchy, and full of carnage. The game's theme is dark, adrenaline-soaked horror, and it pulls that off with aplomb. While the game encourages you to run when you can and shoot only when you absolutely have to, there's plenty of room to cut loose, and when you do it's very, very satisfying.

The game looks great, but even better than that, it sounds freaking incredible. The soundscape is just plain terrifying - you *feel* like you're plodding around an actual, factual man-made structure, and you can just hear the stresses in the floorboards. Every sound, every little bump and scrape and thump in the background carries with it a palpable weight, a sense of grisly death closing in all around you.

The UI is refined to near perfection. Shortcuts make swapping weapons in real-time snappy and natural, and the inventory interface is no longer a chore to manage. Weapons and equipment show up on your characters which in my book is a huge plus.

Gameplay wise, RE2 is a survival horror game at its heart, as it should be. On higher difficulties, you are squishy and very vulnerable. There are no magic karate kicks to save you if you make a mistake, and every encounter threatens your rapidly-dwindling resources. Subweapons like knives and flashbang grenades can get you out of a bad situation, but if you use 'em you lose 'em (well, technically, you can yank the knife back out, though the zombie you stuck it in might want to keep it).

Easier difficulties allow you a more relaxed experience, if that's your thing (I'm not judging, it's cool), but for those who really want to feel the stress, Hardcore mode lives up to its name. It's not brutally difficult or even particularly over-the-top, but the struggle *is* very satisfying. Just like the good old days. More than once, this game had me saying to myself "God, I'd never survive this. I'd just lay down and give up. I'd be so done." I was genuinely glad I'm not Leon Kennedy. Props to the guy, though. What a nightmare.

Shortcomings? Well, for those fans of the original, you lose out on the unique "zapping" mechanic that emulated a single, side-by-side playthrough in which events in one character's story would directly change what happens in the second run. The remake offers a second run, with different events, but your prior choices have no effect on how it plays out. Little bit of a bummer (big bummer, actually), but it doesn't take a point off the score or anything, so to speak.

Also, the combat mechanics are fine for the first few playthroughs, but once you "get good" and figure it out, the combat alone won't bring you back. The additional survivor stories will, however, because surviving that kind of pain takes a lot more finesse than resource management. Still, it would have been nice to have RE3's timing-based dodge mechanics. I loved that. Maybe it'll make a comeback in the RE3 remake...?

So, yeah, at the time of this writing, this game is twenty bucks. I bought it full price and I don't regret a thing. Highly recommended for fans and non-fans alike. There's a lot to like here, and even plenty to love (Leon is hot, no ♥♥♥♥). This is a straight-up phenomenal horror experience, whichever way you look at it. Remember, though - it's not for the faint of heart. The game doesn't rely on cheap, unavoidable "BOO!" jumpscares, but the atmosphere will keep you in a state of constant dread. When something bad does happen, you will probably make embarrassing sounds as you struggle to run away. This may or may not cause those around you to think less of you. You have been warned.

Oh, and the combat is quite nasty. I for one consider this a super-positive, but if you're squeamish about violence, there's your fair warning. If you're like me, there's your wink-wink-nudge-nudge advertisement.

[h1]Resident Evil / Biohazard 2 Remake[/h1]
[b]5/5 - Do you know that feeling when you are super hyped about a game and somehow it goes above and beyond everything you thought it would be? No? I definitely do![/b]

One of the biggest hits of 2019, Resident Evil 2 Remake is a great entry for fans and first timers alike. With an incredible audiovisual performance, finely tuned gameplay and a rock-solid PC version, RE2 leaves almost nothing to be desired (RE3 Nemesis Remake cough"cough"...).

+ Stunning audiovisual experience delivers a massively dense and rich atmosphere.
+ Super stable PC version leaves us only monsters to deal with, no bugs or performance issues.
+ PC features like Ultrawide aspect ratio and high framerates are supported.
+ Nice array of difficulty levels with different mechanics.
+ Superb soundtrack and the (paid) option to use the original classic bgm and sfx.
+ It builds a lot on top of the classic, so even if you've already played it on PSX, you won't actually know what to expect, everything is familiar but different.
+ It's a full game for once! Even though there are a few paid skins and stuff, all of the game is available on the standard edition.
+ Steam family sharing works as it should.

- Some post game activities can be a little frustrating
- Unfortunately, some skins and the old soundtrack are available only as DLC
- The story could have been better, but honestly, it does the job just right.

As someone who loves watching Resident Evil speedruns this was a great introduction to Resident Evil 2. The game stays faithful to the things I've watched in numerous speedruns while changing things up to make it a unique experience. 

While it's very reminiscent of how Resident Evil 7 works it actually builds upon that and makes Racoon City PD a very vivid place to be. As someone who loves an atmospheric game this ticked all the right boxes and the tension built further when faced with the challenge of facing a Licker or Mr X. 

A big difference of course is that Resident Evil 2 remake is a 3rd person game. You could claim that this could detract from the gameplay somewhat. Using the camera controls to peek around corners removing some of the tension. If the game had been in first person I feel like this could have provided a much more immersive experience and truly added to the horror. I feel hardcore fans of the series may be a little sad as they've ditched fixed camera points and tank controls but the fluidity of movement just makes it much more fun to play. 

Overall a pretty enjoyable game and one that actually lived up to the hype and the massive marketing campaign that Capcom funded. I highly recommend it.

Resident Evil 2 is a near-perfect re imagining of the 1998 PS1 original. It has been updated with RE4-style over the shoulder third person controls and modern visuals and sensibilities, adding to the world while remaining faithful to its roots. 

The game is dripping in atmosphere with great art, sound and game play design almost across the board. Weapons are fun to use and are well balanced, with each having its use cases and weaknesses. Puzzles are generally pitched at the right level, generally serving to prompt planning of journeys through dangerous territory rather than posing a real cerebral challenge in and of themselves. Enemies are well designed and pose a good amount of threat, increased by expanding on sound elements present in the original. By the time zombies become trivial to dispatch the game introduces Mr. X who is a constant menace for much of the game. Instead of just killing zombies in your path there is the added element of gunfire drawing the much more threatening Tyrant, forcing the player to not get complacent even with weaker enemies. 

One negative point is that the A-B scenario system isn't quite as deep as in the original, with the B scenarios being more stand-alone rather than feeling like another part of the story occurring in parallel. Despite this there is still a lot of replayability with an initial scenario A playthough typically taking around 10-12 hours. Since release Capcom have added in a free update called Ghost Survivors mode which are short, action-packed scenarios typically taking no more than 15 minutes to finish. Both the Ghost Survivors and main game modes have unlockables which are gated behind achievements of varying difficulty. Achievements are used to good effect, challenging the player to complete the game in particular ways such as without healing or using a storage box. It being 2019, of course the option to unlock everything by paying a fee has been added, which does cheapen the experience a bit.

Overall this is a very good game which I highly recommend.

An amazing remake of the classic Resident Evil 2. Capcom once again steps things up when it comes to remaking their games. The graphics are the best yet from the RE Engine, fairly easy to run a smooth 60fps on a variety of hardware, as the engine is very scalable. Since the game was designed for consoles which already target 60fps, the PC version benefits from that engine scalability. Character models, lighting, etc. are top notch work, with only a few issues such as artifacting  and dithering on some light/shadow sources.

The developers did a great job of marrying old school design and mechanics with the new school. The camera is no longer static and pre-set like the original, but rather behind the shoulder that has become the norm of third person shooters, which was popularized by Resident Evil 4. They also adapted newer mechanics from the newer RE games, like having defensive items to release yourself from an attacker's grasp. The map is hugely improved from past RE games and conveys clearer information, keeps track of things you have to investigate, and makes the next objective fairly clear, making it more difficult to get lost. Just like the original, the game has extra modes and items you can unlock after finishing the main game, giving it extra replay value for those looking for more.

The game is not a one to one remake of the original RE2, they redid alot of scenes and took some new liberties with the story and how the events play out. The overall story remains more or less the same compared to the original. With that said, there are some changes that I'm not a fan of that I think the original did better. The 2nd Run scenario, which is where you can replay the game in a slightly truncated path with items and enemies moved around, feels like an afterthought to the "B" scenario of the original RE2. It feels incomplete, as if they had bigger plans but ultimately decided to scrap those ideas. I'm also not a fan of some of the choices they made with the story characters and some of the content that was cut from the original "B" scenario of RE2, which I won't post here for spoilers sake. While a new player will not notice these changes at all, I think a veteran of RE2 will pick up on these changes immediately

Overall, I highly recommended it if you played the RE and RE0 Remaster HD and want to continue the story of the series.

Resident Evil 2. The original released way back in 1998, and I only recently played the original to get myself ready for the remake. Solid game, 8/10.

Jump all the way to 2019. After a couple of missteps into making Resident Evil more accessible by taking the action all the way up the notch, they eased up a little and they finally delivered on the RE2 Remake clamoured for so long ago. Is it worthy of holding the Resident Evil 2 name?

For the most part, yes. This game captures the spirit of RE2 to a tee. It's not a 1:1 remake that the RE Remake was with some added stuff to make it the superior version. There's some slight missteps in the fact that the characters who had development in the original game, somehow feel worse in the remake. Leon is now hopelessly naive rivalling that of a child, Chief Irons loses any subtlety at all, Ada comes off as more cold and is responsible for one of the dumbest lines in video game history ( [spoiler] "It's secret weapon time." Who at Capcom let that one through? [/spoiler]). Annette is somehow less sympathetic in this as well, and comes off as even more uncaring for her daughter? Anyways, I doubt anyone is here for the story. What's the gameplay like? 

Well, it's pretty good. It's got the RE4 angle, but that's all there is in common. Each zombie feels like a huge threat, which feels like a far cry from RE6. Most of the weapons feel like crap though, thanks to the game's adaptive difficulty brought over by RE7. (Spark Shot and Flamethrower are buffed tremendously though from the original) However, this only adds to the survival horror element. Unlike RE4, the adaptive difficulty only serves to make the game harder (which is why that zombie takes 10-20 shots to kill late game when it took 2 to kill in the early game). This also goes to make the early G1 boss fight to be a slog to get through when you don't have any real power weapons in A scenario for both characters. RNG also seems to be at a higher play here for enemies, since no two playthroughs will yield the exact same attacks by enemies (I.e. getting grabbed by a Licker versus just getting hit outright). You also take way less hits than you could in the original, making it more proactive to evade enemies or not get hit. The movement is very fluid unlike the original tank control scheme, and all the better for it, making juking a bit more of an active effort this time around. Inventory slots can be increased, however this is capped for Hardcore mode, which is a bit iffy but understandable. Mr. X is now a stalker similar to that of Nemesis in RE3 but he is much less annoying than that stupid thing (People complaining about Mr. X have obviously never played RE3, and you also don't have to fight him to get better stuff). He also appears in all of Leon's and Claire's campaign (He was previously limited to Scenario B in the original). Yes, he's a nuisance after the first couple of times he appears, but he is a fine addition to the game for the most part (Only bearable when you have the song associated with him, you know the one). Standard difficulty has an unlimited amount of saves at typewriters, which can be a turn off for some people, but don't worry, Hardcore has you covered by bringing ink ribbons back, and also making the game hard too while you're at it. 

Graphics look nice, everyone got a nice facelift, and '98 Leon and Claire are available for the nostalgia. The gore on the zombies looks unreal at times, this is much more brutal than in '98.

Soundtrack is alright, but classic one is better (obviously). Dumb that you have to pay for it though.

Be warned that Scenarios A and B vary very little in story changes, unlike in the original. Scenario B gives you a better handgun and it's own special ammo, but that's it, and it's slightly harder than Scenario A. [spoiler] You also kill G5 but that's such a short addition it feels unnecessary for it to be exclusive to Scenario B [/spoiler] The story pans out the same, which is disappointing to say the least. Don't buy this expecting different story beats like in the original. 4th Survivor and Tofu Survivors are back (Never did beat the original ones) for those guys that like it. 

Overall, it's a very solid game that does the RE2 name justice for the most part. Not exactly GOTY or 10/10 material, but it's close. Get it on a sale though, preferably the Deluxe Edition for that classic RE2 soundtrack that makes it much better. Also there's mods for this game, since everybody knows that Mr. X is gon' give it to ya.

Resident Evil 2 was a well-anticipated remaster of a late 90s classic survival horror game that helped shape the genre we know and love today. While some may see the remastering of the game as tainting the legacy of the original with its modern twists that Resident Evil 4 grounded many years ago for the future of the series, many people like myself see it as an exciting new way of experiencing the game from a new perspective.

[h1]The Story[/h1]
The game allows you to play through a specific story for both protagonists; Leon Kennedy, a rookie Raccoon City officer on his first day on the job, or Claire Redfield, a college student looking for her brother Chris, a protagonist of the first game. Both stories divert into their own plot, with the unchosen character appearing in certain situations to provide a connection and interaction with you while the story progresses. Leon follows after the mysterious Ada Wong, while Claire protects the innocent school girl Sherry. Both characters are fighting to survive and escape the city while on the run from numerous monstrosities created by the Umbrella Corporation that lurk in the overtaken city, some more persistent than others. After completing the story, you're allowed to play through the 2nd character's story, though it's only slight changes to if you played as them first instead. Although the game is based off the story from the original game, the differences between both characters' scenarios, along with the A and B scenarios, are underwhelming in providing a unique story experience for replay value.

[h1]The Gameplay[/h1]
Unlike the fixed camera angles of its original counterpart, this remaster uses the over-the-shoulder third person perspective that's been used in all Resident Evil titles (save for the 7th game) since the 4th installment. While some may dislike this change for altering the mechanics of the original, I don't really mind it, as it provides that new perspective of the game and this control style is a lot more fluid and precise. On the topic of the game's character scenarios once more, the "A scenario" (1st run as selected character) and "B scenario" (2nd run as the other character) have somewhat different functionalities when it comes to items. A scenario has ammunition scattered about for your starting weapon, while B scenario provides ammo for an alternative weapon you receive at the beginning, with ammo for your starting weapon being scarce and having to be created manually from gunpowder that's also around the map. Both scenarios between characters aren't that different in this remaster, with barely any noticeable changes such as these, though the pacing is similar to the original B scenario that has different item placement and progression. If you prefer a more classic and more difficult experience, hardcore mode is for you, with enemies dealing more damage and saves being limited to the classic ink ribbons around the map.

[h1]Mr. X[/h1]
I thought I'd create a completely different section for this enemy since he's an iconic piece of this remaster. Mr. X is a mass-produced variation of the Tyrant, being programmed to commands given by Umbrella. X's commands in this game are to eliminate any survivors in Raccoon City at all costs, primarily Leon and Claire. Instead of scripted sequences where he appears like in the original version of the game, he will wander around and tail you constantly throughout sections of the game, being sensitive to any noise you may make. Memes aside, X is a force to be reckoned with when he starts inevitably following you, only stopping to wander once more if you stun him for a short time from damage or if you manage to run far enough to lose him, so watch your back and keep an eye on your volume control when moving around the Raccoon Police Department.

[h1]The Modes[/h1]
After completing both A and B scenarios, a new mode will unlock known as "The 4th Survivor", telling the story of infamous Umbrella mercenary Hunk, who needs to make haste to his extraction point from the sewer in order to deliver a G-Virus sample to his benefactors, being faithful to the original game. While this mode is simple, it is quite difficult, having to bee-line straight to the front of the police station, having to take alternate routes from obstacles blocking you. Along with this, many of the difficult enemies appear from later in the game, with the dreaded Mr. X following you for some time and zombies being obstacles in your way. After completing this, you unlock "Tofu Survivor", another nod to its predecessor, where you go through the same scenario as Hunk, but as a block of tofu. While this sounds goofy, it's much more difficult than before, with Tofu only wielding limited healing items and a ton of knives for defense. Along with completing this, you're granted new Tofu modes that are new to this game, all having different weapon/health load-outs and personalities, providing new ways of challenging the player.

[h1]The DLC[/h1]
Shortly after the game's release, Capcom released the Ghost Survivors DLC, which is free. This DLC followed non-canon scenarios of characters featured in the story, along with a brand new character. Each story has an objective to complete, and providing an alternate scenario for the character's fate. Despite the cheap price of being free, many players and fans, like myself, found it to be underwhelming and slightly disappointing. The stories, while interesting in concept, just aren't that appealing when it comes to gameplay, especially due to not being canon. Other free DLC that was later released was once again, another nod for fans of the original, being costumes that are the original low-poly models from the original PlayStation 1 release. Paid DLC, however, is also included, though only cosmetic, such as alternate costumes for Leon and Claire (one of which is a reference to the unfinished original version of RE2) and a soundtrack modification, providing the fan-favorite music pieces from the classic.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Taking all this into account, Resident Evil 2 (2019) was a well-anticipated remaster of a survival horror classic that did its best to be unique and innovative from its 1998 predecessor, while also doing its best not to alienate fans of the original games to provide an enjoyable experience for old and new fans alike.

RESIDENT EVIL 2 was already a legendary game, being what cemented Capcom's survival horror franchise on the map of long-running video game series, so a remaster felt all but inevitable somewhere along the line of success for the company and for the ongoing development of video game technology. 

But Capcom went further...instead of merely a remaster, this version of RE2 functions as a complete remake. It is it's own game, combining the best of what made the Resident Evil franchise so exciting and fun for fans for the past twenty years since it's original iteration was released. It even takes cues (of course) from Resident Evil 4, the greatest of the series, but also 5 and 6, the less stellar but similarly innovative sequels that moved the series further and further away from it's roots. 

The RE2 remake isn't just a great game in it's own right, being frightful, fun, and challenging. It is a clarion call to all developers that remakes and remasters can be works of art in their own right, instead of just cash grabs and nostalgia bait pick-me-ups. It's almost overwhelming how potent and effective this game is.

I just replayed it after finishing the classic. I had played the classic previously, but I only did Leon A, now I just finished all of the scenarios.

I didn't really like the game, but I wanted to give it another chance and came back to it with an open mind after a few years.
So, here are my overall thoughts on it:

The gameplay is nice, some of the redesigns are pretty good, and the new layout of RPD makes a lot more sense. Puzzles are far better too.
Story-wise.. it sucks. The original does it far better, while the remake takes a lot of parts that made sense out, including pretty much every single encounter Claire and Leon have in the game. Yes, there are some pieces that are better, such as Marvin's role and Annette's entire character, Brian Irons is also fantastic now, but overall the story is pretty bad compared to the original. The A and B scenarios of both of the characters are also handled really poorly, only changing the way you get into the RPD and making some puzzles different. Differences between Claire and Leon's campaigns are pretty slim too, especially considering how the B scenario doesn't change anything relevant.

I think one of my biggest complaints tho is the atmosphere. It just doesn't do it for me.. the game is silent almost all the time, all you hear are your character's actions and the enemies', and a few creaking noises from the ambient or some machine making sounds in specific places, sometimes nonsensical noises from things falling that aren't there, and even the rain can barely be heard throught the game. Yes, there are a few dramatic songs that play here and there, but a lot of them annoy more than they contribute to the feeling of the areas. And the save room song despite being good is too silent and only plays once in the entire game once you hear it in a room.
The original had such a great and macabre atmosphere, with the howling wind as if it's a ghost town, and zombies' moaning echoes in the background. Most of the rooms have songs that give you an eerie vibe, it's just really good sound design all around. The remake's just isn't good imo, and it really hurts the experience.

Another thing I have to point out is what they did to some of the enemies. The crows and the spiders were completelly removed from the game and I really missed them, especially the spiders since you get so many blue herbs and hardly ever get poisoned. They also removed the moth, which was a pretty short appearance of an enemy but it's role made sense to me. The ivies had a really poor redesign, going from slow poisoning plants that attack from afar and attack you even after they died and that, as the spiders, poison you. They also removed the green lickers from the lab area, which may not be a big thing but it made them fit into the area where they were in.

That's pretty much it tho. Only other thing I have to mention is the unnecessary futuristic take they had on the game, with Ada's ridiculous hacking device and the labs being straight up garbage compared to the original, both in the way they fit into the story and into the time it's set in.

Is it a good experience? I'd say yeah, it's fun. It's short tho, don't expect this to be different compared to RE3, even in my first playthrough exploring everything I could I finished it in 5 hours.
Is it better than the original? Nope, not at all. It just can't replace it.

[h1]Resident Evil 2: Remake is a fun and tension filled homage to classic Resident Evil games with an excellent modern twist.[/h1]

[b] Speaking from a guy who has only played Resident Evil 4 and 5 and never experienced the true survival horror capabilities the Resident Evil franchise has to offer i’d say the game is perfect for anybody curious about diving into the series as well as being satisfying for long time fans.[/b]

[h1]+Pros[/h1]

[h1] [b]+Gameplay[/b] [/h1]
Instead of the fixed camera angles the first RE2 had this version is updated into a 3rd person perspective allowing for a more organic and natural feel for gameplay. Despite the perspective changes you’ll often find the game to still be quite claustrophobic as many zombies will try and snuggle up with you while in a small corridor so no worries there.

Shooting is the same in this game as the other Resident Evil titles so make sure to position yourself carefully and aim for the head so you suddenly don’t find yourself with a chunk of your flesh missing.

The game also allows you to be a little creative when dealing with zombies. So say you want to shoot them but don’t want to use too much ammo, you can also shoot them in the legs and disable them so it’s easier to run away and trust me it’s quite fun to do. 

Still though, running away is still the most optimal way to play the game as ammo and healing items are worth their weight in gold, especially on hardcore difficulty, and it’s best not to waste them by fighting every zombie you come across.

You’ll also find various puzzles you’ll need to solve in order to progress through the game. The best addition to this game is that whenever you fully explore a room, the room will then be colored blue telling you that all possible items have been retrieved so if you ever want to find out where to probably check out next just check your map and you’re on your way.

All in all, the gameplay is fantastic and definitely can keep you on edge throughout your entire playtime. 

[h1][b]+Audio[/b][/h1]
This game is absolutely meant to be experienced with headphones as it really adds to the horror factor hearing the zombies constantly banging their hands on windows and doors trying to break into the police station and it also helps gameplay wise when a zombie you thought was dead suddenly starts snarling back to life.


[h1][b]+Graphics[/b][/h1]
The game looks absolutely gorgeous as you’ll soon find out that with every bullet you put inside a zombies dome the blood and character models on the zombies look both beautiful and terrifying at the same time.

The lighting is also top notch as most of the areas you’ll explore are very dark and you’ll make use of a flashlight in order to navigate and it can be seen that a lot of effort has been made to make sure it looks both good and is functional for gameplay.

Facial animations during cutscenes and the environment you’ll explore is also well polished and pleasing to the eyes.

[h1][b]+Story[/b][/h1]
Just by examining a general overview of the entire story so far and all the lore the Resident Evil series has established so far it can be seen as a little convoluted and ridiculous even for people who are long time fans of the series. 

However, seeing as how the story has just relatively begun, the story is more simplistic and easier to follow as well as a few changes being made in this game to streamline the action.

[h1][b]-Cons [/b] [/h1]

[h1][b]-Slight Inconsistencies With the Story[/b][/h1]
As you do get to play as both Claire and Leon in the game it can lead to a few slight problems with the continuity in the story. 

For example, who got into the police station first? Who met Sherry first? Are there multiple Mr. X’s?

Small stuff like that that continues to make the timeline a bit skewed here and there.

[h1][b]-Overall Very Short[/b][/h1]
The actual game itself is very short as it would only take me about 13 hours to fully complete both Leon A and Claire B and that includes running around getting all of the collectibles. If you play on hardcore difficulty it may take you a bit longer but for a standard playthough you should be able to beat the game relatively quickly.

Now while there is replay value in playing throughout all the different routes if you’re a one time playthrough kind of person, you may lose some value in this game.

[h1][b]Final Verdict:(9/10)[/b] [/h1]
Resident Evil 2: Remake works both as a fun action/zombie game and tension filled, survival horror as you’ll constantly be on your toes as zombies will barge through doors and windows to get a taste of your delicious meaty flesh. Story is also easy enough to understand so anybody can dive right in without any prior knowledge as to who these people are and how they stand in the franchise. 


All in all, if you’re like me and just want to find out what all the fuss was about it’s definitely worth a pick up at full price and for long time fans you’ll feel right at home

With a slightly different take from the original story in Resident Evil 2, and a few over-the-shoulder elements, RE2 Remake manages to create a unique feeling of dread and panic. The game turns away from the action entered gameplay as seen in Resident Evil 4, and focuses solely on horror. Gone are the quick time events, unlimited supplies of ammo, and giant hordes of weak zombies following you.

During most of the game (if you haven't got used to it), you'll feel trapped and helpless. With only a few supplies available to you, and limited inventory space, you'll have to think twice before unloading your precious bullets on a zombie that most likely will not die from that run and gun decision.

Easily the most interesting part of the game is Mr. X, who changed from a pack of expendable henchmen to a single, immortal, entity. Mr. X will follow you around the station, with solely objective of finding you. His footsteps are the best way to describe him, as they are loud and often comes from confusing directions, forcing you to sit in a safe room until you think the outside is clear... just to end up face to face with him once you finally leave.

This game made want a Resident Evil 3 remake as well, and if Nemesis is anything like Mr. X I will certainly buy that remake if it ever comes out.

This was my first [b]Resident Evil[/b] game. Was more of a [b]Silent Hill[/b] fan back in the day and kind of ignored the whole series, however [b]Resident Evil 2[/b]'s remake is an excellent entry point. The game does a good job of introducing you to the world of [b]Resident Evil[/b], including the Umbrella corporation and other key players.

There are 2 main characters you get to play as, Claire Redfield and Leon S. Kennedy. Their routes are relatively similar, however they meet different companions ([spoiler]Sherry[/spoiler] for Claire and [spoiler]Ada Wong[/spoiler] for Leon) and each route has some unique locations that the other character doesn't visit. In order to get to the true ending you will need to beat both routes. This is pretty similar to [b]Nier: Automata[/b]'s routes A/B, but much shorter. Your first run will probably take about 10 hours, and the second only 5 or so.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
- This is one of the best looking games I ever played. And it runs really well even on mid-range systems.
- Just really amazing graphics. The face scanned models look so lifelike and [spoiler]the girls are all very hot[/spoiler].
- Playing dress up with all the different costumes never gets old, especially here on the PC where you get many fan made outfits, definitely check out the RE2 Nexus.
- Actual puzzles. In an AAA game. Some will definitely make you scratch your head, and it's quite refreshing.
- Adjustable difficulty. Normal is pretty challenging and it's easy to run out of ammo, Assisted is pretty comfortable, and then Hardcore has limited saves and much more dangerous enemies.

[h1]Cons:[/h1]
- I know it's a survival game, but the damage you do is so random, even with focused crosshair headshots it can take anywhere from 1 to 10 bullets to kill a zombie. And there's still a chance that they might rise again.
- There's inventory tetris and even tiny items like keys each take up their own slot. Constantly running back to the storage box to offload your stuff felt like a waste of time, but I suppose it's true to the original game.
- Mr. X stalking you can get pretty annoying, especially when you're not sure how to solve a puzzle and he just doesn't give you any breathing room.

[h1]Mixed:[/h1]

When one of the most beloved games of all times is remade, there are essentially two possible outcomes:

1) The game is a cash-grab and spits on the legacy of its' progenitor.
2) The game is amazing... no... like, really amazing; everything that could be hoped for and then some.

The remake of [b]Resident Evil 2[/b] falls into the second category. Is the game flawless? No. Does it represent a major leap forward in game design? No. Is it a faithful - best-in-class - representation of what the [i]Survival Horror[/i] genre can be? Yes.

While the game differs from the original quite significantly in some ways, other details - many of them easy to overlook - have been painstakingly recreated with obvious love that cannot be overstated; as an example, the original menagerie of zombie faces-and-models have been gloriously updated in what might seem like a strange bit of attention-to-detail, but this greatly helps the remake maintain a generalized similarity to the visuals of the original that might otherwise be lost because graphics have changed so much in the intervening twenty years.

One thing I can't say that I'm an enormous fan of are the redesigns of the three main characters, Leon, Claire, and Ada. We have seen all of these characters in other [i]Resident Evil[/i] games since their introduction and - like their counterparts Chris and Jill in [i]Resident Evil 5[/i] - the liberties taken with their design simply don't add anything to their character and might actually distract veterans of the series from what is otherwise an amazing game.

The remastered soundtrack is brilliant in its' own way but the original was, is, and will remain one of the seminal scores ever composed for a video game. In that light, I feel that it might be best to play through the game as one character with the new music and the other character with the old; mileage might vary.

Regarding the actual mechanical components of the game itself... There remains little to be said beyond the age old wisdom: "If it ain't broke, don't fix it." Under similar scrutiny the graphics can hardly be faulted; they retain much of the campy charm that the original had on the [i]PlayStation[/i] while simultaneously being a nearly immeasurable leap forward in fidelity because, well, twenty years of GPU technology goes a long way when everything is dark and covered in blood.

TLDR: It's a great remake and you should play it whether or not you're new to the series or a tried and true veteran of Umbrella's scheming.

RESIDENT EVIL  2/BIOHAZARD RE:2 is a remake of the 1998 play station one classic Resident evil 2.
Resident evil is a survial horror franchise developed and published by capcom. Resident evil 2 has two protagonists fighting their way through the city in the quest of in turn saving it.

Story

Whether you play as Leon or Claire you are terrified to find the state the city is in,a virus breakout turning the city into a nightmare filled with terrifying creatures and hungry zombies at every corner ,and  you the hero/heroine the city needs.Both,Leon the rookie looking forward at his first day at work and Claire a brave college student trying to find her brother get sucked into  trying to save this virus infested city and finding  the reason the city turned into a living undead. Both the main characters find unique and interesting side characters during their escape from the virus infested city.Some of the side characters are really well crafted getting you to care for them.So the story is really straight forward that  you are the Savior the city needs but the gameplay and the characters is what makes the game great.The only problem I have is that both the main characters Leon and Claire although have completely different story but traverse the same path and have to solve the same puzzles ,that just makes me a bit disappointed and sad.

Gameplay

The gameplay is frustratingly awesome especially on the hardest difficulty getting you to sweat at every moment.On the hardest difficult  especially the ammo management plays a vital role getting you to care for every bullet you fire.Both leon and claire have to deal with unique weapons giving their respective story a different dimension along with the story
There are 3 massive locations you need to explore and fight through in this game dark and silent hallways of RPD ,dirty sewers and an umbrella lab.Each area has multiple puzzles you need to crack to advance.The puzzles are one of the reason that make the original resident evil games  so loved and revered. Imo puzzles are heart of a great Resident evil game.
Resident evil 2 does a great job of keeping you on the edge due to its blood thirsty zombies, horrifying creatures and especially Mr X. The sound Mr X's footsteps is a fuel of nightmares,his unflinching face ,his mammoth size makes him much more horrifying and scares the living ♥♥♥♥ outa you when you see him outta nowhere.Resident evil 2 does a great job of making you feel your in constant danger due to its ammo and inventory management, awesome zombies and a terrifying atmosphere and background scores.


All in all Resident evil 2 remake is a welcome reminder of how Resident evil games should be like,full of edge of the seat moments,great story and characters and a terrifying atmosphere.Resident evil 2 is a modern day classic and a must play for everyone and especially for fans of the original resident evil games.

-Durability ever, unless for actual mechanics

All in all, great game and a credit to Capcom for not adding another tick against the series.

Being based on one of the most beloved games in the franchise and coming after the, especially at the time of release, incredible remake of the first RE game, RE2 had big shoes to fill.

I'm glad to say Capcom nailed the project, almost in its entirety. From the new, dark and thick atmosphere to reworked puzzles and areas, combat and controls that are modernized enough to feel comfortable without plunging the player straight into the action game territory of some of the more modern episodes in the series, RE2 is a remake done just right. 

And how not to mention the imposing Tyrant (Mr. X for his old friends), which will stalk the corridors of the police station, his stomping to be heard from the other side of the building, closer and closer to your location.

The only sad note I must add is related to the second scenario of the game, unlocked after finishing your first playthrough, which only adds a couple new weapons and skips/reworks some of the early bits of the game, instead of providing exciting new locations and situations. This lack is likely dictated by time and budget constraint, but it nonetheless feels like a wasted opportunity that would have made a great game even better.

Regardless of that, RE2 is one of the best horror games of the last decade, and one every fan of the genre is obliged to play through at least once.
