[b] This game's always felt kind of off to me and for years I couldn't figure out why.

It's been a gradual realization for me actually, it's sort of been brewing since RE3 Remake. 
RE4 Remake made me think on it more. 
Then RE9 released.

Then it finally clicked.

[i] This remake is ground zero. [/i] 

This one is why this series turned into a babymode casual type game and it's why most of the fans act like they do. It's almost like they regret how camp and crusty the original games were and want to brainwash them out of the communities heads with the remakes or something. 
What a conspiracy that would be.

Maybe I should go dig back into the MGS community, at least they're the funny type of schizophrenic.


[i] Anyways [/i], community hatred aside.

Anyone whose played the original games (albeit it's a very small audience now given how tourist infested this franchise has gotten) can very easily tell they got rid of a ton of the gameplay in this remake just to make sure the modern audience doesn't get bored playing it.

While playing through this, I managed to slog through Claire's story but didn't even finish Leon's story because I kept running into too many "why was that removed/changed, that's stupid" situations to bother.

Such as:

-They got rid of certain parts at the start of scenario 2 in general, as well as not replicating the added lab parts of scenario 2. It was just the same as scenario 1 with different passwords. 
Which is weird, because that never felt like it was out of place or anything. 
Must've just been a playtesting skill issue.

-Speaking of skill issues, I've noticed this game downscales the difficulty if you die too much on hardcore. 
It's interesting, but also kind of defeats the point of hardcore?
In the older games (RE4 up to I think RE8) the games adaptive difficulty scaling reacted to your performance even on professional. It scaled health items and ammo drops, but never messed with the damage scaling so you could learn what you could survive enough times in the situation. 
Seemingly a lost art these days, which is a shame.

-Lots of non compulsory elements which you could just skip over, felt like artificially extending the game just because they cut things out of it which is pretty counterproductive.

-In general scenario A and B don't feel like scenarios, they feel like completely separate stories that coincidentally connect with each other occasionally because they remember it's meant to do that. Far better fleshed out in OG. 
Depending on who you play first, the other character's side of the same story unlocks after you beat your first choice. The remake chooses to ignore this feature and make each character's playthrough an alternate universe of events, where the other character you don't pick is forgotten about for most of the game.

[spoiler] -They removed the lore-point of Sherry’s pendant having a sample of the G virus which is [i] literally the reason why Mr. X chases Claire. [/i] [/spoiler]

-Claire seems to have generally higher stun and safer options from far away, but lower speed and less bullets/ammo. Punishes inaccuracy and risky play, while Leon has access to more consistent damage, but getting the most out of your weapons encourages riskier strategies. Punishes bad timing and a lack of risk taking.

In the original, Claire and Leon's next weapons were kind of interchangeable and just stop and swap type things. 

(This isn't a [i] complaint [/i] per se, it just threw me off as I'm used to this concept being a difficulty scaling mechanic over a passive mechanic).

-OG RE2 directly references RE1 at several points. It's also the version of events that are referenced in games/films going forward in the series. The remake chooses to mostly ignore all the mentions of RE1 to accommodate new players who may not have played it. Which defeats the entire purpose of it being a game series. 
I blame them making the Remakes canon to the timeline and since RE1 Remake isn't babymoded people haven't played it, so they just got rid of the connection.

Games like Metal Gear Solid vaguely referenced almost every game in the series with each game, on purpose, so you were basically forced to play the other entries to get the full story, [spoiler] until MGS4 basically retconned almost everything that we were told up until that point, however it still counts as an example [/spoiler] even with the "remake" games such as Twin Snakes. I don't get why devs are so allergic to connecting lore these days.

-Some characters roles in general were altered to account for the lack of references to RE1, like Ada. Some were altered to be completely different and some were almost completely cut out of the plot and rendered more like a cameo.

-This complaint is just my inner Car Freak coming out, but Leon's key for his 1980s Chevy Caprice shouldn't have a keyless FOB. 
Also all of the police cars are just 1980s Chevy Caprice look-alikes. 
No 1990s Crown Victorias at all, like the original had. 
You know, of-era.
Because it's 1998.

-Upgrading your weapons doesn't make them sound different anymore, Birkin doesn't have the iconic roar in his fight anymore, in general the audio just feels like the forgot we live in a world where 8D audio exists now

-The music was a pinnacle point of the game's story telling and general atmosphere building, so hearing how quiet and in the background it is was insanely disappointing, but I guess since the general game aesthetic got "revamped", they had to "revamp" the soundtrack too. Luckily, for the low price of [i] 3 dollars [/i] you can experience the original game score and realize how critically tied to the game it was back in the OG.

-So much of this remake is the [i] game [/i] trying to jumpscare you over [i] you [/i] jumpscaring [i] yourself [/i] through the choice of what you do. 
This is more of a blanket "modern horror is abysmal" complaint, it's been happening since the mid-2010s. [i] Don't get me started on it. [/i]

-I can't tell if it's was just me running an older card at the time I was playing, but the graphics really did not feel "groundbreaking". 
I've noticed modern RE games in general really struggle to render hair properly. 
Most footage I see of RE7, RE8, even RE9, their hair has the same crusty texture problems where it just doesn't render the full thing properly, there's pixilation and gaps in the textures of the hair. 
It's more noticeable with Claire than Leon but both have the same problem. 
This problem also extends to the Dead Rising remake as well, so it's definitely the engine not knowing how to render hair.

This was also the first game I've ever played that ran smoother if you maxed the settings compared to lowering all the settings, which confused me, because it wasn't like I was dropping frames or anything, the game just felt like it was straining the lower I put the settings so I had to ramp everything to max. 
That may just be how games work these days, I don't know.

-The hottest take of this is gonna be I [i] kinda [/i] don't like the new VAs.
Granted, obviously, I'm the oldest resident evil gamer to exist therefore new thing bad and I want the 90s back.

However, as I've slowly gotten used to the new Leon voice.. I still think Haddad, Mercier, and/or Mercer fit him a lot better.

[spoiler] I also definitely don't not like Claire's new voice because they never contacted Alyson Court to come back for Claire due to them being cheapskates who refuse to work with union actors that've been voicing their iconic characters for almost 3 decades

:) [/spoiler]

Point is, if you're not like me you'll enjoy it. If not, you'll probably still enjoy it.

Just keep in mind if you want the actual lore and/or story of the game, the originals do it way better than the remakes do.
But I can't say that, the Reddit will hear about it and then [i] they [/i] will appear.

Maybe I should just go replay the original RE3 again so I can think back on when all this wasn't real. [/b]

As we come to closing out the year Resident Evil 2 has consistently been my GOTY choice since its release. Capcom was able to successfully re-imagine a beloved classic with more modern game play mechanics that do not hinder the survival horror experience we fondly remember, while still providing a game that doesn't need nostalgia alone to appeal to a new audience.  

Avoiding zombies when possible and killing only the enemies you need to grab that one key item is usually the best approach. Careful use of your weapons is a must especially on higher difficulties as you can find yourself facing down a boss without adequate firepower especially on the hardest difficulty. The game also can be ruthless in that the better you are doing on a run the harder it can get. Difficulty scaling based on performance will lead to enemies that take more resources to kill and deal more damage. This is a game at its heart that is designed to destroy any sense of comfort and ultimately try and kill you.

The third person combat works really well here. One thing I was worried about was if the introduction of over the shoulder shooting would make the game too easy and eliminate a lot of the challenge of the original game. I can gladly say that is not the case. Standing still while aiming nets you better accuracy in that the reticle will shrink providing a more precise shot. The zombies themselves are not guaranteed to be downed by a single shot to the head with basic handguns, that instead is tied to a chance to critically hit which results in a satisfying cranial explosion and feels rewarding when it happens. Due to this it is often better to stun one momentarily and run past. Of course things like the shotgun and magnum will down your basic zombie with a well placed shot to the face but the ammo is more rare and therefore you want to save it for when its really needed.

The game is soaked in atmosphere that instills great dread and the original games gothic police station makes a return here in perfect form. Everything from the materials rendered to the lighting makes it one of the most terrifying locations in a horror game. The mystery of this former museum turned police station is intensified by the extremely impressive visuals. Capcoms RE engine is incredibly well optimized and runs fantastically on even what some would consider "lesser hardware". The puzzles of the original make a return here and are improved. Helping you along is a fantastic map system that tracks locations you have and have not entered and any important items you may have missed and may not have had the inventory space for at the time.

The story of the game remains largely the same but this time the convincing facial animations, motion capture and vastly improved voice acting help to sell it. It follows the original game very closely while adding a few new interesting segments that differ from the original. It's interesting enough to keep you wanting to progress and as far as Resident Evil plots go is one of the better ones. Sadly though the "Zapping system" of the original game is really not present here. Before items and weapons could be left behind and used for the other characters B scenario but unfortunately this is missing. The A/B scenario itself is also relatively unchanged from your standard run through as a single character. It serves more as a shorter experience of the story rather than a true scenario with its own story beats that change based on the other. Overall though it is very good for what it is.

On top of all of that there are extra modes that are unlocked and also downloadable content which can be challenging and fun to play. If all you are after is just a single play through it can be a short game, but if you want to do the A/B scenarios for both characters as well as the extra content there is quite a bit here to enjoy.

No game this year for me has matched the level of suspense that this title has. It's an incredibly immersive experience that should not be missed. It is almost a perfect remake in every way aside from a few small flaws that really aren't deal breaking. Just make sure you wear headphones. The sound design is fantastic and it really adds to the experience.

I decided to update my review and post the one I made few months after release of Resident Evil 2 / Biohazard RE:2, because I like it more but at some point I was sure it's lost (I found it on my second HDD). So enjoy!

I was hoping to post this review earlier, but sadly I had no chance - I was to busy enjoying this masterpiece. Beware! My review containt spoilers and opinions made as a huge fan since first game. At this stage it's only made on my experience with first Leon's scenario, so don't be mad if there are some errors in my review :) I wonder where I should start. There are so many things I want to say about this game, how I felt during my first playthrough, how I feel playing it even now. So maybe I will start from saying that original Resident Evil 2 was never my favorite game and I completed it very few times. I probably haven't catched every easter egg, details and such snatched into this Remake. Still, I felt very nostalgic running around Raccoon Police Station. "I know this place!", "This is where the first Licker was!". Seeing a classic game in the modern visuals is a fantastic feeling. Once again, I felt like a kid who discovers the magic of survival horror for the first time. 

About my first run. I was thinking that since the classic RE games are my favorite, I should start with hardcore: you know, enemies are harder, limited times of saves because of ink, avoiding enemies and such. That was, at the time, good idea. Oh, and I was thinking using a Steam Controller, which I used to play for like few hours, would be a great idea. I failed the first section around 8 times. I managed to miss every shot twice. I'm yet no used to it so I switched back to keyboard and mouse. Ah, it was much better! 

Clearing the gas station was easy. Then, starting in the middle of the horror, that was just awesome. I mean, I'm running this game on rather old PC and all I can hope for are medium/high settings and yet, everything looked so freaking great. Resident Evil 2 (Remake) set a new high standards for the visuals in modern gaming. And I know this game could look even better on maximum settings! The zombies looks super disgusting, cutting their legs, hands, exploding heads, everything feels just right. Their moans, way the behave, how they are "waving" and making it harder to land a good hit, the way they hits the windows and boards - trust me, it's really scary if you are using a headset. At times I was thinking that maybe it would be better to just let zombie in and kill every one, so there could be some quiet time. But yeah, we all don't have enough ammo for that. The lights are also doing a great job to make this game even more scary: sparks, fire, flashlight, and you know there must be something lying in the darkness. Really, there were only few games that made me "WOW, IT LOOKS BEAUTIFUL!": Far Cry, Crysis, and now RE2 joins the club.

Since I mentioned zombies, these are not the only one that are disgusting. Yeah, you know it: Lickers! While playing, I felt that Hunters in the remake of the first Resident Evil wasn't that bad. As I mentioned, or not, I'm not a very skillful player. Jumping around, crawling at rather fast pace, and being a really tough opponent, Lickers are the worst kind of enemies. There were a time at the lab when two of them jumped out and it really was bad for my ammo and health (both mine and Leon's). I haven't yet played every scenario so I probably haven't met every type of enemies. Anyway, normal (not boss) monsters are really well done and everything feels like a threat to a player.

But, the bosses! I feel like the crocodile part was rather easy, it wasn't also that hard in original RE2, and yet I managed to die at this sequence. Sucks to be me, lol. One of the best part of bosses was definitely Mr. X. After meeting this guy, after he doesn't seem to care if it's a save room or not, I was really happy. I mean, have you ever played Resident Evil 3 and fought against Nemesis? Yeah, this guy gives you the same vibe in the Resident Evil 2 Remake. I felt a huge relief and because of this I know people at Capcom will do a great job on the remakes of other Resident Evil games. So Mr. X is unbeatable (at some point), you don't want to waste ammo on him, but also you don't want him to get closer. Solving puzzles while running away, trying to explore new areas while running away, hearing just those stomp sounds of his - this is such a perfect job. I wasn't feeling safe no matter where I was: is he around? Will he enter this room? Will he smash another wall to jump and kick my butt? This is how bosses in survival horrors should be made! And there is one more guy, Birkin, but he wasn't my favorite or anything. Until the last fight... this part of game was also something amazing. Probably one of the best boss fights in Resident Evil franchise! It's so intense, the final Birkin's form looks terrifing, it's just perfect for the (almost) last fight.

I'm not sure if there is much I can say about weapons, since in the Leon's first sceneario there aren't many. But, I really liked the flamethrower (it's fun to burn zombies!) and... handgun. Maybe I need to get used to it, but the shotgun wasn't really my thing, I had a troubles aiming at the zombies heads and if it takes 2-3 shots to hit them (and not even kill) then yeah, I'd rather stick with small pistol. Oh, the subweapons were great but at the same time I felt like I wasted some of them: way too many grenades went into zombies mounths instead of more dangerous enemies. Well, that's just my luck (and lack of skill!)

So, in the end, is this remake any good? In my opinion, it's much better than original. I know original Resident Evil 2 is very high rated game, and it's one of the best classic games ever made, but I feel like I like playing it much more playing than the original. This game is worth every price. Be it at sale, or at full price - as long as you enjoy good games, and perfectly made survival horrors. Resident Evil 2 Remake is my pick for the best game of 2019. Cheers!

[h1] RESIDENT EVIL 2 [/h1]

Resident Evil 2 is without question the greatest remake ever created, period. It's now the standard by which all remakes will be compared to and for good reasons. It improves and removes pretty much all aspects of what made the old Resident Evil games tedious and frustrating to play and make it better than ever before. Let's count down what this game got right:

[b] 1. No more fix camera angles [/b]
I can't even begin to stress how much more fun the game is without this needless and useless implementation of the past. Exploration is now more fun and faster, and maneuvering your characters has never been easier and more intuitive. 

[b] 2. The transition to 3rd person over-the-shoulder shooting [/b]
No more will you have to rely on the game auto shooting for you. Now, the freedom to aim your weapon however you want and getting critical headshots are entirely up to you. It makes combat less clunky and more engaging than any previous entry in the original trilogy. Players who played the old Resident Evil games will appreciate this change immensely.

[b] 3. No more loading screens of doors opening [/b]
With the technology of today, gone are the days of constantly having to watch a loading screen every time you enter a new area. With how much this game emphasizes exploration and backtracking, this improvement is no doubt the most appreciated of them all. 

[b] 4. More backpack spaces [/b]
It sounds like such a simple upgrade, but it makes a massive difference in a Resident Evil game. Backtracking is no longer as prevalent and tedious in Resident Evil 2 because you have so many opportunities to upgrade your backpack, making the flow of exploration MUCH more enjoyable and fun to play.

[b] 5. A more functional map [/b]  
The map in this game does much more than show your current location. It does everything from showing which key opens which door, where items get remembered on the map, whether there are still more items to be found in an area, and how to open particular doors more apparent than ever, making exploration even better and effortless. 

Here's a quick rundown of everything else Resident Evil 2 got right with this remake: 

The graphic is gorgeous and beautiful to look at; It elevates the horror to a whole new level. The dialogue and voice acting are superior in every single way. The atmosphere is incredible and unrelenting; You are at the mercy of the city, and you genuinely feel like it. The varieties of enemies are also adequate, presenting just enough with each to make fights and encounters feel different enough. The level design is superb, and the puzzles are never too hard to solve but sufficient to be enjoyable and engaging. 

[u] In conclusion [/u]

Resident Evil 2 is a game begging to get replayed over and over again. Literally. From top to bottom, this is one of those rare gems that managed to surpass expectations in almost every inconceivable way. Resident Evil 2 has officially redefined what it meant to be a remake.

RE2 was one of my favorite gameson N64 ( and hard to find in my region ), and I'm glad they did this remake and not just a remaster like RE0 and 1 ( which are pretty good too ).

They took the original game, but instead of just improving the graphics they made it feel new and different, but not too different. It looks really good and the engine is capable of awesome lighting, which really helps with immersion, as does the sound design. There is almost no music compared to the old game, but you can hear every creaky noise and zombie groaning or banging on windows and doors, while exploring a dark hallway with your torchlight. The ambiance is top notch, at least most of the time ( mostly at the beginning of the game in fact, before it all goes to hell when the Tyrant appears and you have to run everywhere like a headless chicken ).

Now, this game is far from perfect. Maybe it's just nostalgia speaking, but I enjoyed it despite its flaws, which is generally the sign for me that it's a really good game. I also thinks it's a way better game than RE7, which was already quite good.

But the difficulty was really off-putting at first, I started on normal and I was stuck after 1 or 2 hours because the enemies are so hard to kill, I was all out of ammo. I started over on "assisted" difficulty to learn the game and did Claire A and Leon B, then played Leon A and Claire B on normal difficulty and it was a lot easier.

The main problem here comes from the adaptive difficulty : the better you play, the harder the game becomes. But it can become so hard that basic zombies take 6 shots to the leg before falling down, and then another 6 shots to the head or many knife slashes to kill, and even then sometimes they come back to life... all the while the game gives you 2 bullets at a time ( not kidding, at some point I only looted two 9mm bullets every time ) and reduces the amount of crafted ammo you make, and also adds more enemies here and there, like frigging zombies popping out of the water in the sewers when there are already these huge mutants in your way, which instead of dying with 2 incendiary ammo suddenly take 3. Zombies also become more agressive, and faster, and won't give you enough time to down them when there are more than 1 in a small corridor, so you have to waste a hand grenade if you don't want to be gang banged.

Resident Evil is all about learning the game to be able to speed-run it and unlock the bonuses, but this adaptive difficulty makes it random in a bad way. It actively punishes you for being good until it's unsustainable.

And it becomes far worse when this ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ Tyrant appears. IN.EVERY.SCENARIO. And you can't just KO him like in the old game, he'll constantly chase you down, preventing you from completing puzzles like the one in the library, so you have to bait him in another part of the police station before proceeding. The Tyrant completely ruins the game, he's supposed to make it more stressful but instead he's just annoying, forcing you to wait in a safe room unitl he goes away. He pissed me off so bad I installed a mod to remove him from the game ( except his boss form ).

Another minor weakness I can point out, reminiscent from RE7, are the weird faces. Especially Claire's and Annette's, there is something wrong with their faces like the mom, Mia and Zoe in RE7. Maybe it's something with the engine and motion capture, or the exagerated animations/smiles, or maybe it's the modelling based on real people, I don't know but Leon, Ada, Sherry and Irons look good compared to Claire and Annette, who are deep in the uncanny valley.

Last thing I didn't like, special mention to that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ annoying herbicide puzzle in the lab, which is the more retarded thing ever because there is NO way a real scientist would use that ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ machine to fill a vial. They'd just, you know, take the vial and fill it up with the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ liquid, done. Stupid puzzle is stupid.

Anyway I hope they'll remake RE3 and especially Code Veronica too.

It's very well done, and definitely worth the money to buy if you are a fan of the series, or if you've spent time with the original RE2 back in the day.

Its manically detailed environments, amazing voice acting, smooth combat mechanics and mind-blowing graphics make this game an outstanding achievement in the [url=https://store.steampowered.com/sale/resident-evil/] Resident Evil series [/url] and also in recent video game history.  

Survival horror became the huge market it is today thanks to titles like Resident Evil, and all the elements that made the first entries in the series classics are present in this game, refreshed and revisited for newer audiences and platforms. 

[h1] Make Zombies Scary Again [/h1]

The whole thing with zombies was that they were undead creatures. This meant, in the beginning, that they were terrifying on their own. [i] How could you kill something that was already dead? [/i] As this shock value grew thin over time, the entertainment industry (including video games, TV and film) seemed to automatically shift from horror to action. This change could also be seen in the Resident Evil franchise, especially in [url=https://store.steampowered.com/app/221040/Resident_Evil_6__Biohazard_6] Resident Evil 6 [/url], arguably the least scary in the series. A return to the basics was long overdue, and Resident Evil 2 did it flawlessly. Zombies can't be killed easily in this game, and if you take the risk, there's always a chance that they might actually kill you. You have to be careful every time you are around them. And as weapons are on short supply, often running might actually be your best shot.

[h1] Racoon City Never Looked This Good [/h1]

The level of immersion that the graphics and the sound design in this game give you is a great part of what makes it work so well. Every inch of the city feels alive, filled with a level of detail that can only be achieved through hard work and a masterful artistic direction. Every step you take makes you feel like you're actually there. All locations have just the right ambient sounds to make you feel that. This makes the whole experience realistic and honest, and the scary moments ten times scarier. 

[h1] Yes, Mr. X IS That Horrifying [/h1]

I just had to mention it. The design put into Tyrant (or as everyone is calling it, Mr. X) is just fascinating. Ever since you first encounter it you won't feel safe in the game anymore. [spoiler] The feeling of safety you get from reaching a new location is quickly wrecked by those heavy steps and those lifeless eyes relentlessly approaching you. The fact that the game provides little to no information about it makes it all the better. Mr. X becomes this presence in your head as you play the game, you think it is following you all the time. [/spoiler] While most games these days make you feel like an unstoppable killing machine, Mr. X makes you feel small and helpless. An element that was worked into the experience in such a way that makes it fit perfectly into the terrifying orchestra that Resident Evil 2 is.   

[h1] Bottom Line [/h1]

In my opinion, this game is worth every penny. From the way it makes you experience fear intimately and deeply to the remarkable graphic and sound design, Resident Evil 2 is an experience hardcore fans of the series and new players can enjoy. Definitely a must play.

Resident Evil 2: Remake is in my opinion THE definitive Resident Evil experience of the modern generation. It takes core components of the original games, such as puzzles and survival horror, and brings them up to a modern standard through the retailing of Claire and Leon's survival of Raccoon City. Ammo is scarce, survival is up to your wits, and boy does this game challenge you with its big guns. While I wouldn't call this the scariest game I've played, it does certainly prey on your fears, and ups the tension once certain formidable enemies make their appearance.

This game is also fantastic looking. Coming from Resident Evil 7, Capcom's other recent title, I was expecting a high standard of graphics and performance, and the game did not let down. Not only can the game be very cinematic at times, it looks amazing all across the board. Even on the lowest settings you would be hard pressed to think the game looks terrible. The game runs better than RE7, or at least more stable, and entry-level system owners should expect to have a decent experience with some graphical tweaking.

Gameplay as mentioned above centers around survival horror. You have limited supplies, which can be found all over the Raccoon City Police Department and other areas of the game. You must learn to be resourceful, and the game can be unforgiving at times, but that adds to the horror experience. Combat with the undead is the best it had been, allowing you to shoot zombie's limbs off and mutilate them in gruesome ways. The gore in this game is top notch, and I hope to see more in upcoming titles in the series.

The story in RE2 Remake loses the cheesyness the series is known for, and goes down the more serious route. There are some touching and emotional moments to offer in this game, and it will keep you hooked especially on first playthoughs. The game is centered around Leon and Claire, and you will play as both though two separate runs of the stories. The second run is a bit weaker with both characters, and ignores some continuity of the first run for gameplay sake, but you will still find both runs enjoyable.

All-in-all, this game is an absolute must play for anyone who are fans of horror, story, zombie-killing, or Resident Evil in general. I highly recommend this game to anyone!

Resident Evil 2 Remake is everything you'd expect a remake to be.
It's not perfect, it has a few minor details that prevents it from being the ultimate remake...
Starting with how Capcom handled Claire & Leon's Scenarios, which in my opinion were far stronger in the original than they are in the remake. But that's a minor detail that doesn't really take away from the game itself.

Gameplay wise, the game has benefited from a lot of improvements the series has seen over the years and makes great use of them. The 3rd person, over the shoulder, camera view isn't something I would've associated with "Survival Horror" but it works great and even helps push the "horror" vibe more at times.
The expanded freedom of the camera perspective helps breathe new life into a genre that was often thought to be dead or at the brink of death.

I do miss the Extreme battle mode that was included with the original but Hunk & Tofu do make a come back which I'm really happy with! The additions of the Ghost Survivor's DLC also helps bring more challenge and some more meat around the bone in terms of replayability. But without any kind of Multiplayer, whether it is in form of COOP or competitive gameplay, the game soon loses some of its luster.

That being said, the Residentevil.net community brings extra challenges on the table, I suggest you check them out if you wish to spice up your gameplay.

Final Note : 8/10

Biohazard RE:2 is an "avoid the zombies if you can" type survival horror game.

The best part of this game, in my opinion, is that you get to see the story from two different perspectives. You can play as Leon Kennedy or Claire Redfield and each have their own campaign ... very cool. However, if it were not for the excellent trainer mods available for this game, which I used to transform this game from a "survival" horror game to an "action" horror game, I may have requested a refund as this game isn't really my cup of tea.

For me this is a very overrated game. I liked Resi 2 back in the day, but things have moved on in the last 20 years, whilst the design of this remake hasn't (other than the controls no longer being awful)

Games being challenging is one thing, but putting a game on hardcore mode and having it be utterly ridiculous is another. It's very stingy with giving you ammo, and is bizarrely inconsistent about how many head shots an enemy takes to put down. Sometimes it will take one handgun bullet, and other times the same enemy takes ten (not exaggerating there) 

Those ten bullets will most of the time be all that you have, and there'll still be more enemies to face. So you'll end up running away much, much, more than ever shooting anything. 

This is further compounded by making you face bosses where there is the bare minimum of health and ammo  given for the task (if at all) and then it instantly makes you do another action / boss sequence without giving you any more. 

I'm at the end of the game, and it seems to think I spent the last 10+ hours hoarding bullets because I HAVE PSYCHIC POWERS, AND KNOW IN ADVANCE THAT THERE'LL BE A BOSS FIGHT AT THE END THAT GIVES NO AMMO WHATSOEVER. Yet the game has also made evading enemies tricky enough that I had no choice but to shoot them, so, uh, haven't got that ammo it seems to think I have. 

As an example: a boss that you face upon a relatively small platform has a charge attack that kills you instantly, and is UNAVOIDABLE. The game tips helpfully tell you to "hit it with everything you've got when this happens", and I'd love to do that, except...well, "everything I've got" adds up to the sum of....*fudge* all and the game isn't going to lift a finger to help. 

Plus: its normal attack lunges faster than you move, so you're constantly wanting to (sluggishly) get out of range. While doing this it can quickly break out the HOMING UNAVOIDABLE INSTA KILL ATTACK, and you die trying to turn and shoot it in this extremely short window of time......so, so, sooooooo much fun.  Every single boss in the game is tedious like this, and having faced four so far not a single one presented an interesting or enjoyable challenge.

For an action game it's riddled with moments where the clunky controls  and miserly level design (no ammo, no space to really move) make the action really, really bad. You can't dodge attacks, and once hit you start limping which makes further evasion very tricky. You have no melee attacks without a knife equipped, or any offensive capabilities at all when out of ammo. 

Clubbing away zombies with the butt of your empty gun? nah, chief - never heard of it. 

Knock a zombie to the floor, and then stomp on it's head while it's prone....er, sorry chief! Never heard of it (despite it being a design idea from a 2008 game - Dead Space)  

Shoot a zombie in half with your shotgun to slow them down? er....chief, have you had a blow to the head? cos that there is crazy talk (despite it being from 1998....and, er,  is from the original Resi 2.....) 

Shoot a leg off, or an arm, or indeed any body part at all, to give yourself an advantage.....er....nah, chief etc etc etc 

Bunch of zombies standing by a fire extinguisher, and you get the clever idea to shoot it in the hope that it explodes, taking them all out? er....congrats - you just wasted a valuable bullet! Compressed gas containers don't explode in this universe (well, unless they're in the jaws of a giant alligator and you want to end with some "big spectacle" to an otherwise crappy set piece) 

I guess making your game very pretty excuses it having even lesser action than the twenty year old original! It feels super backwards compared to the likes of Dead Space, which quite nicely removed a lot of the tedium and awkwardness from the Resi formula without sacrificing the exploration and survival aspect. The Evil Within is also much better at being survival horror whilst giving you a much more flexible character, proper stealth and enjoyable combat.

Action set pieces are non existent (there's not even the faintest whiff of Resi 4 to be had here), the puzzles are stupid, and stealth is a concept it claims to have but in practice it's terrible. There's blind enemies who hunt by sound, so you walk by totally silently and they still move into your path and just sit there leaving you stuck. 

You walk forwards - they sense you and you die. You walk back - they sense you and you die.  You stand still - they creep forward and you die.....

You expected their AI to eventually move away so that you could proceed? Ha! Ha! You poor deluded fool.....  Gotta go back to your last save point, and pray that on the next attempt they have a brain fart and let you pass quickly enough. Is that good game design? I don't think that it is.

Even if the difficulty wasn't ridiculous this would still have enough things that, despite enjoying it up to a point, I'd still stay it was pretty average game play wise. And that nostalgia, or sexy graphics, are covering over a fairly mediocre and outdated experience. 18 hours into the game, and stuck at an impossible bit, I didn't enjoy it enough that I'm going to restart it all on a lesser difficulty! 

If I played it on normal to begin with then this would probably be a moderately unenthusiastic positive review. There's enough deficiencies here in the game play mechanics, and in it's rather stunted ambition, that I wouldn't rate it that highly regardless of the excruciatingly badly judged challenge. Game play design that's barely moved on from 1998 doesn't cut the mustard for me in 2019.

When you scrape past an encounter it's tense, and it is this thing called being FUN. But more often than not it immediately descends into being a tedious chore after those enjoyable moments, as the gratification of ACTUALLY SHOOTING SOMETHING inevitably makes the next heavily scripted, and unbelievably stingy, section a pain in the neck.

Ironically, the Shotgun becomes your best zombie killing tool and the Handgun becomes the go to boss killing tool.

Rating: 9/10
Genre: Third Person Survival Horror

The Good: 
+ Every room/location/area is dripping with atmosphere. Capcom spared no expense in making sure that everything feels perfect in how it looks.  The game also supports an impressive amount of graphical options, each option shows you what it effects, how much ram it utilizes and how the image will look like.  

+ The game finds the right balance between survival horror and action especially in the harder difficulties where you have to make tough decision whether you fight or run to conserve resources. 

+ Every area is very designed; the game lets you explore at your own pace without holding you hand but also ensures you are constantly making progress 

+ The map screen provides valuable information like showing you which rooms you have collected every item, which doors require certain keys, and the map automatically shows you which items are in a room so long as you look at the item directly. All of this, leads to an easy to navigate environment and allows you to make decision quicker in which items you want to take with you and what items you want to leave behind. 

+ Both Leon and Claire get access to there own set of weapons, and each weapon feels satisfying to use. Shooting zombies causes brain matter to splatter, chunks of flesh to fall off, bones that shatter etc. 

+ The bonus DLC is free courtesy of Capcom although compared to the main game is a lot more frustrating and unforgiving. The DLC is reused areas from the main game with a lot more enemies a lot fewer resources. 

+ Mods that can change the game, although the majority of them are just specific outfits for Claire. 

+ Fantastic soundtrack 

The Average:
+/- My biggest complaint is more of a missed opportunity for the game. Both Leon and Claire campaigns are essentially two completely different games that share some similarities. I feel it would have been a lot more effective if Capcom treated the game as one story being told from two different perspectives where the actions in Scenario A carry over to Scenario B. 

+/- Story and dialogue were never a strong aspect of the Resident Evil franchise and this game is no different. The overall plot is pretty basic and certain plot/story elements are not explained compared to the original. 

Conclusion: 
A fantastic remake that does a great job of being faithful to the original.

I LOVED the original RE2. I honestly don't know how many times I've beaten it at this point. This remake is fun but it pales in comparison to the original. People that are relatively new to Resident Evil franchise will probably love this.

As a longtime RE fan, here's where this ranks for me:
RE1:Remake > RE2 > RE3 > RE0 > RE1 > RE:CV > [b]RE2:Remake[/b] > RE7 > RE4 > RE5 > RE6

The Good
[list]
[*]Graphically this game looks great. I love the lighting effects and how often this game makes you walk around in the dark with a flashlight. It really adds to the tension.
[*]The map now marks all items and key areas as you discover them. This makes backtracking for a specific thing easier to do.
[*]Story telling and voice acting has come a long way in 20 years.
[*]Items get a little pop-up when you're approaching them so you're not just walking against the edges of the levels spamming the "pick up" button like in the original.
[*]It may not be my favorite Resident Evil game but it's still better than 99% of horror games these days. Hopefully this gets some younger people into the horror genre and shows other developers that it's ok to be able to fight back in horror games. The "unkillable enemy following you endlessly" trope in horror games is very hard for me to get into.
[/list]

The Bad
[list]
[*]You can now freely aim which is fine BUT every enemy feels like a bullet sponge. [b]I DESPISE BULLET SPONGES[/b]. You will burn through ammo so fast in this game. It's not uncommon to have a basic zombie take 10 headshots to die. Good aim doesn't feel rewarded and enemies die based on a high and seemingly random bullet count.
[*]Enemies are much harder to dodge. After watching a speedrun, apparently the strategy in this game is to kneecap them and run away. This also is the common strategy for people who don't want to deal with bullet sponges. Blah.
[*]The inventory system allows you to add expansion slots and get a massive inventory BUT they flooded the levels with so much random stuff that you can't even begin to pick it all up. Key items and sub-weapons also take up space in your inventory like everything else, leaving out some important quality of life updates to the series. No RE4 key item inventory, no RE1 Remake sub-item inventory, and no RE0 drop item mechanic to be found here. You'll be making frequent runs to storage chests if you don't want to discard valuable items. I never had this much trouble managing my inventory in the original game.
[*]There are a good number of new key items and puzzles but tons of them unlock optional stuff that I honestly would have skipped had I known the reward was something like 3 shotgun shells. This part of the game is super bloated compared to the original. All puzzles in the past games where around directly progressing the main game OR they rewarded you with something optional but awesome.
[*]No dedicated combat knife.
[*]I loved the self defense items from the RE1 Remake. In this game self defense items show up and are combined with throwables from RE4 in the form of knives, flashbangs, and grenades. You can use any of these to stop a grab attack BUT they will be much less effective than if you just used them normally. That precious combat knife i mentioned? It's now replaced with knives that degrade quickly with use. Oh, and all of these items take up inventory space.
[*]There are 1-2ish new enemies in place of old fan favorites and I really don't like fighting either one of them.
[*]The gun powder system from RE3 is back and the game leans on it way too heavily. I don't understand the draw here since the game can easily just give you ammo instead of making you pick what you think might be useful. It feels like it's here so you can make mistakes based on what you think you might run into next while [b]once again[/b] bloating your inventory. [spoiler]As Leon, just craft magnum ammo whenever possible. Handgun is only worth it if you combine two large gunpowders to make 50ish shots all at once. Don't bother with shotgun.[/spoiler]
[*]Mr. X feels shoe-horned in. I don't know how they managed to make a character from the original feel so off. It feels like a half-assed RE3 Nemesis just showing up to annoy you and rush you along to the next part of the game.
[*][spoiler]There is at least one boss fight where you can only finish the fight by doing some environmental attack. Finding this out after using all of your high powered ammo on them is nothing short of infuriating since all resources are so scarce.[/spoiler]
[/list]

Notes after playing Leon's A scenario and Claire's B scenario
[list]
[*]Claire's campaign is better than Leon's across the board. If you're only planning on playing one scenario, play Claire's. She gets cooler weapons, has a better story, much better characters, and doesn't have to do some of Leon's campaign's most frustrating moments ([spoiler]Claire has maybe 2 run-ins with Mr. X and Sherry's section is way more engaging than Ada's hacking tool BS[/spoiler].
[*]This game was INFINITELY more enjoyable on a second playthrough. This is partially due to playing as Claire and largely due to doing what I could to get around inventory bloat, bullet sponges, and backtracking.
[*]Shooting enemies just enough to stun them and run by isn't nearly as satisfying as killing them but it helps hide the glaring bullet sponge issue. I also realized shooting them and running away feels so wrong because in old games the damage done to enemies reset once you left the room. In this game damage is persistent.
[*]Craft ammo ASAP if the recipe sounds useful. If you try to conserve these for later like old resident evil games taught you, you'll bloat your inventory and drive yourself insane with all the backtracking.
[*]I have no regrets on just looking up the lock combinations up on my second playthrough. This avoids a TON of backtracking and inventory bloat due to carrying and developing film or finding combinations in notes across the map.
[*]Knowing which enemies or phases of enemies are largely invulnerable to bullets makes the game infinitely less frustrating. I finished Claire's scenario with an absurd amount of ammo left over and on my first run as Leon I was cutting it close.
[/list]

You couldn't ask for a better remake of game. That said, you also couldn't possibly ask people to pay a full AAA price tag, on a game with as much content as one from 1998....

Resident Evil 2 is remade beautifully into the current gen. But do not go thinking this is as far as a reboot, for it's closer to just simply a remaster. The classic from 1998 has simply been brought into the current gen and that is it. Few minor changes to accommodate this and that's all. Leon's full playthrough takes around 8 hours to complete, and here's the catch, Claire's campaign is the exact same, re-used campaign, with only a few minor changes here and there, like different weapons or enemy/boss spawns, and of course a different perspective on what is still the same story with just a different, accompanying side character. So you're paying €60 for 8 hours of content, and then only another 8 hours of the exact same content, just with a few twists....

It's a shame what is still a brilliant remake, is being cheeky enough to ask for what other games provide up to 60 hours worth of content and more.. Now, Resident Evil 2, besides the one campaign served twice depending on what you prefer to have between your legs, does have some side content. Such as three sort of mini side-quests where you play as characters from the background of the main story, trying to escape whatever situation they're in, in an almost speedrun style of gameplay. There's like 20 minutes of gameplay there... And then there's the classic 'new game +' option which slightly changes the start and end of the campaigns but nothing more....

All in all, this game is not nearly worth the asking price. It's brilliantly done, and really rings true to the classic survival-horror/puzzle genre. This game actually succeeds where Resident Evil 7 miserably failed. It's genuinely scary at times and has a decent mix of that Resident Evil action and overall vibe. But still, for what amounts to less than 10 hours of true content, and replayable content that amounts to nothing more than a grinding feel as you attempt to unlock everything... You can't possibly pay full price for this remake. 

Wait till it drops below €40. Even for die hard Resident Evil fans, do not waste your money till it drops in price..

Resident Evil 2 (2019) is a superb re-imagination of the survival horror classic. Capcom managed to keep intact all aspects of what makes a good resident evil game: inventory management, puzzles, non-linear environments and backtracking.

The first half of the game takes place in the police department and for me its easily the best part of the game due to its very open-ended nature.

The gameplay feels more modern: there is no fixed camera angles and tank controls. While I did enjoy tank controls back in the day, they existed more due to limitations of the hardware from when the classics games where released. Instead, this game creates its tense atmosphere by limiting you visibility with a darker RPD, where most of the lights are out, and through the use of flashlights. Also, having an over the shoulder camera is not as useful as it may seems because of the small and claustrophobic environments.

New mechanics were also introduced, such as the ability to block windows in the RPD to prevent zombies from entering and a dismembering mechanic. Shooting a zombie in the arm will make them easier to dodge, while shooting in the legs will make them slower, adding depth to the encounters since shooting in the head in not your only option anymore.

The story remains mostly unchanged from the original game, despite curiously not becoming canon in-place of the original, like the remake of the first Resident Evil.

My only critique of this game was the implementation of the two scenarios. In the original, while playing through the first scenario, some of your actions would have consequences in the second scenario. Also, Leon and Claire would interact multiple times during the game and you could see both sides of this interactions. In the remake sadly none of this happens. The second scenario is much shorter and less inspired that the first (and you could even say 'main') scenario.

In conclusion, this was a very solid experience and I recommend to all Resident Evil fans that were waiting for a return to the survival horror roots of the franchise and to everyone who likes the survival horror genre.

[h1]"Hope I don't have to write a report on this!"[/h1] 

[b]O que é Resident Evil 2 Remake?[/b]

 Resident Evil 2 é um jogo de sobrevivência feito pela Capcom onde você controla Leon ou Claire e tenta escapar de Raccoon City que está infestada de mortos vivos. Aliás, é um remake do jogo original lançado em 1998.

[b]Gameplay:[/b]

 Em Resident Evil 2 Remake você escolhe o seu personagem e devido a alguns acontecimentos você acaba parando na delegacia de polícia de uma pequena cidade, você então precisa se virar para descobrir o que está acontecendo, com poucas balas, uma arma muito básica e uma mochilinha pequena você começa a sua jornada. 

 Independente de quem escolher você pode ter certeza que algo não vai mudar nesse game, o ambiente assustador é igual tanto para Claire como para Leon, uma coisa que me chama a atenção é o fato do "gore" ser bem visível, se você atira na perna do zumbi ou no braço, dependendo do dano a parte atingida pode cair ou até ficar deformada, as marcas de tiros, facadas, explosões são bem notáveis. São inúmeros detalhes que deixam o jogo mais bonito, seja pelo gráfico fantástico ou mesmo pela modo de jogar mais lento, mais realista, aliás, realista no sentido de que você se sente mais humano em Resident Evil 2 em comparação aos últimos títulos lançados, me refiro a Resident Evil 6, 5 e 4. É muito mais fácil ser morto nesse game, qualquer morto vivo pode te matar sem problemas se você não prestar atenção em pequenos detalhes como ter munição suficiente, ou até mesmo armas secundárias no inventário como uma faca, granada, flash, etc.

 O jogo é cheio de quebra-cabeças, você vai precisar ir e vir em vários lugares, pegar chaves, achar melhorias para suas armas, abrir cofres com combinações escondidas pelo mapa para poder ganhar mais espaço no seu inventário e claro que você faz tudo isso tendo que levar em consideração diversos monstros pelo mapa incluindo o famoso "Mr.X". Agora, se você me perguntar que infernos é Mr.X? Meu amigo provavelmente você não está ligado nos diversos memes feitos com o "garotão" pela internet, enfim, Mr.X é um Tyrant ou seja, ele foi criado para perseguir sobreviventes e eliminar evidências, ou seja, VOCÊ. 
 A sensação de correr pelos vários corredores sendo perseguido por um brutamonte que não morre nem a pau é agoniante, a música que começa a tocar no momento em que você encontra ele é muito bem feita e deixa uma sensação muito ruim no jogador, os passos do Tyrant podem ser ouvidos de longe e te ajudam a evitá-lo, outra coisa que achei fantástica e amedrontadora ao mesmo tempo é o fato de você poder ouvir quando o Tyrant abre portas em outra sala perto de você, o jogador sabe que está sendo perseguido, então é preciso levar em conta inúmeros fatores enquanto se tem um objetivo em mente. 

 Digamos que você precisa de uma chave para abrir a porta B, mas para conseguir a tal chave você precisa achar uma ferramenta para destruir as correntes da porta A que fica em um quarto do outro lado do mapa para só então ter a chave em suas mãos e fazer todo o caminho até a porta B novamente, isso é claro contando com monstros, jumpscares (sustos), gerenciamento de inventário (Se sua mochila ficar cheia de itens você se ferrou) e um Tyrant enorme correndo atrás, não é mole não meu consagrado.

 Quando você termina o game com Leon por exemplo, é liberado um modo chamado de "Second Run" algo como um New Game +, é a mesma campanha por assim dizer só que vista aos olhos do personagem no qual você não jogou da primeira vez, o jogador terminou o game na primeira vez com Leon por exemploe agora vai poder jogar com a Claire nesse modo, lá as coisas serão um pouco diferentes, bosses mudam e os mesmos caminhos são percorridos com outros objetivos em mente, alguns puzzles (quebra cabeças) são resolvidos de outra forma e o game não muda completamente, mas fica parecendo um lado diferente da história.

 Existem diversas outras "mini" histórias para você jogar quando termina a campanha principal, a mais divertida na minha opinião é chamada de "O quarto sobrevivente" onde você é um soldado da umbrella que ficou para trás em Raccoon City e precisa chegar até o seu resgate. Algumas dessas mini histórias são algo como "E se..." Ou seja, personagens que já morreram na campanha principal poderiam ter sobrevivido, ou seja, é você que tentará mudar isso, são modos de jogo mais simples e mais difíceis se me permite dizer, em um dos modos é possível ver mortos vivos usando mochilas, quando você abate algum deles eles derrubam itens importantes como munição, armas, etc.

[b]Pontos positivos[/b]

*O cenário é bem sombrio e bota medo, ou seja, a proposta do game foi muito bem feita.
* A trilha sonora é muito bem elaborada e ajuda muito no clima aterrorizante do jogo.
* Qualquer erro te leva a morte
* Você precisa gerenciar muito bem o seu inventário para poupar tempo e evitar dores de cabeça.
* Nunca tive tanto medo de um cara enorme com chapéu na minha vida.
* O game possuí vários modos diferentes (reimaginações e mini histórias diferentes) para você rejogar.
* Os gráficos são de tirar o fôlego, não gosto de falar de gráficos, nem detalhar tal coisa, não considero gráficos algo importante para recomendar ou não um game, porém, é importante dizer que Resident Evil 2 remake fez um trabalho fantástico quanto a esse aspecto.
* Sinceramente não encontrei nenhum bug, ou pelo menos que eu pudesse notar.

[b]Pontos negativos[/b]

* O jogo pode não rodar extremamente bem, pode haver algumas pequenas quedas de frames dependendo do seu sistema operacional, eu praticamente não tive problemas com isso, mas em alguns momentos era possível notar a mudança de frames.

[b]Vale a pena?[/b]

 Recomendo sem problema algum, a proposta do game é de um mundo sombrio e escuro, talvez até claustrofóbico em alguns momentos, se a intenção era assustar o jogador e fazer com que ele ficasse sobre pressão, os desenvolvedores conseguiram e muito bem. Mesmo que você já tenha jogado o game original eu posso afirmar que vale a pena, jogue novamente porque com certeza você vai amar, acredito que até aqui Resident Evil 2 é o trabalho mais bonito feito pela Capcom recentemente.

Somehow manages to not only be better than the original, but also somehow manages to tie with RE4 as the best game in the entire series. This is less of a remake and more of a reimagining, as it only takes the base story and set pieces of the original, but presents the entire thing in a very different way.

It retains the Metroidvania-esque map layout of the original and merges it with the over-the-shoulder shooting of RE4, only heavily refined (no tank controls to be found here). Like RE7, there's also a heavier focus on the horror aspects of the series and has the strongest writing, acting, and cinematic storytelling the series has ever seen.

Don't get me wrong, there's still some Jill Sandwich cheese to be found, in typical RE fashion. But it's heavily toned down, only used sparingly, and it's only for the better. It also only turns into an action game at the end, which is how it should be - overcoming fear and turning it into empowerment.

If you've never played a RE game, I'd strongly suggest starting with this one, if not with RE4/RE7. The story is for the larger part entirely standalone, as it doesn't rely too heavily on the events of RE1, and they got rid of the more controversial aspects of the older titles gameplay wise, streamlining the entire thing.

REmake 2 is a return to form, in a more modern perspective. If you were a fan of the original game on PSX, you'll love this. 

The RPD feels like a real living & breathing location, and the level design is superb; playing through the game for the first time, while exploring and solving puzzles, feels like being a kid in a candy store. The atmosphere gives off chilling and spooky vibes just like the original, and Capcom have figured out ways to create jump scares even while in a third person perspective.

The combat is par for the course and satisfying, but what really makes it shine is the behavior of the zombies, you can strategically shoot or cut off certain limbs so that you can save bullets, or just straight up turn them into giblets. The zombies are quite scary as well, especially when you dismember them and they continue to move relentlessly towards you; this game has the best zombies of all time.

The character design was pretty polarizing on release, but I've personally grown to like Leon, Claire's, and Ada's designs, their outfits and style are grounded in reality and their facial expressions and voice lines properly relay to you when they're scared, shocked, or in pain. Additionally, you can also swap Leon and Claire's costumes with other ones in the menu if you wish to do so, I stuck with their standard outfits though.

The graphics are amazing save for the wonky screen-space reflections, though they are still worth enabling because in certain situations they really make a scene pop, but the game will continue to look great years afterwards regardless of that.

One thing I do wish could be better is the music, I much prefer the music in the original game to this one, because it acts as a better backdrop to the general gameplay, but the music in the remake has its moments as well. You can enable the classic music if you own the deluxe edition or have purchased it as DLC, but I believe this is something that should have been included in the game for free. 

There's a lot more I could say, but in short, Resident Evil 2 Remake is my personal favorite, with the first Remake being my second, I strongly recommend playing it if you are a fan of Resident Evil or horror games in general, it's a powerful contender for game of the year.

[h1]Pros:[/h1]

+ Making the game third person was a good move IMO. I don't like tank controls at all (Although I respect fixed camera angles). 

+ Completely new puzzles and didn't re-use any from the original. Which makes this game a completely new game and not just a remake. More like a re-imagining.

+ New areas in the police station. The sewers and the [spoiler]Umbrella Facility[/spoiler] are basically 100% original levels too. 

+ Graphics. Easily one of the best looking games this generation. 

+ Soundtrack. Mainly the Mr.X theme. The rest ranges from good to serviceable. 

+ The police station is so well done. It connects together and flows really well.

+ The classic Resident Evil puzzles of seeing something you can't open then going forward and finding the thing you need so you go back, is "back" and it's better than ever, IMO even surpasses the original. It's not confusing, but it doesn't hold your hand. Really well done.

+ Zombies sometimes wake up after they went down which can lead to tension and stress when visiting old areas. At first I thought it was annoying but I liked it with time.

+ Atmosphere. It's one of the best in the business. 

+ Scary. Does have a lot of intense moments with the combination of zombies and lickers being in the same room or lickers and Mr.X. You don't know if you should run from the zombies/Mr.X and get hit by the lickers or move quietly and risk being hit by zombies/Mr.X.

+ Making Mr.X more prominent than the original was a great choice. He is so awesome...... in a horrifying way. 

+ Bullets leave holes in enemies and limbs can even be torn off.

+ Free DLC and Retro Skins.

+ I love what they did with Knives, Grenades and Flash Bangs. They are now a mix of the sub weapons of Resident Evil Remake and their normal uses in other games. You can still knife and throw grenades and flash bangs but if an enemy holds you, You can use it to escape without damage. If you use a knife you can still grab it if it isn't broken after you down the enemy. This is amazing.

+ A bunch of quality of life improvements like placing a red tick on an item after it is no more needed like opening all the doors for this key. Now you can throw them knowing you don't need it. Also rooms will now turn blue, from red, to signify that you collected all items within the room and finished it's puzzle. Although combining weapons and ammo in the inventory is missing which is not a quality of life

+ The idea of being able to shoot while moving, but for you to be accurate and do more damage your have to stay still and slow down your shots is genius. It's smooth unlike RE4 and RE5 but still scary unlike RE6 because you still need to stay still if you want to make shots count.

+ I like how they made the films actually useful. Before they would give you lore but honestly that's a lot of pain in the a** just for lore.


[h1]Cons:[/h1]

- I would have liked for there to have been a way to dispose of "sleeping" zombies, Like what Resident Evil Remake did. Burning the bodies so they don't come back. Even if it was in short supply. 

- I wish zombies had normal swipe attacks and not just grabs. Feels cheep at times when you get grabbed and grabbed one after another, even if it's less often than grabs. 

- Voice acting. It ranges from OK to so bad it's distracting and completely breaks the immersion. Except for Lieutenant Marvin Branagh. Claire tries too. Leon & Ada are [i]really[/i] bad though.
 
- The dialogue is meh. It's not terrible but it feels like a non native speaker wrote this, and this is coming from a non native speaker. 

- Screen Space reflections are broken in this game, it gives these weird reflections that change with the characters movement, Only happens in main lobby though. And the game lacks MSAA Anti-Aliasing (best anti-aliasing for less edges with minimal input lag).

- This game does change some of the characters from the original, Like making Leon more naive and the chief less deceiving. Some people like it, some people don't. 

- Zapping system is gone. You can't pick and choose between items and leave the rest for your second run like in the original.

- Leon and Claire didn't speak to each other a lot and only met 3 times from beginning to end and only in cutscenes. I miss this from the original where they met in person 3 times and talked a lot on the radio to give each other updates and requests giving a feeling of a co-operative experience. The remake did try replicating this with notes lying around from the other character in your second run but it doesn't really work.

- There are contradictions and inconsistencies between your first run (A) and your second (B). For example, In (B) you go around doing a lot of the same puzzles that the other character should have done in (A). I can excuse this since they have to use the same place and without puzzles you would just walk through the game, (even though the original did have some playthrough specific puzzles), Though it is different enough, with different enemy placements, guns, items box locations, rooms (since you get a different key than the other character which opens different rooms but the original had more different rooms) and Mr.X is changed a bit that it feels like a twist on the experience. I can excuse gameplay contradictions for the reasons I explained above. The original had the same problem, It still stings though. Story and cutscene inconsistencies and contradictions are another things though, For example:

1) The first and second boss for both playthroughs are the exact same boss and they enter and leave the room the same way (by distroying a path and then that path gets repaired the second playthrough to be destroyed again) 

2) Apparently, [s]Annet Berkins[/s] dies 2 times, 1 in each playthrough in the same cutscene.

3) Sherry isn't seen in Leon's playthrough.

4) There isn't any moment like in the original where when you play the second playthrough some things start to make sense like how the [s]helecopter crashed[/s] or how the other character was there when this happened and stuff like that.

5) Doorways and pathways are locked and destroyed in one playthrough but is repaired magically when playing with the other character.

6) Little details are missing like the train being their for both playthroughs, even though the other character just used it. In the original, you had to call the train in the second playthrough. 

I just wish there were subtle changes to hint that another person was here, Like how you can block windows for the other character in the original game. Of course, Completely new places and puzzles to do for the second character would have been fantastic. Even though the original didn't have it, The remake was a chance for the developers to change it and it's not an excuse. 


- Bossfights are the same stuff over and over, Melee brutes that swipe at you and you have to run and shoot. Wish there had been more variety in the bosses (In the bosses them selves as in another person/stage of transformation and in the way it is defeated). The original did change it up more by giving different bosses to the different characters.

Resident Evil 2 is a remake of the game which was released in 1998. I never played the original version so this was a completely new experience for me.

The good

•	Play as either Claire Redfield or Leon Kennedy. After you complete the game with one character, you can play a new game plus mode with the other character where the story will be slightly different, you’ll meet different NPCs and find different weapons.
•	Excellent survival horror gameplay. Every enemy is legitimately dangerous if you don’t respect them, even the basic zombies. Ammo and health pickups are limited, so you have to be careful not to waste anything. Sometimes its best to avoid enemies and conserve ammo.
•	Enemies include zombies, lickers, dogs, a couple of strange mutants, and multiple bosses (who, in true Resident Evil style, just won’t stay dead).
•	Good weapon variety including handgun, magnum, SMG, shotgun, grenade launcher, shock rifle, flamethrower and minigun. Plus secondary weapons such as knife, flashbang and frag grenade that can be used to escape from enemies who grab you.
•	Some weapons and upgrades, like weapon mods and pouches to increase inventory size, are earned by solving puzzles, which rewards you for exploring.
•	Interesting locations including the Raccoon City police station, a nearby orphanage and an underground laboratory. The graphics look amazing, and the areas where the lights are out and you’re exploring with a flashlight helps to create a horror atmosphere.
•	Good story and great voice acting.
•	Controls are fully rebindable and work great with mouse and keyboard.
•	I didn’t suffer any bugs, crashes or framerate issues.

The bad

•	Inventory system is occasionally annoying because you’re not allowed to simply put an item on the floor and pick it up again later. Any item you drop is discarded forever, which means you sometimes have to go back to a storage box to free up space to pick up a quest item that needs to be used on an object 10 feet away.
•	£45 feels a bit expensive for a game that takes 16 hours to beat twice.

The recommendation

Resident Evil 2 is an amazing game, a must play for every fan of the Resident Evil franchise, or survival horror games in general. I actually think this is my new favourite Resident Evil game (I’ve previously played 0,1,4,5,6,7, Revelations 1&2). Don’t hesitate to pick it up next time its on sale.

TL;DR This game is an easy 9/10. It scared the crap out of me. Every enemy is a threat that you cannot ignore. The atmosphere, the graphics, the gameplay, it is near perfection. Not only is the a faithful remake of the fantastic original, it will easily standalone as a classic. It is 100% worth the full $60 price tag and I don't regret a single penny spent. Should you see it on sale at any point, buy it because it is a freaking steal.

In-depth review:

The original Resident Evil 2 is one of my all time favorite games from one of my all time favorite franchises. However, like most long time fans, I began to despise the series with every game *after* the legendary RE4. It wasn't until Resident Evil Revelations 2 that the series showed potential again, then with Resident Evil 7, hope. When Resident Evil 2 remake was announced, and even more so, the amazing trailer, the hype... the hype was unreal for EVERYONE. I'm happy to say, this game surpassed my expectations. I tried going to in this game with as little bias and as much skepticism as possible. Regardless, the game blew my mind. 

Gameplay and Atmosphere: 

I'm combing these two, because when it comes to horror games, atmosphere should have an affect on the gameplay. It is superb on both ends. The controls are fluid and more similar to a typical third person shooter as opposed to the classic tank controls (that I know and love). You are very limited in what you can do, as your characters aren't the super heroes that they become in later games. You can walk/run, shoot annnd that's about it. That's how it should be, you dodge by running away and keeping your distance. Enemies are bullet sponges, your handgun is ALMOST useless as a weapon to kill with as enemies can take 8-20 HEADSHOTS to put down (luckily you can disable zombies by shooting their legs and/or arms off, it's up to you to decide if it's worth it). Ammo is incredibly limited so you have to save it for emergencies, running away is almost always a better option, assuming you are able to. Until you get more powerful weapons, fighting is not recommended (as it should be). The atmosphere in this game is on par with the legendary Resident Evil 1 remake. It's dark, it's eerie, it's forboding and more importantly it keeps you on edge and makes you hope that noise you heard around the corner wasn't something that wants to kill you. This game has made me NEED to take breaks because the stress of being low on ammo and knowing what I have to deal with outside the safe room was too much for me. 

The Difficulty: 

This game has 3 difficulties; Assisted, Standard, Hardcore.
I'm in the minority here. I fully recommend on your FIRST play through... play this game on Hardcore difficulty. It's what I did. 
Ammo is even more scarce, enemies deal far more damage, and most importantly, limited saves. On Hardcore mode you must use the Ink Ribbon items to save your game at the type writer, and Ink Ribbons are finite. Also, if you die, it's back to the last time you saved, no check points (so for example if you die near the end of the game without saving at all, you'll have to start all over.) 
This adds SO MUCH tension, fear and consequence to the gameplay. Hardcore difficulty is tough, but damn if you're patient and careful, it's fair. This was the best gaming experience I've had in a long time. 

Graphics: 

Not much to say here. Beautiful. The games well optimized. My computer is pretty old, but at medium-high settings with a consistent 60FPS.

Story:

It's decent. Characters are a lot more believable and more fleshed out (Marvin's really cool here). Still, it's nothing special. However, in the flaws section of this review, I will explain why the story does not make sense in some places. 

Flaws:

In classic RE2, you can play as Leon and Claire in both the A and B campaigns, each campaign is ALMOST completely different from each other. You can use each character in either campaign. So you can do Leon A then Claire B to get the true ending, or Claire A then Leon B then the true ending. Technically giving your 4 campaigns. Thank fully this returns in REmake 2. However, the difference between the campaigns is noticeably less than the original. The first half of the campaigns is the only real difference between, for example, Claire A and Claire B. After that, it's indistinguishable. Also, each campaign reuses several bosses, and routes (something absent from the original) which is not only repetitive, but also makes 0 sense for the story (some characters die twice). It's not enough to make me dislike the game, but it is the sole thing holding this game back from a 10/10.


Final Thoughts: 

This game's a masterpiece and I know it sold well, which means Capcom will likely make a Resident Evil 3 remake (I hope so). 
Easy 9/10. Buy this game so that Capcom hears our wallets and knows they did this game right. Capcom's on a roll and I knew that one day, they'd rise from their hole that they dug. Thank goodness they did. I went from completing Leon A on Hardcore in 16 hours to beating all 4 campaigns in under 2 hours each, getting S+ rank for each campaign. That's how invested I was.

If you played Claire A, and you took the machine gun from the sewer locker, it would not be there for Leon B. I wouldn't mind a different system, like Zombies started moving faster or becoming more frequent. But hitting a Zombie with 8 perfect headshots to take them down feels completely unsatisfying.
