In the January of 1998 (unless you lived in Europe at the time which in that case, [i]April[/i]), Capcom unleashed onto the gaming world the follow up to the 1996 big PlayStation hit, [i]Resident Evil[/i]. A game that defined the survival horror genre much in same way the FPS genre had been defined by [i]Wolfenstein 3D[/i] and [i]DOOM[/i] 3 years prior. Though while [i]RE1[/i] focused on a small team of elite police officers known as S.T.A.R.S. attempting to escape a mansion filled with zombies and all kinds of monsters, [i]RE2[/i] brought the horrors of the Spencer Mansion to Raccoon City itself, with rookie police officer Leon S. Kennedy and college student/younger sister of Chris Redfield Claire Redfield caught in the middle, trapped in the RPD station fighting for survival and discovering the truth behind the outbreak. 

Much like first game, [i]RE2[/i] was acclaimed by both critics and gamers alike and is often considered one of the best games for the PS1 (but then [i]every[/i] game in the series released for the PS1 except [i]Survivor[/i] are considered among the best PS1 games ever made). That is unless you grew up in my generation which means we were all ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ infants when it came out and most likely didn't even know [i]Resident Evil[/i] was even a thing until about (in my experience anyway) well into the franchise's life into the GameCube/PS2 era and/or when the first couple of the live-action movies were coming out. But despite my personal experience with original [i]RE2[/i] is the PSN release for the PS3 20 years after the initial release, I can say it still holds up well. But enough of the original because good chance you've come here to see if the remake is either up to the praise its gotten since it finally launched in January, ooooor a steaming pile of s*** that isn't even worth the bargain bin price. 

Well I can say as someone who's played since launch that this game is [i]fantastic[/i]. Already a huge GOTY contender in my book. Everything's here for [i]RE[/i] fans new and old. The classic [i]RE[/i] formula of the older games with the gameplay style of the more modern titles (basically it has the over-the-shoulder and adjusting difficulty of 4 with the controls of 6). Using the RE engine, this game looks fantastic and even borderline photo-realistic at times (in fact the closest released games I've seen come close to this level of graphical quality this year so far being the Pirates of the Caribbean world in [i]Kingdom Hearts 3[/i] and [i]Metro: Exodus[/i]). The environments, the characters, the monsters, and well just about everything looks fantastic with great lighting. The game also runs very well and in general feels like Capcom developed it for the PC first (especially since for me, gameplay videos showing aiming with a controller made it look clunky and not as good). Especially since the graphics options also show how much VRAM the game will use based on the settings/presets chosen with the game even giving you a warning about possible graphical glitches if the settings start to get close to using the max amount of VRAM available.

Now the basic story of the [i]RE2[/i] remake is pretty much the same as the original game, focusing on Leon and Claire as they try to escape the zombie-infested Raccoon City through the police station and happen to run into dark secrets about the outbreak in the process. I won't spoil anything but what I will say is that some sections are completely changed or reinvented to fit the more dark and (slightly) more realistic tone the devs were going for. And the music by god is the music good, sure while it ultimately doesn't match up to the original (which through the deluxe edition or a optional DLC, the audio can be changed to use the original music and menu sounds), it still does a good job at setting the tone it needs to set. With my personal favorite being the chase theme for Mr. X (which unlike the original game, appears in both scenarios instead of just scenario B) when he will no doubt pursue you throughout RPD. And the end-game rewards definitely make some of the hassles of playing on higher difficulties worth it in the end.

Now does this mean the remake is perfect with no flaws whatsoever? Welllllll no. For starters, both the A and B scenarios don't really have that much different from each other and Leon and Claire run into each less frequently than they did in the original game (like there's about 3 instances where they meet face-to-face in the entire story in each scenario). And the B scenario's ending being pretty much a copy and paste with the only difference being the character and what weapon you used on the boss prior (though admittedly, that was also the case in the original as well). And the enemies can be bullet-spongy at times but it's something often up to the adapting difficulty.

The TL;DR of it all is, buy this game. It's really really fun.

If you were a fan of the original, you will enjoy this remake. However, don't expect a nostalgic blast from the past. Enough has been changed here that I didn't really get a nostalgic feeling from playing. Room layouts are different, entire new areas have been added, items and puzzles have been changed, and one villain who had only a few appearances in the original has a much more prominent (and incredibly annoying) presence here.

The game is gorgeous and audio is top notch. The arguably awkward camera angles from the original have been replaced with a third person over-the-shoulder view. You can wander from room to room seamlessly without any loading screens.

Despite the upgrade to a modern feel, there are some things that stand out as just frustrating. The game has an auto-save feature but unfortunately the checkpoints are too few and far between. Did you die after picking up 8 items from the adjacent room? Sorry, you have to restart and pick up all of those items again. I lost count of how many times I took a break from playing because I didn't feel like doing tedious tasks all over again after dying.

Finally, the boss fights are just awful. Too often the bosses charge at you swiftly, while your character can only sluggishly run away in a feeble attempt to avoid getting hit. Then when you die from being too slow, the game offers to turn on "aim assist" - a nice gesture, if it would even help at all.

It's a great game and as a Resident Evil fan I will get many entertaining hours out of it. But for my taste, it could have been just a bit more faithful to the original and modernised a bit more by allowing more checkpoints.

Resident Evil 2 is a full remake of the 1998 Classic ps1 title, and does a fantastic job of it. This honestly should be amongst the standards of how remakes are judged from this point onward. It changes just enough to be modernized but doesn't make itself unrecognizable from its original iteration.

What do I mean exactly? First and easiest example of this is the perspective and controls. The original being in fixed flat images to simulate the feel of a 3D environment, obviously something had to be changed for today, they perfectly rebuilt the world in 3D models and gave a 3rd person over the shoulder perspective. I know what everyone is thinking "oh great... they turned it into Resident Evil 4" not exactly thank god. While it shares its perspective and basic game-play with RE4, the game-play itself is a lot less action orientated, centering around evasion and actually bringing the sense of danger back to the single zombie. You cannot defend yourself from a grapple move unless you have a defense sub weapon, so no "counter waltz" dancing from one end of the map to the next like in RE4. You will actually need to play intelligently. Also enemies got redesigns to their mechanics to make things more interesting. Its also genuinely nice to have a knife and not feel you've got a worthless hunk of metal in your hands like the originals.

One downside(?) 3 core enemies got cut from this version of the game; The crows, The moth, and the Spiders. To be honest I am glad the crows got cut from the game otherwise without a massive overhaul to their mechanics (like adding in huge moments where they stood still to get a chance to shoot them) they would have just been annoyances to the game. I do kinda miss the spiders and moths but I can't say I'd have liked to see a spider as detailed as the ones in this game. So while this negative is convenient to me, its still a negative and I wish the game was complete with all the enemies.

The game also got modernized in story elements as well, some things got streamlined and changed, most noted Ada got a section that more melds with her modern iterations of her, and Sherry's section is now more a puzzle mode in a band new area to the game. Overall it flexes but doesn't break the games known canon and is quite acceptable as it is.

The music of the classic resident evils have always been an important part of them, and this is one bit I feel the remake does fall flat on its face. The remakes' music blurs into the background and is extremely forgettable. If you have the original tracks dlc it feels a better even if a little tacked on, but kinda sucks you need to shell out $3 to fix this problem.

Overall this game kind of set a new standard for how remakes should be handled. I hope to see more remakes of this quality in the future, proper remakes instead of ports or "HD" upscales.

To start off I would like to say that I am not really a fan of the resident evil franchise nor am I well read on its lore, the only other games I have played before this one is RE4 and RE6 and to be honest I'm not a big fan of either of those games (especially 6). At the point of this review I am yet to play the B scenarios but I have completed both Leon and Claire's A scenarios. That being said I absolutely adore this game, its a breath of fresh air for survival horror titles and is genuinely one of the most immersive games I have ever played. In this review I will talk about the two key elements to this game, horror/immersion and gameplay.

Firstly horror, obviously horror is subjective but this game is honestly one of the scariest ive ever played (right next to Amnesia). The first few hours of the game are tense and when you don't know where to go or what to do you find yourself terrified of what lies behind the next door, just when I thought I was becoming accustomed to the mechanics of the zombie's I encountered Mr X which I can honestly say is one of the most pants ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ amazing moments in the game. admittedly on a second play through I wasn't the slightest bit scared (apart from when facing the Ivy monsters) and Mr X becomes more of an annoyance than an actual threat. To sum up the horror, its great when going in blind but after a while the game becomes less scary (which is to be expected when you become desensitized to its scares).

The gameplay of RE2 is really centred around two elements, puzzles and combat. The puzzles in the game are rather long winded and reward people who have a keen eye (however they are not overly complicated), for example you may inspect an object that seems useless only to find out it has a hidden use (such as the stars badge which is essential in picking up either Leon's Lightning Hawk or Claire's Sub Machine Gun).

The gameplay is outstanding in this game as all of the mechanics piece together to provide a challenging but fair experience. Ammo conservation is everything in this game as zombies take a hell of a lot of bullets to kill however they can be "knocked out" in relatively little (they will only be knocked down for a certain period of time) this makes strategy an essential part of RE2 as in some rooms that you will be exploring a lot, you know its probably in your best interest to clear out enemies so that you have less chance of being bit by them when back tracking. The combination of enemy types also make for interesting gameplay as the Lickers can be completely avoided by simply walking past them however if you are being chased by Mr X while also running though a Licker infested area you will be as good as dead, as running triggers the Lickers to attack (dealing high amounts of damage), this once again ties back into strategy as you must decide which Lickers are worth clearing out and which are best left alone. 

There is much more I could talk about but I think it is best experienced first hand, I highly recommend this game.

ok so it's been a while since i wrote a game review  on steam.   but i just had to do this one. After countless runs and many hours i can say i'm definitely ready to review this game.  

The amazing 

Graphics -   the graphics look  awe inspiring.  don't believe the graphic reccomendations though.  if you got 8 gig video ram , go ahead and jack the texture quality to the max.  i'm running every thing maxed out on my old system @4k interlaced  setting  and it runs smooth at 45-55 fps.  with only a few cutscense dipping in the 30's or below. this is one of the best games visually  out there today. 
 
camera/Gun mechanics - I was skeptical when they announced it would use a RE4 style camera with more action based gun mechanics.  that said i was impressed when i got to play it. it works , it just works so well it's beautiful.  not an action game here  , but definitely good mechanics the addition of the timed aiming mechanism  also brings back the old feel of the original game where you have to stop and shoot  if you want to get real accurate.  it's just nothing more to say about this aspect it blew me away.  

Free DLC - and lots of it ... nuff said

The Good 

Unlocks - tons of unlocking potential means heavy heavy replay value.  durring replays  the game never feels stale or old.  there's just so much content to unlock in this game it's almost never ending fun. almost. 

Puzzles - the puzzles are pretty fresh  , but definitely bring us back to the 90's when RE was all about those puzzles , that said most puzzles are easy enough  , with only a few posing any real thought  to crack them.  so meh  , but a good meh , i just wish the game utilized them more and had some with greater challenge , but what is there certainly is good.  

The not so good  and meh 

Deluxe edition  price versus what you get  -    The deluxe edition cost a pretty penny  over the regular game , but as far as content  it doesn't really deliver.  the hand gun you get is just a reskin of the first  infinite ammo gun you unlock , minus the ammo part , it's not very powerful or even game changing , just cosmetic , i found myself never using it again after the first run. the costumes are nice but feel like they should have been base game stuff along side the unlock costumes.   last but not least the original game's music , this should have been part of the base game  from the get go.  for this reason alone i  reccomend  people get the deluxe edition but ouch does that price sting.  

Story Changes and missing bits  - (spoiler warnings)    The dialouge is good the voice actors are great , but the story feels less explained and less deep than the original game's.   you never get a clear picture of how the out break started , though they do show birkin  inject himself in flash backs and on the video. the two touchiest pieces of this were the aformentioned videos,   in the original game you find a video from the commando team that umburella  sent in , it clearly showed  them trying to take birkin's work  and then shows how they opened fire on him (and the virus container he was holding ) releasing the virus into the sewers causing the whole mess the game is in.  in this remake however  they only show  the point where this team attacked birkin and not how they were at fault for causing the outbreak itself.   That said there are several other examples of where the story lacks compared to the old one, but there are a few examples of where it was better (ada and leon's romance-y  bits).   however the thing i dislike the most  with the remake story wise is how out of touch Leon and claire are with each other , in the original they constantly ran into each other  and often contacted each other on a radio . in the remake they run into each other just one time before the end and that's it , no radio  not meet ups , and this brings me to my next point.   Continuity is all over the place in this one.   in the original you got a continuously flowing story by playing Clair A and then Leon B (or vice versa)  with thing in one campiagn affecting the B run  for the other character. While in the remake this mechanic is gone , and the A and B runs just feel like an alternate dimension with no connection tot eh A run at all. It's a developer oversight that makes the remake  lack heart in soul (and replayability) in many of the places where the original delivered. 

The ugly - 

NOthing .... nothing about this game is trash , ugly or terribly bad.  while it does stumble a litle in continuity , this can be easily looked over for  every thing it does right.  i give it a 9.5/10  score .  i definitely reccomend the game even the deluxe edition.

I am a long time fan of the (older) RE games, and RE2R is a strong remake.  However, it has many glaring flaws that become grossly apparent after the initial playthrough.

First of all, I don't really see this game as a remake per se, more of a "reimagining" of the original.  This is good because it does seemlessly connect to the first REmake, but it also creates a lot more plotholes in the context of the series at large.  Hopefully this leads to a further remake of RE3 (and if God willing, Outbreak).  

Graphics are great and the gameplay is to RE what MGSV was to MGS: the new standard.  Although, I wish there was a subtle dodge mechanic included, like with Revelations.  Atmosphere is very well done.  However, the lab is missing aspects that made the original great, and it just doesn't make a whole lot of sense (you're telling me the entire G-Virus development took place in two small rooms?).  The original OST option is a much better experience, but really, it should have been included.  

Enemy design is excellent, and the ability to blow zombies into pieces is what RE4 should have been in the first place before they nerfed the final design.  The Ivy Zombies designed as Regenerador clones is inferior to the original design though.  Mr. X is done very well.  

Characters are also well done, and the plot itself I feel is presented much more coherently than in the original, more or less.  Except for Chief Irons, while creepy is certainly no comparison to his original take as a ruthless psychopath resembling Gregory Peck in The Boys from Brazil.  It's also somewhat shallow: for instance, Leon doesn't even know who Sherry is when he meets her at the ending, unlike in the original where he runs into Claire numerous times.  

The biggest flaw in this game became apparent after the very first run: all of the four scenarios in the main campaign are essentially identical.  I do not understand how Capcom could not have transitioned the very satisfying and fully complementary scenario system from the original to the remake.  What exactly is the point of two different sets of A/B scenarios when they are almost identical?  If they wanted something like with REmake where there is one campaign per character, and the cannon is derived from imagining a combination of both, then why not just have one campaign each for Claire and Leon?  Seriously, what a disappointing muck up.  What was Capcom thinking?  

It is also great that the Ghost Survivor scenarios are given for free.  However, these scenarios also suck.  I say this because, for one, they are done in the same arcade-style as the HUNK/Tofu scenario instead of being story-driven.  Secondly, these scenarios are non-cannon parallel universe plotlines, meaning they are pointless by design.  Why does it need to be this way?

RE2R did managed to avoid a lot of the nonsense that has run down the RE franchise and has successfully stuck to its roots by trying to stay true to the original RE2.  Unfortunately, this was a half-baked effort that missed out on some aspects that made the original RE2 a truly great game.  I'm just curious if the RE2R developers actually played the original RE2, or if they just read a synopsis of how the scenario system worked.

Great remake for both newbies and returning players. 

The remake for Resident Evil 1 is one of the best remakes I've played. It's perfect, it does everything the original did, makes it look better but adds enough twists and aims to surprise returning players. A well designed puzzle box of a game. It straight up replaces it, which isn't the case for this game. 

Resident Evil 2's remake is really, REALLY good but it's not a replacement for the original PS1 version. They've changed the game enough where things are familiar but the execution and mechanics are entirely different, leading to a different experience. That isn't a negative because the devs clearly cared for this game and wanted to make it super replayable like the first and give you lots of scares and fun. Is that a bad thing? Well, no. It just means you got 2 great games that are worth playing. 

Why it's replayable? Short spoiler section for that:
SPOILERS----
You get everything the PS1 version gave you, A & B scenarios for both characters, Hunk and even Tofu! ...Actually there's a few variants of Tofu, as well as free DLC that plays similar to Hunk with different characters. So, you can replay this game a lot and get tons of fun out of it. 

END SPOILERS-

The game looks super good, and even though areas are redesigned they still look familiar somehow. The sound design is really something else, the game sounds unique and sounds will stick with you after you beat the game. Gameplay is not like any RE before it, it's similar to the originals with your character being a bit difficult to control, there's weight to your character so you can't turn on a dime and dodge around- and this isn't RE4 so there's no suplexing any monks. 

You have a limited inventory which they will make you think on what to carry, boards to seal off windows from zombies, various gun powders, key items, gun parts. You gotta plan what you're doing/carrying so you're not constantly running into items that you want...but can't take. 

Zombies are resilient, you're better off dodging the ones you can and taking out the ones in areas you're frequenting. You're not rewarded for kills here so, unlike Revelations and other titles claiming it- this really is a jump back into true survival horror. Taking out a zombie's reward is you get to live. 

There's even a hardcore mode which is VERY, hard. I thought it that case of "How the game was meant to be played" well, that maybe true for some but you can die in 2 zombie bites on hard mode. Zombies take more hits it seems and on top of this less ammo...oh yeah, and ink ribbons. 

Negatives? Well I think the game takes itself too seriously. Characters you might have quoted in the past in a mocking way are, without spoilers are made into quite the tragic thing where you genuinely feel bad for them. Also Leon and Claire don't chat much, I'm sure that's to make you feel isolated but a bit of radio chatter like in the original might have helped tie the story together a bit more. Their stories feel super disconnected because of this.
Does this ruin the game? No, the gameplay, atmosphere and such more than make up for it. It's just another reason why I feel this and the original are still both replaying.  

Do I recommend this? YES, it's one of the few games that have come out that I think qualify as survival and horror. Not just a horror game. It's well made, well thought out, scary, there's tons of extras and no stupid microtransactions stuffed into the game. There's even free costumes, what freakin' year is this!? 1998!? You get everything the PS1 version had and more. It's super replayable and if you like zombie/horror/etc you owe it to yourself to grab this game.

I never really had any problems with the gameplay as most of it is determined on player decision like, for example, managing inventory space. Since this is a survival horror game, finding materials and items in the world requires you to make smart decisions when it comes to picking up items that help progress the story, heal and protect your character, and unlock secret weapons and attachments. Also, whenever you are reload a save or continue from an auto-save going back into areas that were previously cleared only to find more zombies lying in wait always keeps the scares fresh and Mr. X a constant threat.

The story is very well-done and is an amazing retelling of the classic Resident Evil 2 story. However, there are some things that still make me question the stories chronology. Depending on who you choose to play as on the first playthrough, you have to complete the other character's second scenario to get the true ending of the game. When doing to the second run, you find notes that are left by the first character saying that certain areas are completed and unlocked, but the other character still has to find the same items to unlock the same areas or when running into key characters that were already met in the first playthrough. It's more of a continuity issue and I understand the need to have both playable characters meet all non-playable characters, but there was a character that I met in my first playthrough that should not have reappeared in the second run.

Outside of that, I believe the Resident Evil 2/Biohazard RE:2 2019 Remake is a very good introduction to classic survival horror and to the Resident Evil franchise as a whole.

After about 49-50 hours of gameplay i've finally 100% completed the Resident Evil 2 Remake. After experiencing all that the game has to offer i thought it would be appropriate to finally review this gem. I'm pleased to say that the Resident Evil 2 Remake is a new and improved version of the original RE2 with a lot of replayability! The best way to play this game is to either go Leon A and then Claire B or start off with Claire A and then go Leon B. Experiencing the second scenario is worth it for the secret final boss fight (i don't consider this a spoiler since the game shows you at the end that you're not quite done yet) besides that the B scenarios feel a lot more hectic! I personally felt a lot more stressed when playing through the B scenarios compared to just doing the regular A scenario. One issue that i do have with the scenarios tho is that Claire and Leon for the most part experience the same events. They both fight most of Birkin's transformations, they both visit all the same areas and the puzzles doesn't really change depending on which character you play as. My problem with the little variety in their 2 scenarios is how certain situations play out so differently (i'm mostly reffering to cutscenes) and these alternative scenarios doesn't make a whole lot of sense since sometimes they act like what happens in Claire's story already happended in Leon's and then other times they just ignore that and Claire and Leon get copy pasted cutscenes are feel rather odd. However this doesn't ruin the game by any means, it's just a small detail that i wish Capcom would have thought about when creating the game. The ammo management in this game is some of the best that i've ever seen in a Resident Evil game! It really makes you feel like you're always at the verge of running out of ammo (That is if you play on Hardcore and sometimes on Standard mode) i absolutely loved having to leave zombies alive every now and then just to save a couple of bullets. Speaking about the zombies they're all scripted and they don't respawn. If you decide to waste enough ammo or cut them enough time with your knife then they will die. If you block off all the windows you'll also stop the occasional new zombie spawn here and there. However i have played through this game 12 times and they are scripted. Eventually you'll memorize how many zombies come from that one specific window which is cool. The enemy variety in this game is pretty poor to be honest, only Resident Evil game with worse enemy variety (atleast the RE games that i have played) is Resident Evil 7. I absolutely adore RE7 but it's enemy variety is terrible. If i see one more molded imma puke. The RE2 Remake has 4 major sections (I consider 2 of these sections to kinda be the same but friends of mine all considered it to be seperate sections so oh well) You'll start off at the RPD police station as expected. Then you get to a parking lot, you move on to the sewers section, and finally you enter Umbrella's secret lab. I love the majority of these sections! the only section in the game that i hated was the Sewers. After doing the Sewer section for the third time i started to hate the place! the reason i hate the sewers is because everything down there looks so boring, and there's a new enemy type that can really screw you up if you come unprepared. The game also comes with a few extra modes but they're really nothing special. In the mode known as the 4th survivor you get to play as Hunk (Who???) no but seriously a lot of RE fans either don't know Hunk or forgot about him since he's really not too important to the story. Hunk's game mode is basically just you running through the sewers section of the main game up to the police station of the main game... But wait! There's a small twist that makes this task a lot more difficult than it should be. There's a lot of enemies... A LOT OF THEM. Basically every single enemy is walking around in the sewers and in the police station (except for bosses of course) your only reward for completing this insane game mode is another insane game mode where you play as a piece of Tofu. The 4th survivor mode felt pointless and i didn't enjoy it at all. Then there's the ghost survivor stories! These 3 extra game modes are kinda the exact same as Hunk's mode but with new enemy types and way less enemies. I didn't really enjoy these game modes either since they all required you to keep on running and never allowed you to stop up to catch a break. There's no dialogue in the ghost survivor stories and the stories are kinda all alternative scenarios that didn't end up happening. Sooooooooooo in other words they don't add anything to the story really. Oh but wait you unlock a new game mode after beating the 3 ghost survivor stories! Well that's cool! In this new game you play as the sheriff at the gas station that you first encountered in the beginning of the main game. He's locked himself up inside of the gas station and his only objective is to kill 100 zombies! Now this game mode is a lot of fun! It's basically a sort of wave defense mini game, however the zombies come in big blobs and with some ''special'' abilities. It's very stressful once you get to the 75/100 mark in my opinion. I remember getting 92/100 in my first attempt. After that i kept getting 96/100 in 3 other attempts! It was really frustrating, but it always felt like it was my own fault for wasting some of my more powerful weapons when i should have saved them for tougher enemies. You don't really get anything for completing these extra game modes except for in game cosmetics that can only be used in the extra game modes. Honestly i could go on and on about this game but i feel like there's so much stuff to cover that it would take ages to write. This game get's a solid 9/10! if they replaced the sewer section with something less boring then i'd easily give it a 10/10! :)

It's an exceptional game. If you take your time, your first campaign could stretch over 10 hours. And it's 10 amazing hours. That alone is worth the price, in my opinion. But the RE games are meant to be replayed over and over, and RE2 is no different. There are two versions of each campaign for each of the two characters, plus a few short free DLC campaigns. The game incentivizes efficient play, so it can be really fun to speedrun through and see how flawless you can be.

But before you think about the replayability, which it does have in spades, you should really focus on your first campaign experience. Mine was pretty damn strong. I recommend you take your time with it. It's meant to be an immersive experience. You should wear headphones and be dead to the world. I personally think Leon's campaign is the definitive choice. He's a more interesting character, and the feeling of being the plucky rookie stumbling into chaos is something that isn't matched by Claire's more generic feel.

I also recommend playing in Hardcore mode, as it is really the only way to understand what RE is about. Trying to chunk together decisions in order to get as much stuff done in between limited saves makes for a very engaging game. The increased difficulty raises the tension and reward. The only caveat here is that there is one boss fight about 2/3 of the way through the game at the end of the sewers that is just not balanced properly for Hardcore mode. I highly recommend conserving power weapons for that fight. I had to reload an earlier save and redo the entire area because I didn't have enough ammo on my current save. It created an absurd difficulty spike in an otherwise perfect curve.

In addition to the main campaign, which has 4 (extremely) slightly different "routes" to play, there is also a handful of bonus modes, most of which involving timed runs through a gauntlet of zombies. They're really fun in their own right. They can push total playtime over 100 hours if you're really into them and re-running campaigns. Otherwise, you get an exceptionally good single-player campaign experience.

Playing on Hardcore mode, RE2 is possibly the best survival horror game I've played. No playthrough will be as good as your first, but you will still find yourself playing it over and over again and having a ton of fun each time. It rewards learning its systems. I hope that Capcom continues this trend into the future and that we get more games like this from other developers. 

It's not perfect. Some of the VO is under-delivered. None of the actors play with particularly much personality. There's some jank animations here and there. That one crap boss fight. But  CAPCOM knows how to make a frigging game. They know what's fun. It's as good as it gets. Plus, it's got one of the best gore systems I've ever seen, so it's got my recommendation for that.

This is an excellent remaster that keeps the Resident Evil series rolling in the correct direction. Six hours is more than ample for a single play-through leading to easily replayability. Enough has been changed and added to the story of the original game that players that are quite familiar with the original should find enough new content in terms of characters, settings, and combat encounters. I liked the hybrid style of a Resident Evil 4 third person perspective with a Resident Evil 7 inventory and combat system. One extra that I loved was the ability to turn on the original music (main hall and library scores are just too good) and sound effects. 

Most of the other extras aren't great, as the additional gameplay modes are very short, and I personally felt little interest in replaying any of the modes after beating them. The costumes vary from nostalgic to farcical and really don't add much to the game for me. The actual Leon and Claire dynamic is extremely lacking. Other than the opening, ending, and a few impersonal notes scattered sparingly throughout the campaigns, they only share one VERY cringe-worthy scene together. In a remaster with interesting character additions and elaborations on existing characters, this one aspect seemed lacking. 

The last nitpick I have is with the campaign ranking system, as all that matters is the time required to complete the run. I thought this grading system was fairly shallow, as I don't put much weight into clear time. This is exacerbated by the fact that one of the extra modes has a secondary grading system for how many bullets are fired from a certain gun. This proves an ability to track various statistics which I thought could be incorporated into playthrough rankings or bonus achievements, but I digress.

Any shortcomings of this game are mostly neutral in nature. The costumes, campaign rankings, and extras do not detract from the main story and campaigns, and are completely optional. I, like many a Resident Evil fan, am just glad that this title finally got the remaster it deserved. Following the success of RE7, this series appears to understand the correct balance of story and combat that produces quality entries that make this series, unlike many other large title series, be trending in a positive direction.

Resident Evil 2 is a wonderful remake of the 1998 classic. The developers managed to update every aspect of the game to modern standards while still keeping the core concept of survival horror alive. This game is a great experience for both newcomers and people who played the original. However as successful a remake as it is there are some flaws and game design decisions that some people may object to.

the cons: 
 - Game camera: The game does not include the classic fixed camera angles. For some fans, this is bound to be a disappointment. However the over-the-shoulder camera is tuned as to balance the game so for fans who worry that having free aim will make the game too action-oriented or easy, fear not. 
- hardcore mode: This difficulty is indeed hardcore and I believe even series veterans will find it hard on a first play through. I do not recommend this for newcomers who only started playing RE with the last 2 or 3 releases. Key challenges include less ammo, way more need of item management, and enemies doing more damage and being way harder to kill than their standard counterpart. It is punishing.
- enemies being bullet sponges: As mentioned above, hardcore mode can make enemies bullet sponges, where a single zombie might take anything from 5 to 10 bullets to put down. Even on standard difficulty zombies already can withstand anything from 3 to 5 bullets to the head, so know what to expect. My advice is if you don't need to revisit an area, avoid combat in said area. Conserve ammo where you can.
- new location designs: This is more of a con for older fans who played the original RE2. Personally, I found the lab's redesign to be a bit disappointing. A very minor issue, but just keep in mind that some locations are changed significantly.
- cheap situations: Very rarely you may get chain grabbed when surrounded by zombies. Or you may get grabbed by 2 of them at once, which can be fatal if playing on hardcore. Also enemies will do some unexpected things at times, and zombies tend to double lunge in this game. Use of defence item is disabled when you are grabbed on stairs. Without knowing all the details of the enemy behaviours and game rules, some things might feel cheap when initially experienced. 

With all that out of the way the rest of the game is simply amazing. RPD has never looked and played better. The graphics are gorgeous, and every game element is meticulously designed. The developers have certainly shown their love and respect for the original game in remaking it, and as a fan I want to say thank you for a job well done.

Capcom has fully revived the survival horror experience of Resident Evil with this game. It takes the success of Resident Evil 7 and adds even more to the experience. This game handles amazingly and looks absolutely beautiful and shows the true power of the RE engine. This is a game for any type of gamer, but that doesn't mean it's not difficult. The amount of bullets a zombie takes is supposed to be high, as it forces you to make a choice between killing the zombie now, or saving bullets and dealing with it later. This adds to the tension of what is a SURVIVAL HORROR game. In addition, it also adds to the satisfaction when you completely blow the head off a zombie on the first shot. And enemies are rarely able to stunlock you, and I've been completely surrounded by zombies and have been able to escape relatively easily. Overall, this game wholeheartedly deserves the praise it gets, and I look forward to the next installment in the series.

After finishing the campaign 8 times, all the DLC missions and getting 100% achievements, it's time I give a mini, spoiler free, review. I played the original RE2 when it was released 20 years ago. It's the first and the best resident evil game I've played. And I've played ALL RE games that are available on PC. RE7 took me by surprise and it was really good. This one tops RE7. Today, Capcom faithfully remade RE2 (I'm so glad they chose to use RE2 as their first 'remake' project). It's called 'remake' and not 'remastered' because it was completely remade from scratch/ground up, using RED engine (RE7). It is NOT an 'enhanced' edition of the original RE2. But they stayed faithful to the original game, redesigned the entire game while retaining the tension, horror aspect, story, etc and made them so much better for 2019 audience. And they are really successful at that. 

[h1] PROS: [/h1] 
+ amazing graphics, especially the cutscenes. 
+ In-game rendered cutscenes
+ Great plot and some very emotional / realistic facial expressions. 
+ manage to keep me tensed/scared throughout the game, yet addicted to find out what happens next. 
+ great PC port with many graphical settings to customize to your computer's specification. does not feel like a cheap console port. 
+ very good story and single player campaign that seems so rare nowadays in the growing sea of oversaturated multiplayer shooters. 
+ although they share many similarities in puzzle solving and plot points, both Leon and Claire have their own distinct campaigns, guns/weapons that are only available to them, unique accessible areas. so, it's a joy to run through both campaigns. Even the new game (second run) has some differences to the first campaign. 
+ Excellent puzzles that can all be solved in-game without using a walkthrough if you explore all parts of the game.
+ I dont know about other countries, but in my country, the price of the game is less than half the price of other full price AAA games. 
+ does not charge microtransactions (even though they could have done so) for powerful guns early in the game, bullets, healing items, cosmetic skins, etc. Respect. 

[h1] CONS: [/h1] 
- not all the gameplay graphic looks as amazing as the cutscenes. sometimes at some part, I wish the graphic looks better than it is. but overall, it's excellent. 
- some consider the game short. For me, it is just nice. Average gamers will probably take about 6 to 8 hours to complete a single campaign. 
- Does not support multi-GPU (Nvidia SLI / AMD CF), but you can easily tweak the Nvidia inspector and use a custom SLI profile for it and it works quite well.
- game might be too scary/gory for some to indulge. 

[h1] CONCLUSION: [/h1] 
If you like all the PROS I've listed and you like what you saw on the trailer as well as RE series, buy it. Capcom deserved to be praised and supported for their effort in this. If my review is not convincing enough, just take a quick look at the overall reviews on steam. Currently at the time of my writing, it's standing at "OVERWHELMINGLY POSITIVE". Cheers

Resident Evil 2 is more than just an HD remaster, it is a full remake of the original game from 1998. The game feels like how veterans will remember the game, but with 20 years of retrospection and game design improving the end result. The main story has three gamemodes (Assisted, Normal, Hardcore) and substantially change the atmosphere of the game on each. For many players, 8-12 hours is typical of your first play of the game, while subsequent plays drop towards around 2 hours.

Which is important, as to complete the entire story, there are four campaigns: Leon and Claire each have their own, slightly tweaked, version of events, and both have 1st and 2nd Runs, depending on which character you play first. If you're looking to complete the entire main story, you're looking at a minimum of 4 plays, though this is only for achievements and completion.

The game does reward you for each of these plays, with overpowered weapons, costumes and extra gamemodes, as well as concept art and a model viewer. The extra modes feature far more difficult gameplay with their own challenges.

This game, personally speaking, is worth the price if you intend to complete a significant amount of the challenges and the various campaigns. Much like the original, Resident Evil 2 gets its value from replaying the game and striving for everything hidden and unlockable. If that doesn't sound appealing, pick this game up on a sale and play it as a modern action-horror game. If that does sound worthwhile, then it's worth the full price for the time you'll get out of it.

Classic horror game is back and this time in new wrapper, but fortunately with same filling. Resident Evil 2 from 2019 it's almost perfect re-imagining of original resident evil 2 from 1998. The fans, including me, have been waiting for this game for years and luckily the remake didn't disappoint me.

GRAPHICS
RE engine is back with some improvements. The remake looks absolutely incredible. Photo-realistic graphics able create impressive picture.  It's not open world game so it was expected that environment will have a lot details. And I mean not only amount of polygons but items that fill game's world. Unlike in original game now police station really looks like place that was used as emergency sanctuary. You can see beds in main hall. More corpses of last survivals, more blood on the walls and etc. Sure original game had hardware limitations but it nice to see that once those restrictions were lifted the developers use new creation freedom. Rest location also received significant boost to their look and design. Very good work was done for proper implementation of lights and shadows. It's cool to see beams of light come from outside or your flashlight in dark room. Overall the game has dark colors but it's never pitch dark. It's always enough light sources even if it come from flashlight. The game is full of good gore. The zombies are capable to create tension and keep you on the edge. They have very detailed bite animation. You can shoot their limbs. Seeing hand / leg falls apart very cool. Also respect to motion capture team. They achieve highest quality. The only issue that I have with graphics is surface reflection. Sometimes under some angle you get weird blinks on surface of walls or floor. My recommendation is to turn off this setting.

STORY
Story follow two main characters: Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield. He rookie cop just arrive to city to his first day on job. She came to city to find her older brother. Both found themself trapped in city full of deadly creatures and they are looking the way to escape this nightmare. During their adventure you will different characters that will tell their stories and find you to find out what caused this mess. The story based on original game so development team didn't have much freedom in writing. I think they did pretty good job to improve narrative and even small character have memorable scene. HOWEVER interactions between stories are my biggest issue with game especially compare to original. If you look on each story separately it is good, but if you try to create full picture of events it will have a lot of contradiction. Somehow character fights same boss in same place or discover fate of same character basically in same time which not possible. Second scenario is weaker compare to original version. To be fair devs didn't promise A/B scenario like in original but still this aspect pretty disappointment. Voice acting done well. Even the characters like reporter Ben or gun shop owner Kendo that appears in only one cut scene did pretty good job. Not to mention to main characters. At the beginning of story Leon sound like green rookie but he grows as character. By the end of story he developed badass tones in his tone when he confronts other character (no spoiler for newcomers). Same apply to the rest characters. Every character has unique voice tone and use it (along with face mimic) express their thoughts and feelings.

SOUND
When it's come to sound the game have decent samples. Not bad but not great either. From one hand zombies screams sounds creepy but from another hand I wish the guns have more impact effects because their shoots feel weak. However I must mention 3D sound. If you have good headphones I highly recommend use them. Ability to understand where is enemy only by hearing important feature for survival horror game. Especially, if you try to escape from Mr. X. To stand in room and only hear how he bypass your location and not entering in your room create tension. Very cool feature that definitely enhance game experience.

SOUNDTRACK
Honestly I am kind of disappointed. The game have memorable soundtracks but only during boss fight or when Mr. X chasing you. It's not enough. I gave the game chance and play Claire A and Leon B with new soundtrack but once I switch to original I never wanted to comeback. Of course as someone how played original game many times I can have prejudice but still I don't think that remake have enough music. It’s up to you decided if you want to invest and buy original music.

GAMEPLAY
Classic, like in original. You explore various locations and rooms; solve puzzles, craft ammo and health item, upgrade weapons, looking for key or other items that will help advance in story. Occasionally fight with monsters or run from them. Backtracking, save room, item management and box - all here. Map useful tool that allow you to plan your route and automatically mark any item that you discover but didn't pick up. Exploration is rewarding. There are couple inessential puzzle that will reward you with weapon/inventory upgrades. The game also marks items that can be thrown away once you use them in all possible ways (keys for example). Like residents evil 1 you have defense item that allow you to escape grab. But this time those take regular space in inventory and can be used in any time. For example, you can throw flash grenade that will disoriented enemies and give chance to bypass them. Also want to mention cool new mechanic that allow to border windows and prevent zombie jumping from street. Speaking of them. Now they are tough foes. Couple headshots not enough and 2-3 of them on same screen can be challenging. Dogs have low HP but they are quick. Lickers have more HP than original but can be avoided since they are blind. Rest enemies are kind spoilers. But I want to mention Mr. X. Unstoppable enemy that will follow you about 1/3 of games. Can be deceive or stun but till some point he always there and looking for you. There are certain rooms that he cannot follow you if you want caught the breath. Cool challenge and probably CAPCOM test the water before introduce Nemesis if(when?) remake of RE3 come.

REPLAYABILITY
This factor was always a core of classic resident evil experience. Once you beat game you can play again but with different outlook, different difficulty or trying to get some achievement. You can try to improve your completion time and different gun with infinite ammo, or chase challenges set by developers or even by yourself. It will keep gameplay fresh and will require from player to invest in tactic or strategy. How to finish without opening item box/using recovery items? Or complete various tasks that will unlock models, animations, concept arts and etc.

PERFORMANCE
I use i5 9600k, GTX 1080; 16GB RAM. I run game on 1440p resolution with max settings (scale 100%). The game runs very smooth, fps between ~70 and 90. Zero crashes. My only issue (aside reflection that I mentioned previously) is animation for enemies in far distance. Apparently in order to save some resources the game locks enemy movement to 30fps as long they far from you. In result their movements look like slow-mo. Once you approach them, zombies "catch up" with you fps. Luckily the game doesn’t have many big locations so this effect not widely common. It's very good port.

SUMMARY
Definitely it is game of the year contender. It’s worthy successor of original game. The game is not perfect but very enjoyable experience for veterans and newcomers. I strongly recommend this game for purchase. Single-player is still alive. No force online, coop, multi-player, loot boxes or live services. Just complete very good game on day one. The game is real AAA product and it’s up to modern standards. It's good to see how much effort development team put to create world that enhance experience and immerse you this world. If this standard for future games I am in. So resident evil 3 remake next?  Dino Crisis?

This does something very few other linear/story driven games do: you can get stuck. If you manage your health and resources badly, you could find yourself needing to restart the whole scenario, or at least reloading several hours back. This only really applies on "hardcore" mode, where both resources and number of saves are limited. But it's an interesting concept that really helps drive the tension.

I never felt like this game was *scary* per se (except a few jump scares), but it's incredibly tense because of this resource management aspect. Getting hit is a real cost, especially if you're on hardcore, where you need to portion out your savegames. You don't have enough ammo to kill everyone, and you're going to need to backtrack through areas you didn't fully clear with the old threats plus some new ones added. All this together makes it a stressful, clenching experience.

There are some minor flaws. The game is quite short, even with the backtracking, weighing in at about 6-8 hours for your first run. There are 4 scenarios (2 characters with an "A" and "B" plot each), but you'll be going through the same areas and mostly doing the same things. If you add together everything plus the free DLC, there's maybe 10 hours of content stretched over 20 hours of game.

The graphics are generally great, but have this awful greenish/grayish filter over them (get ReShade to fix it) and heavy viginetting (there's a mod for that too). And the characters are incredibly bland, with not enough one-liners to truly be campy, and not enough actual emotions or character development to make you care. The overall story is basic B-movie zombie fare about evil corporations developing bioweapons. 

But the core gameplay loop and exploration is what makes this game really worth it. It's tense and fun with great environments and great design. Just one tip to maximize enjoyment: PLAY ON HARDCORE! The limited saves and inventory are big parts of what drives the game's tension. Don't worry - with mouse aim plus playing smart, you shouldn't have too much trouble even if you're not great at games.

I can't imagine a better remake/reimagining of RE2. Ever since I played RE4 on the PS2 over a decade ago, I always wanted a version of RE2 with more modern and accessible controls like RE4 had. That's not to say I don't like the original, the Original RE2 is a perfect sequel to the original RE1. It really is superior on paper in almost every way compared to RE1, and is my favorite of the original 3 games in the series. 

I also really loved the RE1 remake back in the 2000's, many people consider it to be better than the original. This REmake however is on another level. Save maybe a few purists that refuse to abandon tank controls, this might be the best game in the series. Anyone can play this game, whether you've played any of the other games in the series or not. However I should warn you, the inventory management in this game is considerably more hardcore. Those who've played the originals know that you have to pick your battles and conserve your resources. RE4 (which is still my favorite probably, go play it) will give you far more ammo than you will need to kill virtually everything in the game. This game however forces you to really think about whether you have bullets to spare on something blocking your path. Even though RE4 is a Survival Horror classic as opposed to a straight action game like RE5 (still a good game) and RE6 (not a great game), REmake 2 is considerable more "Survival Horror" than RE4. There's no kicks, no QTE's (save the subweapon usage when grabbed), and waaaaay less one-liners and ammo. Also, if you've played the originals you know that one shot to the head won't kill a zombie. That's nothing new, but you'll a see a few people here and there complain about that (git gud). Mr. X is actually fairly easy to avoid, as long as you clear out a few areas to retreat to if he shows up. Don't waste ammo on him lol.

I really recommend the series as a whole to people curious about the Survival Horror genre, along with Silent Hill. Capcom did a really good job resurrecting this franchise with RE7 and REmake 2. One of my biggest complaints about RE7 was a lack of enemy variety and design, and this game definitely has both of those. I really liked RE7, but I missed the classic aspects of the originals after that. REmake 2 was a real gift. The only complaint about this game I have is a lack of continuity between the scenarios (but if you played the originals you already knew that). Also, the music is a little bit less memorable than the original, though I really dig that 90's grunge track "Saudude" at the end of B scenario, as well as the Industrial Electronic tracks they use for the 4th Survivor, Tofu Survivor, and self-destruct sequences. Also if you purchase the Deluxe you get the original soundtrack which is implemented perfectly into the game, shifting tracks as you enter new rooms like in the original.

If you are a horror and survival horror fan, grab this. It's well worth the price (though I think the deluxe is a little pricey, still nothing absurd) and you'll easily get at least 20 hours out of it. It's very replayable, so I predict you'll get even more out of it than that.

Resident Evil 2 in my words is the game of 2019, though many see it as a Horror/Adventure game, which it is, this game lives up to much more than just another zombie shooter. Thrown into the fight very early on, you come to realize this game is more "difficult" than expected. Most zombie genre games will give you the ammo you need to devour a horde with your bullets. Resident Evil is quite the opposite, making you pick your shots wisely to better the overall fear and wonder of whats coming next and which zombies you'll need to avoid rather than fight. 

-Graphics-

Going back to the 3rd Person view we've seen in previous games, feels very smooth and tuned for the series. CAPCOM has confirmed that the following RE3 Remake is already in the works and will use the same mechanics. The graphics in this game surpass any I have seen recently (In my opinion) such as Battlefield 5, Tomb Raider and many others. Visually this game goes to the top of my list. This game is not a remaster of the previous version, it is a remake which means most if not all of the game has been changed, though certain thing feel similar "story wise" you would be wrong to think this is a copy & paste. everything about this game feels new. Visually seeing what the RE engine is capable of i'm truly excited for the future of the franchise.

-Sounds- 

Whether playing this game in the dark with your Headset or enjoying it on a nice day with the surround sound, this game will pull you in and not let go. Every place you go in this game has its own eerie vibes to it, keeping you on your toes wondering what the next creature you face around the corner will be. Whether it be the screams of a Zombies, the cries of a licker, the growls of the dogs or the footsteps of a certain someone. Resident Evil keeps things fresh the whole way through.

-gameplay- 

When you start the game you are given three choices for difficulty. Assisted, zombies are easy to kill, auto saves are frequent life regenerates to yellow when in red. Standard, zombies are harder, auto saves are less, life does not regenerate. Hardcore, Zombies are hard, no auto saves ink ribbons are required to save, less items to find, healing is harder. I would like to talk about the difficulty first because there are few that play this game and simply don't realize that changing the difficulty can reap many rewards. Not to spoil too much but if you are reading this. Make sure you give a play through on harder difficulties. These are the best type of games that add a replay value to it making every run through more compelling then the last. Did i mention that there's 4 play throughs, each with their views not seen in the others. After completing  the story you unlock different modes that keep you dragged in. Worth it in every way. And on top of it they released free DLC for stories of survivors and what was going on for them during the times of Resident Evil 2. 

PROS
- Graphics are beyond incredible
- Can replay the game and have a different run everytime
- Amazing story that grabs you the whole way
- Multiple Stories
- 

CONS
- The only con I could think of was'nt in the base game it ended up being in the DLC. In the main game, burning zombies burn out and die. For some reason there is a tunnel section in a certain part of the game that has 2 zombies already burning and it seems no matter how long you wait they do not burn out.

For me, that was my only CON for the game and look at how minimal it is. I think that truly shows how good this game is, you can tell when companies put their all into their projects and the RE team at CAPCOM is certainly amongst them.

My personal Rating : 9.6/10 The .4 Missing is all personal thoughts on the game thing I would have enjoyed changed, added or whatever.

I easily give this game the 10/10 it deserves.

I hope this review has helped anyone interested in purchasing the game. I know there's plenty more I will be adding to this review. But as it stands I hope it helped, thank you for taking your time to read this. I hope to see you all in Resident Evil 3.

It's good son... It's really good... More action than classic RE, more horror than new RE, this game is similar to RE7 in this aspect, but at the same time much more loyal to the original games. It plays similar to RE4, but the game is much closer to survival horror.

So I'll just get this out of the way... How does it compare to old RE2? Well you will recognize a lot of areas, characters, and story events, but many of them are altered in some way. This game is very very different from the original, but it's not really worse or better, just a different game all together. Rather than a super HD remake like RE1 Remaster, this game is a fantastic reimagining. We now live in a world with two different and fantastic RE2s and there is plenty of room in my heart for both. I think it's best for players to experience for themselves the twists this game made to the original.

If I had any complaint for this game, it's that B scenarios are rushed and very heavy in plot holes. Also a lot of classic enemies are missing in action, never making any appearance. The game isn't worse off for it, but I still wish they were here in some form. In fact that last sentence embodies how I feel about this game. It doesn't feel affected negatively by changes or removal of certain things, but I wish it was there just to see how cool it would have been. 

This game is so awesome that it just makes you beg for more and more. All I wanted was more enemies, more areas, more more more. It's such a awesome experience with so many changes and cuts that I find myself wishing it just had more content getting the reimagined treatment, some new areas, enemies, the crossbow (T . T), or anything.

As for the most positive aspect of this game... Mr. X. You've likely seen his memes by now, and for good reason. A generally noteworthy miniboss in the original game is now a huge part of the game, stalking you like nemesis in both A and B scenarios. He is truly an unstoppable wall of muscle and trenchcoat, stomping with relentless speed and determination to crack your cranium like Chris Redfield cracks a chicken egg. Mr. X is the perfect proof of concept for nemesis and a good reason to get excited for a possible RE3 Remake.

More specifics: 

The game is much darker, much more violent and aggressive than it's 1998 counterpart. It fails to capture the feel of the original game in a lot of ways, but the new atmosphere is equally awesome in completely different ways. Many enemies were cut, but those left behind are much more impactful (zombies have never been this dangerous!).

Character's backstory, design, actions, and personalities are altered a lot, not really for better or worse for the most part, just different. What happens in the games is changed but the results are the same, both Original and REmake2 can easily be canon. Factory area before the lab was cut, to be fair it was only 4 rooms or so and some aspects of it were built into the sewer now which is a much larger and more fleshed out area. 

HD William and his forms have changed art direction a lot, they are generally similar in shape to their originals (Except for G4 which had a awful redesign), but they give me a more Dead Space vibe this time around. Most of his forms are absolutely awesome, especially his final form.

Difficulty settings are modernized. Assist mode is for casual players. Standard is for first time players of the game (Even RE veterans should probably start here). Hardcore mode is the new super challenge mode, incorperating some of the old mechanics of RE including ink ribbons, no dynamic difficulty adjustment, no autosaves/checkpoints, and most notably, very hard hitting enemies that will almost always put you in danger.

The port itself seems solid, I get ~120 fps most of the time, and have seen no bugs at all in 50 hours played, but did get one crash.

tl;dr: It's different than RE2 1998, but it's a top tier game that any survival horror or RE fan must play!

A pretty bow on top of poor gaming choices

Overview
Claire and Leon are about to have a really bad day. A virus outbreak has turned the town into zombie like enemies (that we'll just call zombies) and the player has to make their way through the hordes of em to escape the nightmare. But it's a bit of the shame of a lack of memorable set pieces.

Graphics
Easily the strongest part of the game is the graphics. There is a good sense of realism, particularly with the zombies and their hit detection. You can see chucks of them flying off or being seperated from a limb. The cutscenes are really sharp as well save one character model.

Story
For something as simple as virus outbreak creates zombies, they sure messed it up. You can play as leon or claire and completing their A mission gives you their B mission. The various missions completely ignore each other. Several people die in different locations or at different times - there is no sense of what's cannon. There is also a real lack of character development or even interactions, particularly between Leon and Claire. The lack of narration really comes to one of my annoyances with the game - the huffing and moaning. Since characters jog at a leisurely pace (more on that) and there are few people to speak with, our protagonist just kind of make noises. listening to the same 3 sounds on a loop for hours on end is irksome.

Gameplay
Shoot enemies in the head and hope for criticals or shoot their legs to slow them down. That's about it. Boss fights are pretty much the same giant enemy in a small area. They are bullet sponges save for obvious weak spots. These fight are more to do with knowing which weapon will be more effective. In fact, the game does little to disguise the fact that it is trial and error. Got right - get mauled. go left and you're fine. I dropped my overall playtime by 66% on my 2nd playthrough.

And then there is the RNG of bullets. It is possible to 1 shot and kill an enemy with a critical headshot. Sometimes it can take as many as 13. So you round a corner, get ambushed and your pull of a crit and you're fine or you don't, and you die. Players are giving to options - path differently, or hope they land their shot. When first playing I would simply allow myself to die (and wait through the unskippable drawn out death scenes) just to run an area again because I felt it wasn't to much ammo. It's a pretty bad feedback loop. I get the idea is to cause tension of "will i get out of this or not" but I can just restart. And on non-hardcore difficulties there are unlimited saves and checkpoints, which is really forgiving.

That's in part because there is very little difference between the scenarios. As I stated, there are four, and i would be surprised if the overall game play varied more than 15%. It's probably a good thing the game is relatively short, because it's a bit tedious to replay the same areas and boss fight 4 times. Then there is the back tracking. So, back in 1998, games were small because there was only so much room for their information on a cartridge so RE2 was designed to have a lot of backtracking to pad the gaming experience. Except now, games can be massive open world adventures (they don't have to be) and making your way through the same room dozens of times can be a bit boring. And again, they don't disguise this. There is an item that requires getting 5 other items. Now you can hide this repetitive task by making the items make sense.
Getting electrical components to open a gate is fine and I'll allow for the necessity of rewiring puzzle game. but the items involved into getting access to a weapon are silly.

Speaking of silly, the jogging. Dead Space and Alan Wake have slow moving protagonist but the games make them work. Wake is an author who gets ambushed, so running away is seldom an option. Isaac of Dead Space is wearing a heavy suit of armor - and yet they both seem faster than the starring characters of RE2. It's eye rolling painful watching Claire look like she's out for a Sunday stroll, even taking time to prevent rain water from falling into her eyes, while a mutated zombie chases her down. Then there is the major obstacle that the player cannot hurdle despite it being less than a normal stride.

Immersion
And that's my biggest grip. I was seldom scared or had any sense of tension save the late parts of the first area (though again, the slow motion running made me think of baywatch vs dealing with an undead apocalypse). There isn't much in the way of music (again, save for the late parts of the first area). The supposed fear and dread would normally just manifest itself in annoyance and anger. Whether it's watching an enemy eat a stupid amount of bullets the poorly delivered dialogue. Nothing perhaps encapsulates the disconnect with the game than Sherry who seems surprisingly upbeat despite the absolutely brutal, violent and scarring events she's witnessed instead of a traumatized mess.

Also - If you are struggling on standard (which means dying 3 times) the game asks you if you wish to switch to a lower difficulty. I could see players doing this on accident and it simply shouldn't exist. I also would be hesitant to link the game to the RE website as it seems to not properly connect and feels the need to remind you every time you load a save.

DLC
Challenge maps... does anyone actually enjoy these? I played through 2 of them and couldn't be bothered with the trial and error of know which way to walk through a room of enemies so they magically don't trigger. And the "you messed up this part so have to restart and playthrough the stuff you can no complete while blindfolded.

Overall
If you are familiar with the RE series, the camp and wonky movement, I assume you'll enjoy this game. Since i had not played a resident evil game, I felt myself not favorably comparing this game to Dead Space 1+2, Alan Wake, Metro 2033 or other games that built upon the foundation that the Resident Evil series created. It's not 1998 and games have evolved in so many ways. It looks nice and worth a playthrough but I think the lack of diversity of its 4 playthroughs, depth of story and characters doesn't make this a must have.

I recommend this game, but only once you know what to expect. It has a lot of little gripes that might add up to be dealbreakers for some folks.

First of all, this is a full remake and overhaul of the old Biohazard 2. Tank controls and fixed camera angles are gone in favor of a closer perspective and standard third-person shooting. The story has received some updates, both good and bad. Some characters were fleshed out more and made more compelling, while others had almost their entire story ripped out to give them a bit part. A few of the more gonzo enemies have been removed or redesigned, unfortunately. Additionally, the famous A/B story system is gone; you play two separate campaigns that tread over most of the same scenery with a couple of unique bosses and plot priorities being the only separation between which character you follow. There is no active gameplay interaction between Leon and Claire mid-game, so actions in one playthrough do not affect the other character's next run.

Outside of up to four very slightly different campaign runs, you are given an extra challenge mode to make a speedrun through a predetermined path with a multitude of characters. The first run as H.U.N.K. chronicles his canon escape from Raccoon City, but all subsequent characters with their own loadouts are just for fun (or frustration). The game seems to have been built to cater pretty hard to speedrunners and challenge runners, which may leave casual gamers or explorers feeling a bit starved for content after everything else is done. Lastly, all but one of the infinite ammo toys is locked behind speedrunning the main campaigns.

DLC seems to be an issue; some of the retro nostalgia content that most people would want as an unlockable is barred behind paywalls, while the free stuff may be unavailable in many regions. The playable Ghost Survivors DLC adds 3 new speedrun challenges with barebones "what if?" stories attached to each one. It also adds a single arena mode where you engage with all of the new enemy types in a truly claustrophobic arena, but their generation follows a fixed pattern. Again, the speedrunner catering is strong.

Actual gameplay is fun, but occasionally tedious. Despite what a lot of the negative reviews claim, there is plenty of ammo and supplies to be found, and a lot of the "impossible" bosses just require good strategies. It is not a full run and gun game, but it will punish supply misuse and wastefulness if you flippantly fire shots and crunch herbs for mere scratches. You may actually find yourself with so much stuff that you'll make tedious runs between a new room and the nearest safe room's item box to store all your new stuff.

I absolutely recommend grabbing this on sale, despite its small gripes and major story oversight. If you're a speedrunner or challenge player, then you might be able to justify the full price, but normal folks may feel a bit shortchanged on content as of this review's date.

When you play through Leon, Annette dies in the WEST AREA just before he goes through the elevator.
