[h1]The gist of it:[/h1]
Resident Evil 2 Remake is a third person shooter horror game and a good example of how a remake should be done but not without some issues that just don't click with modern times.

👍 [u]The good parts:[/u]
+Fantastic atmosphere
+Character models are great
+Guns and overall gunplay feels nice
+Despite cheesy/average writing the actors do a good job at voicing the characters.
+Sound design

👎[u]The bad parts:[/u]
-The story even after you get the true ending is average and it shows its age
-Inventory management
-Weak environmental physics, try to shoot a bottle or through glass does nothing for example.
-Having to replay the game again and go through the same key puzzles but with different placements to get to the true ending is very tedious and most of the times makes no sense with what you did previously with the first character. 

[h1]Story[/h1]
The game is a remake of a 1998 game and sadly the story will feel very cheesy or average, nothing we have not seen over the years in horror games. A virus, zombies, 2 protagonists that get caught in the aftermath, a secret corporation that tests multiple viruses for world domination, other secret parties that want the virus for themselves, overpowered creatures, it's all there. The problem with a remake, even if it's perfectly done, you simply will not be able to surprise fans or people who have already played the old games. On the other hand, new fans of the series may find the story mysterious and interesting even with its cheesy classic writing. 

The story allows you to experience the story from 2 points of views each having mostly similar stories. Sadly in order to get to the true ending, you have to play a second time with the other character having to go through all the puzzles and locations all over again but with a different starting point and item/puzzle placements. This could've been great if they showed the story from the second person's perspective in parallel with what you did with the first character. Sadly that is not the case, everything you unlocked and did previously is locked again, puzzles included. On one hand, it does allow you to have a challenging long 2nd run but on the other hand, it makes no sense from a timeline/story perspective and it just feels tedious and boring, for me at least. I could not go through the 2nd run again entirely. The true ending is hardly worth it but it is a proper ending anyway so feel free to look it up if you feel exhausted doing all the things again in the 2nd run.

Story rating: 7/10

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]
I truly disliked the fixed camera from the previous remasters and classic games and I'm super glad they decided to go with the third person. It also increases the horror aspect more, at least in my opinion though not as much as it were in first person view. 

As with all third-person horror games, you have to progress through a series of claustrophobic environments and deal with the zombies and monsters you encounter. The guns you acquire are great and feel great to shoot as well. You can even upgrade them further to help you in dealing with tougher enemies. 

Besides the typical survival shooting the game also has a lot of environmental puzzles. In order to advance you have to find specific keys which go into specific locks which are placed all around the level masterfully. It may seem overwhelming at first with all manner of locked doors however the map is incredibly useful. It shows you what rooms you have explored fully what type of lock is in a room you have not explored what objects you did not pick and many more. 
 
The only negative aspect of the gameplay and it's something I hate in mostly all Resident Evil Games and that is the annoying inventory system. It's a very outdated system in which you have very limited space, you are not able to swap items you find in the world with what you have on you, nor can you drop items which can make some puzzles a chore to keep going back and forth to your box to drop and grab what you need among many other small negatives that keep piling up. No nicer way to put it, it's ♥♥♥♥. Some like it and I guess that's why they keep using it. In a sense, the inventory is a puzzle, which fits with the whole gameplay. I still dislike it. 

Gameplay rating: 8.5/10

[h1]Audio[/h1]
The audio design is surprisingly really fantastic. Voice acting may sound cheesy but that's due to the weak/classic writing. The actors do a good job portraying their characters.
 
Environmental audio is quite well done, as you can hear zombie growls and specific footsteps of a certain individual around the level that just panics you whenever you're close to him or them. 

The soundtrack fits well with the horror and it's never too annoying or very loud. The rest of the sound effects are all decent. 

Audio rating: 9/10

[h1]Graphics, performance and tech analysis[/h1]
The developers did an amazing job remaking the environments, as they look quite nice from an artistic point of view. Level design is great, never too confusing or hard and everything just falls nicely into place while exploring the maps. 

All the characters in the game have superb details, shadows are quite nice, the textures are quite detailed though not every single one and the lighting sets the mood perfectly. 

Sadly they had to cut some other things due to budget, time or just being lazy and that is the environmental physics. Everything around you is mostly static. Try to shoot a bottle or a book on a desk? Nothing happens. You can't move chairs or anything else. Most of the times it feels like you're playing a 2D game in a 3D environment. It hides it well but not all the times. Puzzles are also not real time, which emphasizes what I said. 

From a performance point of view, the game runs smoothly. To summarize quickly I ran the game at 1440p with a GTX 1070 at around 80-100 FPS with most settings at max with the exception of shadows and lighting which really offer no difference between the max setting and the one below it. Those two settings at max seem to eat a ton of frames on my system while visually there were no perceivable differences so if you're on a weaker system lower those settings a notch. 

I have not encountered any game breaking bug and surprisingly not even minor ones. 

Graphics, performance and tech analysis rating: 8.5/10

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
I'm quite impressed with the remake and this is coming from someone who dislikes the franchise and might be biased against it. Not much else to be said, in my opinion even if you're not a Resident Evil fan, I still recommend the game and hopefully with its success the third entry and hopefully the next ones will get some form of remake into full survival horror and less action ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that RE6 gave us. 

[h1]Final score: 8.25/10[/h1]

Resident Evil 2 is a remake of the 1998 original, where you play as either Leon S. Kennedy or Claire Redfield, as they try to escape from the ill-fated and zombie infested Raccoon City. In true Resident Evil fashion, you will be facing a whole lot of zombies and weird, creepy creatures along your journey. 

And what a remake. Capcom has nailed almost every aspect of this game. 

+ Visuals are incredible. Cutscenes are cinematic, well-acted and engrossing. 
+ Sound design keeps you on your toes. Zombies shuffling around, Tyrant footsteps, lickers hissing - the audio's a treat. 
+ The backtracking in this game is so well done (any of the RE games for that matter). The clever use of locked areas to funnel you into certain areas, puzzles with treasures that become relevant later on in the game, and well-designed rooms that make you go "Oooooh that's where it leads" are all the indicators of fantastic level design - something RE2 has in spades
+ Gameplay is smooth, with an over-the-shoulder perspective that is super comfortable to control and a silky 60fps throughout. Some slight drops when transitioning to new areas but other than that, game runs perfectly
+ Post-game content is plentiful (though I miss Mercenaries). Two additional game modes, "second run" scenarios, and there is post-game content coming in February
+ Mr. X is terrifying and reminds me of the Alien from Alien: Isolation

- The "second run" scenarios are too similar to the main story and don't make sense as the second character fights the same bosses and goes through the same story beats even though the two scenarios are supposed to be occuring simultaneously
- Leon and Claire don't interact all that much
- Lip-syncing is sometimes off, most noticeably with Claire in cutscenes
- Not enough music. Safe room theme oddly only plays the first time you switch on the lights, and other areas are completely quiet aside from some ambience. Shame, as the music isn't bad at all. 

The game is  rather short, at around 8-10 hours for one scenario. But this is definitely a game where multiple runs are encouraged to get the complete picture, in terms of story and unlockables. Replay value is high. 

Definitely worth it at full price. Can we get a remake of RE3 and RE4 now?

The first playthrough on standard was reasonably challenging, but not overbearing.

I don't recall much about the original, I played it forever ago when I was like 12. So I know a lot of people will defend the faults by saying it's true to the original. 

Graphically, mechanically, and cinematically, the game is amazing for sure. I think the gameplay is nostalgic of the horror games in the 90's and 2000's. Not because of the mechanics, but just the level design and the progression pacing. I think it did a damn good job hitting the right feels in that department. I think it's also a graphically gorgeous game with some great level design. I have some legitimate gripes beyond that, though... 

Firstly. I think it's ridiculous that they have these side character missions. Both play off stupid gender stereotypes (Claire gets to be mommy and Leon gets to be distracted by an FBI woman who doesn't know how to dress appropriately for her job), but that's basically it. 

There are parts in both the storylines where you get to play these distracting side characters in this subplot sort of scenario. And I barely see the point in the two side characters at all. The FBI Agent was far less infuriating than the child by a long shot. The child's little side mission is so irritating, it took me twenty minutes to figure out where I was supposed to hide, because there was literally only one place you could do it. That was totally worthless. 

Leon is the epitome of a dumb blonde. Not the trained police officer one would expect. Claire is basically a piece of cardboard, but her interactions at least felt more realistic. Leon's forced last-minute romance with the FBI Agent was totally ridiculous. He met her for literally like, twenty minutes and then he's so distracted by her boobs that he starts acting like a complete moron. And I get that the Agent's outfit was an homage to the original- but that doesn't really make it any less obnoxious. I'm glad they had enough sense to change up Claire's outfit to be more practical and less annoying. 

The plot is honestly the worst part of the game. And I know I'm gonna get a lot of hate from the RE community, but RE has barely ever patchworked together a cohesive plot in its entire run as a franchise. I'm not gonna get into it because I am trying not to spoil everything, but the way the characters act about the crisis that's happening around them is so stupid and unbelievable, it's not even funny. 

I very, very rarely say that a game's gameplay and graphics make up for its bad characters and plot- but honestly, I can't help but enjoy playing this game. I really think it's worth something more like $30, at most, though. You can replay after you beat each story in a New Game + to get different endings, but I don't really see why you'd want to grind through the game to get those. 

RE7 was absolute trash and I am glad that the RE team made this game more challenging, they made resources more scarce, and they rewarded accuracy in shooting. I thought they were making zombies HP tanks like they did in 7 to try to make up for the abundance in ammo- but I very quickly realized I was just an extremely bad shot and that ammo is actually pretty damn scarce. It felt like a real survival game, though the HP items were waaaaay too abundant. I think the RE team needs to steer more towards Silent Hill and less towards typical shooters. But that's just my opinion on the franchise. 

Overall, I'd give this game about a 7.5/10. It's not quite an 8 for me, but it's definitely not horrible. I had fun playing and it did feel very nostalgic. But if one more person said, "Go on without me Leon, I'll just slow you down," I would've docked another point. Lol.

I have played Resident Evil 2 on Playstation long ago, and I will say that this remake is just as good.  It was actually Resident Evil 2, that two disc playstation game that got me into the Resident Evil franchase.  Okay so those were side notes, now to review this game in particular.

RE2: Remake has all the graphic power you'd expect from the RE Engine giving the game a real life feel and atmosphere.  The game is genuinely spooky and gives you the creeps when going from one place to the next.  The controls can get wonky sometimes when moving around with a mouse and keyboard which can result in you running right into monsters you are trying to avoid.  The funfactor is great, you will spend a lot of time searching for ammo and managing your inventory while being graded by the game at the end by how fast you completed the game and how many saves you made through out.

You have four versions of the game in one.  You have Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield to choose from.  Leon has two scenarios A and B and Claire has two scenarios A and B.  You don't get the full ending of the game unless you beat the scenario B which doesn't unlock until you beat scenario A.  So if you have played the original game back in the 90s, then you'll understand the scenarios, it's the same.

I recommend this game to people that are casual that want to enjoy the story, just play on easy.  I recommend this game for people that are achievement hungry too, because this game has a lot of replayability.  I particularly did not put  a whole lot of time into this game, but that's probably because I spent most of my childhood playing it all on the original console. 
 This remake is fun, but I was content in beating it one time which I will probably come back to it in the late future for scenario B.

I have been playing Resident Evil games for over a decade. I was hooked on RE2 for the PS1, and played RE1 on the same system, then followed every entry onward with either the PS2 games, emulation or PC ports. I'm incredibly fond of this franchise and its tropes, both narratively and mechanically. So when I looked at the difficulty settings for Resident Evil 2 Remake, I scoffed at the idea of shooting my way through Raccoon Police Department without ink ribbons. “Autosaves [on Standard]?” No way. “For Hardcore Fans of the Series?” Sounds like it was made for me. I selected it and hoped for what I had felt upon playing Resident Evil 1's remake – the same, but more. 
This game is not that. 
It is different, yet less. 
Before I get into the downfalls of the gameplay itself, I want to address the elephant in the room that somehow nobody is talking about. There is no Scenario B. In the 1998 original, Scenario B was a somewhat different route for the characters you picked. An armory that was looted in the A Scenario would be empty in B. Devices activated that weakened enemies in A would strengthen them in B. Bosses would evolve in the B scenario after taking damage in the A scenario. Not only that, but paths would change as well. Side characters' fates would change depending on who you played first, leading to four different campaigns for players to experience. In the 2019 remake, it all has been scuffed to who doesn't get Marvin and who gets a sidearm that messes up ammo drops. You do not even get to run from the cop car to the RPD in the B Scenario – a first sign of many that corners were cut. Notes in the B Scenario disclosing vital character information were cutscenes in the 98 original, delivering plot in an engaging manner. Ada's exposition stroll about Umbrella in the 2019 remake [ Kendo's Gun Shop to the Sewers ] is delivered throughout the 1998 original from characters in conflict. In fact, most plot points from the 98 original are shotgunned into the game so that the game itself can commence. This method of storytelling in the remake somehow dis-includes the entirety of Resident Evil 1's story line – forgoing all information about the S.T.A.R.S. team, the mansion, Raccoon Forest, and the cover up that threatened their lives. Imagine if the film Aliens did not discuss the Nostromo, its crew, or even include the survivor Ripley. We would still have marines blast the hell out of xenomorphs on LV426, but the informed audience would wonder what the hell happened to the prior entry. Capcom couldn't even get the canonical story correct, as it is confirmed knowledge that Claire A, Leon B is the route intended for the official story line of Resident Evil. A story line not even delivered in the remake.
But a game doesn't need the best story ever to be a great game. Doom 93 is still captivating from its first level to its last thanks to amazing game design.
The same cannot be said about RE2 2019's gameplay. On Hardcore, every enemy hits as hard as the next, which makes every encounter frustrating. Zombies can now kill a player in two bites, just as much as a licker can, just as much as Birkin in his final stage can. Damage becomes a meaningless variable to gauge a monster's power when the player is reduced to tissue paper. The weapons are also equally useless. Leaks have shown that damage delivered to the body is always non-specific, which means headshots hit just as hard as arm or leg shots. The chance to crit-hit a head is pointless when leg shots make a zombie almost entirely harmless. On a base level, when a zombie in your game is best defeated by shooting its legs, you are either re-inventing the genre from the ground up, or failed to deliver the expectations of your game's franchise (and the genre as a whole.) Shotguns which have always been the powerhouse of Resident Evil 2 are now useless as zombies can shrug off blasts at random. Advanced enemies will not even notice the shotgun blasting into them as they charge through high-velocity lead obliterating their flesh. The adaptive difficulty in this game creates a sense of constant unreliability as your performance dictates the amount of damage you deliver to enemies. This is incredibly frustrating for me, but it isn't for others. Regardless, the guns in the 98 version put the remake's to shame, as a fully upgraded shotgun can destroy halls of zombies. It was incredibly satisfying – something that should have been passed on from the original to the remake.
A complaint can be made that I want the game to be easier – or that I should play on Standard. However, I like a challenge. I like to feel overwhelmed by forces beyond my ammo count. Standard suffers from being far too easy, as you stockpile more ammo than the original RE2 gave its player – not to mention the ability to save whenever. Hardcore allows zombies to take more lead in their brains in mass than the actual brains that are being destroyed. It feels moronic to be unloading shot after shot into a human skull with no affect taking place. This wouldn't be hard to fix. Add more enemies. The city is completely infected, after all. Take away some of the ammo. Give players a  greater sense of conservation. And of course, make guns feel great. The act of using your weapons in a Resident Evil game should feel like a solution. The puzzle to a hallway full of zombies is a shotgun blast that knocks them to their feet. And of course, get rid of the insane magnetism that this game has. Time after time, I have been pulled into an attack that I was nowhere close to. It was so aggravating to be on an adjacent angle from a zombie's grab, only to be sucked into an animation and bitten. Lower the detection range of grabs. It is ridiculous.
A hope that I had was that the Ghost Survivors DLC would patch up the missing story elements in a neat fashion that Resident Evil 7 had done for its DLC. Unfortunately, we got a horribly scored, remixed version of Hunk's escape mode. After going through each available mission and seeing that Capcom was steadfast in their current vision for the franchise, I quickly dropped the game. I wanted to love this game. I love the franchise and have loved it since I was a kid.
My opinion is that Resident Evil 2 Remake is a poor game, but you can observe that there is less sophistication in the 2019 version than the original game that came out over two decades ago on hardware laughable compared to modern smartphones. Graphically, it is great. Everything else was executed by either cutting corners, ignoring the source material, or forgoing an enjoyable experience for a 'scary' one.
This is a remaster that all remasters need to be judged by.

Note: I just finished my first run. Planning to do a 2nd run.

Resident Evil 7 was my favourite game of the last few years. It was very different from what I was used to in a Resident Evil game, but in its core, it managed to tick all the marks of a great Resident Evil game.

Resident Evil 2 uses that core and cranks it up to eleven. While RE:7 felt like a traditional horror game with scary moments and jump scares, RE:2 mostly gets rid of that and focuses more on the item collecting and puzzle aspects of the series.
The most important change though is the return of classic zombie enemies instead of those swamp monsters.
Similar to RE:7, the game keeps it minimal in terms of enemy variety, but with some added twists. There is no more "3 shot to the head and it stays dead" since a seemingly dead zombie can get up one or even two more times to attack you, when you least expect it. This makes regular zombies much more intimidating and keeps you on your toes. The animations perfectly complement this mechanic. There is a certain kind of risk/reward system to let zombies come close enough to get a clear shot, but not too close for it to lunge and bite you in the neck. If they do though, it is not over. When you're equipped with a knife or grenades, you can use those to resist an attack. Shoving a grenade into an enemies mouth and then shooting it just feels very satisfying.

Now let's talk about the elephant in the room: Mr. X.
There will be a time in the game, where your starting to feel comfortable, when most zombies are dead and you're just running around looting stuff. Enter Mr. X. He will show up at a certain point in the game and after that you'll never feel safe again. You can't kill him, but he is not unfair. You can hear his footsteps, when he's nearby. You can try to avoid him, but if he notices you, he will chase you down. He will force you to make suboptimal decisions that will result and chaos, violence and bloodshed. You wouldn't want to waste any bullets on him, but he will make you lose resources and your nerves anyway.

The gameplay loop is great, the sound design is unparalleled, the graphics are amazing. The amount of options and graphics settings and the way they're presented is awesome. I really love the intro cinematic that comes after the tutorial.
If you enjoyed any Resident Evil game ever (apart form RE:6 maybe), you will most likely enjoy this game as well.

I am really hoping, there will be another co-op RE game at some point. I just hope it won't be such a mess as RE:6 was. Let's just hope they learned their lesson and continue to make great Resident Evil experiences such as RE:7 and RE:2. I, for one, am cautiously optimistic.

Allow me to preface this review: Unlike many other people, I have had no experience playing any game of the Resident Evil franchise. My experience with this game is not from the point of view of playing a remake. To me, this is a brand new game and an introduction to a video game franchise (no need to worry about nostalgia here).

With that preface, let's begin!

[u] Would you recommend this game? [/u]
Absolutely. Why? Quite frankly, it's really fun. I enjoy the puzzle solving elements mixed in with the action and tension throughout the game. I felt that there was a solid balance between these three that pulled me in as I progressed. Some sections were certainly more difficult than others, but I never felt like giving up because it was hopeless. I genuinely wanted to see things progress and see things to the end.

[b] Gameplay [/b]
Like I said, the overall feel for the game was solid. The controls were good on mouse and keyboard, allowing me to move around without issues with the camera (especially considering a third person shooter indoors). The inventory and "crafting" system were very simple and to the point. I love that. X+Y=Z. Nothing much else to it. I like it that way, which was something that could've been me in other survival horror games like in Dead Space 3. Picking up items at times was a little annoying since you sometimes needed to align yourself a certain way.
Combat was pretty straightforward, though I would say that the upgraded shotgun and flamethrower made things a bit too easy on Standard difficult. To be fair though, you rarely had quite enough ammo and inventory space to go guns blazing. Especially when Mr. T chases you down at the sound of a pin drop.

[b] Story [/b]
What can I say? The voice acting and some of the cut scenes were a little cheesy at times. The story moves rather quickly once you know your way around every. The story itself was very out there with Umbrella Corp. and the events in RE2 involving Raccoon City. Yet for some reason, I actually enjoyed it. The game didn't take itself too seriously as a horror game, which was a good thing. I felt that I was playing through a story that was designed for a video game, if that makes sense. Thankfully, RE2 did not feel like some trite horror novella. It was something to be have some good fun and to be enjoyed across two different people with similar, yet slightly diverging story arches. You know what, for a single player horror, I totally didn't mind playing a second time. Nor would I mind playing a third or fourth. 

[b] Graphics [/b]
The graphics are definitely nothing to write home about. That's okay. I enjoyed everything else and did not feel like we needed some hyper-realistic graphics. Plus, much like I tried to explain in the story, the visuals really made me feel like I was enjoying a video game, not some intense VR experience that sacrifices on the action.


Anyway, to those who see this review and are considering purchasing this game, I hope it gives you some insight. I loved it, nice work Capcom!

[b] Summary of the game itself [/b]

I've been waiting for this game for a very long time and since they announced they are working on this I waited years till it is finally out. This game has been an amazing adventure  and worth all the hours I put in within the short time. Resident Evil 2 2018 is based on the original Resident Evil 2 which came out in 1998 and has become modernized with it graphics, game play, and design. There are many nods to the original especially during the opening and with a few confrontations with certain characters. You still recieve both A and B scenarios from the original however it is titled "Second run". They have also added new parts to the game where you get to play as Sherry Birkin! I do believe I got my money's worth especially for the deluxe edition and for its price range is more than fair for what you get. It is also very well optimized with its RE Engine working well even on a 1060!

[b] What comes with the deluxe edition though? [/b]

- 3 costumes for Claire

- 2 costumes for Leon

- DLC Pistol(s)

- Retro Soundtrack swap for the original Re2

[b] Is it worth to buy the Deluxe edition? [/b]

The deluxe edition of this game is not pricey by any means and is just 10 dollars more than the original version at 70 dollars rather than 60. If you are interested in cosmetics then I would say it's worth it especially for the soundtrack swap which brings back a lot of nostalgia for those who originally played the 1998 version. However, if you do not want to then you still get some costumes even if you by the original! You will receive Leon's 1998 outfit after beating Claire's campaign for the first time and receive Claire's costume by beating Leon's campaign for the first time and there are extra versions of those by beating hardcore mode with an S rank and above!

[b] How much content do you receive within this game? [/b] 

There are 4 campaigns however 2 are distinctly different while the other 2 seem to just be the same but playing as the other protagonist. The difference would be playing a new game and then doing a second run (B scenario). After completing these campaigns you will also receive the 4th Survivor mode where you play as Hunk! If you also beat this mode you will unlock Tofu which is a comedic version of 4th Survivor which is much harder and Tofu has 5 versions that you can unlock! If you are a Completionist and like to do everything and unlock everything there are plenty of things to do as well as challenges to unlock special weapons! If you are just a casual gamer I'd still say there is plenty to do if you would like to do everything once and it is still fun to replay if you like to. They're are also adding free content on February 15th which will add short stories of playing characters you learn about within the game and some you will learn more about! It will also contain a more HD version of Polygonized Leon and Claire from the 1998 version as costumes.

[b] TL:DR [/b]

Resident Evil 2 Remake is a beautiful recreation of its 1998 predecessor with lots of content even if you are just casually playing there is still plenty to do after with bonus modes and new content coming February 15th. Very well optimized due to their RE Engine being great for this game. Graphics are stunning with it. If you want costumes its entirely up to you it is just 10 dollars more and it also comes with a 1998 soundtrack swap you can use. You still get the 1998 costumes by just beating both campaigns and free polygon versions of them coming on the 15th of February if you want to get costumes but not buy the Deluxe package.

Resident Evil 2 Remake:

Some spoilers ahead, so if you're looking for the TL;DR:
Aside from the odd bug or 2, HDR issues the game is just incredibly good, its more than just the average remake, this thing is borderline a new game at times and easily tops RE4 as the best entry in the series.

To begin there are 3 gamemodes "Assisted" "Standard" and "Hardcore". Hardcore has ink ribbons and no auto saves, and I mean none. Not like RE7 where there were a few autosaves this has none. Inventory management is also still a thing with limited space, but you can upgrade your inventory similar to RE7.
So it's not fixed camera, which is a good thing as 90's mechanics should mostly stay in the 90's. It is however in 3rd person and this has affected how the gun play works as in the old games it took usually a full clip to down a zombie. However with the 3rd person they decided to keep an element of that but with the added bonus of crits when focusing shots and aiming directly at the forehead (Difficulty adjustment may vary). The amount of gore in this game is just off the walls disgusting and something that has been missing from the series IMO since re7 brought it back, but this game does it so much better, if better is the right word? Other weapons include the traditional shotgun, the grenade launcher, the magnum and the machine gun. All of these weapons can be upgraded. Sub weapons are also a thing in this game the first up being the combat knife. Knives differ from almost every other entry as they now have durabilty and act as both sub weapon and a defensive weapon akin to the REmake. Other sub weapons include flash bangs, and frag grenades both with their respected uses. 
When it comes to enemy types you know what you're getting. First new boys, the G-Adults. These things are easily the worst part of this remake, they are annoying, a nightmare for speedrunning and worst of all, not even remotely creepy or scary. Thankfully they only make a brief appearance and are gone forever. The second of which whilst not "new" have undergone a significant change to be classes as such; "Ivys" which are these plant type zombies that 1 hit kill you if you do not have a defensive weapon. In contrast to the G-Adults these guys are possibly the best new addition, the creepy sounds, the heads shaped like venus fly traps, there is a lot to love about these horrifying things so I won't say too much more.
Finally Mr X himself. Jesus this guy is terrifying, like hearing his footsteps through entire rooms as he hunts you down is easily the most anxious i've been playing a horror game, its similar to Alien Isolation. I really don't want to say too much about him as he's one to experience first hand but he's great.
Last thing, puzzles. They're fun not too hard but harder than RE7 puzzles but yeah not much to say here, if you've played RE before you have an idea of what these puzzles are like, they're not hard but they're well designed and fun nothing here will leave you sat for hours but they might make you think for a few minutes.
To quickly touch on the locations of the game, they are all just as a younger you remember them, if you didnt play the old game, then they're horrifyingly detailed with blood and bodies all over the place, the police station is wonderful, the sewers are a bit of a mixed bag due to the inclusion of the G-Adults and it being a bit too dark in some areas and the lab area, which has been fully redesigned and is my favourite area in the game.
Last second edit here, fourth survivor and tofu survivor are both in this, there is also several unlockable like infinite weapons.

To begin there is an option in the delux version for the OST, personally I was really worried that the old OST would feel a little disjointed or would cut in and out between rooms horribly, thankfully this isn't the case so if you don't care for a new OST the old one works fine with old SFX included.
As for the new OST it IS good, there simply isn't enough of it. For instance the save room music plays once when you enter the save room but never plays again and the main hall theme is the same story. The Tyrants theme as he chases you is anxiety inducing and the 4th Survivor has easily one of the best tracks in the entire OST. Overall it's solid, I just wish it played more.

Graphically this game is astonishing, the RE engine just keeps improving. There is a wide variety in the options menu including an FOV slider and the option to disable motion blur, the game will also tell you when you are overdoing it on the graphics option which is a nice touch. Overall options menu is solid. There are a few issues though, There are some HDR problems that are rather significant, there is also some issues with black screening both on launch and during certain cutscenes in the game, is a simple .ini fix but can really ♥♥♥♥ you over on hardcore runs.

I honestly love this game, it has it's flaws such as the G-Adults and the black screening etc but even with those issues this is easily the best entry in the entire series. Suppose since people tend to wonder, the game is roughly 7-9 hours per campaign although you could spend longer if you take it all in. As of now 61 hours in (most of that pausing and hiding in the stars office/clock tower from Mr X tbf) and i've 100% completed it.

Now this is how a survival horror game is supposed to be done. I played the original RE2 along with almost all the other RE games and I absolutely recommend it to both long time fans of the series and newcomers. Resident Evil 2 Remake keeps the elements that fans love from the original and at the same time it manages to be fresh and impressive as a 2019 game. It has beautiful graphics and that is something you'll be reminded of through out your playthrough. Gameplay is smooth without any major issues(the game crashed only twice in one specific area during my 1st playthrough). The controls, pace and general feel of the game are very similar to those of Resident Evil 7. Well except for the obvious fact that this one is 3rd person, not 1st person. Puzzles aren't too difficult but they're still challenging enough to give you that satisfaction after you solve them. The inventory system forces you to think carefully about what to carry and what to store. As a result you'll find yourself backtracking quite often, especially in your 1st playthrough. Even though some people view this as a downside to the game, it really shouldn't be a con because that is the essence of survival horror, being forced to go back to an area that is filled with zombies and danger to retrieve a valuable resource or key item. The point is to feel the horror, not have your hand held until you reach the end. You got 2 campaigns, Leon's and Claire's. Both campaign's have almost the same puzzles with a few different paths and characters here and there. After finishing the main campaign's, you unlock 2nd run modes that basically put in the shoes of the 2nd character. For example, Claire's 2nd run mode allows you to experience the game from her perspective as the 2nd character after she and Leon split up. It's different from Claire's main campaign because in that one Claire is the main or 1st character(Parallel universe type of thing). Even though there are some plot holes in the progression of the game such as solving puzzles that were already supposed to be solved and finding locked doors that were supposed to be unlocked, I highly advise playing both campaigns and both 2nd run modes as each has its own little twists and new weapons. Plus, you'll get a better understanding of the story with the true ending. The game has binaural audio and it is phenomenal. The sounds that zombies make when they're in your vicinity are terrifying and I love it. I highly recommend playing the game with a headset for the best experience. Overall, I had a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ great time with this game and I give it a 9.5/10. Hope you enjoy it too.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is an example of the modern hype train over a genuinely good product going overboard and turning it into a God.

Let’s clear two things up categorically – this is a fun, fun game and a worthy remake, but it is neither as good as the original, nor as good as the disgracefully underrated Resident Evil Remake.

Let’s start with the basics – remaking RE2 is a true sign, that despite the end product’s quality, that Capcom are completely out of ideas and have resorted to remaking sequels in order to find something new. And the fact the game is pretty darn good justifies their lack of imagination.

But I do wonder when this series will be permanently shelved – RE7 was good, it was, but not very RE’y, while this one is good, it is, but doesn’t really capture the feel and vibe of the original games.

For example – RE Remake absolutely captured the ’96 original, plus massively improved on every aspect that time dictated need a new lick of paint. It is, for me, hands down, by far the best video game remake in history. I didn’t expect this one to match it, and it didn’t.

What is good about RE2? It’s a fun, stand alone survival horror which feels like Outlast in places and RE7 in others – it is visually decent if not stunning, and the gameplay is the RE Engine gameplay the series has evolved into – it is not the gameplay of the originals even if you think it is. It, like RE7, feels disconnected from the earlier games, but even though that is a bit disappointing it’s not the end of the world.

One review made a very fair point – the new police station isn’t well designed. I don’t like the new stairs in the lobby, and the navigation is horrific – it is not intuitive and the frequent backtracking is a nightmare.

I also dislike the hoops you have to jump through to get the magnum – I didn’t get it, completed the game without it, but blow me if I didn’t expect it to be given to me as part of the game. No, turns out you have to bend over backwards to earn it, and I don’t really agree with that. I also don’t agree with making chief Irons’ office non-standard plot either. I didn’t find the club key on my first playthrough so didn’t get to see the backstory there.

But this didn’t ruin the game – I know it sounds like a hating review – I really did enjoy this game, but it in no way captured the magic of the original RE2 and a lot of the changes it made were frankly unnecessary. 

It’s a good game in its own right, but it’s perhaps a little overrated – perhaps others were expecting something different to myself, but I wanted to play a game which felt like the game it was remaking, rather than a RE Engine contemporary take on it.

It didn’t feel like I was in Raccoon City, it didn’t feel like Umbrella’s Lab, and it didn’t actually feel like Leon Kennedy – not that I mind, because he is the most boring and overused protagonist in the series’ history anyway – give me Jill, Chris and Barry any day.

It also bothered me that Leon's scenario saw very little interaction with Claire, unlike the original - for example, no Sherrie in Leon's till the end, and her character being made kind of irrelevant in his first playthrough.

There was also a slight 'bug' whereby the 'so far' summary on the loading screen was illegible because it loaded too fast to read!

I also wasn't fond of the rejiggling of the order of game aspects - and I didn't really like the change in the gun shop owner's character.

But, back on the point – the game is good, very good – it has its faults (zombie bullet sponges are just old and completely idiotic by now) for sure, and anyone thinking this game is perfect has very different standards to me.  

But it isn’t RE. RE will always be the original 90s games – 2001’s RE Remake and more recent HD remaster nailed the old feeling while bringing it into the present. This one just doesn’t.

But I’d still recommend it anyway.

Resident Evil 4 was the first horror or survival horror game I played and quickly became one of my favorite games of all time. I didn't get a chance to play the older games when I was younger, didn't like 5 and 6 very much but loved Resident Evil 7. Needless to say, I was pretty excited about the remake.

I really didn't look into the game at all and knew very little other than the two characters in it. Boy oh boy was I in for a surprise.

This game is no joke.

I thought I was pretty good with horror but this game is much better at scaring me than I am at playing it. I've been fed this idea that being conservative in a survival horror game means that you need to make sure you are efficient... I now realize I didn't know what an actual survival horror game is.

They have done such an amazing job with this game. The RE engine they made for 7 is fantastic. It looks great and runs great but most importantly, it's perfect for horror games. Even though I didn't play the original game, I've watched gameplay and this is definitely a game where technology made everything about the game better.

An adventure or action RPG like Zelda or Diablo will never benefit from better ai, sound and graphics as much as a game like Resident Evil 2 could have. It's visually impressive, the sound design is incredible and enemies are very unpredictable. You would expect zombies to be some of the most predictable enemies and they sort of are... It's how you never know how many bullets they can take, if they're really dead, where they're going to be, how far they'll follow you. I was honestly taken aback at first, having no idea how many bullets a zombie would take before being dead for good. The atmosphere is so perfectly terrifying I hate it. I dread playing this game and I want to stop, but whenever I do, I just want to get back into it.

I'm honestly surprised they didn't try to do something else with this remake. That they made it as difficult and unforgiving as it is. They were very faithful to the original, made improvements where they were needed and didn't remove or break anything that was fine. It's especially surprising to see nowadays, but Resident Evil's future is looking bright (ironically).

I was looking forward to clearing the game and starting over almighty, but RE2 had other plans for me. You get to play as either Leon or Claire and once you beat one, you play the other... Except the difficulty starts basically where it ended.

This game frustrates me. I want to complete everything but it's so nervewracking. It's terrifying but it's too good for me to stop.

If you don't like feeling helpless and scared, you probably shouldn't play this. Otherwise, get it. It's worth they money.

I thought the entire classic genre of RE was dead and lost to a bygone era but this remake has inspired me by giving us a Resident Evil that ditches the clunky controls and camera angles of the originals whilst still maintaining the ambient feel and style of the originals. RE2 expands and is faithful to the original gameplay and story whilst adding enough minor changes to keep veterans like me from finding it predictable, even the voice acting is pretty decent.

I am beyond ecstatic to report that I was wrong, and if Capcom releases a Resident Evil 3 remake in the same style as this one- you can consider me sold. I went into this game with pretty high expectations and I have to say I have mixed feelings about this game.

On one hand it looks amazing. The atmosphere is great, the zombies look amazing, the game is a visual masterpiece. The sound is great, they did an amazing job redoing the levels to make them more modern. I'm really happy with it.

That being said they changed a few things that they should have left alone and didn't change some things that really should have been fixed.

Mr X chases you way earlier on than he did in previous games, and he follows you longer, and you can't kill him. He doesn't drop anything, and his model is so big he can trap you in rooms even if you down him. I'll be honest when I had to do the library section and he kept coming in and stopping me it was infuriating and I wanted to put the game down it was so annoying. That's the long and the short of it. He's annoying. He's not lethal, he might be scary at first but then you get used to him and you just want to solve puzzles in peace. Couple that with the areas that have lickers and him and the player is basically boned since running aggros the lickers and you can't walk faster than Mr. X. Add in the fact that he literally teleports when you fire a gun and you have a recipe for frustration if you didn't already kill everything in the station before he shows up.

The other major problem I have is all the enemies playing dead. It's a zombie, why would it play dead? How does it know to do that? How is that scarier than it just getting back up over and over again? Why does it take 10+ headshots to kill one? That's a tad excessive and I'd prefer they just gave me less ammo and made that ammo actually do something. Couple that with the zombie corpses that you can literally shoot in the head and they won't move until you grab a specific key and you have a recipe for ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥.  Why did the zombie wake up when i grabbed a key and not when I shot him through the eye? It's really odd that a zombie would be so interested in a key and not a yummy person standing on his balls.

All in all the game is decent, has a lot of issues, but it's alright. Makes me very nervous that they'll try to "update" Resident evil 4 at some point and I really hope they leave that game alone.

Amazing remake of old RE2 into modern graphics. Rookie cop and Chris' little sister explore police department, labs. You can play Leon's side or Clair's side of the story, they a bit different. This is easily the best third person horror shooter since Dead Space 1. There are lots of very tense moments and the supplies are rationed out just right to make it feel like you're just on the verge of running out. I'm a little disappointed with how little Leon and Claire actually interact in the story, but it does help with the feeling that you're on your own in the scary situations you're put in.
The only really bad thing I can think of about this game is that you can only experience your first playthrough of it once, and for the price the first playthrough with both characters isn't particularly long. However on the flipside this is good for replayability, as the game is structured in a way that you're meant to play through it more than once, just like older games tended to be. Replaying on a higher difficulty is a thrilling challenge, and the rating system encourages replaying the campaign for faster times to get an S rank, and there are fun rewards for finally getting that high ranking.
There's also FreeLC coming out next month that will help extend the playtime, and hopefully more DLC in the future.

Pros:
- Tight, resource-intensive gameplay which can leave you helpless to the dangers lurking around corners if you play like a mong, or an unstoppable killing machine if you carefully invest in victory.
- The voice acting is MUCH better that previous RE entries. I know it's a bit of a staple of the series to have bad voice acting, but this feels a proper professional outing.

-Well optimized on PC. I manage to maintain solid fps on my old potato PC, so anyone with a half-decent computer will have smooth sailing. It also looks like pretty damn good as well.
-Replayability. A handful of scenerios to choose from, and added challenges for a plethora of unlockables including art, models and infinite ammo weapons.

Can go either way:
-Enemy variety; the bosses have been expanded upon but the vanilla enemy roster has been shrunk.
-I wasn't overly invested in the music. There were some good tracks, such as HUNK's theme, but I wasn't even aware it was there most of the time. The can be different for person to person though.

Cons:
-Last act of the game is pretty weak, same with the original. Enemies are no longer max spook and you have enough guns and ammo to kill everything in sight, generally speaking.

All in all, a very satisfying experience, and I look forward to the Ghost Survivors scenario and a possible REmake 3.

[h1]【[i]Resident Evil 2: REmake[/i] Review】[/h1]

[b]-Still-[/b] a true master class in Survival Horror.  Palm-sweat inducing tension, Tetris-ing the hell out of your inventory space, visceral combat boasting the best zombies ever created in a game, and navigating confusingly familiar-yet-supremely new hallways all make for a truly distinguished afair that only [i]a good Resi[/i] game can provide.

[h1]+Tasty.+[/h1]
[i][u]+Graphics[/u][/i]
1998's Raccoon City looks pretty spiffy with such a fresh lick o' paint.  Some minute textures are blurred, but overall, this game is HOLY CRAP!  On top of that, I was surprised how optimized this game is.  By all accounts, my CPU should "just barely" run this at Minimum settings.  I can run this thing full-beef, albeit removing things I don't personally like, such as Godrays and Motion Blur.

[i][u]+Gameplay[/u][/i]
So much better.  As a "loyal-to-a-fault" fan of the PSX-era Resi's, I willingly admit that the shift to over-the-shoulder works far more in favor of Survival Horror.  The too-cozy confines of the RPD truly make for just uncomfortable scenarios.  In addition to this, I feel the combat has substantial weight.  Tactically knee-capping a zombie to try to pluck a headshot on the one right next to it, all while [i]praying[/i] the loser you just dropped behind you doesn't wake up while you can't see him.  While it provides different experiences than the fixed-camera/tank control combos of yester-century, it still honestly provides genuinely fun Survival Horror moments.
- -I recommend playing with the UI off, and Controls Type B.  I've come to know it more intimiately as "Nuevo-tank" controls.  Everything you can interact with isn't highlighted so you gotta search areas proper.  And, man, does it really make your shots count not having a little dot there to guide your headshots.- -

[i][u]+Zombies[/u][/i]
Yes, they deserve their own mention.  These are [i][u]the[/u] [u]best[/u][/i] zombies you will see in any video game.  Perhaps because of the interactive experience - in any medium.  They are in numbers, they are annoying, and even just one can be lethal.  Oh, and they're genuinely creepy as all get-out.  Their mouths go agape with hunger when skulking towards you.  Their bodies crumple to the floor and uncrumple as they rise.  Their speeds vary.  They scream, shriek, and make some truly gutteral sounds.  I love this game solely for the extra-emphasis Capcom placed on these guys.

[i][u]+Pacing[/u][/i]
I liked the pacing.  The beginning bits are slow and exploratory, then Mr. X shows up and it becomes a game of cat and mouse (and dog programming), then it veers closer to slick action.  The alternative scenarios and all the unlockables that have become part-and-parcel for the series keep an excellent pace outside of the story, itself. 

[i][u]+Setting[/u][/i]
The RPD, the sewers, the Umbrella Facility... the 90's.  It's all captured here with pretty good fidelity.  Some may pick and squabble over certain technologies, but overall, I genuinely appreciated the overall setting of the game.  Additionally, the sound effects are superb.  And the classic Soundtrack swap, as all these new games seem to be doing nowadays, still lends itself nicely to the overall experience.

[i][u]+Fanservice[/u][/i]
The classic outfits.  The classic sound effects.  The setting.  The continued support via upcoming DLC's - even if they're only sidestories and blocky PSX models.  Seeing it all blend so fantastically.

[h1]-Itchy.-[/h1]
[i][u]-Lore Bits[/u][/i]
Okay, masterful writing [i]RE[/i] has never been.  But, reading the various notes and things throughout the game,  I found this to be the [i]least genuine[/i] part of the experience.  I dunno if it's for lack of trying on the writers end, or Bethesda's fault for taking the ball from Capcom and running with it in an open-world space, but damn I found these notes quite boring to read.  They didn't ...haunt me like the notes from the original [i]RE[/i]'s did.  Even the initial [i]REmake[/i] had some chilling lore added (i.e. - Lisa Trevor).  What was gained in the ability to show was seemingly lost in the ability to tell.

[i][u]-No Crimson Heads[/u][/i]
Possibly the most ingenious addition to the original [i]REmake[/i], I was kinda sour over the lack of Crimson Heads.  While the zombies are genuinely better, nothing beats that first moment we all encountered a Crimson Head.  Claire's lighter woulda really came in handy this time...

[i][u]-Intro Sequence[/u][/i]
Yeah, the trek to Kendo Gunshop - and even Kendo, himself (due to DLC reasons) - is absent from the beginning.  Instead, you're met with two streets full of zombies, and one little alleyway that connects it to the RPD.  While still impressive to see from the perspective, it's still quite a lack-luster opening to an otherwise supreme affair.

Also, why does Claire [i]start[/i] with a gun?  One that's openly holstered on her leg?  I get it - Chris taught her to protect herse- yadda yadda whatever.  But still - why does she have a gun, and why is she so comfortable having it on display? I'll suspend my disblief for all the other b.s. in this game, but that was a bit problematic to me from a narrative perspective.

[i][u]-Claire's Face[/u][/i]
Yeah, no.  Why is she constantly smilling?  Did she Vaseline her teeth?  People are dying and trying to eat you.  Also problematic from a narrative perspective.

[i][u]-Mamby-pamby Hand-holding[/u][/i]
Everything that you can interact with has an "A" button over it.  And you can't have the UI off but the crosshair on to avoid this, so it's either theme-park central, or hardcore aiming.  The map marks not only what specific items are in what specific rooms locked behind what specific keys, but the literal physical location you can access these items simply by lining your triangle up with it's icon on the map.  The keys have a constant check-mark on them, letting you know you can safetly discard it.  Every quarter of the game, your inventory expands (whilst still constrained, it's way easier than it was).  I would have loved for them to take the hint from the last craptastic [i]Tomb Raider[/i] game and set these things by degrees.

[i][u]-The Longing for the Next Entires[/u][/i]
[i]Nemesis[/i].  [i]Code: Veronica[/i].  [i]Outbreak[/i] (Files 1 AND 2!).  Yeah, we all want them, same as we've been wanting RE2 since the first [i]REmake[/i] back in... bumbumbummmm dramatic reverbbbb.... [b]2002[/b].  Seeing Mr. X as more of a relentless presence gives me hope they were laying the groundwork to perfect the tech for Nemesis, but who knows when/if we'll see it.  They know we want it.  We know they can do it.  Until then, we'll always have this and the original [i]REmake[/i].

[h1][u]Final Verdict:[/u][/h1]
As a serious fan of the original trilogy, with RE2 being my first entry into the series at the ripe age of 9 years old, I had high expectations. This was/is my quintessential remake.
 This title greatly exceeded those high expectations in almost every substantial way - from overall performance to the gameplay to the narrative (I was worried they'd overplay Chief Irons creepiness - he was just right).

Old meets new, and literally everybody wins!
... except for maybe, once again, the denizens of Raccoon City.

This started out looking like it was going to be a great game but the ammo rationing got really stupid, really fast and essentially ruined the game for me to the point I doubt I'll finish it!  Zombies take about 10 rounds to kill on medium difficulty but you'll probably never have more than 20 rounds in your inventory at any one time.  And you can just forget about taking on anything bigger than a zombie with a handgun, you'll just die over and over.  I know this game isn't an action/shooter but spending most of your time running away from everything because you're always nearly out of ammo isn't scary, challenging or fun; it's just irritating and frustrating.... at least to me.  And don't get me started on Mr. X.  Whoever thought having an unkillable, unstoppable monster that chases you around the entire game guaranteeing you can't take any time figuring things out should be horsewhipeed.  

On the positive, the graphics look great and I really enjoyed Claire's character.  She's hot to look at and well played by her voice actor.  The atmosphere is also superb and since I played the original 25 years or so ago, all the throwback designs and references were really nice. 

Overall this is a really well made game with great graphics, voice acting and gameplay.  Unfortunately the ammo rationing just sucked all the fun out of it for me.  If you love horror games more like Alien Isolation, then you'll like this one.  If your tastes lean more towards Dead Space then avoid this one or at least wait and catch it on sale so you don't waste $60.

A maze of horror, filled with puzzles and nasties and limited resources and pockets. You will find yourself walking into every room praying for either a typewriter or a greenherb. Zombies that you're sure you've put and end to, unexpectedly resurrect at the worse of times. The labyrinth of rooms means you need to check everywhere properly, including items you find otherwise you might actually get stuck. Boss fights require mutiple attempts and a tad annoying, but ultimately this is riveting survival/exploration horror done right. The sound effects and dread tones as you walk into some of the rooms genuinely gave me goosegumps sometimes. Eeek!

Play this on the hardest difficulty.

It turned the game into the best survival horror game I've ever played.

I dreaded thinking about where and what you have to do next. I spent 10 minutes panicking, just looking at a map dreading what I knew had to do...

Every aspect of this game is designed to make you anxious, stressed, and rethink your decisions. 

Movement is quick and responsive, but not fast. Running will still be your best option a lot of the time. But running perfectly around zombies is really hard to pull off. Which makes for a sense of mastery when you get better at it. Moving while aiming also increases your guns cone of accuracy. So you'll have to choose between well-placed shots, or making distance between you and the enemy.

Guns are satisfying, varied and well paced throughout the 2 campaigns. Zombies will take what seems like a random amount of headshots to die though. Again, adding to the stress.

Ammo and items are given to you at the perfect rate, and in the right amount. On my first playthrough, I barely had enough to beat the bosses... And I was conserving ammo earlier in the game.

Item management is tough. You can use some ammo to make your fight easier, but you'll likely need it later. You can carry many items like grenades or herbs to help you, but then you won't have enough room for other items on the ground. Then you'll have to backtrack through enemies (possibly making you use more ammo than if you just had room to pick it up the first time you were there) or delete an item in your inventory. Item management is hard. And affects the game in serious ways. It's perfect for this game. 

Enemies are introduced at a rate that keeps things fresh. And Zombies alone can be VERY hard to deal with early on. 

I don't want to spoil anything but this game does have a timer during sections of the game. You'll have to deal with things quickly. It adds SO much stress to the game. And it is implemented perfectly!

I also had a note pad with me to keep track of some of the puzzles for later use, I've literally never had to do that in a game and it was awesome lol

The game also has a pretty long run time.

Finishing with Leon on my first playthrough had me wanting more. And playing the Claire 2nd playthrough delivered on a variety of gameplay, and story. That might be annoying to some, but the differences were enough for me to love it!

For me, this game is perfect. I cannot find one thing I didn't like about this.

Pros:

+THIS is how a remaster/remake is done. Its hard to believe this is a game from over a decade ago, but it is. It feels and plays like a 2019 AAA horror game. 
+Character models, facial animations and superb voice acting make each character feel real and easy to empathize with. 
+The narrative is decent, its a run of the mill zombie outbreak via viral bioweapon story where you must save the day. But its hard to criticize the writing for being cliche due to the fact that it was written a decade ago, so by those standards it was unique and new.

+The gunplay feels great, there are some really cool weapons and the resource management is balanced perfectly. You'll never be able to swoop through the map killing everything, but youll never be completely out of ammo either. 
+Zombies sound and look amazing, their clumsy and rigid movement and gait really sell it. 
+The sound design is superb, guns, zombie groans, glass breaking, cars crashing, it all sounds like its from a movie.
+Graphics are amazing, and its optimized very well. No performance issues, im on an i7 8700 and GTX 1080 playing 4k with most settings at high or max and getting 60 FPS stable.
+Havent encountered a SINGLE bug or glitch, this game is polished incredibly well.

Cons:

-For $60 the game is really short. Youll beat the campaign in about 4-5 hours, which is absurd for a AAA $60 game. Luckily you can do additional playthroughs with one of the two characters, Leon or Claire.

-Sadly the two character campaigns are mostly the same, and only diverge for short side narratives. For the most part its the exact same playthrough.

-Mr. X (an unkillable enemy that will relentlessly stalk and try to kill you) is a total nuisance. I get that it adds to the tension since your constantly being hunted, but since he is so slow and easy to avoid, it really just ends up being an irritating detour to whatever you were trying to do. Interrupting puzzling and exploring constantly, its a poorly implemented mechanic.

Overall: 8.6/10

The original RE2 is one of my favorite games of all time. After RE4 came out however Capcom changed the direction of the series to a more mass appeal shooter approach. They tried to walk it back some in later games but never seem to actually reproduce the lost survival horror feel of the original games. I'm glad to say that despite choosing to use the over the shoulder camera style for this game, they have finally managed to reproduce the feel the original games created. That perfect blend of horror with dangerous enemies, limited ammo, and just the right amount of ability to fight back with whatever you can find to survive. All while exploring a large intimidating Gothic style Police Station reading notes left behind, and solving puzzles that force you to revisit that hallway full of zombies you really didn't want to have to go back through. And that's all before you even get stalked by a massive unkillable enemy who follows you everywhere.

That experience alone is worth the money. But if your a returning fan wanting to know how well it holds up as a remake. The answer is pretty damn well. Almost every location from the original game is revisited in a heavily reimagined way. All the characters return too though many act very differently. It can be very entertaining seeing the story again through this more serious dark tone. The few negative faults I can find with this game is the new soundtrack is very dull, and quiet. Making it almost necessary to buy the original OST dlc. And that the games 2nd run feature feels hastily implemented. It does not completely change the story, and boss fights like the original game did to make the games narrative make sense from both characters point of view. This gives it a little less replay value but does not ruin the game.

RE2 2019 captures the charm and horror of the original 1998 release and reinvigorates it with modern mechanics that are balanced to modernise the horror of the undead successfully. 

Resources are scarce and enemies hit hard, meaning that there's now a better emphasis on dodging or stunting their efforts by shooting the limbs off of the undead rather than outright killing them. Pair this with the aimed critical hit system which improves damage and accuracy the longer you take to aim, and the game rewards thoughtful and calculated uses of every bullet.

After completing the first run, the second run of the game for the opposite character is unlocked. It doesn't matter how you experience the routes now as Claire A/Leon B from the 1998 release is now canon regardless of route.

Once beating that, you unlock The 4th Survivor. Beating that unlocks The Tofu Survivor. Additional free DLC in the form of The Ghost Survivors also adds more play, but is recommended to beat both runs first before experiencing. If you're comfortable with modding the game, I highly recommend the First Person Camera mod as it ramps up the horror experience even further. I played with it for my S+ ranking for Claire A, and it works a charm.

The Deluxe Edition isn't needed to enjoy the game, but I do recommend the Classic OST pack for those who wanted to hear the aesthetics of the 1998 game in this newest release. The game's design is so faithful to it's concept that the Original OST still fits perfectly. You even get the Classic sound effects like the chilling Title Screen call and the beeps of the old menus.

This game has me emotional in a way I can’t explain. I’ve loved the Resident Evil series with a fiery passion ever since I played my very first entry with Code Veronica X on the PS2. After I finished playing the hell out of that game, I devoured every Resident Evil title I could get my hands on and was a dedicated fan (even wrote my share of fan fiction) all the way up until Resident Evil 6, which thoroughly ripped my heart to shreds with what the series had become. While RE7 was something of a return to form despite the first person perspective, it was missing the one thing I loved so much about these games; the characters. I didn't realize until now how badly I missed my time with them, but stepping into Leon S. Kennedy and Claire Redfield’s shoes again felt like coming home.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1639405393
That said, I was terrified that like so many overly-hyped, high profile titles these days, that Resident Evil 2 would stumble and miss the mark. But let me tell you, they nailed it. THEY NAILED IT! Granted, the story has been somewhat simplified, and the B scenarios feel rushed and a bit tacked on (likely a result of the devs not wanting to disappoint the fans when word leaked that they wouldn’t be included), but those are miniscule grievances when the rest of the game is so supremely satisfying. Everything that I loved about the series is back, and it all looks, sounds and feels so good that I’m literally getting choked up right now just typing this.

Even the swap to over-the-shoulder camera feels fitting and natural, and I’ve long been a champion of fixed camera angles. But the way the action is framed, the long, dark, endless corridors, the creatures that lurk in the shadows, the terrifying sounds they make, it all makes up for the loss. Fortunately, the characters don’t move with quite as much agility as they do in post-RE4 titles either. There’s no dodge button, no quick time events, no counterattacks. If you’re grabbed by a zombie, you either shove a grenade down its throat or suffer the consequences. This heightens the suspense tremendously. No matter how heinous the foe, you need to tread carefully, and wisely.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=1640404534
And that's not even mentioning how much better the writing and acting is. The dialogue actually sounds somewhat believable, albeit cliche at times, and the interactions between characters are so much more organic than they used to be (thank goodness there’s no “I love you” moment…) All of this is elevated by the voice actors giving great performances which really help bring these characters to life. We already know who bad-ass super agent Leon S. Kennedy is, but it’s refreshing watching the rookie cop become the man we all know and love.

I honestly could continue gushing about the game for several more paragraphs, but there’s already thousands of reviews that’ll say the exact same thing. So I’ll just say this; if you’re an old school Resident Evil fan and you can get past the modernization of a classic, then you need to play this game. YOU NEED IT! This is old school survival horror in a gorgeous new wrapping, and every bit as good as the original.

I remember when I played the first 3 games on playstation 1, I was a kid and didn't know that much of english back then, so I've completed the games few years later, but I liked them from the beginning. They were intense and scary but fun too.

While I think that the RE 1 remaster wasn't that good (graphically it was, but the controls haven't aged really well), I'm glad they decided to remake the second game, bringing the over the shoulder view (which I think is a major point why this game plays so well). You can see that they put effort in almost every aspect of the game, bringing new stuff to the old stuff, this is how you do remakes.

Gameplay is awesome, they kept some good aspects of the original game (ink ribbons, save stations, safe rooms), but they kept the game modern, it doesn't feel like a remake of an old game, it's feels like a 2019 game in almost every aspect.

The graphics are top notch, perfomance too, and the settings are vast and even someone with a lower tier pc can customize the settings to try to squeeze as much fps as possible. The only thing that I don't like about the graphics is the Screen Space Reflections. They are broken, muddy and overall you should disable the setting until they fix it (but the same problem was in RE7 and they didn't fix it so they probably won't fix it in the remake).

The audio is awesome, the ambient sound is so real and creepy, it's not only that visually it's scary to walk through the dark hallways, the sound and much more horror to it. And the intense music is just the icing on the cake! Especially when Mr.X comes chasing! One tip: enable binural audio if you are playing headphones, it adds 3d space so you can better hear where from the enemies are coming.

The story is alright, they kept it fresh even though the original game is 20 years old, I just wish that the A and B story had much more gameplay tyings (like what you do with Leon in A affects significally on Claire B), but hey, it's good enough right now. And there's free dlc coming on 15.2 so that's awesome!

At the end, thanks to Capcom for making such a good game and I totally recommend it, hope it will sells well (it already shipped 3 million copies) so maybe we can get more remakes in this fashion (RE: Code Veronica, RE3).

I am very glad that Capcom went back to this style of RE. It's pretty much the old way it used to be with keys, puzzles, backtracking, ammo conservation, and horror elements. But now its also fully 3d and has more precise control. In order to compensate for the constant headshots you will be pulling off, the developers made the zombies major bullet sponges. I kinda wish there was a bit less ammo available but the zombies died a bit quicker (4-5 shots to the head seems like it would have been more appropriate). Sometimes I found shooting the same zombie in the HEAD 8-12 times and the thing was still alive... This was kinda annoying to be honest. 

The story is told rather well, with a great 3 act structure and fairly well acted characters. Although, Claire and Leon seem to be really unfazed by any of this zombie outbreak/mutants/viruses/ They act like they are already confident and barely ever show any emotion or fear. I am not necessarily against this, but a little fear at the start of the game would have sold these characters more I think.

One major complaint I have is with the presentation. The game uses heavy color grading in places which in my opinion ruins a lot of the atmosphere. One area will have a blue tint, another will have an orange/brown tint, another will have a teal, etc. Game looks the best by far when there is no filter involved (eg: garage areas). I wish there was a way to turn that **** off. 

Also the tonemap in this game is f***ed.. No matter how you set up the brightness the highlights will be too dim and the black levels will be raised, so the game will look washed out. I fixed this by using ReShade and adjusting with "levels".  Wish the tonemap was correctly balanced as it was in Resi 7. 

Another gripe I have is with the music. The overall sound design is great but more music is badly needed. I wish all saverooms played the saveroom music at all times. Instead this game plays it only for a bit when you turn on the light in certain saverooms. Don't understand this change. RE7 had a great saveroom theme and it added a lot of personality to the game. Also made it more memorable.

-there are 3 free dlcs planned as of right now, but based on the atrocious re7 DLC's I am not really hyped in the slightest
