Resident Evil 2 2019 is probably going to be my game of the year. 2019 has a lot of games coming out that I am interested in, including but not limited to Metro Exodus, Days Gone, Kingdom Hearts 3, Devil May Cry 5, and more. But this game holds a special place for me, because I was around at the time Resident Evil was introduced into the world and started setting standards. I played the original RE2 demo on PS1 when I was a kid. My friends brother talked about it constantly. Without internet access back then it was hard to guage how amazing it was doing but the Playstation magazines and reviews written inside them told me how well it was doing. People loved RE2. But does it hold up to my expectations? I can't say. I never played the full original game. But what I can say, without being a massive fan of the series at all, is that I absolutely loved this game.

What does it get right? Mostly everything. I have a bit of a bias for games that have very obvious game mechanics. I love that this is a horror game trying to tell a story in which there are zombies, while simultaneously there are ridiculous puzzles as well. How do we open the door in the sewers? Oh easy, go and find all of the chess themed electric plugs and plug them in! On the surface something like that is just so farfetched it's almost comical, but I seriously love it. The puzzles are the main focus for me. Having to find the spade and club keys to open those doors, find all the medallions to escape the police station, make sure you mix the chemicals right to douse the plant life, these things offer so much more than simple tasks to do. It fulfills that itch I have for exploration and progression.

The story here is nothing super noteworthy. Without spoiling it I will just say that it's pretty simple. But I loved the characters performances and it kept me intrigued. The option to play as two characters and get different playthroughs is really awesome too.

So what did I like? Pretty much all of it. I loved the locations, the puzzles and the story wasnt amazing, but still good and interesting. But do I have complaints? Of course.

First the map. When you press M and bring up the map it shows your location and what rooms you have come across. It also shows you if those rooms and been thoroughly explored aswell. If you haven't found all the items in a room it will be red. If you have then it will be blue. If the room is black that means you haven't been there yet. I can accept that a room will be black and light up blue when you enter to show you have been there, that's fine. But I don't like it when the rooms are red until you have found all the items in it. To me this killed that sense of exploration a little. Rather than always be thinking there might be something else I haven't found yet, instead I just used the colour coded map to figure out if I was wasting my time. Once a room was blue I didn't have to worry about that room anymore. I really don't like this feature. This is my one major complaint.

The second is similar but less of an actual complaint and more just a nitpick. When you find a key item it goes into your inventory. Once you have opened all possible doors or locks with that item it gets a little red tick on it to indicate that item has run it's course, it has no more use. Meaning you now should discard it since it's just taking up space. When I first noticed this tutorial message pop up after using the spade key enough times I was really disappointed. The message left me knowing there were no more spade doors and to me that killed the sense of exploration yet again. I was so taken aback by this I immedately went into the options and turned off tutorials. I would rather have not known. Even if there weren't any more, let us imagine that there are. Let us think there are. That makes it so much better for me personally because I don't know whats ahead. There COULD be another spade door. But there also might not be. Who knows? Lets explore more to find out!

But those two things aside, this game is incredible. They did a massively amazing job with this remake. The third person camera angle works very well. The zombies seem a little bit random when they decide they're going to legitimately die or not, but I don't see this as a negative. I think the way these zombies behave and the way they just get up again sometimes is extremely intense and somewhat nerve wrecking. The boss fights are challenging if you don't know what they do. The game also runs very smoothly. I have heard people having problems with stuttering but for me this didn't happen so  maybe do some more research on what cards and setups people seem to have issues with.

Overall a very good game and I'm extremely satisfied with it. A perfect start to a new year. I'll be keep close attention on this supposed Resident Evil 3 Remake.

[b]Resident Evil 2[/b] was initially released for the PlayStation back in 1998 and it was a huge success, easily becoming the favorite of the vast majority of the Resident Evil player base, this version is a complete [b]remake[/b] ([b]not remaster[/b]) of the 1998 original game, built on the RE Engine that was created by Capcom and used on the also very successful Resident Evil 7, because of that the game has very beautiful graphics which helps to create a perfect terror atmosphere.

In Resident Evil 2 you play either as Leon S. Kennedy, a rookie cop arriving for his first day on the work as a police officer in the Raccoon City Police Dept. or Claire Redfield, a student who recently just arrived in the city to look for her brother, Chris Redfield, also a cop and one of the main characters in the first Resident Evil game.
They arrive in a city taken by chaos because of a viral outbreak that turns people and even animals into flesh-eating monsters, seeing as the streets are taken by zombies they decide that the best course of action is to head to the police station as it's most likely the safest place, however that isn't the case and most of the story goes on in the police station.
The game offers the viewpoint from both characters in "different" (more on the quotes down in the review) scenarios which in the original game were labeled as scenario A and B, which means you have at least 4 different plays in order to see both scenarios on both characters, so that paired with extra modes such as the 4th Survivor and Tofu (don't ask), which you unlock by finishing the game, means Resident Evil 2 has a significant re-playability.

 This game was remade from scratch using the latest of Capcom's engine, RE Engine and has similar graphics to Resident Evil 7, however it's uses the over-the-shoulder camera, similar to Resident Evil 4, instead of first person, a change that fit really well with this game.
The game is graphically demanding, however it's quite well optimized and runs really well even in computers that are not in the recommended requirements range.
I've seen very few complaints regarding bugs or performance issues with the game, the ones I've seen are actually related to drivers and not with the game itself, so the quality of the game is very good.

Now the pros and cons:

[b]Pros:[/b]
- Wonderful graphics
- Fantastic gore system
- Familiar locations to old school fans
- New locations that make even the oldest fans surprised
- Great re-playability 
- Very well polished
- Runs very well
- Good variety of characters to play as (2 main characters, 2 "4th survivor" characters and 3 extra characters coming in the free DLC)
- Free DLC with 3 extra stories
- Reasonable priced for such a good game

[b]Cons:[/b]
- "Different Scenarios" are actually the same with minor changes, so either A or B feels the same, just some items and puzzles change
- Zombies are ridiculously strong, depending on difficulty you play on it can take up to 15 [b]head shots[/b] to kill one (although it will usually take 5~8, which is still insane)
- Can get repetitive
- A lack of coop or "versus" mode
- Capcom tried to improve the story but forgot several important elements that relate Resident Evil 2 to the first game, also a lot of interaction between both main characters that happen in the original game was completely left out of the remake

As you can see, I am very impressed with the game, not only it looks nice, but it also plays nice.
The original 1998 Resident Evil 2 was my favorite game in the franchise, I've played it a lot not only on my PlayStation but also on my Nintendo 64, so it's no surprise that I was extremely excited and hyped for this game, fortunately Capcom did not disappoint, the game is absolutely amazing and is probably one of the very best games I've played in a forever, heck, it's probably the best in the franchise right now, it brought the psychological terror back to the Resident Evil franchise in a familiar, yet new and exciting way.

In my opinion this game is a masterpiece and even if you have not played the original or was never a huge RE nerd like me you should still buy and play this, as long as you're a horror game fan you'll enjoy.

It is rare that a game actually moves me to post an online review but here I am writing about not only the great aspects of this game but… the unfortunate let downs it had for me.

While the game feels familiar they devs did a lot of rework to the interior of the station and the overall atmosphere is captivating to say the least. From the main hall to the side rooms that we oh so fondly remember clamoring through all those years ago were faithfully recaptured in the redesign. On the same not the atmosphere of every section of the game and its lighting are top notch and really draw you into the story and tragedy of Racoon City. Also the voice acting was not totally garbage! For all my zed killers out there all gun models and upgrades made their way back into the remake for us to go hog wild with!

Moving to combat all I can say is ♥♥♥♥! ♥♥♥♥! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! BULLETS! RUNNING OUT! ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥! That is in no way a bad thing! Your ammo expenditure is a major factor in playing this game. Zombies are absolute units and take a ton of shots just to keep them down but remember, the goal is not to kill them it’s to survive! The biggest enemies in the game are the most deserving of your freedom pellets. Also the inclusion of the grenade and knife mechanic when being attacked is a god send. You will find yourself more times than not ramming a grenade down a zeds wind pipe or shanking it to throw it off. These are in fact VIABLE options to make your way through certain areas. If you don't believe me I got one word for you Tofu. The combat functions similar to RE 4 but it is fixed to the RE 7 engine so everything is just as smooth as we would expect for a 2019 game.

Transitions are weird! So the survival aspect of this game is something that takes into account everything from above and mixes it with your own intelligence. Barriers for windows are plentiful to help with the worst halls and herbs are in no short supply if you play with half a brain. Healing items are not unlimited past “easy” mode and you must weigh out if that one hit really requires a heal or if you can limp it out for a short time. This game will stick you in do or die situations where your bullets do not count for a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ thing and only your intelligence will save you. There is a rather large man that goes by MR. X that would agree with everything I said. Take into account also that dynamic sound is something that enemies use in this game to track you and find you… ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ lickers.

The Story has had several major adjustments that I am going to keep spoiler free but Clair is BEST GIRL. The character development is fairly fluid and it makes sense given their circumstances. But the best character change in my opinion is Annette Birkin. Anymore and I risk messing up the story for newcomers. Also you get some playtime outside RPD and that's ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ neat if you ask me. It's now time to dive into the disappointing aspects of this game.

Resident Evil 2 had such a diverse story between Leon and Claire in the original and I am sad they could not recapture that same synergy in the part B playthrough. They crossed over a lot of the same content between the two and that sort of killed my vibe on the part B. Also the sewer segment of the game just did not feel as treacherous as the first iteration of the title. Also where the ♥♥♥♥ are the spiders? The boss battles have a lot of hate from some people but to me they are way to easy. The build up to the swings are fairley telegraphed and the game gives you some really obvious openings to hit the vital parts of their body. The zombie models while looking good could have used some more variety in my opinion.I honestly killed the same model 5 times in one playthrough. 

In closing I would like to recount my personal favorite moments that moved me to give this a positive review. Mr. X attempting to kill me at every turn while dodging lickers like a baller. The model designs for G are absolutely grotesque and I LOVE IT! Annette Birkin. The constant struggle for ammo and weighing out medical supplies and defence items. The exploration and puzzles in every section of the game. Honestly no area ever felt dull or out of place.

From a guy who has enjoyed this series since the PS1 Director's Cut RE1 I would give this remake a 9/10.

Thanks for taking the time!

This is a fantastic remake of a classic. Where so much could go wrong, practically nothing does. Graphically it is amazing and the soundtrack is brilliant. The enemy design is top notch not just visually but their behaviour; my favourite being the Tyrant chasing you through the police station. As Claire I think I did about ten laps of the police station with him chasing me. I think that the strongest choice they made though was not to have it as just a straight up copy of the original release, and the new sections give us some of the strongest moments my favourite being the orphanage section. 

There are some things I dislike such as fragile combat knives; weapon degradation is not fun. The other gripe is unskippable prolonged death animations, after the first few times some of them are so protracted it feels quicker to forcibly close the game and restart; just let us bring up the load game option so we can get on with it. The final thing isn't so much the game but a design choice: games grading your performance. I always prefer it when the developers leave it so you can just play your way and not feel rushed so to unlock certain things that a lot of use would like to see like concept art and close ups of the 3D models.

All in all this is an amazing remake which doesn't just cash in on nostalgia as much as it sets it up to be remembered on it's own as an amazing product. Bring on the Resident Evil 3 Remake!

This is the single best game remake of all time, bar none. Resident Evil 2 (from 1998) was already at the peak of its genre, even if the tank controls and fixed camera angles haven't aged so well, and the 2019 remake takes it one step further by bringing the game into the modern era with absurdly good visuals, much improved voice acting, a brilliantly composed soundtrack, and a buffet's worth of bonus material. You get to play the game as one of two characters, each having their own unique storyline that takes roughly 3-6 hours depending on whether or not you have the Gamefaqs walkthrough open on your other monitor like the pleb you are. Upon beating the campaign as one character, you unlock the alternate scenario as the character you didn't choose, and upon beating [i]that[/i] campaign, you unlock a bonus time attack mode starring the best character in the franchise,[spoiler]Hunk[/spoiler], which then leads to more and more modes until you end up surviving a zombie apocalypse as a [i]♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ piece of tofu armed with 16 combat knives and Japanese insults[/i]. Needless to say, this game has enough content to justify the $45 I spent on it (shoutout to greenmangaming for the preorder discount code they hooked me up with, y'all are the best).

I have to say though, as someone who beat the original numerous times as a toddler, I wasn't prepared for the difficulty spike from the 1998 version to the remake. Whereas [b]literally[/b] every other zombie game on the planet says "shoot their heads to make them go pop", Resident Evil 2 takes a different approach by making zombies into bullet sponges and giving the player very little ammo. Instead of aiming for the head, you should either just run past them, or, and I cannot express how much I appreciate the dismemberment system in this game, you can shoot them in their feet to tear their legs off. There's an available hardcore mode that's simultaneously more and less faithful to the original game by making the zombies [u]even more resilient and giving you less than half the ammo[/u], while also forcing the player to use consumable ink ribbons to save the game, meaning you can only save a finite number of times per playthrough on hardcore. I figured that with my experience of the original that I could handle hardcore, but no. I wasn't even remotely prepared. [b]Don't even think about playing on hardcore for your first playthrough[/b]. Stick to normal (or assisted if you're using a controller, since it has aim assist), learn the in-depth mechanics like AI lasso ranges, and then consider hardcore.

I truly hope that this game sells well enough to justify Capcom remaking Resident Evil 3: Nemesis in a similar fashion, because it gets a solid 10/10 from me. This is the best game of 2019, and it's only January.

Overhyped? - In my opinion, yes. It's not that's it's not entertaining or fun, it's just not a game that offers anything remarkably new or fascinating to those who have been there and done that, it's a remake so the story is already known but it stil provides a positive experience, mostly with controls and camera work if you remember the old games. It's a polished and decent game, but as a veteran, not something you should be racing to buy because you're expecting this new and
amazing experience. 

I bought it knowing what it would be, a zombie game with familiar and nostalgic puzzles, but I think it's worth waiting for a sale if you're not too anxious to play it now.

With that being said, experiences can vary wildly with a game like this, ESPECIALLY, if you are not familiar with the series, the mechanics, puzzles, atmosphere can be new or sort of familiar. You've just might not have seen before these elements in a game before quite done like they are in Resident Evil, which is what makes it a Resident Evil game.

Experienced players - if you're an old-time gamer then you will see familiar elements in this game, the puzzles, the enemies, the story line, these will all be familiar to you, there's really not much to say about it, they're not incredibly variable and unique, if you have a thing for zombies and such, it'll probably enchance your enjoyment greatly, but objectively, it's not excitingly revolutionary at it's core. The puzzles are casual and the typical kind of what you would expect if you've played these types of games before, you'll get the rythym of what they want you to do or where to go for clues, you'll be racing around fairly casual after some time, it's not too frustrating just to be difficult and that's a nice part of the game. I didn't go hard mode because I didn't feel like shooting zombies X times to kill instead of X, which I assumed would be the difference, which wasn't the kind of challenge I was looking for at least, but I had a good time. If you're a veteran that needs a difficult shooter challenge then you should try hard, normal shouldn't give you too many problems except for here or there and with ammo mostly, I was surprised they didn't give you more ammo for normal mode, which begs the question, should you kill every creature? it definitely adds to the challenge running and survivng instead of killing, and maybe that's the intention because my shooting accuracy is very high, I don't miss much at all and never waste ammo needlessly and I still ran out of ammo at certain moments, I typically finish games with lots of ammo left over, even when it's scarce so this did catch me offgaurd and much more suspenseful. Normal was challenging enough for me to be enjoyable. I finished the story modes at a relaxing pace (first one - 8 hours, second one 6 hours) and you can play another round I guess on a more difficult mode, so you'll have determine if 60 bucks is worth that amount of time.

New players - there's probably a lot of things for you to experience here. The creepy factor is good, the puzzles and the way resident evil series integrates it's puzzles with the environment is something you'll always remember, the atmosphere and the way it implements art and decoration is something that always sticks out in the series. The challenge should be strong for you, maybe even too strong at times, if not overwhelming at times, you will get spanked if you try to run and gun through it, the difficulty level can also spike wildly with the bosses, don't be afraid to try the easier settings, it's supposed to be fun, not stressful. You will get the hang of it eventually and it will likely add the suspense, as you won't know how to always react to situations.

Overall, I'd give it a rating of 7.5 to 7.8. I had fun and was entertained but found it a bit cheesy at times, poor acting or depth from the characters, but the game is solid in terms of functionality, you can feel the improvements in gameplay and I had no issues or bugs, it just depends on what you are expecting from the game, your gaming experience and how much you like zombies, really.

Having never played the original Resident Evil 2, I went into this game without any sort of nostalgia factor influencing my opinion. That said, it's been a great experience thus far, and has made it worth pushing through any brief moments of frustration. 

Managing your ammo feels even more important in this game than in the remake of the original Resident Evil, where I tended to just blast most anything that got in my way. This game forces you to think strategically about your engagements: do I need to clear out this hallway? Will I be coming back here? Do I even have enough ammo to do it? Certain enemy encounters also force you to flee rather than fight, lest you waste your precious few bullets. Some of these enemies could get frustrating at times, especially when they keep you from engaging with puzzles necessary to advance the plot, but can usually be overcome with a little tactical thinking (at least on Standard, I'm sure Hardcore is a nightmare). 

If you're looking to simply blast enemies with reckless abandon, this may not be the title for you. However, if you're looking for a game that will make you feel anxious with every bullet expended, or keep you watching every dark corner out of fear of what might come lunging out of it, you may have just found your next great game.

If nothing else it makes zombie games scary again; it does however do a whole lot more than that. It is a shining example of why some older games should be remade, because as many know, some things do not stand the test of time. If one was to go and try playing the original Resident Evil 2 now, especially for the first time it would not be a welcoming experience at all. This remake has the same plotline with some changes to the "A" and "B" Scenarios, but with the graphics completely overhauled. It features a superb modern control scheme on PC, voice and sound design that both captivates and horrifies, and some astounding level design, all without shedding the core feeling and approach in the gameplay systems that made the original such a hit. Anybody who likes survival horror and or third person shooters will not be disappointed with 'Resident Evil 2 2019'. 

Gameplay
Firstly the shooting mechanics in this title are pretty solid, with a smoothness and responsiveness expected of a modern "triple A" third person shooter. Holding Right click enables aiming which brings a reticule on the screen that will either be a standard crosshair for pistols or open and close brackets for heavier weapons like shotguns. What’s interesting is the time that it will take for the reticule to contract and focus the center dot on what the respective character is aiming at. The default pistol for Leon, 'Matilda' takes a longer time to focus than the special 'Samurai Edge' pistol, which can make a great deal of difference in situations where the player is taking on two or more shambling undead in a closed corridor space. The movement controls are pretty standard "wasd" etc. and feel right. The menu controls is often the area where many of Japanese developed PC ports get weird, but not this one. There is different ways to exit a submenu to a previous menu or switch between menu panels that don't seem totally out of place. The player can choose to use the escape key or the right mouse button the second of which makes a lot of sense ergonomically as it can save a good amount of time. Now the fluidity of game menu controls may seem inconsequential to most, but they are quite important as the player will be using the menus a lot to check the map, manage inventory, look at picked up clues to solve puzzles, and check out the cool concept arts and models that are unlocked in the main menu for performing certain feats. Safe rooms are scattered throughout with typewriters that serve as save stations and a unified item box with which to hold goods that aren't currently being used. The item box will be used quite often as the player is only allotted a limited amount of inventory slots, until they find upgrades later on. Those who have played the Deus Ex games will recognize this inventory system immediately, its a good system that makes the playing think about what they should bring or leave and adds another layer or immersion to the gameplay. Throughout the initial play through the gameplay seemed flawless.

10/10

Story
To boil it down, the plot follows along with the story of either Rookie police officer Leon Kennedy, or College Student Claire Redfield whose fates become intertwined after they meet at a roadside gas station on the night that the zombpocalypse happens. They are headed to Raccoon city for different reasons, and decide to head to police headquarters; it is there where the story really kicks off, with new characters and threats introduced along the way and with some harrowing revelations throughout. They must eventually find a way to escape the station with their lives. It is a plot line that has been done before, but the creepy atmosphere, horrifying monsters, and timely pacing make the story feel exciting.

8/10

Level Design
The way the map is set up is quite astonishing; it is quite interconnected with some paths blocked until finding ways around these various barriers that open up shortcuts that can be used later on and will come in useful when trying to avoid some particularly dangerous enemies. For people who didn't grow up playing the original 'Resident Evil' games, the level design could be easily compared to the first 'Dark Souls', which is a good thing. The interconnectedness of the world brings another level of player satisfaction when opening shortcuts or new areas. It is not only this interconnected feeling that makes the level design seem flawless, but also the way that the developers use of space to induce tension on the player. The small corridors and constricted boss arenas just give the game a little more edge when it comes to the excitement usually experienced in survival horror. Another important aspect of the level design is the puzzles, locks, and clues to solve or unlock such things that are scattered throughout which offer the player key items needed to progress the main story or special items/ weapons that feel quite satisfying to obtain. It can't be said enough how well the level design is done in this game.

10/10

Graphics and optimization/Sound
The sound of enemy footsteps and disgusting vocal noises are absolutely terrifying, especially using headphones with the binaural option selected from the settings menu. The graphics and lighting are quite stunning, with many bells and whistles that can be applied or forgone for better performance. There is some slightly odd shading artifacts that appear on walls in well-lit environments feel not right, but other than that the graphics are grade 'A'. The player can scale the resolution up or down, set the amount of VRAM that the textures will use, SSAO, anti-aliasing, anisotropic filtering, mesh quality etc. With all the graphical options the game can be made to run pretty smoothly across a wide variety of systems both AMD and Intel or NVidia based. For review two machines were used, one of which consisted of a stock i7 6700k, 16 GB 2133MHz speed RAM, a GTX 1080, and running off a SATA SSD. The Second was running an AMD R7 1700 at 3.55Ghz, 16 GB 3200MHz RAM, and an RX 580, running off and NVMe SSD. The loading times on both systems were very similar with only a couple seconds difference seen between the two. The graphics could be pretty well maxed on the i7 system running in both DX11 DX12 with DX12 reducing the performance with no visual gain or benefit. At 130% scaling it consistently hit 60fps at 1080p, or with Vsync off anywhere from the high 60s to around 125fps with aforementioned settings. The R7 system was running consistent 60fps with AMD's Enhanced Sync at mostly high settings and ran between the mid 70's to 133fps with no Vsync enabled and at 110% scaling. MSAA 8X was forced from the Radeon Settings options on the desktop. For some this will look really nice although the built in anti-aliasing options can offer good picture as well with TAA+FXAA. The AMD System was also running DX11 and was very briefly switched to DX12 API which didn't benefit the experience in any way. Overall the performance was stellar across both systems running on the DX11 API. The only thing that would have been nice to try is AMD crossfire to see how performance would have been with dual RX 580s comparatively with the i7 GTX 1080 System. Across both systems the experience was both beautiful and smooth in DX11.

9.5/10

After the excellent RE7 released 2 years, I was so glad to play Resident Evil again.  Capcom has once again delivered with Resident Evil 2 Remake and it's the best Resident Evil to date, as well as already one of the best games in 2019.  I never played through the original (only played 4 and onward), but I knew enough about it and the series to know what to expect.

You play as Leon and Claire in their own campaigns, and while they are nearly the same, they both have their own stories, interactions, and even specific items/weapons at their disposal.  On the 2nd playthrough, the game switches up the items and puzzles in order to keep the game fresh.  The game encourages you to explore to find any and every item, and doing so is very rewarding and will definitely help you down the line.  The combat feels smooth and both campaigns offer diverse weapons that get the job done.  Item management is absolutely key, and you will want to do more running than shooting to preserve ammunication and sub-weapons for later; you're going to need them.  While I did love both campaigns, I liked Leon's a little better, but I preferred Claire's weapons.

This game is also terrifying and keeps you on the edge of your seat; especially if you play in the dark and with headphones!  Not only are there good jump scares, but the atmosphere really provides a sense of dread, despite having the ability to fight back.  There are various zombie types who are tough to take down and keep down, and you have Mr. X stalking you along the way to add to the challenge and dread.

If I have to provide any negatives, I wish there was a dodge button, or more options to avoid attacks.  Because of the precise movement there really isn't a way to avoid zombies running towards you except for running at just the right angle, and if you don't have any sub-weapons to counter with you are forced to take damage.  This can be especially frustrating dring boss fights as they deal some of the most damage out of all enemies.  Also, as cool and scary as Mr. X is, I felt he was a little too good at stalking you.  It did get annoying at times when, for example, I was trying to complete an objective or save my game, and then he just so happened to be nearby, forcing me to run and hide before I could proceed again.  It did create some pacing issues, but not enough to detract from my experience as a whole.

Resident Evil 2 is a superb game that fans of any horror games need to own.  It offers fans nostalgia and easter eggs while still making it feel new, and offers newcomers a good starting point for the series.  Finally, being a remake, it also sets the standard for how future remakes ought to be done.  Capcom is on a roll with Resident Evil, and I only hope it continues to go up from here.

Capcom has really found a way to revitalize not only the gaming experience of a classic game, but to do so with a robust flair that blends nostalgia with a perfection of current gen engines.  To top-off the icing on their Umbrella decorated cake; the video game company spread the game with a tender love and care that we only could generally wish half of the companies showed to their products; and more importantly, to their fans.


Right off the bat the fan service cooked into this game is some of the best I have ever seen in a game, if not THE best.  Walking into the police station for the first time, the nostalgia glasses seemed to be working just fine, this was an event trying to take in every little bit of the scenery.  It wasn’t quite so cut and dry as it sounded though, as you try to soak in each area for the beautiful rendering and design over the original, there is a large tension to keep things moving along as quickly as possible.  The old safety blanket of knowing that enemies were bound to specific areas of the game are no longer there.  Enemies have and most certainly utilize the ability to travel room to room in search of their next victim here, which ramps up the tension to a high level.

Obviously playing the game on PC has been a truly remarkable event, having so much liberty to tweak with and adjust the graphical settings to find that delectable sweet spot of performance to visuals felt like a mini game ushering in its own unlockable rewards to the game.  

This game could not have been done any better justice outside of the ‘over-the-shoulder’ style, there I said it.  Taking in the fast pace action and scenery blended well with this format proving that the direction the games prior detoured to (we all know the ones *also side note: I am a fan almost all the games*) didn’t have to go solely for a more is better encounter.  The RE Engine the game runs on allows for a buttery smooth experience a vast majority of the time, showcasing all the incredible details in environment with extensive clarity and relatively inexpensive (less taxing) demands on the hardware required to run the game.  All this is soaked in the fact that there is always a level of tension as trying to figure out the best ways to survive in the new game crafted upon an old foundation of a time since past franchise.

When I say I tip my Mr. X fedora to Capcom for all the care they put into this game, I mean it with the utmost sincerity.  Right off the bat, the way current game companies operate nowadays tends to be about how to milk in game content (current and future) for cash; want that alternative costume? Gotta pay for that!   Ohhhh you want a mode of play that was there before?  Guess what Jimmy!  
Well Capcom this time around pushed all of those models to the curb and just gave gamers the full experience with baked in goodies that we all remember from the past, and sprinkled on newer generation troupes such as achievements, collectables *breakables?*, and leaderboards for those die hards that like to go head to head; all of this… WAS FREE!!! Let me say that again… FREE!!!  Well played Capcom m’lady!

Resident Evil 2 is arguably my favourite in the series now, replacing Resident Evil 4 by just a smidgen, Capcom has yet again struck gold with this Entry of the series.

Let's talk about a few Pros and cons, this review will be edited/added onto as I get time to restructure, for now, it'll be a few pros and cons

[h1]Pros:[/h1]
-Atmosphere is amazing, near perfect, always kept on my toes throughout the entire game
-Gunplay has struck a balance between new and old, allowing you to shoot on the move, but punishing it via lessened accuracy.
-The story feels believable in that, the amount of shots it takes to really kill a zombie would explain how the RPD got overrun even with armed Police Officers.
-The new VA and Facial capture, while it has a few hitches is really good, and obviously a massive upgrade to the original
-The overall Station layout has some tweaks and changes, but remains for the most part the same station we know and love. playing homage to the original RPD.
-Leon's Alternative Costume is a nice homage to the original as well, keeping his bulky shoulderpads.
-Zombies fall apart in glorious ways when blasted with shotguns and magnums
-Hardcore is extremely difficult
-Free DLC on the way, including 3 new small "What if" stories as well as 1998 Costumes for Leon and Claire in all their low Poly glory
-Ammo and health management important like the original
-No more Fixed Camera angles (Can be a con for some purists, so leave this where you will in your personal opinion)
-Mr. X is an amazing mechanic
-He also has a hat.
[h1]Cons:[/h1]
-Claire's Alternative costume is lacking her old black sleeves, it feels off because of this.
-Adaptive Difficulty feels like a very bad choice for a game which offers rewards for speedrunning, as inconsistency is a big detriment to the concept of speedrunning, it is hard to plan for moments when sometimes it takes 1 shot to stagger a zombie, and others it takes 5 or 6.
-This also makes Hardcore mode feel fair in difficulty sometimes, and others, it feels off because of just how many more shots you're wasting on a single zombie each run.
-Mr. X doesn't pick the hat up if you shoot it off :(
-B Scenarios are not that different from the A scenarios, including some story segments such as say... a character dying, happening in 2 different places, meaning they don't actually fit into the canon.
-After completing the game, I do wish Mercenaries existed in this game, perhaps in a DLC or RE3make


Overall? Resident Evil 2 is an amazing Reimagining of the original 1998 Classic, and I heavily recommend it to anyone who is looking for a good Horror Experience, as well as Oldschool Resident Evil fans

20 years ago, I went to my grandma's house on Mother's Day and my uncle called me over to his room and introduced me to the PlayStation. The first game I saw was of course Resident Evil 2. Never played the first and I heard it was good, but i heard the 2nd was scary. I showed him the game and he put it in and I was so excited. Until I pushed the start button and that voice came. My excitement turned to nervousness and soon turned to fear as I played it. My stomach churned as I sank back in the couch hearing that first scene music and the zombies moaning right when you start. Of course, I didn’t know how to work the controls and I watched Leon get eaten by the zombies. I was so traumatized by the game, that I never touched RE until the 2nd and 3rd came for GameCube followed by the 1st remake. Now we get the redone, reimagined Resident Evil 2 and there are some hits and misses in the game but overall, I liked it.

Now I'm now one to talk about graphics in video games, but this one I must. Everything was so brilliant, the details of the characters, the animations of both them and the zombies, the details of where you shoot the zombies, watching their arms and legs fall off, their heads popping when you get that critical shot in. The lighting was so awesome like the press conference room where you turn on the light and when you close the door, you see the light coming from the bullet holes on the door. William Birkin's 1st form was so detailed and seeing the veins and stuff popping from him and the eye blinking was superb and was one of my most favorite fights. The blood details coming off Leon/Clair when you take damage from zombies/dogs/lickers and seeing the bite/claw marks and seeing Claire and Leon wincing in pain the looks on their faces when you're on caution or danger. I could go on talking about the graphics all day if I must, but overall the graphics of course blows the classic version out of the water.

Everybody knows the story of RE2 so don’t need to get to that but the story telling and dramatization for this game was awesome. I loved how they gave some of the minor characters more screen time like Marvin Branagh, Chief Irons, but not enough screen time for Ben Bertolucci. I didn’t like how Ben just died so fast and how they didn’t throw the options of him being killed by Mr. X or William like in the classic. As a matter of fact, in the classic, he wanted to stay in his cell because of the dangers in the police station as in this one he wants out. I loved how they did Marvin as you watched him slowly turn into a zombie, but it lacked a cutscene which is a huge sin in Resident Evil since he was an important character. I love how they added a new perspective of Chief Irons as this crazed character, but I think the classic did Irons better as he started off completely normal and had the body of the Mayor's daughter and he cried on how he failed to protect her. But later on, in the classic, you take his journal and learn that not only did he work for umbrella, but he was sabotaging the police department by taking ammo and slowly hunting other police officers and eventually hunted and killed the mayor's daughter, which bought that suspense in the classic version. I loved how they did Ada as this cold, heartless mercenary who was using Leon but soon started to have feelings for him. Sherry wasn't as annoying as the classic, so I'll give them that. And finally, William Birkin's 3rd form. The best boss fight in the entire game. And that nostalgic opera shout in the beginning along with the roar of the 3rd form was perfect. It got my adrenaline pumping as I gathered all the ammo...but then realized I had the magnum on Leon/upgraded HP bullets on Claire and shot him down. And finally, Mr. X. Hands down, he is better than the classic version, I can’t lie on that part. Him being this bullet proof, unstoppable terminator along with that theme music had me on edge. And he didn’t stop chasing me. Best part was when I you lose him, and you can hear the heavy footsteps. Best part of it was that whenever you used a weapon, he would hear it and come to the room where he last heard it. But, like the licker, he lacked a intro cutscene. In the classic, you can see that he was airdropped by umbrella. Here, he just appears without a back story behind him or little to no lore on him. Other than the minuses, I still loved it.

The misses of this game. First, the title screen. There was no voice saying the name of the game in that eerie horrifying voice and I don’t understand how Capcom could miss that iconic moment. Another is the intro. Don’t get me wrong I loved the new intro and how it started, but they didn’t give a back story as to what happened for newcomers that want to play Resident Evil. Another is the lack of background lore. In the classic there were notes containing of what happened after the mansion incident and during the first few days of the T-Virus spreading. I recall one journal from a cop explaining how he was playing chess with another man and how the man was slowly starting to become infected and slowly explained date by date on how the man's health was deteriorating and eventually leading the cop not feeling too well, either. There was lack of lore of the Licker and why it was named for it. I know why I know its name, but for those who are new to RE, they would want to know. The S.T.A.R.S room was empty. In the classic version, it explained whose desk it was and the pictures along with the trophies explaining that Chris Redfield won them for best marksman ship. Not only that, it explained the behavior of those who sat in those desks. Like Wesker’s desk was explained as neat and organized while Barry's had replica guns and books stating that he could be from the N.R.A. Rebecca's was all clean indicating that she was new to the team. None of that was there. And there was no fax coming from the US feds indicating and explaining that Chris was still investigating and how Chief Irons needed to be watched very carefully and how he was paid by umbrella to cover up the mansion case. Here it’s some coded letter stating that he was in Europe and how William Birkin was paying him instead of Umbrella. I liked the new approach but there should've been more detail on how messed up Chief Irons is. He doesn’t even explain on hunting and killing the Mayor's daughter. It just says pig and how he loved the white skin on it. I mean for us who played the classic we knew what he was talking about, but the newcomers probably didn’t until they got to sherry's story.

Finally, the biggest miss in the entire game: The B scenarios. I was so excited to play the B scenario when I beat the A and was thinking it would be different. It wasn't at all. Once you got past that first door, everything just repeated except that the key items were placed in different areas and the puzzles changed. And Mr. X came earlier that was it. Also, there was no interactions between Claire meeting with Ada or Leon meeting with Sherry. Along with Claire or Leon meeting face to face or interacting with each other until like the end of the game. I mean realistically, you would be worried about the other survivor that you met and hope he/she would be alright. Does Leon/Claire do that? No, they just go their own way until they see each other in the lab and are like, "Wait you are down here, too?!" Also, where are the crows and the spiders? Sure, the G-adults were a welcoming addition, but it’s not RE without giant insects and crows. 

Overall the game is great as I said with the graphics and dramatization of the story, it succeeds in some places over the classic, but also lacks in some areas the classic had. Hopefully that can be improved when Capcom works on Resident Evil 3.

188man Reviews Resident Evil 2 (2019)

-Spoiler free review--

I will preface my review by saying that I have completed the first scenario with leon on hardcore difficulty and I'm playing Claire's B campaign now on standard.

--UPDATE: 2/1/2019 - I've completed both scenarios, I've also updated the review in general.

--Positive--

First of all, I was a huge fan of the original game as well as the other golden age era Resident Evil titles such as Resident evil 1 and 3. I played the franchise from it's conception and for the longest time I was more or less devoid of any hope for this series returning to greatness. I can safely say that my prayers have been answered, this game is excellent and is mostly faithful to the original.

Make no mistake this is Resident evil 2 despite having a RE4 style camera view and aiming mechanic, which I might add at first was a disappointment for I being probably the biggest advocate of the fixed camera angles and controls. The essence is intact with even the same signature rhythm of gameplay that the older entries are renowned for. The scares are still there, albeit in very different places compared to the original, which makes going through this title even more jarring, even if you're a veteran of survival horror games. 
Survival tactics and strategy has returned yet again and is in full force, you have to plan ahead for most engagements if you want to survive. Provisions are low in this game so you'll have to conserve and only attack when you must otherwise you'll be faced with a very hard game indeed.

The puzzles have come back in style and are a nice addition to the game, although if you're not aware of how many challenges their are, you might get frustrated. Personally I love puzzles It's not a problem for me, it's what I come to expect playing many survival horror games. I like what they did with the creatures in this game, they're very aggressive and tough, even your lowly zombie is a much greater threat in this game compared to the original iteration, so be advised. 

The Tyrant aka Mr. X who was the hulking trench coat wearing terminator type character who stalked you through Resident Evil 2 B scenario, makes a come back and is also enhanced. This monster follows you almost everywhere this time and is a far deadlier opponent compared to the original beast, which really does remind me of Nemesis from Resident Evil 3.  The environments are richly detailed and are full of dread with a bespoke frightening quality, luckily there is a good variety of places to venture, seeing that backtracking and exploration is a major part of this game.

Their are no loading screens in this game besides the one that starts the new game, which is amazing seeing how big this game is. This helps the experience immensely, I'm very impressed. The graphics are very nice although not the best I've seen but very good nonetheless, it's not an issue with me, however you might want to upgrade your PC if I were you.

The controls handle very nicely considering I'm using a mouse and keyboard. By default you have the WASD keys for movement with space and auxiliary buttons like E and F for other tasks. The mouse is used for most interactions as well as shooting, it's very easy to grasp and master, soon enough you'll be zipping around the police station and shooting like a gunslinger. If you use the controller it's probably easier, both options are equally good. 

To end the positive aspects I'll touch on the fact this game is best played on 'hardcore' difficulty being the hardest settings and considering the nature of the game, it's my preferred setting.

--Negative--

Their are small grievances, first of all you'll understand quickly when you play it, it's not a case of difference that might concern you, it's primarily what the developers replaced or taken out completely. Some creatures have been affected by this issue, please be aware of that. Environments that were present in the original game are no longer there, also the 'zap system' has been removed.  

Some cut scenes from the first iteration are not here and the direction of the scenes in general lack that iconic flair that the original game had. Voice acting however crude and campy it was in the original entry, is redone here but again lacks that memorable cheese that the original game featured so very well, although that might be down to personal preference.  

--Overall--

What we have here is probably the best Resident Evil title in many years and I hope future titles will be as good if not better, we can all hope. Bring on Resident evil 3 capcom!

For obvious reasons they didn’t remaster the original RE2. If you’re familiar with the original then you’re probably aware that today’s audience wouldn’t appreciate the gameplay mechanics and control schemes of 1998. I mean, imagine playing a AAA title today with the forced camera angles of 1998… it just wouldn’t work. 

That being said, this is as good as a remake can get. Resident Evil 2 stays true to its original atmosphere, fear tactics, survival, puzzle’s, and themes while taking advantage of today’s hardware and adapting well to modern control layouts and gameplay mechanics. Today’s graphics bring the horror to life in a way that wasn’t fathomable in 1998.

The opening scene and prologue were a nostalgic reminder of things to come. For reasons unknown they changed the when/where/how the gun shop scene plays out, but overall the opening is impressively adapted for today. Also, the police station might be more eerie than the original. 

Any newcomer is going to think this game is amazing. But, this is going to be a particularly good game for those who played in 1998. I’m excited for all of you who are about to experience this masterpiece.

SIDE NOTE: I encourage you to buy the Original Soundtrack Swap. It’s included in the deluxe edition. Or, you can buy it for $2.99. Alright let me make this as short as i can, do you like games? i mean, do you? yes? no? well if the answer is yes, this is a Game, yes an actual video game, no "life service" no "platform" no "always online multiplayer because we can't make money with single player games anymore" ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥, it's the real deal, a GAME. 

First and foremost let me say this: It's an absolute masterclass in Survival Horror, well considering the early RE titles are themselfes the ones that started this genre proper, it shouldn't be a surprise. Now since this is a complete remake, the story was slightly altered and modernized in a good way, the progression is slightly different than the original but most notably we get the RE4-6 Third person action camera that really stands out this time around, because RE2 is the PERFECT fit for this, over the shoulder camera angle which manages to really give the game a claustrophobic feeling and adds a lot of "gravity" to the overall gameplay. Guns feel heavy, gunshots feel impactful and overall the gameplay itself is just excellent if you like, well action games.

Now let's get to the one thing that will probably turn off people who never played any game before 2010: The controls CAN be clunky, but it is part of the design, boss fights in particular can make you curse a lot because both leon and claire somewhat behave like trucks on a muddy road during those, but this is a deliberate part of the design, so you commit to your action and strategie going forward, bolstered by it's particular focus on resource management and the overall theme of planning ahead for a few minutes. Now a lot of people that are not used to these kinds of concepts will curse the game, while i sat there and admired how well all of the gameplay functions synergize and how well executed the entire thing is. 

Another "con" could be said about the game's lenght, my first playthrough took me about 6 hours (while clearing out the entire game - all items, every room accessible with that character etc) and the second scenario took me a tad longer cause i chose to play leon first and claire second (claire, being the harder of the two due to slightly less powerful weapons and i believe she also takes a bit more damage overall). So overall i'd say the average player will probably spend 7-9 hours per Playthrough which amounts to about 17-20 hours for the "full story". But there is a TON more to do afterwards, re-explore the different scenarios, try to optimize your time for higher rankings and unlock new guns and outfits etc. 

And yes you actually have to PLAY to unlock guns/skins/outfits for your characters, you can't spend 20 bucks on it.. you actually have to play.. unbelievable, the nerves on this dev, eh? And the most unbelievable part of this all? FREE DLC coming feb. 15 with 3 new scenarios, that's what i call madness! MADNESS!

Well, turns out this was rather long, so sorry for this, yet i haven't even touched on some of the most important aspects of the game, so to wrap it up here are a few more bullet points that might be of interest:

- Great optimization (running over 250+ fps maxed out (1440p) on a Vega 64 - a SINGLE Vega 64, yes my rig has 2, but that'd be a waste of electricity at that performance) 4K runs at around 120-140 with, like i said everything maxed out except deactivated Motion Blur and Depth of field for personal preference. 
- Sometimes cheesy, sometimes good story backed by STRONG performances from the voice actors (well done!)
- Still, since the original some of the best level design in gaming history, backtracking that doesn't feel like work but an actual revisit with a few twists here and there.
- Despite what i said about the overall controls earlier the Keybinds for PC are PERFECT you can certainly see this isn't a simple console port but done by people who know and understand PC players.
- NO SPIDERS! (yay!) Thanks Capcom, from the bottom of my heart, thank you for this cause i would have otherwise missed out on this amazing experience! Keep them out of the RE3 Remake too please! ;)

Resident Evil 2 is arguably the most beloved game in the franchise & in the opinion of some — one of, if not the best sequel to a game ever created.  To say that Capcom was under immense pressure when they undertook this project would be an understatement.  Thankfully, this game exceeded all of my expectations.

While there are jump-scares, the game relies more on a genuine sense of dread & fear that is usually lost with the shift to an over the shoulder camera angle.  This game won't hold your hand & reminds us all what made the series great to begin with.  There is not enough ammo in the game to kill every enemy so don't even try.  You will have to play smart & tactfully if you wish to survive.

Sound is a big factor in this game & while it is visually stunning without being a drain on your system — it is the sounds that you hear that will create an atmosphere of absolute fear & tension.  Each creature makes it's own unique noise & you will soon come to know them.  To be completley honest the thing that sold me on this game was finding out that with the deluxe edition of the game, you can swap out the new soundtrack for the original one from 1998.

If I had to find fault with Capcom, it is their refusal to hire back Alyson Court to voice Claire Redfield — a character she has voiced since the original Resident Evil 2 — the only exception being Resident Evil: Revelations 2.  Still, Claire's voice actress does a fine job — as does the rest of the cast.  It's a small detail but one that carries with it a lot of weight amongst the fans.

That being said — this title is a must buy for any Resident Evil fan.  I have enjoyed my time with it so far & I plan to spend many more hours in Raccoon City.

第二，1998年的科技跟游戏不相符。这个游戏应该是90年代末带上近未来的科幻，所以原版已经做到极致了，例如当时应该都用钥匙卡，哪有什么手环？还有警察局在1998年就开始用定制化外观的U盘了？？？所以这已经是一个动作乱飞的星战射击游戏。
第三，这个剧情改成这样的垃圾了。主角的里关和表关一样，基本上没区别，所以你不需要打4遍。原版的剧情已经非常好了，4个剧情相互照应。所以还不如不改，直接套用原剧情还好多了！
第四，角色更加垃圾了。例如记者Ben，威廉博士等等都改了，个性和造型都改了。原版的威廉博士很酷，声音和造型都很冷酷，阿尔法小队来抢G病毒的时候那段很冷峻，结果新版里头跟奶油小生一样，各种乖萌。还有，我记得原故事里头Ben的戏份比这个多多了，而且死法都有两种，本来是Leon叫他出来他不肯，这里是他自己想出来Leon不让，然后就瞬间被暴君KO。我真是服了。

I'm going to make this short to begin with. This is a good game, with good gameplay. It's fun, and it's pretty good at keeping things fresh and switching stuff up as you progress. Buy it, odds are you'll enjoy it. Parts of the story feels like they cut content though, and the development team more or less successfully stitched the completed pieces roughly together. 

What it is not good at, is being a remake/reimagining of Resident Evil 2. If you're a hardcore fan thinking, "I really liked RE2, I'd like to see what it'd look like if they spent the time to flesh out parts of the game that seemed small or lacking" you're going to have a bad time. The differences between the "A" and "B" scenarios are extremely lacking, Leon and Claire interact with each other less, and at least one boss fight has a big gimmicky set piece that can't be avoided to end the fight. 

This segment is kind of nitpicky stuff. Feel free to skip it if you like:
The "B" scenario has no "streets" segment at its begining, which feels really weird. The "Zapper" system, as limited as it was, has been completely stripped out rather than expanded. Chief Irons still has a secret door in his office, but it goes to an elevator with a guard room attached to it. Annette's characterization starts off similar to what we're familiar with, but then pulls a 180 for no obvious reason partway through the game. The new Mr. X is kind of a toss-up. While it is kind of interesting to have him always stalking you throughout the station, he also doesn't drop anything when you defeat him. He has very few scripted events, so he doesn't have as many exciting or dramatic entrances. He'll likely get the drop on you once or twice, even if you're tracking his movements with headphones. Finally, you'll never get mobbed by zombies, like the old East Hall. The developers seem to think that more than 4 zombies at a time is an insurmountable challenge. They might be right, with the way this verion plays.

Bottom line for returning fans of the original: 
It feels like someone described the OG RE2 to the team making this one, and the new team got rushed partway through and had to jam what they had together to make the ship date. It's a shame that the game looks so good, but seems to be lacking critical details. Perhaps RE2 is just lightly cursed, doomed to always result in a game that shines through lackluster portions that become more obvious with careful observation.

Amazing game! Resident Evil 2 was one of my favorite games when I was a kid, and this is a wonderful remake..its not shot for shot the same game, but I think the differences actually make the game better. Capcom has earned a lot of good will with this one, and I can't wait for the RE3 remake now.

[h1] Introduction [/h1]

Resident Evil 2 is a remake of the original version and as a remake, there are a couple of differences between this newer version and the old one. One such difference is that this version opts to use the third person camera angle since it's alternative take that's fresh and fun. Others could be that there is no need to use ink ribbons on difficulties below hardcore and that they have created an atmosphere that is felt with tension. New enemies can appear in previously explored rooms while others will continually chase the players during most of the game. I think that Resident Evil 2 is trying to mix together aspects of the original with elements of RE 3 and RE 7. This is brilliant.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

The gameplay is very solid and creative with the player having several options to manipulate rooms or enemies. The player can use a knife to cut zombies legs to incapacitate them in order to save ammunition or use the environment to escape chases more easily like with stairs in which zombies are slower or wooden barricades to slow down the horde. Weapons have a kick to them which makes them more enjoyable to use yet enemies are quite resilient to them, the player knows that their weapons can kill enemies with ease for the most part but they will eat all the ammunition fast. Classic Resident Evil games tend to have one particular element that decides if a run ends in success or failure and that is item management. However, do note that this version is more forgiving than it's previous ones.

[h1] Some Notes [/h1]

The story remains the same for the most part, with small changes present that don't alter the take of the original. The developers did a pretty good job when it comes optimization as graphics cards such as GTX 1060 or 1070 will manage to run at 60+ FPS with everything on high/ultra. The game takes on a more darker-wet approach as areas feel desolated, murky, and with hidden dangers lurking around. While it borrows elements for newer entries, it still remains true to the original in most aspects.

[h1] What Makes It Special [/h1]

The RE 7 style graphics are beautiful and breathtaking at times and the chases that happen through the main story keep the players focused, scared, wary and on their toes for the most part. Enemies had become even more dangerous than ever and even the simplest ones such as normal zombies or dogs are able to take you down with ease if you give them the chance. This game is a perfect quality title which everyone can play and enjoy, old fans will be in awe at the chance of reliving one of the best games ever made and new ones will have the chance to enjoy a classic revamped to their liking.

[h1] Sum up[/h1]

+ Revamped for new players, remade for old ones. 
+ Adopts elements from newer entries with ease, making them it's own.
+ Has a good amount of base content and will get even more with free DLC.
+ 4th Survivor mode for all of those that love speedrunning and chewing more than they can bite.
+ 2nd run keeps the game fresh even after beating it. Remixing enemies, item placement and more.
+ Dynamic difficulty, it becomes ruthless if you are doing well and forgiving if you are having a hard time.
+ Superb graphics make the game look astounding, details give life to its creatures and surroundings.
+ Extremely dangerous enemies will chase the player through rooms, creating an atmosphere of tension and keeping players on their toes at all times.

- Some puzzles can be bananas to solve without a guide.
- William Birkin encounters are a disappointment in contrast to Mr. X.
- Lacks bosses, while there are some they sometimes get repeated and it feels like it should have more variety.
- Last bosses are rushed, they lack momentum and could have used a little more time to develop more tension.

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

Resident Evil 2 is a spectacular game and one in which it is hard for me to find any major weak points or cons.  All I can think of it are good things due to its perfect balance and mastery over keeping alive it's true essence while adapting to modern times. I consider it to be a masterpiece in its own merit and must get game for every gamer who wants to enjoy a spectacular game.

Awesome game and a benchmark on how a remake should be done. It's RE2 at its core without any of that remake ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ other companies tried to pull of. Compared to the original it  seems to provides no significant changes in gameplay or story and there are only a few changes in the level design but on closer inspection the game has changed quite a bit (https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=HBibAdNZ53U). Still, the slight changes that have been made are interesting and provide a good mix up as well as a whole new challenge level. People who know the original RE2 by heart will immediately feel at home in Racoon City but will see many changes to reduce the time spent on backtracking and a very different way of how you deal with the zombies.
The best part of this game, however, is its presentation: The sound design is amazing. From little things like the sound of your boots on the ground to the more important ones like the music ore the well-known Zombies that scream and moan... Still, even the sound is outclassed by the graphics. I can't stress enough how impressed I am with the damn graphics! The game always looks amazing and at certain parts it even manages to look real. Now that's not something I say often and I even think that videogames should concentrate on their own visual style rather than trying to recreate reality but RE2 does concentrate on its own style and achieves the photorealism along the way by having an incredible attention to detail. Faces and clothing look impressive, rain looks awesome, animations are fluid and believable... Everything is spot-on. Capcom even took the time to add facial expression to the characters so that they squinch their faces when injured. Considering the game is played in an over-the-shoulder perspective, so you might not never realize your character is doing this, it only shows how much Capcom cared about the details here.
There is only one thing that might put you off: The game can be a bit short. Since there are two playable main characters, it provides you with two campaigns that offer just enough differences between them to count as seperate and only playing both of them will let you see the whole story. After finishing the game once you can then start a "2nd Run", which basically is kinda New Game Plus, and only this mode let's you see the true ending. Again, finish 2nd Run once and you can start to play additional modes that don't offer much new except very tough challenges. Now, if you're a completionist, you will probably play the normal game twice and then the 2nd Run twice, too, because 2nd Run makes the enemies tougher, changes the location of items and weapons and starts you off a fair bit into the game by skipping the Prologue and the arrival in Raccon City. If you're in it for the story, however, you might not be interested in playing the game four times and after you've played it once with a character, you can then start the 2nd Run with the other. This way will let you see the whole story and the good ending in about 15 to 17 hours.
So, if you're gonna play it several times, the game is definitely worth every penny. If not, however, full price might not be a good idea since you will pay almost sixty bucks for 15 hours of gameplay. I still wholeheartedly recommend RE2 to everyone but those who are in it to see the story and don't plan on playing it several times (or simply don't have the time to do that) might want to think about waiting for a sale.

Exactly what I asked for, but turns out it wasn't what I actually wanted, and a perfect example of Steam needing a 'It depends' option for recommendations.  

Technically, this game is a really great piece of work, especially the graphics settings. My only technical issue has been some sound cutout issues when moving between rooms.   Storywise, they tightened up the story and it flows better.  The new voices aren't as good, but are perfectly fine taken on their own.  Gameplay wise, the game controls as well as it should, and the third person camera angle is a trade off from the original, but the gameplay improvement combined with the fact it makes you worried about what might be sneaking up on you greatly outweighs the cinematic elements the static images allowed the original game.  If you never played the original, this is a must play.  

If you played the original, especially with the goal of speed running it, thats where things get hairy.  The gameplay, once you've seen the story, is all about speed running and efficiency.  It's about pathing to increase how fast you can pick up necessary items and knowing where to spend your resources.  Zombie games today are more about resource management and exploration, and while this game gets the resource management part right in the sense that it creates tension and fear, I feel like the lack of exploration, bordering on penalization of exploration by costing you health and bullets with respawning zombies, (in standard at least) renders that great stage design kind of moot.  And thats just not what I want to be playing these days.  I'll try dropping the difficulty down and seeing if that makes a difference with this feeling.

TL;DR: It's a great game, especially if you didn't play the original version or still love the original's gameplay, but the old school game's gameplay design of 'do fetch quests in the most efficient line and conserve resources' doesn't feel as good to me anymore, so I just cannot recommend it.

First of all: I hope the guys at square enix (who are responsible for the FF 7 remake) play this game in order to see how THE REMAKE is done.

Now to the game: I played RE2 back in 1998 and I consider it as the fundamental game that defined the branch of modern survival horror. I also consider it as the best Resident Evil and this remake is capturing it at it's best. There is nothing I am missing, everything is there but in a modern fashion. As with the original it is perfectly outweight between action, puzzle, item management and panic moments.

And as if my wishes were heard by Capcom, all those critics I had on RE 7 were captured and improved. There is is mind blowing atmosphere (instead of these dull jump scares from RE 7 or the trashy action from the 6th and 5th...) that reminds me a lot of alien:isolation (I bet they played the game, it's freakin awesome btw), where you are in constant fear that Mr. X is around the corner or that "something may happen just now" and the interventions of Bosses like Mr.X or "G" always happen in those unexpected moments.

Another plus to the atmosphere is the very carefully balanced game mechanics when encountering enemies, where you are definitely too weak to just run through a horde of zombies or run away from lickers safely.

But the most astonishing on this game is to me the perfectly placed soundtrack. Man that gives me chills when playing it alone in the dark.

For graphics I don't care too much but they are as with RE 7 really impressive and the model designs, as well as the environment are just soo full of details that just shows how long it took to create a proper surrounding that compares to the pre-rendered backgrounds from the old days but in realtime.

Story is what you expect from a good resident evil - deep enough to be not trashy but flat enough to keep you get going on afterwards.

What I did not like was missing spiders and that poson ivy has been replaced by those weird plant guys but that has been may be for a reason.

All in one - 10/10 clearly and just defined THE REMAKE. Capcom - shut up and take my money :-D

[h1]Resident Evil 2 is a superb game. It's a triple-A game that's actually good, much like AAA games of yore; high quality gameplay combined with top notch graphics and technology.[/h1] 

It's a faithful return to the older Resident Evil games, with a big focus on survival horror and less so on ludicrous action. Zombies can tank a fair few shots from a pistol, meaning that for the most part, disabling a zombie and then running past them is the optimal strategy. Ammo and resources are limited. 

Unlike Resident Evil 4, where items can drop from enemies, there are only so many bullets, shells, herbs and side-weapons per playthrough, meaning that poor management of the items that you have *will* lead to you being left with no ammo later on. Certain weapons are definite power amplifiers, but you will have to go and look for them if you want them, and they're generally very limited in terms of ammo availability. Not only that but the game is actually not that easy. Standard difficulty is challenging, and Hardcore is brutal, harkening back to the classic RE system of having to use rare ink ribbons to save your game.

The game is also a lot more suspenseful and scary than most recent Resident Evil games (with the exception of RE7.) Zombies act less like cannon fodder and more like tenacious obstacles that, no matter how much lead you might pump into them, there's always the chance that they'll just get back up again after some time. Hell, some will play dead, meaning that you might have to pump a round in the back of their heads just to find out if they're just being opportunistic pricks who will come after you when you turn your back to them. The other enemies in the game are also great. You have lickers that will cling to ceilings and walls, dogs that will gang up on you, G-virus sewer mutants, and the green boys that will one-shot you if you get grabbed by them. [spoiler] Tyrant will never leave you alone. [/spoiler]

The RE Engine is amazing. The game looks beautiful, especially liquids like rain, blood and the poopy sewage water. The high fidelity of the particle effects combined with excellent lighting makes this a very moody and good looking game, and it just so happens that it runs very well too. There are a lot of graphics options to tailor the visuals to your liking too, meaning that this should run on lower-end systems while also having the potential to look amazing on high-end systems. 

The gore in the game is a lot of fun too. A shotgun blast to a zombie's gut can hilariously cause the upper torso to just get lopped off, leaving you with a crawler with its entrails hanging out. Arms, legs, hands and feet can also get dismembered, which will dynamically alter a zombie's movements or attacks. On top of that, the gore is so detailed that when you pump a few slugs into a zombie, it might leave them with gaping holes that you can see through. It's definitely impressive, and my descriptions of it doesn't do it justice.

Resident Evil 2 features two main playable characters; Leon Scott Kennedy and Claire Redfield, a rookie cop and the sister of Chris Redfield respectively. As you start the game you get the choice of playing as either Leon or Claire, meaning that your equipment will be different, and some places in the game will be slightly altered. There are even a few fights that only happen in one or the other of the two storylines. It bears mentioning that Resident Evil 2 is a short game. A brand new player's playthrough might take somewhere between 4-8 hours, while experienced players can beat the game in as little as over an hour. My personal best so far, from ~20 hours of gameplay is 2 hours.

Of course, there are achievements for you to unlock, requiring you to do things like play through the game without using the item box, or healing, etc..
Some of these achievements unlocks some extra goodies for your game, like special guns.  Some of them can be quite tough though, so be ready to practice running the game as fast and effectively as possible if you wanna unlock some of the more extravagant gear.

 There are 4 different playthroughs. Leon A & B, and Claire A & B. The B routes have the same stories as the A routes, but slightly different equipment and paths. All in all, the game's meant to be played through several times, and so far, I'm still very much enjoying it. It doesn't get old to splatter zombie heads with a well placed Deagle shot. At the end of the game you receive a rank based on your performance, which mostly comes down to how fast you beat it. Beating the game on Hardcore mode with an S+ nets you some goodies, so there are incentives to truly challenge yourself. The price tag being so high means that if you have no plans to play through this several times, it might be too expensive for a single playthrough.

I'd say this game's an easy [b]9/10[/b]

In the remake A+B are gone instead we have 2nd run where you start outside the station immediately and must enter a side door, other than a few item locations and the final boss battle on the train for the true ending both scenarios are the exact same which is a let down imo.

Players will also find their first run exploring every area possible with each character that the game should take at least 5+ hours to complete but once that’s all out of the way subsequent runs will take less time, the Game on a speed run is just over 1h long 

Complete the games 2nd run will unlock the 4th Survivor a mode which allows you play as Umbrella merc Hunk the goal is to get from the sewers to the outside of the station as quick as possible while battling hordes of enemies from the game with limited ammo and health,

If you are fortunate enough to complete this you will unlock Tofu, it’s exactly the same as 4th Survivor except this time you’re a giant piece of Tofu…….with a knife, again if you clear this you unlock 2 more Tofu withy different weapons, clearing with either of them unlocks more tofu for a total of 5 Tofu……yes seriously
