The game is good. I never thought zombie game companies can make games that are as enjoyable as Left 4 Dead 2, which is a game that I played for 9,000+ hours already. Never thought that games with slow zombies like Resident Evil 2 will be so enjoyable as games with fast zombie action like Left 4 Dead 2. I played Overkill's The Walking Dead much more than I thought because I never thought I will spend that much time in this slow zombie game, and I can tell already that I will be playing Resident Evil 2 for another few hundreds of hours at least.

PROS:
- Gun mechanics are very satisfying.
- The environment is very dark and sweet.
- Zombies are detailed and feel so realistic compared to Left 4 Dead 2.
- Multiple outfits for your character.
- Special zombies are very sweet.
- There is no running and gunning in this game. You can still do things quickly though.

CONS:
- No co-op mode
- Only two playable characters, but they said they will be adding more characters Feb 15
- Zombies spawn always in the exact same locations. One of the main reasons why I played Left 4 Dead 2 for 9,000+ hours is because of the randomness of the spawn system, which is something that only Valve paid attention to. For example, you will never know when or where a horde will attack you in Left 4 Dead 2. Hordes in Left 4 Dead 2 are one of the main reasons why players receive too much damage on the highest difficulty. This is because players can be quickly surrounded by so many zombies, and if these players do not think quick enough to deal with these hordes they will more than likely not survive. The randomness in the horde spawning in Left 4 Dead 2 makes the hordes more challenging for the player and makes the player always stay on his toe the whole time because he never really know when or where will death strike him. This is something that is unfortunately not in Resident Evil 2. Once you memorize where the zombies spawn in the game, you will know exactly what is going to happen. It is like facing a stupid sergeant who does the exact same thing over and over and over again. This is my experience in real life with a sergeant from the NYPD who messed up my life with what he is doing. This is exactly how this game works. You just have a bunch of enemies who do the exact same thing over and over and over again. Even the big guy who chases you all over the place he does the exact same thing over and over and over until you can easily predict it.  

In conclusion, if you love zombie games you will love this game. It does not matter whether the games you played are fast paced games like Left 4 Dead 2, or slow paced games, you will love Resident Evil 2 if you love zombie games.

not only did this game scare me like I was a kid all over again but the presentation is fantastic, in my opinion this game completely captured why resident evil 2 was so special, but its not just a recreation, its an improvement in many ways.
it is a reimagination

the dialog can still be cheesy at times but it is much more believable and the games engine allows for beautiful real time cutscenes as well as allowing for a very well established atmosphere and seeing these classical places from the PD like the library, leons desk, the stars office, along many other fantastic recreations of places from the original really gave me a nostalgia trip.

not only that but this game made me face my fear of mr. X
I must admit that I never played any B scenario in the original game because I was terrified of mr. x for mostly the same reason I didnt play re 3. (being pursued by a monster in horror games seems to strike a nerve for me but this game was so good I forced myself to overcome my fear)

he will chase you and if you arent ready to deal with it you will just have to deal with it, this mechanic of constantly being chased forced me to make plans, cant just stumble around when he shows up, lickers and zombies become a much bigger threat when just shooting them is enough to get this guy coming for you again.

the story is the same from the original games, just much more polished and told through a lot of new dialogue, new cutscenes, new notes to find and some rather good voice acting on even minor characters, for a lot of the early game neither campaing has much going on in terms of storytelling, in your first playthrough theres some interesting hooks but not much is done with them, marvins death is predictable but at least here he is much more fleshed out than the original game, the story picks up pace after you find the 3 medallions that, unless you use a guide, should take you some wandering around before you actually find them all. 
so expect the story to get interesting anywhere from an hour after you start to 3 to 4 hours of exploring and solving puzzles. 
thats most of what I can say of the story without getting into spoilers.

the gameplay is a mix between resident evil 4-6 over the shoulder camera but unlike those games your options are much more limited, even though round house kicking zombies and supplexing mr X down a staircase would have been a lot of fun, thats not what this game is about, so expect to have full control over your character, but just remember these are leon and claire on their first zombie apocalypse so dont expect fancy hand to hand combat and mashing buttons to dodge lasers, the game gives you complete control over characters with limited power and resources, thats where a lot of this game's fun comes from.

be ready to micromanage the ♥♥♥♥ out of your inventory and engage in a battle for maintaining your resources, zombies are harder to dodge and lickers and dogs will might test your aim if you are playing on a controller, but the gameplay feels safe, very rarely did i feel like the game was screwing me over without warning or reason and unless you are playing on hardcore just eating a tri herb mix will make you invulnerable to poison and greatly reduce damage taken.

theres some boss fights in this game and most of them are pretty good, the first one is a tad scary the first time but they know you wont really be scared of fighting once you are half way through and the fights get a bit more straight forward, the bosses arent that hard to beat as long as you sort of know what you are doing.

the sound design is fantastic and I just wished they used music a bit more often but I can respect the choice of letting ambiance noise take the spotlight

technically the game is stable and I almost never dipped bellow 60 fps with an avarage of 75-80 on decently high settings on a gtx 1060 6gb, only optimization issues i could find happened exclusively when using claires electric weapon, and even those dips were not really enough to ruin my experience, but 99.9% of the game works silky smooth and in 25 hours played at the time of writing this review i crashed exactly 0 times despite alt tabbing often and even, at one point, leaving the game on pause while i left for a few hours, only to return and have the game run perfectly fine like i was gone a minute.
this PC version is impressive to say the least.

As a huge fan of the original game, this game went beyond my expectations, and they were pretty damn high in the first place. Walking around the police station was an experience, taking in both the familiarity and the newness of my surroundings (and an eight foot tall fedora-wearin' trench coat-clad tyrant pulling a Nemesis and following you everywhere certainly added to the charm/tension.) 

I love the return of survival horror aspects, such as limited ammo and recovery items, and relatively strict inventory management. They add to the suspense, especially when faced with enemies that don't necessarily stay down when shot.

It was neat to play this game through the third person "over the shoulder" perspective; I'm probably one of the few people who actually liked the static camera angles of the original series. That said, the third person was a part of the newness of this remake, and definitely did not detract from my enjoyment.

The puzzles were lovely, consisting of brand new ones and updated oldies. There wasn't anything overly complicated, either you combine one object with another then place in X spot, or using logic (and patience) to figure it out. Pretty standard fare, and it wouldn't be a proper Resident Evil game without them.

I can't recommend this game enough. There's so much to like/love about it, and I haven't really come across anything negative. Any frustrations I ran into were due, fully, to my poor choices/planning while in-game.

It's been what...? 21 years since RE2 first released. And a few years after RE1 Remake got released for Gamecube. Ever since, RE fans have been awayting the same treatment for RE2. Ah yes, my first RE experience, and also the one that holds #1 place as my favorite of RE titles.

17 years later... It finally happened. And boy it is a marvelous thing!

Nowadays, it is hard to find developers who are willing to make a game with passion, dedicated to their most loyal fanbase. Single-player games that follow this are specialy rare. But Capcom has done it. They did not need to make this game, yet they did and they went 100 steps beyond that.

Calling RE2 Remake a "remake" kind of falls short. This game is much more than that. Capcom could've just remastered the old RE with updated resolution and softened textures. Much like with what they did with Street Fighter 2 HD remake a few years back. They could've made an old-style remake, using the style of RE0 and RE1. Instead they chose to make a completely new game, not only on engine, but also gamplay and story-wise. If you are an oldschool RE fan like me and have played RE2 countless times, you will get the surprise of your life. Often you will find yourself lost in an unknown new world. This game is not RE2... this is a brand new game, giving tribute to the original. A reimagining of the old 1998 title. A reboot if you will. Yes, you will see familiar things, but they are just there for nostalgia purposes. Every part of the game is different.

Sporting the brand-new RE engine, RE2 Remake is a wonderful sight to see. Ultra-realistic models, lighting and the smoothes of textures that we've witnessed in RE7 are all here. As for gameplay itself, the game chooses the classic OTS camera perspective popularized by the legendary RE4. So in essence, it is still a mix of the new with the old, making it clear that what you're playing is an authentic RE, brought to the most modern standards in gaming technology.

But RE4 gamplay you may ask? Don't be fooled... This is nothing like the (love them, or hate them) action RE titles. There are no QTE's, abundant ammo, endless health, or a companion always by your side; oldschool fans like me, be rejoyced, as this game is true to the original RE formula. Trying to be superhero Leon from RE4/RE6 will only make you find yourself in a point of no return or simply dead. Like the original RE formula, this game punishes recklessness. Item managing, ammo and health conservation are back. Trial and error will be the name of the game. You will miss items, find yourself cornered without exit, making mistakes that force you to restart your game from scratch; this is true 90's survival horror.

For newer generations, specially those who probably grea up with RE4-RE5 and above, without playing the old ones, this game might be a bit unappealing. And it's simply because it's not an easy game where you feel empowered and in control. But please do give it a try. This is what RE should be, and after you finally get into its mechanics, you will be very pleased.

But enough of that. Let's go to the basics.
-----------------------------------------------------------
Graphics: A very impressive 9.5/10.

If you have the system to max it out, please do so. The RE Engine is a gem. No other game looks like RE7 and RE2 remake. the smothness, realistic lighting and textures are an absolute treat to witness. the only minor drawbacks could be brightness issues in some systems. There is a lot discussed in the forums about it. Also, fuzzy artifacting in shadows, which are staple of the RE Engine (also present in RE7) and unfortunately cannot be eliminated without lowering the graphics significantly.
----------------------------------------------------
Sound: 8/10

While not the best in the industry, it has certainly imporved a lot over previous RE titles. the interactive music is terrifying. However, the game is for the most part silent. If you really wish to expand you RE experience, do youself a favor and ge the Deluxe edition with the original RE2 sountrack. You won't be disappointed. Despite is an 21 year-old OST, it surprisingly fits within the game. It has aged pretty well!
--------------------------------------------------
Controls: 8.5/10

It does play very well with mouse and keyboard. Movement is easy and responsive, default mapping is intuitive, shooting is as easy as it gets. There is a mild stiffness feel to the character's movement though, but I attribute this to the slower movement to mimmick the old game. Not a big deal really.
-----------------------------------------------
Optimization: 8/10 

This game runs flawlessly in pretty much any system. There are some scenes, however, that will push the system's capabilities beyond their limit. the first scene has so much detail and dydnamic lighting that will make even a high-end -080Ti card drop it the low 30fps. But for the most part, the game has proven to run without any issues in most systems even at max settings. There are some minor issues reported if you decide to use DX12, so be warned. Also, some setups might cause the game to dim itself to the point of being unplayable.
---------------------------------------------------

Content: 9/10

Once again, going against the gaming industry's current trends, Capcom has nailed it. While some might argue that selling the extra outfits and the classic OST on launch day for extra money is a bit greedy, it is really noithing compared to other developers. Teh game itself has tons of extra outfits, weapons, game modes, various extras, all for free in the game, fully unlockable through playthough. On top of that, Capcom did announce one more chapter and more outfits for free. This is the kind of game that should be supported.

-----------------------------------------------

Replay value: 9/10

Depending on what type of gamer you are, you might rush through this game and finish it in less than 10 hours. But that's about the length of one campaign. However, after the fist campaign, you unlock the alternate second one with the other character, doubling the total length of the game. After you're done with that, you can do the same but with opposite characters, for a totaling of 2 unique playthroughs and 2 alternate verions of them. Not to mention, most unlockable will make you play the game again in different ways, in order to obtain them. the add the other 2 bonus campaign appart from the main ones, and you have a game that you'll be playing for a while.

All in all, this game is a love letter to oldschool gamers and old RE fans. But it is also a state-of-the-art, AAA, high budget game, ready to welcome new players into the franchise. This game deserves GOTY. Bravo Capcom. and thank you very much for this gem.

[h1]An ingenious blend of the old and the new. This is how you modernize a classic![/h1]

Here it is, the remake everyone's been anticipating, and boy has it been worth it! It's everything one can ask from a remake. It modernized all the right bits without compromising the spirit and core principles of the original. This is not your typical "streamlined" AAA game: no, it respects the player's intelligence every bit as much as the original does! Most important of all, it's damn terrifying! And those times when it's not, it's always tense. Resident Evil 2 is an authentic survival horror experience, worthy of carrying the title. 

The gameplay on a surface level is more reminiscent of Resident Evil 4 than the older games, but the focus is now once again on horror instead of the shooting elements. The shooter gameplay has been mostly inherited from the modern RE titles, but it's not about going in with guns blazing this time around. Zombies are now actual zombies, those Romero-style shambling, rotting corpses that trudge toward you if you're unfortunate enough to catch their attention. Gone are the parasite-infested villagers of Resident Evil 4 and subsequent titles.

In true old school Resident Evil fashion, killing zombies is satisfying and provides safety because you don't have to worry about that particular zombie when traversing the area in the future, but you'll often have to consider whether you want to conserve ammo or dispatch a zombie. Do you *really* have to kill this zombie; should you ingest these herbs now, or should you risk it and take one more hit before healing for maximized efficiency? The scarcity of ammunition and healing resources gives value to them, and finding bullets or healing often makes you sigh from relief. I'm a huge fan of this design because it makes the player really appreciate the resources given to them. It's more than just "loot". This scarcity of resources, unfortunately, became less of a factor toward the end of the game as I found myself more or less swimming in ammunition. But in the middle and especially beginning of the game, it's a huge factor and serves to add to the unrelenting suspense. Leaving zombies "alive" is unsettling but sometimes necessary, especially on the hardcore difficulty. 

One problem with the combat is that it seems to be affected by randomization to quite a large degree. Sometimes you have to put around ten bullets in a zombie's head, but other times they may go down in a few shots. On top of the already randomized damage, there seems to be some kind of critical hit mechanic in play which randomly causes a zombie's head to explode into a gory mist. This can lead to frustrating inconsistency issues. I suspect it may be to encourage the dismemberment of enemies by shooting their limbs, and that is an effective strategy indeed, as severing a zombie's leg reduces them to slow, comparatively harmless crawlers that can be skirted with relative ease. 

I could speak of the highly polarizing Tyrant enemy here, but I consider divulging details about it a major spoiler. I think it's best encountered blind as knowing beforehand would spoil the surprise. 

The areas of the original game have been beautifully and faithfully recreated in this remake. One major contrast between the original and remake is that the remake's areas tend to be a lot darker, and a flashlight is often needed. This only increases their eeriness and puts the game's beautiful lighting effects to use. Thorough exploration is rewarded, as there is plenty of optional treasure to find for perceptive players. You'll come across many lockers with combination locks, locked safes, and the like. The number of enemies scattered around the environments feels right. Enemies don't respawn; rather, they spawn at set scripted points of the story. This, I feel, was the right design choice as it allowed the developers to carefully balance the amount of resources given to the player throughout the game. The spawning of enemies is also congruent with the story pacing of the game. 

In addition to avoiding or killing zombies and managing resources, a major gameplay element in RE2 is solving puzzles. These come in large varieties. Some of them are more difficult, some slightly easier, but they're all well put together. Like mentioned earlier, the game respects the player's intelligence and doesn't treat them like a child. The puzzles are mostly challenging enough to confer the player a rewarding sense of accomplishment. This sense of accomplishment extends to every aspect of the game because it doesn't hold the player's hand excessively. 

There is some additional convenience that was absent in the original, but none of this added convenience really detracts from the game's spirit. One example is that for doors that require a certain key, the required key type is now marked on the map for you unlike in the originals. It simply means that you don't need to memorize a bunch locks around the map—or in a perhaps more likely scenario, run around trial & erroring your keys for every possible door because you've forgotten which door demands what key!

Resident Evil 2 is a well-paced adventure that mostly stays consistently strong from beginning to end, with a slightly weaker sewer section in the middle. The gameplay and environments boast sufficient variety to avoid monotony. Your weapon arsenal is also upgraded throughout the adventure with increasingly destructive zombie disposal tools. In addition to new weapons being unlocked, you will also come across upgrades for your existing weapons that are mostly found by solving optional puzzles. They spice up the weapons handily and also make for a strong impetus for scouring every nook and cranny. 

Graphically, the game is marvelous and runs well maxed out on my GTX 1060 6GB, i5 6600k rig. There's the occasional stutter when the game is loading—there are no loading screens and it loads on the fly—but other than that it runs flawlessly.  Animations, effects, character models, and everything else is state of the art. The sound design is also phenomenal and adds to the game's atmosphere in a big way. 

I didn't particularly care for the remake's soundtrack, though, but fortunately there is a DLC available that brings back the mostly excellent soundtrack of the original game. Ultimately, it's of course a question of preference, but I much preferred playing with the original soundtrack. The remake's music is leaning more toward seemingly indiscriminate, amelodic ambient noise whereas the original soundtrack features more melodic, yet still terrifying, and memorable pieces. 

This is the best AAA game I've played since Dark Souls, and there haven't been many good ones in between. It's a remarkable game in every aspect. It brings the scares but also outstanding gameplay, puzzles, cutscenes, graphics, and atmosphere. If RE7 wasn't a return to form for the series (I didn't play it), then this surely is! I've had a blast with it, and I fervently hope that Capcom make a Resident Evil 3 remake. It'll be a day 1 purchase. My faith in the AAA games industry has been restored a little. If western developers don't deliver anymore, at least certain Japanese developers, as evident, still can!

This is probably survival horror at its finest. I hate games like Amnesia, Outlast etc where 99% of encounters are just a very extended game of hide and seek with enemies that kill you with 1 hit. When I think of great horror games, I want something like Resident Evil/Evil Within that gives you a fighting chance. So, early contender for GoTY 2019 and probably the best horror survival I've played since picking up Evil Within. 

Firstly, the graphics are amazing and this game is so well optimized, cranked EVERYTHING to max and getting avg 120-140FPS (i5-8400, 1070TI & 16GB RAM). Have not experienced much in frame rate drops or any technical bugs/issues. The attention to gory detail is jaw dropping, with the limb damage system, arms dangle on threads of muscle, brains splattering everywhere and guts galore. 

GAMEPLAY here is classic Resident Evil. Lots of back tracking, puzzle solving, inventory management and exploration. The key highlight is the inventory management + lack of resources. It puts the survival in survival horror. The 3rd person shoulder camera makes every encounter visceral and a welcome modernization. Zombies tend to feel very bullet spongey tho, but it's not too bad. Exploration is key though and the map design is really well done that you will learn the ins and outs of RPD pretty quickly with the main hall being the sort of "hub" and branching off to different floors/wings. Within an hour of exploration, you could pretty much navigate it sans map. 

Sound design is a hit and miss, the dynamics are a bit off, sometimes you'd think the zombie is right next to you when it's actually well outside the room. Their groans are pretty good tho. Music is alright nothing special. I'd recommend getting the classic soundtrack DLC for extra spoopines. 

Overall, this is an early contender for GoTY. If you're on the fence don't be, probably the best zombie game out there right now. CAPCOM if you're reading this, give RE 3 & 4 this treatment and you will be printing money.

[h1]Survival Horror Reborn[/h1]

When I heard that Resident Evil 2 was getting a remake of sorts I could genuinely say I was excited. Resident Evil 7 brought back everything that made Resident Evil, well, Resident Evil. Skrimping by on supplies and managing your inventory was definately what made the game so challenging in its hay day. And now here we are with the remake and what can I say that everyone hasn't said already? Nothing. So lets get into the nitty gritty.

[h1]A Beautifully Grim Apocolypse[/h1]

Like Resident Evil 7, Resident Evil 2 takes advantage of the RE Engine, a powerhouse that delivers a truly gourgeous retelling of enviroments and set pieces from the original, and it doesn't stop just there. Character models, Props, Weapons, and Monsters are all modeled with incredible detail from blood sticking to your clothes through to how you can individually tear chunks of flesh from zombies. The more open outside segments do deliver with great lighting effects and reflections from rain and street lights and textures on the police station are crisp and highly detailed. 

[h1]A Hero and Heroine Rises[/h1]

Like the original you can take on the roles of Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield, two survivors caught in the middle of a zombie outbreak. Both characters have a unique personality and of course a unique playthrough that varies greatly between their weapons and key characters they meet from Sherry Birkin and Ada Wong. They aren't silent either, both characters will exclaim their current prediciment and even display pained emotions when injured. 

[h1]A Looming Threat[/h1]

As in the original you will encounter familiar enemies and key monsters and one in particular will literally keep you on your toes. The Tyrant T-00 (Mr. X) returns but this time around he's a little different. The Tyrant is a continuous threat that looms over you throughout certain parts of the game and conventional means prove to be useless against him so your best course of action is to simply run since shooting him with even your more powerful weapons prove to just put him out of commission momentarily only for him to come back in full force.

[h1]My Criticism's and Addressing Others[/h1]

If you're expecting to come into this game with the mind set that it will be easy you're surely wrong. Yes. This game is difficult even on the Standard difficulty setting which to me isn't much of an issue. But I do find mild irritation with some things. Yes this is a survival game and yes you're expected to manage your resources since spending ammo to kill certain enemies is pointless and more often then not you can just run past enemies without wasting a single bullet. But sometimes you're going to have to pop a shot off on some enemies and in the original zombies weren't all that difficult to take down especially with a shotgun. Sometimes in the original you could just stand still aim high with a shotgun and blow a zombies head clean off without any fuss. In the remake however the zombies are far more resiliant to even basic gunfire and unlike how in the original a few shots from your pistol could take down the most weakest of opponents in this game zombies can soak up rounds better than Hannibal Buress. Why does 6 critical shots to the head simply stun the zombie? Why does a point range shotgun blast to the face do diddly-squat? I understand that the devs wanted the player to simply immobilize zombies so you can more easily traverse the station but even that feels pointless. A new feature to the game which I do find useful is the addition of barricades but even when a window has been barricaded you will always return to that area with a handful of zombies still wandering about. With how much I enjoy the return of The Tyrant he becomes more of a nuisnace then a threat. Yes. I still shake in my chair when I hear his thunderous footsteps but after that I get a mix of fear and frustration since trying to ourtun him only leads you into more danger forcing you to rush certain tasks which again I understand for the sake of keeping suspense at an all time high.

Some people have complained about the difficulty. And to that I say play assisted mode then. It pretty much holds your hand and raises your chances of survival. And if its still too hard? Then go back to Fortnite and Minecraft. 

[h1]My Vinal Verdict[/h1]

Even with the antiquated controls and mild nuisances Resident Evil 2 is effectively reborn. It has plenty of new twists for seasoned players and is very friendly to new comers and with that in mind it casts a bright light showing that 2019 is off to a great start and that survival horror is still very much alive.

Absolutely outstanding game. A few standout strengths and weaknesses for you, here:

EDITS: Spelling and grammar.

[h1]Strengths[/h1]
[b]The Voice Work and Script[/b]

I put this first, because it suprised me, the most. The RE franchise has notoriously campy/terrible voice work and its scripts often have characters saying the cringiest stuff you can imagine. RE7 might take the cake, outside of the PS-era titles ("Come to the paaaaarty, Ethan!").

But this element of the RE2 remake is great. Leon is voiced like the shy, well-principled introvert in high school. I find that really interesting, especially because I'm so used to Chris's butch/jock character.

Claire is a little more despearate, a little more emotional, a little warmer. College kid trying to find her brother. Great stuff.

The supporting characters also convincingly portray their emotions and say things that sound like things a human would say. Well done, Capcom.

[b]The Horror[/b]

Zombies are resilient as all hell. Shoot them in the head 6+ times in order to kill them (unless you get lucky with a critical headshot that one-shots them). Their intricate reactions to bullets make the resilience feel real, rather than videogamey (I'm looking at you, RE7). So, the "zombie as tank" enemy type feels like flavor in RE's universe rather than like a videogame challenge.

They also explain the resilience: Umbrella's whole point is creating indestructable monsters. Zombies are the collateral damage that nonetheless are at least very hard to destroy. They're like partial, accidental successes for Umbrella.

There's also Mr. X (the Tyrant). He stalks you for multiple hours without stopping. During that time, you're constantly running from him. Before you see him, you hear his plodding footsteps. Terrifying. He also doesn't overstay his welcome--right before you get really sick of him, you've moved past him.

[h1]Weaknesses[/h1]
[b]Part of Mr. X's Design[/b]

He stalks you everywhere except for the save rooms and one special room with a mission objective in it. It would have been terrible to leave the game as-is and just let him go in those rooms. Especially because many of those rooms are dead ends. But, those safe areas don't make any sense. He's on your tail until you pass through one of those doorways, then he acts like he has Alzheimer's and wonders if he left he burner on. It's weird and video-gamey.

Changing the design of the game to allow for constant pursuit would be interesting. Maybe traps you can set that send him packing when he enters a room with a dead end in it.

There's also some minor issue with the threat Mr. X actually poses. His sound design, his posture while he's walking, the speed at which he walks--all of those are excellently scary.  The problem, in my opinion, is what happens when he catches you. He will punch you Dragunov-style 3-4 times before you die. His punch will knock you to the ground, meanwhile he stands there looking at you until you get up. After you get up, you still have enough time to run around him before he punches again.

Call me old-fashioned, but the "death machine" character in survival horror games should always kill in one hit--especially if their routine is to trail you at a speed slightly slower than the player's run speed. The death should result in a gory animation, as well. That's how you get people to tense up when they hear those footsteps.

That mild criticism also applies to normal enemies, I think. Zombies and Lickers should kill in two hits. Lickers should have a special attack that kills in one hit. And Mr. X should always kill in one hit.

That's how you make enemy encounters scary, in my opinion. But that's probably literally just me.

[b]The Final Boss (Leon)[/b]

It's a big bullet sponge on a square industrial elevator platform. It's really bad. This fight would be bad in any game's design, but it's made worse by the fact that your mobility is super weak in this game. No dodge roll, only a quick turn and a jog (not a sprint). Dodging the bullet sponge's attacks is kind of ludicrous with this system. But, if they had given us a dodge roll, the whole fight would be trivial.

The last fight would have been better (thematically and mechanically), if it were a hide-and-seek game that ended with the luring of the bullet sponge into a trap that finally kills it.

[b]Second Run[/b]

Second Run is almost an extremely clever take on a "hard mode." You're scrambling through it more than you were during the first run, and you're playing the character you didn't pick on your first run. So, you're getting some different elements of the story and solving a few different puzzles. Depending upon the generosity of your spirit, second run either rewards you by adding to the ending, or first run begs you to play again by omitting it.

However, too many of the puzzles are exactly the same as they were in the first run. When I was Leon, I had to detonate some C4 in the attic. Now, I have to do it again as Claire? I have to kill Marvin as both characters? Eh? Evidence that the first run has already happened appears when it's convenient (notes left by the first run character), but it's non-existent when gameplay would have to change to accommodate it (killing the same boss in both runs). 

This uncomfortably says to the player "because this is a videogame, not serious storytelling" too many times for my liking.

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
Play this game, dummy. It's awesome. Here's hoping for the same treatment for RE3 (the stinger at the end suggests there will be).

I want to preface this by saying that I have played and beaten every mainline game in the franchise to date to include REmake, OG 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, revelations, revelations 2, darkside and umbrella chronicles, now 2 Remake and I have played code veronica but have not beaten it. That being said, i have roughly over 1100 hours into the entire franchise and it stands as my favorite franchise to date. Now finally on to this game, TL;DR I absolutely adore nearly everything about it minus a couple things. This game has incredible visuals, tense moments, wonderful problem solving, fairly decent mechanics and we'll get into that shortly. But I just can't express enough how near perfect of a remake this is, I would honestly say it rivals REmake. It's incredibly faithful to the original story while still updating aspects of it along with giving more character to damn near every character in the game.

That being said, onto what I dislike because that's probably what makes this review useful. As everyone has been saying, the normal zombies... It's honestly the most dissapointing experiences to find out that you might as well be fighting a mini boss which is incredibly annoying but is downright aggrivating when it's coupled with a few other things. Firstly, the lack of a dodge coupled with zombies that turn into barry allen if you step withing 7 feet of them. They WILL outrun you 80% of the time if you try to run past them which without a dodge mechanic in a thin hallway is just dissapointing. I don't really have any other words for it. Anyway, this forces you to shoot them wasting ammo on a zombie you could've ran past had it been the original game. I get that it's not meant to be easy and that's awesome but it doesn't need to feel like you only have one option if you don't want to take a hit. The game gives you barely enough resources to deal with this so it never really feels like you're too underprepared which is a plus. However, this is hands down the most annoying thing in the game. The balancing on the zombies is just absolutely atrocious no matter how you look at it in my opinion.

This next part slightly gets into spoilers as far as redesigns go so continue at your own risk. 

Mr. X is absolutely incredible and terrifying your first time through. Once you figure out his ins and outs though he can be kind of a pushover as far as getting away from him. I personally love everything about him until... "Super Tyrant". I put this in quotations because as far as looks go it seems as though he downgraded and is actually struggling to stay alive. Now this might just be me because it's not inherently a bad design. I just don't like how it doesn't feel as though he's much more of a threat when he becomes super tyrant. Super Tyrant, at least to me, was like the all ties cut T-103 that has no ♥♥♥♥♥ to give anyone any more and is an absolute powerhouse. Firstly, Ivy is now just a plant zombie. Literally just a zombie covered in plants with a splitting head of teeth. I feel this is very uninspired personally. Now they don't look bad again, nothing in this game does, but it's just a boring concept compared to the original. I would've loved to see an actual update to their original look. Now onto the final redesign and my favorite of the 3, 4th form G. This design I feel makes a lot more sense when compared to it's original. Birkin will now only ever get on all 4s for a certain attack. other than that he is biped in this stage. This stage now just looks so mutated and uncontrolled that it makes a lot more sense that it transitions to his 5th stage. That's really all I'm gonna say about that.

In conclusion, This game is an absolutely incredible entry into the franchise that I feel deserves every praise it gets. I don't quite think it rivals RE4, or that they're even similar enough to compare, but it's just an amazing game that it hands down worth every dollar spent. I personally feel the deluxe edition is worth while for just $10 more but I'm not here to advertise. If you have played a lot or just a little of this franchise and enjoyed it. This game needs to be in your radar near front and center.

With fans asking relentlessly over the past few years for a remake of Resident Evil 2, originally released in 1998, Capcom listened and finally released a long awaited remake. Built from the ground up with their own RE Engine, RE2 Remake really is the definiation of what a remake should be. It delivers an amazing experience from the beautiful surroundings of Raccoon City and it's interiors, amazing motion capture with the characters animations moving great and fluently, the voice acting is top notch and even added in story sections to flesh out the game more.
It had fans waiting for many, many years and it was definately worth it.

PRO
- Raccoon City has never looked more beautiful. The graphics are stunning and it feels great to wander around the RCPD and Umbrella Labs once again.
- The characters all look amazing with some superb facial animations as well as their new looks.
- Voice acting is 10/10 for everyone across the board. Dunno why people have a problem with Leon, he's meant to sound younger.
- The original story has been reworked a little to provide more information or make things flow better in the narrative. You will be seeing most things familiar but others may interest or shock you.
- Seprate stories return even though they were announced ot be cut. Which means Leon A/B and Claire A/B stories.
- In a step up from 7, and using new original ones for the remake, the puzzles are a lot better and not annoyingly simple to solve. It won't take too long but it provides a much better challenge than previous games.
- Zombies, Lickers, Tyrant, Birkin and the Cerberus are all brilliant to fight because there's an actual sense of danger here. With manual aiming and speed being of the essence you must aim well as to not run out of ammo and damage them where it hurts.
- Defense weapons make a return from REmake and 0 which fiti really well and can save your life at perillous moments.
- Bosses each have a strategy to fiure out. Like the puzzles, they're hardly cryptic but make the first battle fun as you scramble to figure out what to do.
- There are plenty of unlockables from weapons, models and outfits.
- As usual achievements are there for the hunters which provides an interesting challenge in different aspects.
- An extra mode known as the 4th Survivor makes a return along with Tofu.
- A new mode coming in February allows you to fight in Raccoon City as familar characters in "What If" scenarios.
- A certain DLC allows you to change the music and sound effects to the original game's one. Perfection!

NEUTRAL
- News before release said that each campaign would last around 10 hours. My playthrough of Leon A came in at around 7 hours and Claire B around 6. RE2MAKE is the most true and honest survival horror you'll ever play. This made saving the world from giant men with claws as easy as riding a bike. 

Puzzles are as basic as ever but the game rewards planning and decision making in its action  (thanks to resources being more scarce than ever before). You will be constantly deciding whenever it's worth expending more ammo to completely dispose of a zombie over destroying their kneecap(s) to give the room a case of hazardous zombie floor to sustain more ammo. This is all greatly aided by the the amazing visuals coupled with top-notch sound design (ambience that even Dead Space cannot compare with) that will keep your hair on edge constantly.

I'm very glad people who somehow missed the original's Scenario B are seeing Mr. X for the first time (who in this game is much, much greater than Nemesis ever was). He's the true star of the re-imagining.
Returning monsters are as great as ever and the Ivies had a dramatic change, now acting like Regenerators from RE4.

RE2MAKE is very faithful, some cutscenes were done better in RE2, but RE2MAKE easily gives RE1MAKE a run for its money.
I would even go so far to say it is on par with RE4 for completely different reasons. If you feel RE4 is the best third person shooter game of all time, I am certain RE2MAKE will be the best survival horror you'll ever play, if not the best horror game.

I was going to wait to write something about this until I finished all four scenarios. I completed three and a half and nothing in the last half of Claire's B is going to change my opinion drastically so here goes.

This is a full remake for Capcom's classic Resident Evil 2/Biohazard 2. I like many as a kid found that title truly exceptional and exhilarating. Even today I can go back and enjoy it. Though some of the cheesiness even the nostalgia factor can't overshadow.

Anyway this is a more modern take on the classic. Control scheme is third person over the shoulder, with ability to move as you shoot. You can strafe and turn with a mouse. Starts out as either Leon or Claire facing a zombie outbreak in Raccoon city. Basic survive the disaster by scavanging resources, solving puzzles to open new areas and uncover story as you go, all while being threatened by zombies, monsters and the like. Fairly simple. The game has four scenarios, two for each character. This game calls the second one 'second run'. I will just refer it to as B, as it was in the original. Anyway when complete A scenario with one character you unlock the B scenario for the other. They are supposed to happen in tandem (somewhat). This gives you two different ways the story unfolds, well at least how it used to be, they did skimp on this a little.

So basic out of the way I'll go over things I did not find positive at first. The biggest complaint is that B scenario does not have enough variety from that character's A scenario. You fight the same bosses as you did in A (minus the true final boss you fight in B), and the story unfolds exactly as it does in A. Which makes 'which is cannon' route moot. It does not matter, they both do the same thing. Puzzles are switched around, key items are in different places (with few being in the same spot, like static statue stuff you would expect). That part they did well, you get stuff out of turn, weapons, resources and the like. They also give you an alternate handgun and alternate ammunition as 'base' in B scenario. Leon gets a 1911 (which he for some dumb ♥♥♥♥ reason holds like an idiot), while Claire gets a Colt Single Action Army (that she fan fires). While overall fun, and not debilitating, I would have liked if there was more variety, but honestly it is a minor complaint.

The other issue is how they implemented damage deviance and adaptive difficulty. If you don't get hit, kill zombies and don't miss, game cranks up the damage enemies do and health they have. That would be fine if the basic handguns didn't have large deviance. Now this is NOT as bad as I've seen people say. To explain, you can get a freak occurance where you shoot 3 shots and all three explode the head of a zombie back to back...or you can get a situation where you shoot double digits of the same pistol ammo and zombie keeps going. Look I personally think the game should have tanky zombies, otherwise this wouldn't be a survial horror, your basic pistol shouldn't be mopping them up left and right, but the deviance should be tightened a bit. Mind these are RARE occurances. In majority of cases you will get somewhat consistent performance from pistols, but it is odd when you shoot a dog 9 times and it keeps going, or shoot a zombie 12 times and it stays up, same as it is odd when you pop a head on your first shot. Higher tier weapons (shotgun, grenade launcher, magnum etc) are far more consitent but they too can occasioonally surpise you, but it is also enemy dependant. Magnum will always put down a zombie with a headshot for example, but can vary when shooting a licker how many times. Overall this isn't as major issue as people make it seem, but it can happen.

So what did the game do well? In my view, most everything otherwise. The atmosphere is spot on. Creepy, gore and blood filled police station, zombie moans around the corner or menecing steps of Mr. X looking for you. This game focuses on survival, not active shooting. You have to pick your fights carefuly, avoid mostly if possible, which increases tension. It is far closer to how older games felt in comparison to the new ones. I for one welcome this. Weapons are also well done, better than I expected. Reload animations are more detailed, even some handling was done better. Outside of freak incidents where RNG does silly things they all perform well, and what you expect. Magnum will put things down quickly, same with a grenade launcher, while pistols are your bare bones survival option. They incorporated sub weapons like knives and grenade which you can use offensively or defensively (when grabbed). Overall great sense of resource management, enemy threat and what you can dish out.

Speaking of resources they decided to put gunpowder mixes in this game. Odd choice, something that was from RE3. For Leon it works just fine, for Claire however you can only make certain ammo, making some of her alternate ammunition as find only. Odd enough her 'high grade gunpowder' is white while Leon's is yellow. if she had both she could have enough combinations for all ammo types, but this isn't a big deal, just an odd decision.

The similarity and differences from the original? Well the way I felt about is that the game was similar in all the right places, and different in all the good ones as well. Locations, some events, they all happen, but they may happen in different order, but they are similar enough to satisfy nostalgia and fit within the game well. Controls, combat and navigation is all more modern, making actual playing far more smooth, less jerky witht he outdated tank controlls. The RPD is familiar enough, but not 100% replica. it is expanded and yet you will recognise all iconic locations. Stars Office, Dark Room and so forth. They expanded the sewers, making that portion last longer, all fits seamlessly. For the hardcore speedrunning crowd, the game is practically designed for such a thing. Being a minimalist, picking your route wisely, grabbing just what you need along the way and so forth. It adds great bit to replaybility of the title. I'd say scenario on first run runs anywhere form 6-10h, while after that it will go faster due to you knowing solutions and area better. I'd say around 5 hours for a decent run that isn't slow and picks up everything (when you know where what is). There are four scenarios to play and plenty of unlockable stuff that needs good speedrun scores (like infinite rocket launcher and infinite minigun).

In conclusion I found the game phenomenal. This to me is an outstanding return to form for the franchise in a big way. My expectations were high and were more than met. True I didn't find the game perfect, I had some quirks and complaints, but it's mostly minimal in comparison to everything the game does well. Feel of being hunted, of constantly scavanging to survive, having to pick your battles, tension mounting up when Mr. X interrupts your fights with other creatures or doing puzzles. Everything felt spot on. Minor issues can be patched, while the scenario issue I can live with. Overall fantastic. This is a remake that should give plenty of old fans something to smile about and potentially draw in a new crowd that finds the old games outdated. I'm now patiantly waiting for inevitable Resident Evil 3/Biohazard 3 remake.
The lighting combined with the sound builds suspense that keeps you alert and and cautious of your surroundings. Overall great game.

A Resident Evil 2 remake. It’s been a long time coming. The first time I heard about the idea of such a thing, was when I watched the Super Gaming Bros playthrough of the original game in October of 2012. They wondered whether or not the game would replicate the style and mechanics of the original trilogy of Resi games, or use those featured in the more recent titles (excluding seven). Well, I guess that question’s been answered now, as the game we’re looking at today is an over-the-shoulder third-person shooter.

Personally, I think this was a good decision on Capcom’s part. After two, playing as Leon in subsequent games changed tremendously, especially after four. So it makes sense that this game continues aspects from the modern Resi games.

What I would like to see is that if they do a Resident Evil 3 remake, they make it like the classics with fixed camera angles and tank-like controls. Think about, the first remake continued that from its roots, so why not make gameplay consistent between individual characters in the series? Hell, if they go as far as to remake Code: Veronica, they could do both. Chris playing with fixed camera angles and tank like-controls, Claire with over-the-shoulder third-person shooting. Now that would be a blast from the past! 

But not the focus of today’s writing and honestly, they’re probably not gonna do that. So yeah, the Resident Evil 2 REmake. I doubt this was a surprise for some of you, I already reviewed the demo for this game in celebration of its release. And if you’re on my Discord, you’d know I even looked at the original Resident Evil 2 for the PlayStation 1. 

I couldn’t post it on Steam because, for no good reason, the original games aren’t available on the platform. Except for say Code: Veronica, Zero, and the first remake. I mentioned in a post on my Discord that these should be available for digital purchase nowadays, maybe in a compilation package. But for some reason, nobody seems to care about them. Even though they are good games even for today. Capcom, fix this. In the meantime, this is my ride on the steam train to the Resident Evil 2 REmake.

I recall mentioning in my review of the original game that there were details I discussed that lead up to the events of this game that weren’t present in its narrative. Here there is almost no explanation for how Raccoon City has been infested with zombies or what the f*ck the t-Virus, it is never mentioned. Neither are the events of the first Resident Evil game. You have got to be sh*tting me. 

There are some things that this game explains better than its counterpart did, like, for example, it’s mentioned that the Raccoon City Police Department building was converted from a museum. Which explains why there’re art pieces all over the place, even in the original, but not why there’s f*cking secret passageways and moving statues. 

This game’s events are largely the same as its counterpart, so I’m not going to cover it again. If you would like to generally know what happens, you can check my review of the original game on my Discord here, https://discord.gg/MK8vme2. Today we’re mostly going to be talking about the differences and similarities between the remake and the original game. Sticking with my formula for constructing reviews, let’s start storywise.

Now this game once again has the feature of picking between playing as Leon or Claire at the start, then playing the game again as the other character you didn’t pick to get the true ending of the game. In the original, depending on the order of who you played as, some events would play out slightly differently between characters. Like different things could happen and different characters could be involved, but there were set events and people locked to Leon and Claire. Like Leon buddying up with Ada and Claire helping Sherry. These “scenarios” would be labeled as either ClaireA, LeonB or LeonA, ClaireB. ClaireA, LeonB is the canon scenario for the original Resident Evil 2, due to events that happen to Sherry which impact the story of Resident Evil 6.

I tried replicating that for my run of the remake, and while what was supposed to happen to Sherry happened, my 2nd run with Leon screwed ♥♥♥♥ up. Characters that were supposed to have died or changed did not in my run as Leon and most noticeably, I fought the same three bosses twice. Both Claire and Leon fight William Birkin’s G1, 2, & 3 forms in the same f*cking places, and there is absolutely no evidence that these fights already occurred with the previous character. Even worse at the end of the G1 & 2 fights, Willy falls from a steep height after taking enough damage, and somehow he climbed back up after fighting Claire? And morphed back into the G2 form to again transform into G3 to fight Leon? No. No. I can only assume that LeonA, ClaireB is canon scenario for the remake, unless they’re really are two Annette’s running around who both get killed. Otherwise, this game’s story is worse than six’s. Yeah, I just said that.

And before anybody’s starts, yes, this was my 2nd Run. When you beat the game as one character, you receive a prompt that you can now start the game again in a 2nd Run mode as the character you did not select first. I started a new game for the 2nd Run and made saves for that run, don’t believe me? Look.

https://cdn.discordapp.com/attachments/525426095214821398/539540116679688212/20190128132256_1.jpg

And yet, a number of events still played out largely the same and again, characters who were supposed to be dead when they should’ve been, were not. The f*cking original game got this right, how did this happen?

While performances from the actors and actresses are top notch, especially thanks to the power of facial motion capture, I’m disappointed to say that yet again almost nobody goes through some kind of arc. Don’t get me wrong, as people, I found Leon and Claire rather relatable in the remake and much more flavorful than they ever were in the original. But as protagonists? I still think they’re sh*t. They go through any major kind of change, even though they had something Leon’s naivety with Ada. Hell, Ada got a better arc than Leon did. Both in the remake and the original.

Designwise, this game is an entirely different beast. The sewers and secret lab got a complete redesign (the sewers more so then the lab) and the only major location in this game that stayed mostly the same was the police station. There have been aesthetic and new architecture added to the building, even a whole new third floor added to the station. Often rooms were you will encounter zombies, lack any sort of proper lighting if any. Dedicated save rooms are still safe havens against any enemy you come across. Even the T-103 that chases Leon and Claire down, also known as Mr. X. I’m not kidding, I stood in a save room with the door wide open and this big-*ss pale mother f*cker didn’t follow me into the room. Even though he could clearly see me. That’s just sad and hilarious.

What is not sad and hilarious is that Mr. Trenchy is no longer character fought in scripted boss fights. This pr*ck actively hunts you down in the remake and cannot be killed. You can shot him to knock him down on his knees for a short time, but it’s often not worth spending the ammo on the *sshole. Especially since firing your weapon attracts him to your location and with the changes made to the zombies in this game.

I mentioned this in my review of the demo and I don’t like this change. Zombies do not go down with a single head-shot. What the ♥♥♥♥. I mean, at least with the updates, you can visibly see you’re making damage to a zombie with all the blood, the skin tearing and other things. But these f*uckers can take a lot of ammo to put down, especially if you’re using a 9mm. They don’t even bleed on the floor after falling down to know if they’re dead or not. Unless you somehow manage to blow their heads off, expect the undead to never stay dead.

This Review if written directly after playing through Leon's Campaign, so I have no experience with the other campaigns but I feel ready to give you a proper review of my experience. 
I also never played the original Resident Evil 2, I only know that game from Story - Recaps on Youtube, so you can say, it was my first time playing Resident Evil 2, although I'm familiar with most of the other Resident Evil Games.
So let's begin:

Resident Evil 2 is a Remake of the original Resident Evil 2 and when playing it, it felt like a Mix of the Resident Evil 1 Remaster and Resident Evil 7
You get 2 main campaigns and several bonus campaigns from what i've heard. There is also a New Game + with new content for the 'other' character you haven't played yet after you beat the game with one of the 2 characters and in the "Hard" difficulty, you also get limited resources to save your game.
I played Leon's Campaign on "normal" difficulty and it took me around 7 hours to finish it.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

The Story:
I won't tell you much about the Story, because either you know it already or want to discover it yourself.
All you need to know: There is a Zombie Outbreak and you want to find out, what's the cause of it.
The Story is presented in Notes you can read and also in Cutscenes, where you talk to other people, which are more fleshed out this time, as in the original.
The Story is easy to follow and nothing special. Your typical RE-Storytelling :)

-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

The Graphics:
I played this game in 1920x1080 with upscaling on my 4k TV with HDR and high Graphic-Setting.
I got constant 60 FPS and the game is really easy and clear to optimize in the options menu, because it shows you, which options needs a lot of memory, which is helpful :)
With my settings, the game looked amazing, the upscaling was on point and HDR made the dark areas really damn dark, which boosts the atmosphere.
Also I want to mention the Character Model Quality, they are insane! The faces and overall just the quality of character models are ones of the best you can get, they looked really really good and realistic, which also apply to the Zombie Models.
I've never seen such realistic Zombies in a Game. Their movement is what you expect from braindead Zombies and when you hit them with your weapons, tou can see their head cracking open with every shot or bones breaking out of their knees, etc. They put a huge detail in the injuries of the Zombie Models!

But I also have to say, some Textures just looked a bit out of place and from the PS3 or even PS2 era.
It's mostly on details like piles of rubbish on the street, but because everything looks so good, those things stand out, but it's not a huge deal for me personally. Just wanted to mention it.

---------------------------------------------------------------------

The Gameplay:
This is a proper survival Horror game, where you have to manage your resources and killing every enemy you see will really make you struggle in the long run up to the point, where you would be better off, restarting a previous save file, if you wasted all your precious ammo.
That being said, if you play smart, learn to know the enemies and how to get around them, without killing them, then you will be doing fine and the game rewards you with smart decisions.
Traversing your enviroment should also be planned carefully, because every Zombie will stay there, where you have left them, so zombie filled areas should be avoided.
I always take a look on the map, while staying in my save room to plan ahead, where I need to go and only take the stuff with me, I need.
Yes, Inventory management is a thing again and your inventory will be full often enough, because for most of the puzzles in the game, you need special items, which fill up your inventory, but there are storing crates in save rooms, where you can leave your stuff for later.
The puzzles in this game are set in a easy - medium difficulty. I've never struggled with the actual puzzles, but for me, the biggest puzzles are those, you to avoid yor enemies, and that can be tricky at times. Because of that, I would call this game overall a puzzle game. Every enemy encounter can be seen as a puzzle with different ways to solve it, that's how I see it at least.
And now let's get to the shooting and actual fighting of the enemies.
You got a healthy variety of enemy typed in the game, each one with their own gimmicks how to beat or avoid them.
Your common enemy will be the standard zombie.
Don't count them off as weaklings! These guys can present a huge threat, even a single one!
The main reason for it is, that they can eat up to 8 headshots, sometimes more sometimes less, but 8 felt like the number of shots I had to take with the standard pistol (of course it differs with what weapon you use, but beware, ammo is precious).
Shooting and Movement feels good in this game (I played with mouse and keyboard). I always felt 100% in control and aiming felt definately easier as in RE7, where I had my problems sometimes.
You can shoot off limbs of zombies, which I would recommend doing, especially the legs. A crawling zombie is easily avoidable and it's not needed to fully kill them in many scenarios.
This game also has some special enemy encounters throughout the game, which I will come to later in the "scary factor".
The bossfights are to be honest nothing special and a weak part of the game in my opinion, I also don't know how you would handle them, if you run out of ammo, since there are no methods to attack without your weapons.

It is possible to find many items to upgrade your equipment or inventory slots, that's the part, where the puzzles come in play and it's the reason, you do most of them, which are not story related. 
It felt rewarding, so I recommend doing the puzzles :)

------------------------------------------------------------------

Sound and also...
How scary is it?

.... It's really damn scary to be honest!
Mostly thanks to the Sound effects and general atomosphere and the lack of music.
If you wear a Headset, you can hear enemies in rooms next to you or even on the floors above you!
I want to get into that last thing a bit deeper:

MINOR SPOILERS FOR ONE ENEMY ENCOUNTER BEYOND THIS POINT!

There is one enemy in the game who is following you all around and since that point in the game, I was really terrorized by him!
I've never felt such terror by being stalked in a long time now, I think the last time was, when I was playing Amnesia, when it came out or maybe Outlast, but I think RE2 did it even better!
Simply hearing his footsteps following you, coming closer and closer and also faster!
That realization, that if you shoot some zombie, he knows where you are and you have to run for it, or he'll catch you.

SPOILER END

This  was the most intense moment in the game for me, and I guess for many other people aswell from what I've heard.
It's also the reason, some people quit the game, because they just couldn't do it anymore.
Seriously, this was some heavy ♥♥♥♥ right here and I think I would recommend the game alone for this part if you really like the horror - This Game has something nice for you ;)

And just to be clear, The horror comes from the Atmosphere, not from Jumpscares! 
Sure the game has a few of them, but they are well implemented and not just right in your face, or ♥♥♥♥ like that.
I always enjoyed it, when the game got me good ;p

-----------------------------------------------------------------

Conclusion:
As someone, who haven't played the original RE2, but overall likes the series, this game is one of the best you can get and in my opinion much better than RE7, which got praised a lot but from what I've seen, RE2 Remake is doing even better right now.
Get it, it's 100% worth the price and we will propably hear from RE2 again this year for the Game Awards 2019 ;)

Resident evil 2 remake is a highly atmospheric survival horror game. The emphasis here is on survival. Ammo, healing items, and sub weapons are in short supply no matter the selected difficulty. Its wonderfully balanced so that you always have enough ammo to deal with your required enemies, or ammo in abundance if you play smart strafing around zombies, and evading the almost omnipresent mister X. Some tips I have for new players to this series. Have multiple save files and keep a notepad or the notes section on your cellular device handy as jotting down puzzle hints and things of note are truly required at times. The map is a massively useful and important tool, as is the documents section in your inventory. At any time, you can check what rooms are clear, what items have been left in what rooms, and review prior documents to review hints, context clues, and general lore. Its important to note the game is split into four campaigns. Two longer and two shorter ones. Leon A, and Claire A being the longer ones, with Leon and Claire B being the shorter. Claire is the easier of the two player characters as she has a larger variety of powerful weapons with her staple weapons being a grenade launcher and a sub machine gun. Although they can easily be tackled in either order. Its also important to note that Leon A corresponds with Claire B and Claire A with Leon B. Neither being entirely canon but a mixture of all 4 required to come to what’s been taken as canon in later games. For tips, tricks, banter or further information I suggest a visit to r/residentevil.

I did play the original RE, RE2 and RE3 back in the day, finished all of them multiple times and returned to replay some of it from time to time. Could never call myself the biggest fan, yet I've got the fondest memories for the series. 
Never got into the genre again, tried RE4 and RE1 Remake on PC, controls felt clunky and the whole system of item management was just plain anachronic.

RE7 was a bit of a different story, I just didn't like that much aesthetically to play it myself, just watched the playthrough on Youtube, yet when this remake had popped up it was an instant Deluxe-edition pre-order for me. 

Hype train is extremely strong right now and I can really see the reasons why. Graphics are neat, sure could be better, yet could be worse, doesn't matter that much, sound is pretty fine but the atmosphere is plain magnificient. 
Still the whole new old Raccoon city police department experience is still behind a thick layer of clumsy controls and annoying item management. 
Yeah, I know, that's survival horror, you wouldn't be really scared if you had Quake razor-sharp controls in here, understand it.

Unfortunately, that's not everything for me. 
There's a couple of unkillable enemy encounters, Tyrant chasing you and the 2nd Birkin encounter when you have to push him off the platform, I absolutely wasted all my ammo on the latter only to realize you have to move on. Don't get me wrong, the atmosphere is great and ominous, nostalgia kicks in pretty hard, zombies are dying in the most impressive manner at times and there are satisfactory parts to it, yet for my taste it's more of a hassle rather than a joy ride.

Just like with the remake of the first game all those years ago, Capcom has delivered another masterclass in reimagining a classic game. 

None of the stories are extremely long (each took me 7 hours on my first playthrough), but you can play them in the reverse order and the game is highly replayable with myriad unlockables, additional modes and hardcore difficulty. The classic games were never terribly long but they got a lot of mileage out of the content they had through their replayability. This remake tries to do the same thing, and in doing so avoids the issue of staying around too long which can be very damaging for a survival horror game (e.g. Alien Isolation).

RE engine looks outstanding again, from character models to the excellent use of lighting. The attention to detail is staggering. 

Every character and every creature is significantly better than in the original, not just in presentation but in complexity and appeal. The T-103 from the original game(or Mr X)  was on the forgettable side, whereas in the remake he usurps Birkin and steals the show. Possibly the biggest change of all is making zombies one of the most dangerous enemies in the game. I haven't played a game that had zombies as durable, unpredictable and lethal as they are here. It can easily take over half a dozen headshots to down a single one -- and then watch them get back up once you've turned around. 

Resident Evil 2 is a fantastic game with stunning attention to detail and shows that Resident Evil continues to be the king of survival horror after reclaiming its crown with RE7.
IMHO, this is the best remake ever done in gaming history. Kudos to CAPCOM for "rebirthing" a classic. More power!

This is a review with opinions based on playing Hardcore difficulty and having played the original when it was released.

[b]Overall[/b], this game is fantastic and is everything you could hope for in a RE2 remake. The game was changed up enough to surprise players of the classic RE2.

I played on a [b]Keyboard + Mouse[/b] and the controls work very well. Capcom just needs to add a PC slow walk button, so you don't need to 'aim walk' to avoid some enemies.

[b]Jumpscares[/b] - I know some people care a lot about these and there are some surprising moments, but none of them are made to be cheap like in other horror games. I dislike jumpscares because they are a sign of failure by the devs to create a true sense of dread, and not fearing when the next loud noise is going to happen. I had no complaints about them in this game.

[b]Difficulty (Hardcore)[/b] will have you on edge if you're not careful with ink ribbons. An unfortunate side effect is that you may need to replay large parts again if you die, and they become very familiar and lose their horror aspect.

[b]Zombies are tough[/b] - this is a big dicussion point that divides people, but I played by avoiding zombies and other enemies as much as possible and I ended up with an inventory full of knives and ammo by the end of the game. I actually had to decide just how many R+G+B herbs I wanted to take with me vs ammo for the final few fights because I had too many.

However, from a fun point of view, yes, guns might feel a bit underpowered when you end up using 10-14 shots (provided you have good aim) to kill a zombie. I do admit that I abused the door mechanics sometimes to lose zombies and try again because I couldn't stop them in time due to their tankiness. This makes the shotgun a very valuable tool since it can guarantee easy headshot kills later in the game.

[b]Graphically[/b], there were some anomalies, but the majority of the time the game looks fantastic. On a 1080GTX at 1440p + highest settings the game remained 60fps all the way through (as expected for being in an inside evironment 99% of the time). Only small issue is that the game currently incorrectly reads my video memory as only 2GB - something that will probably get fixed in the next graphics driver update.

[b]Options[/b] allow for plenty of customisation - including FOV sliders and graphical settings that even come with preview images. Other AAA games always have me file hunting, using ini tweaks or other terrible workarounds to fix simple issues such as mouse acceleration - none of these issues are in RE2 and I had no problems just loading the game first time and gaming on.

[u]A must buy for any RE fan.[/u]

A substantial re-make of RE2 but plagued by excruciating brightness issues.

In terms of the game itself I can really appreciate the quality of life improvements:
-Mostly helpful checkpoints
-Improved combat interface (closer to RE4)
-No ink ribbons needed
-Ada is even cooler

I would have loved if they had taken the time to re-make the stories, giving Claire and Leon completely seperate missions that overlapped at various points with only minor shared areas of exploration. Perhaps Leon could be out in the city looking for survivors, or a hair-dresser while Claire searches the station for clues to Chris' whereabouts. Playing as the other character would fill in the blanks of what happened to them while you were on the other mission. It was kind of excusable in 1998 as it had to fit on CD-ROM, plus we were all a lot younger and didn't know better! Now I'm struggling to see the point of re-playing the game just to see the 5 different rooms that contain re-used puzzles. It doesn't even make any narrative sense, if Claire and Leon's stories were supposed to be happening concurrently, why weren't they seeing each other all the time in the police station? How did either of them end up on the outside of the fence near the fire escape? This is a missed opportunity on Capcom's part and they cheaped out.

But what's really wrong and what actually makes this game unplayable is the brightness. Yes, I said brightness. Holy hell! The mercurial, inexplicable brightness problems in this game! I never thought that would be a problem we'd encounter in 2019 and its behaviour is so random that it must be a bug. Given that there's very little talk about this in people's reviews of the game it probably is a bug.
Let me list the bizarre issues with the game's brightness:
-When the character uses the flashlight the entire screen is washed out
-Different rooms randomly cycle between dark and light
-The same room will display at different levels of brightness each time you enter, depending on which direction you're facing, what your blood iron composition is, whether the moon is in the 7th house
-Brightness levels can drop to near 0 visibility with only a few highlights or light sources visible
-The extreme darkness issue will persist even if brightness is turned all the way up

In fact when I first booted the game the darkness was so pervasive that I couldn't see what was going on in the opening cut scenes and could only barely make out what was happening at the gas station. This was KIND OF fixed by setting it to Direct X 11 but it was still significantly busted and buggy, resulting in the issues I listed above. Ultimately I stopped playing halfway through Claire's story because one room got so dark that I couldn't see the elements of a puzzle.

Overall, this is a mostly enjoyable game that went out of its way to stop me enjoying it. I think the graphics are good, when you can see them. If you're unlucky enough to have the brightness problems you'd be better off getting it on console. On sale.

Cons:
- Devs intentionally removed the ability to stomp zombies.

- Stealth is a mechanic, but you can't sneak attack zombies in any way (not even with a knife). Ontop of that, you can't hurt zombies which you know are playing dead if they haven't been 'activated' by the game's scripting.

Effectively, even if you have precise aim and get all dome shots (with a 9mm), you are punished for going out of your way to kill zombies. In a Resident Evil game. This is part of a trend of artificial difficulty that's been woven into Resident Evil 2. Choosing not to kill zombies isn't a matter of stealth or danger, but resource consumption, which can make combat unsatisfying after a while. There is zero reward for playing well, unless you're actively trying to kill as few zombies as possible. Surprisingly, people who buy zombie games want to do the opposite!

- Some zombies will be activated by in-game triggers regardless of how stealthy you are, and you'll most likely be forced to waste resources anyway.

- What makes all of this extra frustrating is that the game has been designed so that you can only kill zombies with bullets (knives are a precious commodity that save you from being bitten).

I was a big fan of Resident evil 2 when it first released back in 1998. I was hesitantly optimistic about a remake as so many are little more than a reskin or retexture. 

Here they have built the game from the ground up using the same engine as RE7 and it shows. They have put a lot of care into rebuilding RE2 and it is at once nostalgic and modern. With tweaks to character design and in particular, costume design which I think is much better (though they have original outfits available if that is your thing). Lighting and visual effects really help build the mood and really sells the atmosphere well. 

Similar care has been taken on the gameplay side of things. Gone are static camera angles and tank controls, and yet it still "Feels" like its namesake and this is an achievement. It is still claustrophobic, and at times hectic when you are getting swamped. This is RE as it was in 1998, rather than the more action oriented titles that came after RE4. While things are familiar, it should be noted that the puzzles and map design has been tweaked enough that, while nostalgic, it was new for a player who still remembers RE2 1998 by heart. 

Sound design is excellent and the voice acting is appropriate, although at times I do tire of hearing the protagonist say "what the..." as yet another zombie rises. 

Highly recommended.
