Instead of doing a full review, here's a couple quick tips if you're worried about the difficulty: 

[h1]Use a guide.[/h1]
Most of the difficulty comes from getting stuck, having to double back, and risk dealing with menaces you weren't able to finish off before. Using a guide will help you keep your movements on track with the flow of the game and minimal backtracking. This also helps to get weapon upgrades quickly and efficiently, and help you find and keep track of your objectives. 



[h1]Get stuff done before the Party Crasher arrives[/h1]

(Some Spoilers) 

[spoiler]There is a monster that will chase you room to room.[/spoiler] 

([spoiler]Obviously, we're talking about the unstoppable Tyrant/Mr. X[/spoiler]) 

[spoiler]HOWEVER, this monster doesn't start to appear IN YOUR FIRST RUN till you're almost done in the Police Station; if you're using a guide, you can clean out almost the entire place of supplies before he even shows up. This keeps the encounters with this monster pretty much to scripted ones. He's still tough, he's still annoying, but he's much more manageable if you do the leg work early and clear out the station of supplies before his first appearance. [/spoiler] 

[spoiler] In the second run, the Tyrant shows up MUCH earlier, and is persistant through more of the game. [/spoiler]

In the first run, you can get through most of the Police Station before your 'party is crashed'. But in the second run, 'your party is crashed' much earlier. Be ready that the game will use much of your knowledge against you this time by placing enemies and equipment in all new locations, making it more difficult to deal with the crasher. 

[h1]Item Management[/h1]
If you need to use it, use it. If you think you can escape, escape. Ammo is VERY limited in this game, and regular zombies can be... hardy, to say the least. Board up windows when you get boards, use a grenade or secondary weapon when you need them, etc. Don't try to strictly horde every resource for what may come. 

[b]... and the counter to that: don't use items willy-nilly.[/b] Just because you might need to use an item doesn't mean it's time to clean up the town, Walking Dead-style! Be strategic: zombies on stairs or in tight corners should probably be taken out. Zombies in big spaces can probably be avoided after you just shoot off a foot. If there's a zombie right outside a save room, consider killing it. It's much better than reloading and forgetting he's there. 

[h1]Don't get comfortable.[/h1] 
On that note... if you're a particularly good zombie killer, you'll notice that for the most part, once an area is cleared, it stays cleared... with a few exceptions. PAY ATTENTION if you're running through an area you cleared... there are a few times in the game new arrivals will show up. ([spoiler] In the first run, zombies on the first floor of the police station, specifically through the windows or waiting in the hall, one licker in the west hallway, and one licker in the hallway outside the STARS office when you come back, near where you spot your first one the first time. More dogs appear in the kennel and more zombies in the jail after you turn the power back on, AND a scripted Tyrant attack at the same time.)[/spoiler] These were some of the big ones for me.   

[h1] Learn the map, and know your exits[/h1]

I can't stress this one enough. This game is basically a maze, and you're the rat. Keep in mind which rooms you left zombies alive, which are cleared, and what your objective is. It's easy to get turned around or lost... especially trying to get back to a place you've only been once after  a long time... like the parking garage. 

Use the map to your advantage: on my run, I cleared safe paths through the station that I could reliably use over and over; (mostly cutting through the second floor and avoiding the first floor when possible). Use what works for you. 

[spoiler] This also applies to the Tyrant. Before you walk into any room or hallway after he's made his first entrance, you're fair game. Don't get caught in tight corners or dead ends. Try to keep at least one knife or grenade on you at all times in case you need to make a quick exit or emergency blow up someone in your path.[/spoiler]

Last thoughts - [list]

[*]The game's difficulty is less about hordes of zombies coming after you, (like in Dead Space 3 or Resident Evil 5/6) and is more about how each and every monster you see is a definite threat and drain on your very precious resources. It's MEANT to be difficult, but if you're entirely too frustrated, (or completely out of ammo in the later rounds) consider using a game trainer to get you over the hump. Yes, it's cheating, but it also helps you tailor your experience to prevent having to start 3 hours back because you didn't save enough ammo in the early rounds. 

[*]3 zombies in an area is child's play in other games, but is a serious threat in this one. Use the enviornment, don't be afraid to run to get to a better spot, and use the enviornment whenever possible. 

[*]Any corpse that is visible on the ground can likely get up and attack, or grab at you. However, zombies that have been dealt with typically stay visible in the rooms you've killed them in. KNOW THE DIFFERENCE! Don't waste ammo shooting something you've already killed, and it's okay to pre-emptively strike a zombie that may attack you. 

[*]The zombies are very spongey... they will absorb your bullets ridiculously well, especially if you're a good shot. Keep in mind the game will ramp up the difficulty if you're a pro marksman. So consider disabling some instead of eagle-eye headshotting. 

[*] Darkness is not your friend. If you're in a dark area, be wary. Use headphones if you can; knowing the difference between your footsteps and the sounds of anything else around you can save your life. Also, your flashlight has limited range... there will be times something is there but is still out of range of your light; if you think you saw something moving, you probably did. Be ready!

[/list]

That's all I've got right now! I might update this later on, but hopefully, if you're considering playing this game, these tips got you excited! After the announcement five yeara back, my expectations were really high for this game, expecting a remake/remaster in the veins of RE1 and RE0. Boy oh boy did capcom surprised me with something even more better.

The game looks good and runs like a charm. The plethora of graphical settings make sure that any sort of system out there can run this game in any possible way. It still manages to look beautiful in low settings, courtesy of RE engine, which dare I say, is an absolute worthy successor to the already tried and tested MTFramework of capcom.

As far as story and gameplay goes, the plot stays the same. It is the same 1998 RE2 storyline, except certain setpieces changed to fit its remake incarnation. Certain enemies from 1998 original like roaches and bats are missing, and it kind of makes sense. The returning enemy types like Lickers and Plant Zombies are horryfying to say the least and actually make the game tense inside the claustrophobic corridors. Mr X aka Tyrant literally makes the game tense and him chasing you like Jack Baker from RE7 only makes it scary and frustrating during a certain cutscene. Puzzles have a good balance between fun and challenging to them, though safe unlocking forces you to scavenge the police station for clues and codes, which kind of gets tedious at times. Gunplay is good, and Capcom encourages you to play safe rather than play Rambo, as ammo are scarce, and zombies take a good chunk of your bullets to go down, and it is pretty easy to run out of ammo, so taking out that limb instead of wasting ammo on that headshot is of course encouraged more. Zombie damage is brillinatly done, and each limb goes out realistically. There is also a sweet thing I noticed while playing, standard headshot won't take down a zombie instantaneously, as it will just eat away your bullets and get his skins away from his face(takes around 8 bullets in general scenario), instead taking precise aim at where the brain is will take the zombie out completely. Made props to Capcom for the level of detail put into the zombie. Next gen Zombie tech everyone.

Overall, this is the remake which was promised to us five years back, retaining the core essence of the original, but having new things for you to be surprised. There isn't much to complain about this game. If you loved the original, or just want a good single player surivival horror experience, which can manage to spook you out, Resident Evil 2 remake is definitely the game you should play.

This is how you do a remake. Keep what is good, keep the lore, the story and the characters; yet hone, define and reinvent the mechanics that made the original "aged". Capcom did just that. They used the new, beautiful REngine to bring the aesthetics to the current age (and then some), brought the perspective to what fans know as "classic" (RE4 and beyond) yet isn't the archaic static camera angle. Then they took the reinvention a step further by allowing you to experience certain aspects of the original that you couldn't before, explore new areas that you might have seen in the original but couldn't actually explore, and stayed true to what matters (the actual lore, store, etc). But those that played the original will find themselves saying "I know this will happen when this certain cutscene occurs" only to be surprised that said thing is now changed or is absent entirely only for a different event to occur.

I really can't find any faults with it. The PC version is as smooth as butter, the atmosphere is deafeningly quiet, yet you'll hear subtle hints of the original soundtrack; you'll recognize characters before that were quite literally a joke due to the campyness of the original that are now painfully real and will make you legitimately sad that they're in the situation they're in; you'll have moments of aggravation and horror but not because of some crappy, half-baked mechanic, it'll be because the game is genuinely difficult based on spawn points of enemies, lack of ammunition and how you use it (and save it), and of course how you play the game. My one fault with survival horror games in the current age is that MUCH of the difficulty is based on RNG and/or a lack of thought on the developers part, so they simply throw either enemy after enemy at you, or allow the game's lack of precise mechanics to do the work that should've been the work of precision and planning.

This game is well planned, that much is so painfully obvious. The beautiful thing is that the execution is just as masterful. I didn't think I'd have as much fun with a game as I did Resident Evil 4 but this game has surpassed that and more. There's been so few annoyances with this game that I have no choice but to push on despite my fear and lack of skill. Unlike with games like The Evil Within and the RE: Revelations saga, there's (almost) no BS moments of glitches, enemy AI acting randomly, etc. We've all had those moments of knowing we'd dodge an enemy attack...and do, only to have the exact same scenario happen the next time and to die because of it. This game isn't void of glitches, it'll happen time to time but the aggravation is almost entirely absent thanks to the vast majority of the game being a true pleasure to play instead of being an actual stress fest thanks to the mechanics of the game. This time, you'll be stressed and still having fun because the game itself is made so well. It'll be the enemies, lack of ammo, music, and ambiance of sound effects and the truly amazing visuals that stress you out. The fact you can still have a lot of fun in that scenario is utterly amazing. It says something when you watch so many streamers play a game of survival horror and almost none of them rage quit or even get angry, because they know it's their own fault. Almost any other "survival horror" game I've watched in the past decade has resulted in the player becoming truly angry and obviously not having fun. This game breaks the mold and has set a new standard that is ALMOST too high.

The original Resident Evil 2 on the Playstation was and still is one of my favorite games ever. That game, while still a classic in it's own right, has been knocked down a peg. Capcom KILLED IT with this remake/reimagining. 

The presentation is almost perfect. Playing with surround sound will leave you jumping at every ambient sound. You'll swear you heard a zombie in the room with you, but it was nothing, just the creaking and settling of this old police station. You'll hear the thundering footsteps of a pursuing boss as he searches for you from room to room. I caught myself holding my breath more times than I can count, hoping that the monstrosity climbing on the ceiling above me doesn't hear me and swoop in for the kill. 

The environmental graphics are nigh photorealistic on the highest setting. The character graphics are exceptional as well. Zombies and other monsers will look slick with blood and fluid, your character will show grotesque wounds as your health is depleted, and they will become dirty and beat up as the story unfolds. It's truly incredible what Capcom has done here. You just have to see it to believe it.

The gameplay is quite good as well. I found myself inching my way, my flashlight and gun ready, checking corners and cracking open doors to peak cautiously into the next room. My heartrate would increase at the sight or sound of any lurking monsters, which is when I would sometimes make grevious errors in judgement, or pull through luckily without a scratch. Escaping a harrowing scenario would leave you relieved unlike any game I've played in recent years. Sometimes I would be left somewhat traumatized. Ammo is scarce in the beginning, so running if often your only option. I found myself killing very few enemies in the first half of the game, opting to incapacitate or disable them instead to save resources. Though by the end of the game, I was well stocked. If I had any negatives about the gameplay, it would be that some enemies are very hard to read at times, and some are far too relentless with their grapple attacks (dogs and lickers come to mind). Sometimes the reach and speed of some enemies seems almost unfair and overly difficult, but you learn to adjust according and not make the same mistake again.

The story is mostly unchanged from the original, which is pleasant, but not surprising. Some dialogue and voice acting seemed a little off, but for the most part it is sufficient. What do you expect from a Resident Evil game, after all? You aren't so much in it for the story and acting as you are for the survival and horror, and in that, this game excels and sets a new standard as far as I'm concerned.

PROS: Graphics, sound, tension, true survival horror, overall gameplay and pacing and game flow.

CONS: Dialogue, voice acting at times, sometimes enemies can seem unfair/overly difficult.

Resident Evil 2, HD.... Honestly, what is there to be said. A lot, Actually.

I was raised with the original, Literally from the age of two. I've learnt to enjoy the game, and in turn, a lot of the resident evil franchise. Also, As I write this, I have not 100% the game, at most about 50% since I’ve completed a single "Full Playthrough" (Leon A, Claire B Hardcore Difficulty). Now, during this review I will do what I can to remove the Rose tinted glasses from my face. Additionally, I may make mention of a light spoiler here and there, So be warned.

Let's start with the graphics.

I don't have the strongest rig, I swear Running it at 70% Graphics (Some how, it can get up to 200%. Not sure how, but still) was pushing it at times due to the occasional screen freeze, But even at that level of graphics, My jaw hit the ground. The Flesh of certain monsters looked amazingly grotesque, the locations looked realistic and the character animations seemed to flow well, With care seeming to have been taken into making them feel like the ones from the original.

As for Character/Monster Designs, I will say it looks amazing. With the newer variation of Claire and Leon's clothing seeming like what one can find in real life (and better than the original, I will admit), to the clothing choice of other characters. Hell, Even the attire of Zombies seems fitting for the time. And by all that is holy, The visual feed back that an enemy has been hit is... Amazing. One good example I will give is that if you end up aiming for a zombie's mouth, it is possible to actually see their spinal cord there while their skull lazily flops around.

The Sound design... Now, here is where things can cause some issues. For this part, I will be talking about both, The new sound track and the original.

Now, the game's new soundtrack is there, my concern is the fact it's rather... quiet, even when it's meant to be playing, it doesn't sound like it's there at all. And even then, I don't remember any piece in particular, Which can be an issue for veterans of the game, since the original has tracks that bring back vivid memories from just a few notes. BUT the quiet soundtrack is important for one reason, Something I’ve seen people complain about, For some weird reason. Mr. X, The tyrant that stalks you. Once he appears, he will stalk you through out the game, and one of your warning signs of his presence is his foot steps. Similarly, With things such as the lickers, Paying attention to where the sound of their claws clicking on the walls and floors can help you. This means that the quiet atmosphere the new sound track has actually important.

As for the original sound track, Which I will add is part of both the Deluxe edition OR you must purchase it as DLC... Which, I will admit, it's a bit of an "Issue" but that is a different discussion. It's been Remastered to an amazing level, With even inventory "Bloops" Sounding crisp as can be. And the thing is, It's also used SPARINGLY (And by that I mean it's used for certain scenarios, such as boss fights, well known areas have it playing quietly, ETC) which is actually a good thing, since it means you can still hear things in the environment.

The Gameplay has it's pros and it's cons. For this, I was playing mouse and keyboard, since the game does play as a "3rd Person Shooter" reminiscent of RE:4 onwards. Though I will admit, it is likely the game was designed with consoles as a priority, meaning it may be better to play using a controller.

Let's start with a key thing, Aiming.... I kind of have a small concern here. When you move your mouse quickly to aim, Claire/Leon actually have to catch up. Of course, this is to emphasise the horror of the situation, If an enemy gets to close you are going to suffer. But at the same time, One will want perfect 1:1 aiming... I mean, it's a similar complaint I’ve heard about in other games, so I'll mention it here. Going over to interact with items requires you to use the Left mouse button, which feels weird at first but over time it felt rather... fluid. Gun accuracy was pretty good, ESPECIALLY with the grenade launcher. Something about using The "Thumper" felt right. Though, for you vets, They only brought two ammo types into the game, The Flame rounds (The standard) and The Acid Rounds (You can never find these out in the world... You will need to craft them. More on this later.) This means that there is no standard grenade rounds, No freeze rounds, or any other ammo type from other games (Like the B.O.W Rounds)

The design of the world feels pretty good, Honestly. It feels more akin to a realistic police station rather than the former museum turned police station, And it does well to explain some of the weirdness from the original game (Such as the Chess Piece fuse plugs.). Though, there is one thing that does confuse me. There is a mention that the police station was a museum.... and well, as I mentioned, it doesn't feel like it at the moment. Kind of took me out of the game there.

One major complaint I can think of gameplay wise is the fact that in the final area, the underground lab, There is literally just 3 healing items. Two Green herbs (As well as a pair of Blue and Red herbs near each of them.) and one can of first aid spray.... which is found during the pen-ultimate boss. And one of those G+R+B Herb combos is only available before the final boss.

Now, there are a few other things I will mention about gameplay, BUT I will save them for the next section... Which will be appearing now. Key Additions/changes to RE:2 From the original.

This... Holy hell, This is where I commend the game. They added a few things from other parts in the franchise. These are as follows:
Gunpowder has appeared for the first time since RE:3, Meaning it's possible to craft Pistol, Shotgun, Magnum (If playing as Leon for the shotgun + Magnum), SMG and Acid Grenade rounds (If playing as Claire for the SMG + Acid).
The Sub-weapon system from RE: Remake Returns, Meaning you have access to Combat Knives/Daggers (they break over time, annoyingly), Flash Bangs and Grenades.
The Map layout is not only an amalgamation of any game that takes place around the police station, but when you reach familiar areas, it's actually not always in the same order you visited them in the first place.
The additional interactions with certain items when examining them returns from RE: Remake, And I'm not sure, but I think RE:7 (Sadly, never got to play it)
The ability to board up windows returns from the Outbreak games. Yes, They even take ques from those games.
And finally, and most important part is this. Mr. X took a few pages from Nemesis and now STALKS YOU THROUGH OUT THE GAME. I mentioned this earlier, but This alone.... This actually scared me at points, Since it made me feel like I was never safe.

TL;DR 
Overall, I would Happily recommend RE2: HD to both, fans of the franchise and new players. The game felt like a love letter to the original, with it's careful detail on aspects in the game such as placement of items, The right time to bring back original traits of the game or replace them with new designs, to even the design of the zombies roaming Racoon City. Kind of makes me hyped for if they make RE:3 HD as well as DMC 5 due to the similar base engine.

And for those who care about Grades:
Graphics 5/5
Sound Design 4/5
Gameplay 4.5/5
Overall 4.5/5

If there's anything I can say about this game, it's that this game is just great.  The game is incredibly tense and atmospheric, unnerving the player without the need for obnoxious amounts of jumpscares.  The item management is also way better than it was in RE 7, since, while you did have to conserve your items in that game, you never really had to worry if you'd have enough bullets or health items to complete the next area, while this game forces you to constantly think whether or not you need to kill a certain zombie or to let it live and conserve your ammo.  

I also love the shift to the ots viewpoint, even though many others may complain about how it changes the original.  The over the shoulder camera allows the player to gain a certain amount of control over Leon and Claire, but since turning is rather slow and a bit clumsy at times, it's very easy to make mistakes when trying to avoid zombies and Mr. X.  While in any other genre, clumsier controls would be a bad thing, in a survival horror game, where the player is subject to making mistakes, the controls help to keep the player in a sort of panic.

Tl;dr, very fun, very scary, very stressful.

I wanted to add something that I feel has emerged; the more I play the game, the less I feel impressed by it. Maybe I'm just too old and I love REmake so much... I have no idea. I like the concept, I like the design choices and the main threats, I like the limited ammo and strong enemies, but... although the architecture is there, the atmosphere is kinda there... I dont know, I am torn between calling this a great game but not a perfect RE2 by any means, and say it's a "bad" remake and a good game on its own. Beside what I'm describing below, I also feel like there is much unnecessary swearing, some plot points have been changed way too much and the interactions between Leon and Claire have been drastically reduced, and the flow of the story simply doesnt satisfy like the original. Reading a memo instead of meeting Leon in person like in the original has a totally different impact. Chief Irons being ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ crazy from the start is also unnecessary in my opinion. Claire going all "fuc*er" and the like is also unnecessary and broke my immersion. I feel like this remake really made a little too much effort in being edgy and gloomy and reduced the good portions of the original game to a small amount.


I want to be brief and straight to the point, highlighting only what's really important for fans of the series and fans of RE2 in particular, from a long time fan of said title to another.
Of course, graphics are great, sound design is top-notch, and overally redesign has proven itself to be accurate and functional. It's truly a remarkable experience, but is it so for the old timers as well?


[b]PROS[/b]
- RPD redesign : absolutely stellar work here. Going back into the RPD was a joy to behold, and every aspect of it has been kept intact in its spirit and overall function except for a few instances (for example the press room where you had to lit specific candles serves no purpose whatsoever);
- Sewers redesign : very good work, I personally dont like this part of the game but its clear that attention to detail and care has been put into it. The puzzles feel fresh and old at the same time, they're not a chore nor a pleasure, simply something to keep you busy but not annoying to perform;
- Lab redesign : just like the original, it is very short, it keeps the basic layout of the source material while adding a little more to it to keep it interesting and visually appealing. You do the exact same things you did back then, no more, no less. This is by far the most faithful recreation of the lot;
- Weapons : intact, the same you'd expect from this installment. Nothing to add, sound good, look good, pack a punch, nice.
- Mr X : the guy finally does something other than just being there for 5 minutes. He's menacing, powerful, and slow enough that you may feel confident to escape, but he'll catch you again and again. He still breaks walls too. A very fine change, the relentless stalker that he was supposed to be.


[b]CONS[/b]
- No Lighter : any and all puzzles related to the lighter are gone. The item itself doesnt exist.
- Cut Enemies : no crows, no spiders, roaches are just cosmetic and dont deal damage, no walking mutated plants either, they've been replaced by humanoid versions with much less appeal (basically zombies with vines wrapped around them). The iconic G-Virus breeder, the giant monster that would serve as a boss for Claire, is a regular enemy now, and there are multiple roaming the place. It has lost its status of unique monster and it's very annoying to fight against. It's the replacement for spiders, for some odd reason.
- Cut locations : the Kendo GunShop is only a minor location in the later part of the game and completely detached from what it was in the original. If it didnt have the name on its door it could be mistaken for any other generic asset. The same can be said for the city itself: you are literally at the RPD's doorstep, in scenario A you get to see a tiny, miniscule bit of the alleys, in scenario B you start right inside the RPD without even touching the streets for a second.
- Mediocre voice acting : I cant believe they replaced Claire's original and iconic VA for this new girl who clearly has problems expressing herself. Leon is a piece of wood as well, although a bit better.
- Scenario A and B dont match each other's story : in the original, although some items were in the same place, most of them were shuffled around, and more importantly, the bosses that Claire and Leon fought were different. In this remake, they also fight the same bosses.
- No music : you are hearing just small noises here and there and a few notes thrown around to remind you of the original music, but there's basically nothing, no arrangement of the old save theme, nothing.  This is most likely due to the fact that there's a DLC with the original OST that you can play in the game. Not fair in my opinion.
- Ink ribbon system forced on Hardcore mode only : you cant option select your saving method. Either go for easy difficulty and save any time you want, or go for hardest and save only with ink ribbons. I would have preferred a free choice, a middle ground of sorts.
- No ADAAAAAAAAH at the end of Leon's campaign : just unexcusable.


So yeah, take it or leave it, I am enjoyig this remake so far, but I'm not as blind as to say that it's perfect. It has some issues and some design choices are just strange to me. Regardless, I'm happy that this remake exists, it wont substitute the original because it has less content - for now - and it's overall streamlined. We'll see if some of these issues will be addressed or not.

First I'd like to point out that most of bad reviews here are nonsense coming from people who either never played a Resident Evil game in their life or they're the same people who would pay to be taught to play video games. While yes I will agree that the tyrant that chases you thoughout the police station can become annoying, thats kinda the point to put the player in an oh no situation where you need to think quick to just pull yourself out. The tyrant adds a challenge making players think twice about firing off their ammo at every zombie they see at the same time making players take their time and move slow as to avoid drawing him toward them allowing the player to properly explore their surroundings. Yes the tyrant is a challenge but he's meant to be like that, if you're truly a Resident Evil fan or you love survival horror this is an enemy you will appreciate.

As for ammo and other consumables, the only reason why people are having difficulties with ammo is for a very simple reason they're spending it on every zombie they see. The zombies, lickers and tyrant were always meant to be an obstacle to get around, the only reason you should be firing your weapon is to clear space to move forward or to progress past a boss fight. If you manage your ammo correctly you wont have any issues, I've found myself plently of times holding over 50 rounds of ammunition and stock piled with medical supplies. Its simply how you manage your resources so long as you're smart you'll be fine.

The only negative thing I can purely say about this game is there are moments where the graphics could be better or places that could use a touch up but this game is still very new and will receive patches and updates in the coming months so no one can really use graphics as a complaint unless their system physically cant handle the game. I have to say considering previous Resident Evil games (Operation Raccoon City, RE6, Umbrella Corps.), this is a much needed addition to the series, Capcom in my opinion has gone above and beyond with the RE2 remake and I truly hope to see a total remake of RE3 and see a return of Nemesis in the RE engine sometime soon.

All in all this game has received 9's and 10's across the board from critics and it is well deserved. Quite honestly my only disappointment is the people in the forums complaining that tyrant is too difficult and that Claire's character model isn't insanely hot due to SJWs (note: she's based off the actual voice actor), crying and complaining for mods to be made to essentially break the game and dumb it down for them (i.e. removing Mr. X). Once again if you are not a fan of the Resident Evil series and aren't looking for a challenge in a survival horror theme, either enter this game with an open mind or look else where.

Amidst all the positive reviews I just want to throw in a BUYER BEWARE: this game fits a rather specific niche, and unfortunately it won't be for everyone.
Some reviews has already mentioned it, but it's true so I'll say it again: don't expect a full rambo experience grinding your way through hordes after hordes of zombies with bullets. If that's your thing then maybe look up RE: 6.
Rather, RE: 2 Remake is an old school horror survival.
1. Horror: as the word suggests, most aspects of the game are geared toward giving players an intense atmosphere.  Without spoiling too much, you can expect a few good scares and TONS of heart pumping moments.
2. Survival: No not the Don't Starve kind of survival. This is more of a "think really, really carefully before you shoot the last of your ammo". Resources are scarce in general, and even on Easy mode you won't simply have an endless amount of it. This is where the true fun of the game is: you franctically running around trying to find ammos/keys/herbs etc... while being chased by zombies in a dark corridors, stumbling all over. And maybe also pray that the next room you run into won't have another zombie horde waiting.
If the above sounds like your cup of tea, then RE: 2 won't disappoint. But if not, maybe give this a pass, as I have seen people describing this game as "boring". Yes it's boring if you go in expect gun blazing, Bollywood action movies stuff (yes the Bollywood is totally intended)

This game has far surpassed my expectations. It is absolutely amazing. Some CAPCOM games have been a hit or a miss but this, this is absolutely worth every single cent and every single second you spend playing it. Some of the new game mechanics I thought I would hate like having to wait for your aim to narrow in or the random amount of headshots it takes to kill a zombie but all of them I really ended up enjoyinh and liking much to my surprise. They're masterfully done and do nothing but add to the immersion and sense of atmosphere to the game.

My only gripe is how sometimes enemies can take 10+ shots to the head before they finally die or how some zombies can get up five times or more after you've downed them. Thankfully, this is few and far between happening but it also keeps you on your toes. For instance; you're in a room, you shoot a zombie in the head and it goes down. You walk over the body or shoot it in the head for good measure. It doesn't move, doesn't attack. Then you move forward a few steps past the corpse and another zombie gets up just ahead of you, all of a sudden you're in a panic situation where you're tenuously listening for the zombie you've just downed to get up behind you, meanwhile trying to down the zombie ahead of you so you're not stuck with a zombie either side of you closing in. It definitely works, just the fact that this situation might only happen to you once or twice in a playthrough has a huge impact throughout the rest of the game where you're constantly preparing for it to happen. The time to wait between aiming with gunshots adds to this also as you're left firing blindly trying to down a zombie as soon as possible in these situations.

Then there's the zombies themselves. We've come full circle. We're back to where it all began. Shambling zombies that slowly get up, slowly react and slowly grunt toward you. It feels right. It feels refreshing. It feels atmospheric. It feels terrifying. These are the kind of zombies people like me have been screaming for years for and they're back and I am so glad they're so well received and masterfully done. This is how zombies should be portrayed.

There are some things I took issue with; a certain unkillable enemy can become more of an irritating nuisance than anything else, the overall difficulty seems to veer back and forth between unnecessarily punishing and a little on the easy side, there's an irritating stealth segment, and an individual playthrough is a little on the short side (though this is somewhat compensated for with a variety of extra/bonus content, with more apparently on the way.), none of those things were a dealbreaker, however.

On the whole, I'd heartily recommend this game, and it should serve as an inspiration for how remaking a classic game should be done.

Resident Evil 2 is a game that truly needs no introduction. It's a from-the-ground-up remake of the classic 1998 survival horror game of the same name, and one that has been highly anticipated ever since it was first speculated that Capcom was working on such a release. The inspiration to the famed developer/publisher came from a fan project that was aiming to recreate Resident Evil 2 in first-person mode, using a modern day game engine. How well does this release hold up to the hype, and is it one of the best releases in the Resident Evil franchise thus far?

To say that Resident Evil 2 is merely a remake would be a catastrophic misclassification; more-so it is a reimagining of the events that transpired in Raccoon City on September 28, 1998. While much of the core of the original release has stayed intact, just as much has been left out, moved around, or further fleshed out. Players take on the role of either Leon S. Kennedy, a rookie cop who just showed up for his first day on the job, or Claire Redfield; college student and sister of original Resident Evil character Chris Redfield, who is searching for her brother. Leon and Claire meet up in the beginning and proceed to have overlapping story arcs throughout the game, but they both find out that their ultimate goal is to stop the spread of the G-Virus; a creation of the evil pharmaceutical company Umbrella, and the cause of the zombie outbreak.

Although one should never play or avoid a game based merely on its graphics, we should all take a moment to appreciate just how jaw-droppingly gorgeous Resident Evil 2 looks. Leon, Claire, and the rest of the cast look life-like and are visibly younger in appearance; which gives a great additional layer of depth to the franchise. The original release had little to no atmosphere, and was relatively bright; especially in comparison to this gritty and visually dark recreation. Very few areas are not slathered with blood and gore, and many windows burst which causes the flood of rain outside to make its way in. The lighting is just absolutely phenomenal, and players will never be able to guess what's around the next tight, darkened corridor. All of this graphical prowess and the game runs at a smooth-as-butter 60+ FPS with no crashing and no bugs; a much appreciated and highly applauded feat.

Truly Capcom has managed to put the "survival" back in survival horror; a genre that has long since neglected its difficult roots in lieu of the more conventional "fun-for-all" modern day appeal. Though the atmospheric effects and environments in Resident Evil 2 are downright frightening in every aspect, the real scares happen any time an enemy shows up. Mere zombies can take anywhere from 6-8 headshots before they finally go down, and many times they stand back up an additional time or two. With such limited resources, this overwhelming, bullet sponge mechanic forces players to make executive decisions on which foes are worth taking down, and which ones can otherwise be skirted around time and time again through the many back-and-forth treks that will be made within the tight corridors of the Raccoon City Police Department (RPD).

The aforementioned is also one of the downsides to Resident Evil 2. There are just so many zombies at any given time that it makes getting around the RPD a tiring chore. This goes even more for the Second Runs, which are arguably more difficult B-Side scenarios for both Leon and Claire. Capcom has introduced a new feature in this reimagining, and that is the use of wooden planks to board up windows. Of course, the supply of these boards is limited and not every window can be taken care of. Windows left unattended will keep letting floods of zombies in, and in some cases will cause areas of the game to become nearly impassable over time. It also doesn't help that all of the high-octane weapons are kept hidden away until the last hour or two of gameplay, with no means to unlock them as beginning weapons via subsequent playthroughs.

This brings us to another point; the lack of unlockables, which is a staple in the Resident Evil series. Sure, there are tons of character models, concept art, and challenges to unlock. However, Resident Evil 2 is stingy when it comes to anything else. Without providing any spoilers, players will be disappointed in the lack of weapons that the game houses overall, and even more let down with the absence of available unlocks for those that are present. There are two scenarios each for both Leon and Claire, plus an additional game mode that will become unlocked once players finish at least one of the Second Runs. Each of these runs takes 5-8 hours upon their first playthrough, meaning that players will get a maximum of 35-ish hours out of the game with the other unlockable mode. This is of course not counting the die-hard fans who will go back to achievement hunt such difficult gems as getting an S-Rank with both characters and beating the game in under 14,000 steps.

When it comes down to it, the Resident Evil 2 remake is everything that fans dreamed of when it comes down to its campaign. The true ending isn't even unveiled until players make the dedicated leap to finish the game for the third time via a Second Run; a necessity to obtaining some form of closure, as the main ending is underwhelming and jarringly abrupt. However, Capcom has seemed to forget a major component to what makes a Resident Evil game part of their franchise; unlockables. It's what keeps players interested in countless runs through the same slog that can be easily reduced to a mere couple of hours with optimal routes. As far as replayability goes, it's not here, but the game is worth playing a few times over... just don't expect more than 20 hours out of the most casual player.

Twelve hours in, and I already feel it was worth my $70. Let me go over each section, then answer some of the complaints I've seen.

Story: The story is...well, Resident Evil 2. Clare and Leon meet up, both with different goals, but their paths intertwining  a couple times. The writing in this game is amazing. The voice acting is amazing, some cutscenes are very heartfelt, a couple of them in both playthroughs making me shed some tears. Overall, this story is the best I've seen in Resident Evil to date.

Performance & Graphics: Before this section, would like to remind you that Nvidia has yet to release a driver for the release, so everything in this section is pre-driver. Graphics are amazing. RE Engine does great with rendering all kinds of objects. And character models are the best I have ever seen from ANY game. The only issue I have is that some textures look very blurry when close, but that is most likely a compromise so that PC is more in line with console, RE7 did it as well. Performance is almost perfect. Playing with an i7 6700k and a GTX 1080 at 1080p, I get mostly above 100fps with everything maxed except AA (I have FXAA+TAA because I don't mind the softness compared to SMAA which makes hair look dreadful) Dark areas I get anywhere from 120fps-160fps and cutscenes that look great will bring me down to around 85-95fps. I only have two issues 1) When V-sync is turned on, when areas load, there is a slight stutter. Not that big of an issue but does get annoying.  2) I can't find any setting that fixes it, but everything glistens A LOT. Especially on blood. You get used to it though. Overall, the performance and graphics on this game is great, just like RE7.

Gameplay: Ah, the section that everyone has been waiting for. I won't bore you with what changes were made to the systems, as you're sure to have seen that other places, more-so I will focus on my feelings about the gameplay and the mechanics. First off, this game is difficult, you can't just blast through zombies nor just sprint around them. There are tricks to deal with individual zombies but there will be many rooms with multiple ones. Crafting makes a return requiring you to craft herbs and bullets, and the system is actually great. The combinations of items make sense and if you're low on space, you can combine items right when you pick them up. The pacing of the game is amazing. Each section feels perfectly paced, with no section feeling like it's taking too long and all sections really being equal in length to each-other. In comparison, I feel that in RE1 [spoiler] the mansion was much longer than the guardhouse or labs, and they either needed to tone down the mansion or tone up the rest of the game. [/spoiler] Boss battles are not overly tough, and it's very generous in getting you prepared

Common Compaints:

"They don't give you enough ammo/ Zombies are too hard to kill!"
Yes, ammo placement is limited (Welcome to Survival Horror) with later powerful weapons only giving you about one extra clip of ammo. However, Ammo crafting is very important in this game. If you craft your ammo, you should have more than enough. A lot of the game with Claire, I was stocked up on Ammo, never really falling below a comfortable level. With Leon, there was about one 45 minute section where ammo was dangerously low, only being restocked before a boss battle. That being said, I did play Leon first, so it could have just been me wasting too much ammo on Zombies. Speaking off, yes, Zombies are bullet sponges, however if you're trying to kill zombies with bullets, there's the issue. [spoiler] Best way to deal with zombies is not to shoot the head, but the legs. Their legs will break off and while they are down, take out your knife, and go to town. [/spoiler]

"The game is not worth $60/$70! It's way too short"
While yes, each scenerio is short (Leon A took me about 5 hours and Claire A took me a couple minutes under 4 hours) anyone with this complaint clearly has not played the original RE2. The joy of RE2 is multiple playthroughs. While yes, both A story routes are extremely similar, there are different sections that, even while only have played both A campaigns at the time of writing, make me feel like there's enough difference to justify it. I still have both B campaigns to go as well as the bonus modes once I beat those. I am extremely exited about what is to come


Overall, Resident Evil 2 is a great game. It is not for everyone due to requiring a different mindset about dealing with zombies and the full experience requiring multiple playthroughs, but it is a gem, and the best Resident Evil game to date.

This game is fantastic.

Working from the surface level in; the graphics are some of the best that I've seen in a horror game, and are better than most games in general, for that matter. The lighting is phenomenal, casting the player into scenes of black that's somehow deeper than black. Sound bounces around the hallways of the RPD perfectly, echo'ing in the headset so vividly that you feel like you're the one trapped in this nightmare.

On the second layer we find well-made controls. It would seem as though Capcom learned through the years and has finally refined the experience to the point of being buttery-smooth. The movement is natural and easy to learn, with a few points that can be mastered in such a way that your movement is just as much of a weapon as your pistol. The shooting feels healthy, with more powerful weapons being harder to aim than their weaker cousins, for example,  Matilda (Leon's handgun) packs a weaker punch than the shotgun but boasts a massive magazine of 12 that can be expanded to 24 and recoil that's so gentle that you can hardly feel it, where as the shotgun kicks like a mule and only holds 4 shells, but can blow a zombie's head apart in a single shot. It's a game of checks and balances, with enemy types, environments, and resource management leaving every weapon in the game completely viable and useful.

Finally, we reach the skeleton of the game, and I have to say, it's just as solid as the rest. During my play time, I ran into only one glitch. While fighting Mr. X, I was grabbed as I passed through the library door and thrown. The animation pushed me through the door and back out into the main hall and Mr. X got stuck in that door way for a while until he naturally reset back to the Main Hall. During the other 30 hours, however, it was perfection marred only by a few half-second long FPS stutters.

Personally, I'd give this game a 9/10. Running from Mr. X while in the middle of a puzzle was a little bit irritating and the inconsistency with some zeds being able take anywhere from 1 critical shot or 3 normal shots to a staggering 9 that they instantly revive from left me feeling a bit cheated out of the careful inventory management that I fought for throughout the experience.

Regardless of that, I would recommend this game to anyone that has the money to spare. While I was initially worried that the game wouldn't be worth 60$, those doubts have been put to rest. It's completely worth the money and will be a game that I revisit time and time again for years to come.

Resident Evil 2 is a 3rd person survival horror remake of the 1998 release. Set in a seemingly cliche zombie apocalypse after the disaster at the Arklay Mountain mansion (RE1), you delve deeper into a conspiracy involving a popular pharmaceutical company and city officials of Raccoon City. You can choose to play as Leon, a rookie cop on his first day or Claire, a college student looking for her brother. Along the way, you'll come across a few survivors which will drive the story forward...

On the art/graphic side, this game is oozing with professionalism. I thought RE7 was excellent on the facial animations and level design, but RE2 goes even further and drives it home big-time. Instead of going for a 1:1 replica of the old map, Capcom took some artistic liberties and remodeled the layout in a newer, fresher way. Each rooms are cluttered with details that makes exploring even more fun. I spent a lot of time just walking around slowly, stuffing my nose in every possible corners.

In the sound department, it's as good as previous RE's. The long years working on the RE franchise as allowed Capcom to master their craft and it's on full display here, same goes with graphics. Great voice actors that complement well their digital counter-part, providing believable emotions. Great ambient soundtrack that helps build atmosphere. Each rooms and corridor have unique audio range and echo, so each sound coming from your character resonates well with the type of room you're in. It's not mandatory, but I'd strongly suggest you play through this game at least once with good headphones.

Some of the gameplay feature from the old RE2 makes a come-back, including Scenario B, The 4th Survivor, a ranking system and unlockables. Scenario B allows you to experience the event of the opposing character you chose at the start, providing a different view on the story and extending your playtime. It might seem mundane to newer player, but it used to be a neat feature in the original due to how you had to switch CDs and use your cleared save file to access said Scenario B.

In the PC technical side, this game has every possible options to please. Lots of graphic options, sounds configurations, customizable keyboard and multiple controller setup which, thank god, allows me to move Sprint away from the Left Joystick Click, something I hate with a passion in ANY video games ever. I tried both KB/M and controller. KB/M feels tight and as snappy as RE7 (looking at UI navigation). However, it can't be denied that this game is best played with a controller. Controlling your character and camera feels more smooth and natural than KB/M's edgy mouse-look and square-rery WASD movement.

The only negative aspect of the game, for me, is simply the fact that this game isn't 100% original. It's a remake, so, Capcom already had a mental blueprint of it all to begin with. This game reeks of fan service and maybe a little despair from Capcom trying to reconnect with a wider RE fanbase, which was arguably divided since RE4's shift to 3rd person action and its sequels... However, I think this remake is doing it right by uniting all the good things that made each Resident Evil good and fun to play. Perhaps it was a good thing they waited this long. An RE2 remake 10 years ago probably wouldn't have been as impressive as what we have now...

Congratulations Capcom. You did it. I wish you the best in the years to come, either with RE8 or the next R3make, if there's any plans for it.

So, where do I start? I've been a huge fan of the Resident Evil series since I was a child, even though the games scared the hell out of me. I kept playing and I'm even one of the few people who enjoy the later games (4,5,6). But going by this one? Well, Resident Evil 2 was my favorite from the franchise along with Resident Evil 3: Nemesis. I was skeptical about the remake when they first spoke about it being in the works, but seeing the trailers and actually playing it entirely now? It's worth every damn cent you may consider spending.

For Resident Evil veterans:
The game offers old game mechanics and mixes new mechanics in just nicely. I know what you're thinking. You're skeptical about the "Over-the-shoulder" camera angle that was first introduced with Resident Evil 4. But I can tell you, it adds to the atmosphere, because you can't actually see things behind you for example. You may be focused on fighting off some enemies and another one just walks up behind you and scares you. The remake makes you remember places you're familiar with from the original Resident Evil 2, shows you new places and even changes the order you normally would see those places in. Is that bad? By no means. Is it just as good as the original? No. It's better. It looks better, plays better, has more fun mechanics and obviously, due to the lack of technological limitations the developers have nowadays, you can also expect some really surprising new stuff you would never expect in a Resident Evil game. Is the story different? Hmm...There's slight changes, but nothing drastic. 

For the new players:
If you've never played one of the classic Resident Evil games (0,1,2,3,CVX etc.) then this is a good point to start in. Now, I suggest you play the remake of Resident Evil 1 first. It's on Steam as well and not that expensive. I can also wholeheartedly recommend that game. The remake is genuinely better than the PS1 original in every way possible. Now back to the RE2 remake. If you wanna buy this game without playing RE1 first, you can absolutely do that. RE2 is where the story really begins, where everything is explored in a deeper way and where actual character development happens. You may argue: "Resident Evil 1 also had character development!" - Yes, but not nearly as much as this. This is one of the first Resident Evil games that lets you feel some sort of pity or sympathy for the characters involved while the other Resident Evil games usually made you go "Oh damn, that dude's dead." or "This guy's kinda cool." or whatever. As a hardcore Resident Evil fan, I promise you that this game is worth every cent and if you haven't played a Resident Evil game before touching this, you'll wanna play the other ones afterwards to see how the story continues. Again, you'll understand everything even if you didn't play RE1, but you'll understand more easter eggs and references - which add to the experience, if you played Resident Evil 0 or Resident Evil 1.

Surprise surprise:
You can play as the rookie police officer Leon S. Kennedy or as Claire Redfield, who's looking for her brother Chris (who many may remember from Resident Evil 1). Whichever you choose to play as first, once you finished the story - and this is important: Play the story of the other character too. The story is drastically different and answers all the questions that may come up during your first playthrough. I was actually surprised that it's not just a different character with different weapons. It feels like an entirely different game, even though 50% of the locations are just re-used. Trust me on this.

tl;dr:
Buy the game. You won't be disappointed.

[h1]More in depth: [/h1]
 [list]
    [*]Resident Evil games are about as good as the movies in terms of story and characters. They are a little better as you can skip them. But their gameplay is one that only Dead Space has been able to replicate. How does this game stand from the eyes of someone that hasn’t played the original? 

    [*]Yes the graphics are amazing, it’s AAA, it should be. Moving on, the game has you play as one of two characters that each have a different motivation for going and doing the same stuff. Very weak here, as again the story and characters are bland. They do have different weapon loadouts, and some areas that they can only access. I did play both as I was curious and do love the beginning so MUCH.

    [*]The game is a very slow game in the sense of how you and the enemy act. Zombies don’t run, and you don’t really either. You get limited inventory space at the start and get more as you progress. You also can’t kill everything as you don’t have the ammo for it. So you choose what to engage, what windows to board up to block them from coming in. The weapon selection is good with the standard selection with more unique ones like grenade launcher and electric nail gun going to Claire.

    [*]My only few gripes with the game are the inconsistent bullet sponginess of the zombies. Some can take so much ammo that it’s pointless to ever try to rid them. Shotguns point blank don’t head shot zombies. This is dumb and makes having few bullets left and not doing anything dumb. Not having ammo wasn’t an issue, they give you more than enough to deal with what you need. I just don’t like putting 2 smg mags into an enemies head and having him still get up. My least favorite part is the sewers. It’s everything this game isn’t, no puzzles, literal linear halls making it hard to juke zombies. Sewer monsters that you have to kill and waste so much ammo to progress. Cut this out and the game would be a masterpiece and wouldn’t  make me dread replaying the game. Also the boss fights were the same each guy each time in very cramped linear areas or a literal 5 ft by 5 ft platform. Luckily they are trash at hitting each you and not until the final final boss do you get something a little demanding of your brain. 

    [*]The best part is the intro police station. I love the open nature of it, the interconnected rooms and unlocking new shortcuts, along with plenty of puzzles and items to gather here, replaying the section over and over again was a blast. You later get a presence that forces you to allows keep moving to further add tension. You move on from that level of masterpiece design to the mediocre sewer level that luckily is only a few hours or less depending on how knowledgeable you are of the layout. You then go to a third area that brings it back to a great game and ends on a good note.

    [*]Overall the game is one of the best survival horror games I’ve played. Don’t play it for the story, they do give you multiple reasons to replay with 2 characters each with alternative runs that mix it up even more, along with more content that I don't know how to unlock. You get an atmosphere that as a huge zombie fanatic feels right at home despite some shortcomings. Learning to stun zombies instead of killing them to move past them, replaying and cutting your time in half, very few games can get a second play through, even if they really want you too. So this says aIot about the core gameplay being great to make to do it two and a half times. I hope they remake more of the older ones and can’t wait to finish RE7.

I've never played the original Resident Evil 2, but I've seen some videos. 
I hadn't heard about this coming out until maybe a few weeks ago. I saw it, and immideately thought that this looked very interesting. I've played through RE7, and that utilized the same engine as this game. Both of the games are visually absolutely amazing, the detail is beautiful. The visuals in this game have clearly been thought out, a lot. Every place in this game, from the Police Station to the sewers and the underground lab are astonishing. 

The game's story is also fantastic. The game has two storylines, I played through both campaigns and and got the True Ending. The storyline is so intriguing I could barely stop playing. The plot is pretty straight-forward and kind of a cliché, but entertaining nonetheless. The voice-acting is mostly okay, but sometimes seems kind of clunky. 


I started my original run with Leon's storyline on Standard difficulty. Played through that in 6 hours, 27 minutes. I wasn't as thorough as I could've been, but I still took some time. After you complete a campaign, you get a grade for your performance. I got grade B for Leon's campaign, falling short of the 5 hour completion time required for grade A. I'm not sure if playtime resets when you load a save, but I died 10-ish times during Leon's campaign. After I had completed the campaign and returned to the main menu, I got a notification that I had unlocked a new campaign mode: "New Game [2nd]". This meant, for me as I played Leon's campaign, that New Game [2nd] would be the Secondary Storyline for Claire. Secondary storyline meant that most things that happened in my original run as Leon happened the same way (mostly), and 2nd campaign was shorter by some time. I completed the 2nd campaign in 4 hours 26, just falling short of the 4-hour goal for grade A ;_;. After I had completed both storylines I got the game's "True Ending". After which, when I returned to the main menu, I got another notification, saying that I had now unlocked the bonus mode called "4th Survivor", in which you play as a special forces soldier trying to make to an extraction point. In that mode you have a limited amount of ammo, but incredible amounts of zombies and enemies against you, trying to stop you from reaching the extraction point. The challenge is that if you die, you have to start from the beginning. I've yet to complete it, as it is extremely challenging. 

The grade system is where the replay value of the game starts. You can grind in order to get grade A, and it would seem that there is also a hidden grade S, which would take even more skill. The game has a main storyline for both Leon and Claire, and both also have a secondary storyline. If you play through with one main storyline, you will get the secondary storyline for the character you did not play as. If you play through that secondary storyline, you will get the secondary storyline for the other character, the one you originally played as. The difficulty levels also bring replayability. 

The game is fairly action-oriented, with a lot of puzzles and problem solving, requiring you to run around looking for parts and clues. 
The game has a lot of tense moments, especially if you run out of ammo. If you happen to run out of ammo, the game becomes a lot more challenging, but at the same time exciting and adds a sense of dread as you try to get past zombies looking for the next thing you need in order to get further in the story.

If you're on the fence about paying full price for this game, don't be. This game is more than worth it. It's a great remake, and a great game, period.

So after pumping in some hours and completing all the story has to offer, I’ve decided to edit my review. 

While I still would say this is a great game, it falls a little flat of amazing. The problem being the story and variety: there’s not a lot of it. 

In the original Resident Evil 2 you had basically 4 storylines (Leon A/Claire B, Claire A/Leon B). In this remake you only have 2 (Leon & Claire). There are “2nd playthrough” modes, but these are essentially pointless as they offer the same story as before but with a sort of “rearranged” mode gameplay change. The only thing really of value here is the “true” ending. 

The way Mr X is implemented in the remake is a bit poor. Similar to Alien: Isolation’s Alien, he stalks you through various points in the game. But while scary on the initial play through, is just a hindrance in later play throughs as his appearances are scripted and appear in the exact same places every time. Then it’s just a case of RNG whether he will cause a problem for you or not. Unlike Alien: Isolation where the game is built around the concept, in here it feels a bit cheap. 

Some of the enemy types from the old game have been scrapped and are nowhere to be seen in the remake, so the game can feel repetitive facing the same enemy types over and over.

The gameplay however is pretty flawless. It was always smooth and responsive. And the graphics are phenomenal. The RE engine really is a powerhouse when it comes to visuals, especially with enemy damage. Watching zombies fall apart when you shoot them is always satisfying. 

Overall it is a very good game. But, it is let down by a very lacklustre story when compared to the amount on offer in the original. Once you’ve seen the campaign from both characters, you’ve pretty much seen all there is to see.

Resident Evil is a franchise whose entries are kind of hard to rate and compare with one another since the games have seen so much change over time. Despite all that, Resident Evil 2 Remake is an excellent game and a true successor to the original.


TL;DR:

+ Faithful reimagining of the original in every aspect.
+ Everything that could be improved in the original is improved in this game.
+ Meaningful gameplay mechanics. Everything has its use.
+ It is hardcore more than in just it's difficulty settings name. If you ask for challenging, unforgiving experience, you'll have it!
+ It makes your objective clear without holding your hand with markers.
+ Superb atmosphere and overall presentation.
+ All the little nods and homages to the original are very nice to a RE2 veteran like myself.

- More of a neutral than a negative point, but I feel like the characters look rather different than the ones from the original/followups.
- Although already great, the atmosphere would probably benefit from additional music tracks.
- I could do with more in-game unlockables.


OK so, let me start by saying that I'm a big fan and someone who knows RE inside and out. I've played all of the old games and I really loved what they did with RE4 afterwards. However I also loved RE6 (which is not a popular opinion) and I consider it to be [b]technically the best[/b] RE game but also [b]the worst one thematically[/b]. However, no matter which style you prefer, you can't go wrong with Resident Evil 2 Remake.

This game, shortly put, does everything right!
The gameplay just works and manages to put a lot of pressure on the player and keep it going from start to finish. Whether you're being chased around the station by your nemesis, the terrifying tyrant [i]"Mr.X"[/i] or trying to sneak past a [i]Licker[/i] in a narrow hallway and hoping that the downed zombie doesn't suddenly grab your leg and mess up your entire sneaking attempt,  [b]you will feel the pressure weighting down on you[/b]. It successfully invoked the same uptight feeling within me that the original struck me with 20 years ago and reminded me what true survival horror is all about.

On top of all that, it looks wonderful and the games visuals successfully add to the horror.
Without going into detail and revealing the games locations, I'll stick to the police station and it's dark, flooded hallways with narrow passages where the zombies roam free. The game does darkness and shadows right. Your flashlight is absolutely necessary in some areas and when combined with the games light-dark ratio it creates amazing environments.
I've seen that some users were writing that they had problems with the lighting but I had none of that. The game has very detailed brightness settings (3 of them in fact) and improper calibration was probably the cause of the problem.

In traditional RE fashion, going through the game once is not really going to count as a full experience.
Luckily for us, this title has quite the replay value - just like the original had. Completing the game with either of the characters will unlock the [i]"2nd Run"[/i] for the other character which is a replay of the game with quite a few things changed. From objectives and progression to enemies, things will be different enough to keep you interested. The maps are the same for the most of these two runs but the way you play and progress through these will be quite different.

Unfortunately, compared to the original game there isn't that much extra content.
Besides the [spoiler][i]4th Survivor[/i] and [i]Tofu[/i][/spoiler] there are no other game modes at the moment although I've heard that some will be added as a free DLC. There are some extra weapons and original costumes that you can unlock but that's it. It's not bad but I kind of hoped they would add more of these but, we never know what might be in the upcoming updates.


Finally I'd like to give a definite YES to this game, congratulate the entire RE2 Remake team on a job wonderfully done. Now I can only hope that this one sells good enough so that one day we might get a [i]Nemesis[/i] remake of even better quality.

So, here we are about 20 years later and Capcom releases Resident Evil 2 Remake and what's to say about the game compared to the original?

A whole lot of changes, and good ones at that.

Gameplay:
The gameplay is vastly improved from the original where you no longer have to control Leon like a tank and stop and shoot, this time Capcom went for a third person shooter approach where you move in a third person camera instead of the fixed camera angle and no longer have to stop and shoot. The gameplay is very reminiscent of that of Resident Evil 4.

Story:
The story of the game is about 10 hours long and the same as the original with you being a rookie cop on the first day of the job and you witness a Zombie Invasion and now you gotta find survivors within your Police Station and find a way to the girl you were with on the way there. The areas you'll be visiting are somewhat different from the original where somethings are the same and somethings aren't.

Graphics:
Obviously, the remake is one of the best looking Resident Evil games I've ever seen, maybe even of all time at that. Rain effects look so good, and you can see Leons clothes and hair soaking in the rain. What suprised me even more was how smooth the game ran, running at a constant 60-80 on my R9 380 at the highest settings. I only saw some dips when first entering an area but I'm willing to overlook that because the game takes like 1-2 seconds to go back to the regular framerate.

So should you buy Resident Evil 2? I would honestly wait for a sale or find it cheaper but overall it's a really good game and if you're new to the series I'd more than likely recommend this game to you to start out with.

To preface, I'm another person who played and loved the original way back. It was the very first Playstation game I had ever played and owned, and it holds a special place in my heart as such. That said, I want to try and stay as objective as possible in this review, relying more on what the game presents instead of blindly praising everything based on nostalgia.

The game is a faithful recreation of the original that could be described as the world we once knew viewed through a much higher quality lens. It's similar enough to the original to evoke waves of nostalgia while being different enough to create an entirely unique experience. Above all else, the game doesn't rely solely on nostalgia and its own past success to further make a name for itself, and very strongly stands of its own merits.
Graphically, the entire game looks gorgeous. The world looks gritty and well lived in, and the atmosphere and mood created by the various locales you'll visit all feel just right; nothing over the top or too sparse, everything in the world was crafted with purpose and reason. Various graphical settings like the anti-aliasing might be wonky or unoptimal by default though and needs to be played with to get the look you want.

The game handles well and the gunplay feels good, though the one and only real complaint I would have is sometimes the movement can be janky when changing directions, but it very seldomly screws you over when it matters and is an annoyance at worst. A common complaint is how the enemies and monsters you'll find are bullet sponges (and they are), but I think the intent was to be a call back to the original where you had to pick and choose your battles and know when and how to run through the danger. In that regard, the game really nails it. Well placed shots and a general mastery with aiming are crucial; this isn't a game where you can just spray-and-pray.

The sound is good, the voice acting is solid, and the soundtrack offers a new take on the old classics veterans are familiar with, although a DLC that will play all the original songs where appropriate is also available (which I wholeheartedly recommend getting. It's absolutely worth the few bucks it asks for).
While the game does offer DLC in the form of cosmetics, the original soundtrack and an extra starting weapon, the amount of additional in-game content you get off the bat is fantastic and comes with the game by default, something largely unheard of these days from big names where $60 is just the entry fee to a game that wants you to pay for additional content.

Overall, the entire game is a very detailed and meticulous labor of love that pays tribute to the original it was based upon while offering an experience that's exciting and solid enough to shine on its own, whether the player is familiar with the original or not. I'm loathe to ever say it about anything I ever play at the risk of sounding like I'm showering the game with blind praise, but I would dare say that the game is perfect. Or a the very least, a perfect remake that captures the essence of the old while livening it up with a new look and feel. I genuinely cannot overstate how well done the RE2 team did with this remake, especially when comparing it to the original. It's very seldom that I can feel like I've gotten my 60 dollars worth out of a game, but the Resident Evil 2 remake absolutely solidifies that feeling in me.

What could I say that hasn't already been said about this game? Is it the gaming marvel that everyone makes it out to be? I'd say that depends on what you are looking for from a game. If you're looking for a near perfect survival horror game, then yes. YES.

First and foremost, the story is serviceable. Honestly it's probably better than the developers intended. Leon and Claire are very likable main characters. Both infuse their confusion and fear into the game play with their comments. Often these comments came mere seconds after I myself said these things. This makes them very believable and adds an extra layer of immersion and trust that these are indeed real people you're playing as. Let me warn you that the ending will fall flat in your first run. This is intended. Though I think that there would have been a better way to handle that. As it is, your first run will end anticlimactically but the good news is that now you can play the second run, where you can get the satisfying ending you deserve!

The game play is probably the most refined, polished and downright well designed survival horror game play I have seen thus far. It is Resident Evil 7 but even further refined. They continue on their tradition of "learning by doing" and you will undoubtedly stumble through your first play-through only to realize the second and third time around that there are a million (slight hyperbole) tactics that you can use. Figuring out all the tricks to conserve ammo and get past enemies is part of the joy of playing the game so I won't spoil any. This game will get tricky at times if you play on hardcore. But again, this all depends on your experience. I have played the game about 20 times now and am a terminator that never gets scratched when at the beginning I was crying and eating green herbs in the corner. This game frames you in your journey from a hopeless victim to battle-hardened survivor perfectly. Tomb Raider 2013 tried this but didn't even come close. This game does. And so much more.

Graphics and sound are probably some of the best you'll see in the current gaming sphere. All the necessities are there. The only place where you sometimes see through the veil is in regards to the texture quality. Even maxed out, some textures look like they could've used a bit more love. This is, just as in RE7, beautifully hidden through clever lighting placement though. On top of that, the game offers various AO options such as SSAO and HBAO. The HBAO implementation is very good and well optimized, SSAO will not have a big impact on performance but obviously also not look as good. In terms of anti-aliasing the game offers SMAA, TAA and (shudders) FXAA+TAA. For the love of all that is holy, don't use FXAA+TAA. It will make your game a blurfest. TAA alone makes the game blurry as hell but I recommend using it nonetheless and using Reshade to sharpen the image after the fact. SMAA alone just doesn't do the job for this game. Especially since the hairs will become a pixelated mess without anti-aliasing. The other options are self explanatory. What I do have to note is that the game is INCREDIBLY well optimized. We are talking 100+ fps with all settings maxed out here. That is an achievement in and of itself even if I have a good graphics card. There are no frame dips. Nothing. This game runs like butter. And it's glorious.

TL;DR: The game is pretty. And well optimized. Use TAA and Reshade to sharpen.
