In what seems like another lifetime, a relative of mine brought over a Playstation 1 game for me to play called "Resident Evil 2". I don't remember much about how that went except for a few small details: That it was really hard and I did not get very far, there were all sorts of gross creatures, and... it scared the hell out of me. Like nightmare-inducing scary. Ok, I was around 10 years old at the time, but still. It was "the scary game" that kept me away from others like it until I got older and was gradually eased into them by the likes of Half-Life and Silent Hill 1.

So all these years later... and Resident Evil 2 gets a remake around 20 years after I first encountered it. I had some curiosity about it, but then the demo came out and I got to try this out. The result was one of the very rare cases where I opted to pre-order a game, which I normally only do when I am pretty much certain a game would be good.

And this time it was very much worth it.

Despite my past experience, I didn't actually remember much about this game other than images of burning cars, monsters who ate me, and the awful sounds they would make. All of that is very much here, and enhanced with all the visual and gameplay improvements that have come since then. This game's visuals and sound are... well, gorgeous isn't quite the right word for it. I'll just say that it is [i]very[/i] good. It is rare for me to point out how good a game looks, but this one deserves it.

I did play the remaster of RE1 on Steam prior to this game's release, to get some backstory and a feel for the sort of gameplay that I would be likely to see. RE2 is very similar to how that first game played, but with all the benefits of modern technology and good controls. There are puzzles to solve, places to explore, and lots of enemies that will tear you apart if you are not careful. You largely explore the city police station and a few nearby areas. Also a big sewer that... well, I certainly would not want to be anywhere near that. Especially not the things living in it. x_x

The storytelling and characters are relatively straightforward, but it is presented quite nicely. You have lots of in-game cinematics, as well as lots of notes about the world and what led to the events of the game. It is all very well fleshed out, and further adds to the atmosphere created by the sound and visuals. I opted to play as Claire first, and then did Leon in the second playthrough, but I very much plan on playing the opposite as well just to see the differences. There is plenty of overlap in the areas you explore, but the different perspectives and how differently things played out kept things interesting. Beyond that, someone mentioned some Tofu thing I haven't seen yet. Sounds rather silly. :o

There is one minor gameplay nitpick that I have. There seemed to have been a real imbalance between the degree of ammo scarcity I faced in my two playthroughs. What I mean is that while ammo was always an issue that kept me from just wasting everything in my path, it was [i]far[/i] more serious during my second playthrough as Leon. I know it was like that to keep the tension up, but I was genuinely worried more than once that I would not have enough ammo to be able to finish the game. I ended more than one boss fight with ammo levels in the single digits... eek. By comparison, Claire had a sizeable amount of ammo to spare at the end, and only really had shortages at the very beginning. This might have been intentional design, but if I had been completely unable to continue because of a lack of ammo I probably would be pretty upset. It got REALLY close there. :o

But... I think i've typed enough. At the end of the day, there is only one thing you need to know about this new version of Resident Evil 2. It is something I can sum up in two words: It's excellent. Certainly the best game I have played since Yakuza 0 last summer. If you like survival horror or just really good games, then this is one you will want to check out.

This is the first Resident Evil game I've bought and the first AAA game I've bought full price on Steam in ages and I'm so disappointed right now.

I've seen let's plays of Resident Evil 1, 4 and 7. With RE7 I regretted not buying the game myself because the action looked fun, the puzzles were varied and interesting and the boss fights looked cool. RE1 was just too old to enjoy for me by the time I watched it, but what struck me about that game was that it looked more focused on the puzzles and less so on the action. And the puzzles looked just as good as in RE7, if not better. I love puzzle games so both these games look like they would please me for this reason alone. RE4 even though it was a lot more action focused looked overall really cool to me with its many weapons, upgrades, enemies, bosses, locations and solid (for its time) shooter mechanics, but it was also too old by the time I watched it.

Cue the extremely hyped, extremely good looking RE2 remake. The best game in the series they say, and this must be true, why else would they remake this particular one? Surely this is my time to try the series out. If it's better than 1, 4 and 7 then there must be a lot in this game for me to enjoy. I try the 1-shot demo and it teases me with seemingly intricate puzzles and amazing zombie/shooting mechanics. I'm sold, I buy the game.

And then the game is over. Wtf? 7 hours long. Exploring everything, seemingly discovering every secret, and still it ends in 7 hours. I could probably have done it in 4 hours if I didn't go after every secret. I honestly didn't realize there were AAA games this short. Usually my problem with AAA games is that they are too long. But even worse than that the gameplay in those 7 hours was mediocre at best and most of the time is spent going back and fourth in the same levels. The puzzles teased in the demo you're given the solution to immediately, no need to think. The rest of the puzzles involve matching colored keys to colored locks or square shaped pegs to square shaped holes. And the only good thing about the shooting is the zombies. All the other enemies feel rushed and boring in comparison. You can't shoot their limbs, they don't even have ragdolls, they just die in the same way no matter how you kill them. Not to mention how few of them there are. There's only like 5 enemy types and less than 10 of each of them excluding the zombies. And there are no proper boss fights in the entire game, you're just fighting the same "bosses" over and over which would barely be considered a difficult or notable enemy in similar games. In fact the game just progressively gets worse in my opinion.

I realize now that the game wants me to play it again slightly differently multiple times. I probably have to try that to see if it's in any way worth it, but how can it be any less mediocre? And multiple playthroughs is in no way a justification for a short game length. When a game like this is too short it makes the things you do while playing it feel even less worthwhile. All the items you've gathered and didn't use because you saved them for when the tougher enemies or bosses would show up, worthless, the gun upgrades you found just before the game ended, worthless. This game was so short that I barely got to use 2 out of the 4... (lol) weapons in the game.

And worst of all it wasn't until right before the end that I realized I had been tricked. I'm usually able to tell within the 2 hour refund window if a game is for me or not, but everything I thought I knew about gaming and the Resident Evil series (from watching the aforementioned games) and also what the game made me feel when playing it led me to believe there was still a lot left. I had only faced a very limited selection of enemies, my weapons and items were basic and some of them I had just found or found the upgrades to, I had only faced trivial puzzles, everything led me to believe the game would truly get going soon, and then it just ended. 

This game needed more of everything in my opinion, it needed more enemies, more enemy variety, more bosses, more horror (the main antagonist is a tall blue dude wearing a trenchcoat and hat, lol), more locations, more varied locations, more weapons, more items, more upgrades, more puzzles, more story, more actual length.

I'm honestly so surprised right now. I can't for the life of me understand how my opinion can differ this much from seemingly everyone else. From the looks of it there are far better games in the Resident Evil series than this one, not to mention games like Dead Space just blow this one out of the water in every regard.

Lastly, to add some positivity to the review I'll say that everything that the 1-shot demo shows you is fantastic. The graphics in this game are fantastic, the sound is fantastic, the atmosphere is fantastic, the zombies look and feel fantastic, shooting them feels fantastic, and it both plays and feels like a proper PC-game in terms of how it runs and the settings you can tweak. Shooting the zombies is fun enough that I'll probably mess around with cheats doing that for a bit, and maybe I can hope for some mods or more content from the developer down the line as well. A horde game mode would be awesome in this game.

Edit: After playing through the second campaign, I decided to revise my views slightly, and *tentatively* recommend it. I still believe most of the issues I comment on are present, but I have had a bit more fun with the game lately. I think the 2nd scenario (at least for Claire) has almost the opposite problems (the grenade launcher not only stuns lickers, for example, but pretty much kills them in two shots, top), and the final boss tends to be bullet-spongey (although I must say, I was swimming in ammo, so it's not a big problem), but it's overall a better experience.

The script is much better for the 2nd scenario. There are some truly tone-deaf moments in Leon A, while Claire B manages to be more touching than the original RE2, IMO, and the issues with it are minor. The arsenal you have is much more varied, offering better options/tactics to deal with the enemies. I guess my final comment on the game would be that it's truly a game of highs and lows.

Below this point is my original review, which touches on some of the negatives (it's already fairly long, so not everything is listed), and goes into more detail for some of the combat mechanics I feel were poorly designed.


[h1]Rarely fun, but never scary or great[/h1]

RE:2 is a game that mixes two concepts with very mixed results. You get the old ammo management, puzzle solving (if a bit gimped), and map exploration of the old games with incredibly resiliant, stubborn enemies, from more modern horrors (in these games, they are often immortal, here they are just incredibly tough/damaging). This results in unsatisfying fights, no sense of progression (you'll rarely get to enjoy a room free of zombies after you carefully dealt with them), and worst of all, no fear or tension (when the game so constantly puts you in danger, fear gives way to annoyance, and frustration if things go wrong).

A game where kneecapping zombies and finishing them off with the knife is more efficient than planting a few bullets in their head makes for a very formulaic approach to combat. Most enemies will not recoil/get stunned often enough to do anything but either force you to retreat/walk around them, or kneecap them as mentioned.

Lickers will only get stunned if they are stupid enough to jump at you straight ahead (which means you can hit them mid-jump), otherwise, you are forced into tedious moments like use a stun grenade, pop two shots, retreat into another room and then repeat (or use the window of opportunity to run past, but then what are you going to do on the way back?), stealth which doesn't work (most of the times, there is no room to avoid aggroing them) or go for an hail mary and attack hoping they won't use their good attacks, or that they won't attack from a tough angle (the shotgun will hold only 4 shots for a good chunk of the game, which often aren't enough to kill a licker).

Expect to exploit the AI pathing a lot, if you want to play without being hit/bitten every 2 steps (which you want, because zombies take around 1/3 of your health in one hit). Maneuvering around zombies is often not an option, as they lunge from very far, are fast, and grab you from miles away, running away from lickers is deadly, if they don't spaz out and jump in the wrong direction, so you can only abuse their pathing to get past them (or the few rooms that do have enough pathways). Since zombies can follow you, you can also end up being bitten leaving a room, no matter what you do. Either you open the door carefully or not, the zombie camping the door will inevitably grab you, and since that damn zed didn't start banging on the door, you didn't even know it was there, because sometimes the zombies are also silent! Enjoy.

Dogs are annoying as hell (small, fast, can get stuck below you where you can't shoot them, can lunge at you through the door to keep you from exploiting the fact that they can't walk through doors), and bosses are bullet sponges. One of them is a puzzle fight, without any indication that it is one, which means reloading because you wasted all your ammo (the arena where the puzzle takes place is really far and not visible from where the fight starts, so there is no reason to think you can't win in a fair fight). I will say, however, that one or two boss fights are at least interesting, having weak points to target, which fit the shooting mechanics.

The original RE2 was perhaps a bit too easy, but this game is too punishing (not necessarily difficult, just really set on making you miserable for any mistake you make, and trying as hard as it can to force said mistakes). You can still learn it (after the first playthrough, the game is way easy), but it remains a very unsatisfying experience even when you know how to approach it, because the approach itself is pretty much "play it like a bad 3rd person shooter".

Music is too sparse (if you bought the pack to have the original music in the game, use it, because there is more of it in general, and helps the atmosphere a great deal), visuals are really good (on my humble 1050 ti, it looks gorgeous) and it seems to control mostly fine on an xbox one controller (some issues with how shooting works since the shots seem to work as if you were in first person, meaning that if your gun is clearly lined up with the monster, but your crosshair isn't, you'll miss, which means in really close range, or when close to corners, you might miss seemingly unmissable shots).

It's a pity, because it feels like a lot of care was put in the game, but it's a lackluster experience. Maybe the easy setting could make this more enjoyable? That's probably going to be my last attempt, but having finished Leon's campaign twice already (and having taken a quick look at the 2nd scenario with Claire), I feel like this isn't something I should recommend, and that this is something I won't play again (I spent some time experimenting with the game and saving/reloading, so the playtime is fairly high, but a reasonable first playthrough of Leon's campaign shouldn't take more than 6-7 hours, and 4 hours for a second run without cutscenes but at a leisure pace).

So it is finally here and it is all you could wish for but...

Gameplay is appropriately tuned, they seem to have hit a sweet spot between modern mechanics and old school tanky controls. I would say they made the right choice to go with an over the shoulder view as well as this adds tension and gives more of a panicky feel whenever you get grabbed by a zombie for example.

I definitely appreciate all the little details they incorporated like being able to retrieve your knife from a zombie as well as being able to use defense weapons as normal weapons as well, it is a huge upgrade over the original remake defense system just to mention an example of how much thought went into making the gameplay enjoyable. These things are hard to get right.

The graphics are as always the best you will find and level design is amazing. The attention to detail is out of this world and setting a new bar for all other developers with things like dead body collision. No longer will dead bodies magically merge together but instead they fall on top of each other giving you that much more of a realistic feel to everything happening. Heck zombies will even trip over dead bodies, now if that isn't attention to detail then I don't know what is.

Now Capcom said even though this is a remake they treated this as an entirely new game but nevertheless don't think that this means they forgot about the original as tiny things and major story events happen just as you would expect them to and I for one as a fan know how to appreciate that. Without spoiling anything you will recognize a lot of the scenes from the original RE2 albeit they might happen at a different time. As for the tiny things that you would recognize like [spoiler]the first licker running across the window at the start and zombie hands reaching through windows[/spoiler], these will mostly happen during a "2nd run" aka B scenario. They did not include this in the first playthrough to keep things fresh and new and that makes sense but you certainly can appreciate these things during a 2nd playthrough.

Speaking of the second scenario now this is where things start to get seriously grim. The campaign is definitely not as long as it used to be in the original (even if you explore every inch) and I was willing to ignore this if the second scenario would be an actual new scenario as you would then count both of them together in terms of campaign time then but I can't get myself to do that.
From the get-go you feel awkward as the game automatically takes you to the RPD but hey it is a new area so you shake it off until you find out that after this one new area you basically get back to following the same steps as you did during your first playthrough. There are a couple of different areas to explore but nothing fits together with the timeline of the first campaign. None of the items you took during the first playthrough are used, [spoiler]Marvin turns early[/spoiler] and where the hell did the item box from the main hall go? Did Mr. X carry it outside or something? You can tell they added some new areas and a couple different bosses but for the majority of the game both characters fight the exact same bosses in the same area at the same time. The two scenarios just can't happen in the same universe so basically you can't even make out what the canon flow of events in this game is.

And this is where you realise Capcom got lazy with the game, the 2nd scenario is for about 80% the same thing as the 1st scenario. Don't get me wrong, gameplaywise it is something different but I would call this more like an enhanced "Arrange mode" from the classic games than an entirely different scenario. There simply isn't enough content to justify being so lazy with the second campaign in a story-driven game like this.

All in all I love the game, it is a perfect remake as long as you don't look at the second campaign and contentwise there is a free new mode coming called "The Ghost Survivors" so that should help the value proposition but the fan in me can't help but be somewhat disappointed that they did not give the second campaign the treatment it deserved

I liked this game, played it 15.5 hours apparently within the 1st weekend. 
I played Leon A and Claire B and tried 4th survivor 2 times, not beat it yet. 


STORY:

Character relations feel unbelievable, going from hello to OMG EMOTIONAL YOU ARE MY LIFE!

The story characters don't spend enough time with each other, while most of the time spent in the game you are playing (which is a good thing) I feel like characters should spend a little more time with each other. 

Overall emotional beats just come out of nowhere and feel flat. RE7 feels a lot more believable. 

MINOR SPOILERS: 
Leon and Claire meet at the start and never again till the end. They don't even help each other fight the boss. Claire sees Leon on a tv screen during a self destruct sequence and doesn't even wait a second to see if Leon can get on the train and escape with her lol. 
MINOR SPOILERS END: 

LOCATIONS: 
The new location is under developed, it's just sort of there and gone. 
It's like about 4 rooms and no puzzles. 

There's a sewer level... yea it's the worst part. I wanted to explore more of the city and environments similar to the police station. RE1 and it's remake got it right i think, there is just something about a good old haunted mansion/ police station in a horror game. 

GAME PLAY:
It's quite funny how lickers and dogs cant open doors and seem to reset themselves every time the door shuts. So you can head shot a licker through the doorway, wait for it to go back and open the door again and repeat. But that whole deaf thing? You either have to waste something to deafen them or kill them, there is no sneaking past them. 

Tyrant is tense as he follows you around the police station, but also seems to go back and forth for a long time making him annoying as you just hide and wait for ages. 
He isn't like Jack from RE7 who wanders the entire house, but he is like Jack where you sort of know when the game has decided he should leave for a while. 
He also isn't like the alien from isolation who is actually programmed to stalk or leave u alone at the right time. 
They simply gave him a pretty dumb patrolling AI and put him in the map and then take him out when u have triggered a story moment. 

I do miss silly unlockable cheat modes. 

SCARE:
This game is not as scary as how RE7 starts, without ammo and JACK stalking you it's just super tense. This game has some moments like that. After playing a while you will begin to understand how the game is programmed and will feel more at ease. There aren't any game play surprises. Like all previous RE games, the game is built on certain rules. 
RE games have never been super scary for me except the start of RE7 and RE1 remake, but if I was to rank the most scary RE games, RE7, RE1 remake, RE2 remake, Revalations 1 and 2, maybe Code Veronica. Again, all RE games seem to loose the scare factor after the start, but the top 3 do keep the tension. 

GRAPHICS: 
Overall awesome, I had textures set to high but I still encountered blurry floors or police cars. Also some odd reflective surfaces, due to reflection resolution i guess, looked like moving black mould on some wooden beams. 

Oh and the low frame rate of zombies a little far away is distracting... in a charming way? Like haha looks like an old game. 


OVERALL:
I bought the Deluxe game after all the good reviews and free DLC announcements, this game is worth it and Capcom defo needs to be sent a message that RE7 and this RE2 remake is the right step forward, unlike the DLC and microtranscations mess that is Street Fighter V. More games like this please.

[h1]All of the atmosphere. None of the scare[/h1]
[i]It's Resident Evil 2. So we don't care![/i]

[h1]Disclaimer[/h1]

We are walking into [b]HEAVY[/b] fan crowds here and I hope not to annoy anyone with this review. Comments are open and i am willing to discuss my thoughts in greater detail below with anyone who wishes point out any issues or flaws witht his review.
Though I am going to bag on this game (heavily) understand that it comes from a place of love and frankly if you see more bagging than praising... understand last time I played this game I was 8.. im 24 now.

[h1]Specs[/h1]

Lets begin a review like we always do - Specs.

    [tr]
        [th]CPU[/th]
        [th]GPU[/th]
        [th]RAM[/th]
    [/tr]
    [tr]
        [td]i7-7700k[/td]

[/table]

I ran a respectable amount of things on low and medium to begin with, not because my PC can't handle it but because when streaming (and overall gaming) i try to keep my framerate at about 120fps. 60fps on a 144hz monitor looks juttery and clunky. Now onto a more presseing matter: [b]Variable Frame Rate[/b]. Even though I had Vsync turned off I felt like the engine was capped at 60fps. Turns out I didn't turn on Variable Frame rate and in turn it hardlocked my game to 60fps until I turned it on. Don't do a me kids.

[h1]Performance[/h1]

This is one [i]smoooth[/i] game. There were times where I dipped below 120 during specific parts of the game. These were not big action set pieces but compared to the prior pace of the game until then, one can be forgiven if an explosion drops you to 100fps whilst staring at it.

In my time with this game haven completed both the "A Scenario" for Leon and Claire I can say I had [b]ONE[/b] tiny little softlock crash. Honestly was not a big deal. After that the game ran smooth again.

[h1]Story[/h1]

So starting off with the "canon" intro in the the most simple way possible:
Rookie cop is due to start his new job in the Racoon City Police Dept. when he recieves - what can only be assumed is a call from Police Chief Brian Irons - telling him not to come to the city. Leon - in all his wisdom - decides to come to the city anyway and said he'd "bring help". He came alone (initially). After a run in at a gas station and meeting Claire (A college student looking for her Brother Chris Redfield). Both head into the city looking for answers and meet a legion of the undead. After being seperated due to a car crash both (somehow seperately) make their way to the police station. In the police station they must then find a way out meanwhile solving cryptic puzzles and dodging the undead to make their way to the Umberella Secret Lab underneath the city in order to find the cause of the outbreak and escape the city.
[i]Side Note[/i]
Both stories (though 80% similar) take place at the exact same time. Even some cutscenes are just moving people to the other end of a fence. How can 2 people be in the police station doing essentially the same thing and never actually meet.. and how to puzzles remain unsolved.

[h1]Gameplay[/h1]

I hope you're ready for this, this may well be a foreign concept in 2019.. this game include... Backtracking. Lots of it. I will be blunt with you and say that to save time it's best you keep a pen and paper next to you to solve puzzles and remember info. This is the easiest way as you wont be running through menus looking for that 1 "note" with the combination to the safe. Now.. puzzles, It took me about 8 hours to finish Leon - "Scenario A"... im 3 hours into "Claire - Scenario A". Literally [b]NOTHING[/b] as changed. The safe combinations are the same, the locker codes are the same, item placement is the same (if you are doing the same puzzle). Overall this is a wonderful remake, faithful to the original Resident Evil 2 while adding in modern gameplay and game design. Running around in the police station while trying to evade zombies and conserve ammo feels great, just like back in the day. I will say that I'm a bit iffy on certain game decisions, which I'll explain below (minor spoilers ahead!), however overall the gameplay has been changed for the better. Enemies are now a lot more tough, and require much more ammo to effectively kill. Good luck trying to take down a Licker with anything less than a shotgun or grenade launcher now! Also, zombies don't always stay dead, sometimes they get back up several times, which means that shooting to stun-and-run is encouraged, and shooting to kill is discouraged. It can lead to situations like my current playthrough where I only have 2 bullets in my pistol and no more shotgun ammo, and I'm being aggressively pursued by a rather nasty monster, but I digress. Capcom has managed to create a great 3rd person shooter while retaining the survival horror elements, and while I dislike some things, overall RE2 Remake is a solid purchase.

What I don't like (minor spoilers!):
When you reach a certain part in the game, you're pursued by the Tyrant monster (Mr. X as he's colloquially known) relentlessly for a time. In the original Playstation 1 game, whenever he appeared (always at specific scripted locations), you could simply exit the room or just kill him (not that he would stay dead, Tyrant would always reappear later when the script called for it). In the new RE2, after you reach a certain point, this jerk shows up and just keeps chasing you around. You can't kill him now, shooting him enough times only stuns him momentarily (he is a bullet sponge and it's well advised to save your ammo). Your only recourse is to run, run, and run some more. If you can manage to lose the Tyrant (as in get out of sight), you can evade him by not making any noise (running, shooting a gun, slamming doors, etc). The only problem is that there are zombies and lickers around, so not firing your gun or running is actually very difficult. Combine that with the fact that the only way to accomplish some objectives is by interacting with certain highly noisy objects in the environment which attracts the Tyrant to your location, and you have a rather annoying scenario of cat-and-mouse that stops being scary and is more a chore/bore than anything. Seriously, having to lose the Tyrant for the umpteenth time because you're trying to align super noisy bookshelves inside the library in order to reach a room with the special McGuffin you need to advance the game got old very quick. I get that in RE3 Nemesis you were constantly pursued by Nemesis, however in RE2 Remake it just feels more annoying than anything.

Possibily one of the best Resident Evils I have played in a long time, it captures the magic of what made the series so great in the first place, plus the enemies have been updated to be even scarier and more menacing than before.  Give it a shot if your a fan of the series, or want to go on a nostilga trip down memory lane.  Highly reccomand the classic track dlc though since it has some good music from the original game that gives you goosebumps down your spine if you played RE2 back when it first came out, but the choice is yours to make :).  Hope this review made it more helpful on your decision on getting this game!

Okay, slightly longer version? In 2018/2019, we aren't getting games this good, this polished, this packed with content, this faithfully created for fans, this fresh to survival horror, this fun as its own game for newcomers, and this replayable anymore.

Where most of the Triple-A market has grown stagnant with same-y Early Access retail releases littered with microtransactions and loot boxes, and survival horror being relegated to over-the-top co-op action leaving Indie developers to create new horror gems, this game is an honest-to-goodness breath of fresh air of quality that lovingly recreates the source material and one-ups it with modern standards crafted by years and years of experimental horror games.

The visuals are jaw-dropping. The art direction is evocative and bone-chilling. The new touches added to the game are pleasant surprises, especially some of the re-writes. The story is still cheesy as ever but it's fun and pulpy, much like the 90's when this game was made and is based. The locations are dense and full of detail, even full of little easter eggs if you pay close enough attention. The puzzles are great reprieves that tease the brain along with how your brain is crunched, bruised, massaged, and working at full capacity during combat, item management, and learning layouts of the levels. There's a palpable sense of risk-reward throughout the whole experience, where every step toward danger gets you a new weapon, new items, a safe room, a puzzle to take a breather, a clue to solving the greater mystery, an easter egg that pays homage to the fans and rest of the series.

I'm hesitant to go into any concrete detail because the experience is just that damn good and you need to experience it for yourself. If you love classic Resident Evil or new-school Resident Evil, you will love this game. If you love old-school survival horror, you will love this game. If you love bunches of (replayable) content, you'll love this game. If you love challenging games whether they be for speedruns or chasing the hardest of achievements, you'll love this game. If you love great, well-designed, well-structured, and well-paced games, you'll love Resident Evil 2 (Remake).

If Resident Evil 7 was an apology letter to fans, this one is a love letter.

Purchase posthaste.

Okay, two days in, and I've already sunk nearly 8hrs into this game. I have been waiting for this remake for a long while. I typically NEVER pre-order games (Would you believe that my last pre-order was also an RE game? Revelations to be exact 8D), but this was a case in which I felt it was worth the risk and am glad I did.
Resident Evil 2 introduced us to two staple characters: Leon Kennedy, the rookie cop who became a badass when the chips were down on his very first day, and Claire Redfield, the equally badass college sister of veteran Chris Redfield. Young and inexperienced, they had to fight their way through the nightmare of a city gone to hell quite literally. It was a masterpiece, and honestly probably my absolute favorite of the original ps1 era RE games.

So the question remains....how does THIS remake hold up?

As of the time of this review, I am most of the way through Leon's first scenario. I may edit this review later, but I'm currently unable to contain myself :P So how's that?
As far as the game looks...it looks AMAZING. It is astounding how realistic everything looks and how the RPD and everywhere else was built so that not only are we revisiting locations we know and love, but are also experiencing them for the first time as well. By that, I mean that the world is much bigger than it was before, more realistically built, and revamped so that while you will recognize places from the original, things are still different than they were before. As for the characters, they look about as one would expect. The only major difference I feel is that Leon himself looks younger than before, which honestly fits with the premise of a kid cop who just finished the academy and is both too youthful and idealistic for the nightmare that awaits. Maybe that's just me, but I think the look fits him really well.
Gameplay...now THAT'S a whole new ballgame. Resident Evil 2 constantly threw ammo at you in large quantities, enough so that it actually was feasible that you could just about destroy every T-Virus/G-Virus spawn you ran across and still have a bit of ammo to spare.
Attempting this game with that kind of attitude will result in you being a bloody mess on the floor....
Yes, this game actually follows RE1's original premise regarding combat; fighting back against monsters requires you to be VERY careful about how you handle it. Ammo is far more scarce, and while you can craft some by simple means of finding gunpowder, you will still burn through it quick if you attempt to fight every creature you see. As a result, you will have to pick and choose your battles. For those who feel that Resident Evil as a series has grown more action-y and not very survival horror-y will find that it has returned to that root with this game. Be smart, find safe routes to take, and conserve ammo, or you WILL die. And conserve you must, as gone are the days where a pool of blood on the floor told you that a creature was dead. Something is only dead when it ceases to move and doesn't move after return trips. One would think that the zombies are attempting to fake you out at this point, leaving you feeling you're safe when they fell over and yet getting back up 20min later when you thought you cleared them out. Perhaps an exaggeration but point being: treat every corpse as though it's gonna get back up and don't let your guard down. 
Okay, I'm praising this a lot, so are there any BAD things about it? Sure. Every game has a flaw of some kind. The acting can be a little iffy with me. Despite Leon's youth and all, he seems a tiny bit flat when facing everything. Sometimes he gives a yell of surprise, but most of the time one would think this is an everyday thing for the rookie cop. Also for as tense as the game gets, I don't really feel like it's ever exactly "scary". I could simply be too numb to that feeling of terror by now, but aside from the occasional scare here and there, never did the game really get me to a point that I was utterly frightened, so you may find this to be a let-down if you're looking for the "thrills-&-chills" type gameplay. The Tyrant, or Mr X as many of us would call him, now becomes more of a stalker, haunting the RPD and actively looking for you from room to room. This was the closest to terror I felt, but given that it was TOO easy to catch his attention and him hunt me down, too many times I felt I was being chased away from my objective, desperately searching for a route to get him off my tail long enough so I could do what I had set out to. It's scary to start, but quickly can become obnoxious.

Again, I'm not finished with the game. I may edit this review later or something once I complete Leon's story and challenge the second story or Claire's storylines. The game does have some downfalls with slightly sub-par acting, a rather steep difficulty curve compared to the original, and a few nuances that can come off as annoying. But in the end, this is everything I could ever hope for in a remake. If you're on the fence about it, I will say that in my opinion you should get this game. It's true survival at its finest, has the nostalgia that makes me smile, and has plenty of new secrets and such to discover.

Shadows high
Shadow Cache On
Textures high (2GB, even though this is an 8GB GPU)

First thing's first: this game is not a remake. That's an outright lie. It's nowhere near the level of an upgrade that, say, the Gamecube RE1 was over the PS1 version, and this game is like three time shorter than the original RE2. It'd be more accurate to call it a reimagining with better grahpics. 

Anyway, onto the review. 

I suppose I'll get crucified for this, but I'll just lay it out on the table now: I've never thought highly of the Resident Evil series. 

That is, I never thought highly of the first three Resident Evil games and its spinoffs, thinking they were mostly exercises in frustration with a laughable plot and the worst controls a human mind could conjure. I never, not for a second, bought the argument that bad tank controls made the games more scary, because I think bad controls are inexcusable in almost every circumstance. 

I *loved* Resident Evil 4, mostly because its much better gameplay and large departure from the convoluted mess of the first three games, and so it was to my disappointment to see all the lessons from 4 squandered with RE5 and 6. 

So now Resident Evil 2 has returned to us twenty years later, and after playing this remake for a bit, I've come to the conclusion that my distaste for the early RE games was justified. Even with modern technology and a third-person perspective, this remake can't hide how flawed the Resident Evil series was before 4, and in some areas seems to have even taken a few steps back. 

I suppose I should start with how much the game likes to throw toolbooths in front of you. These aren't toolbooths where you pay money, but ones where you are forced to cough up weapons or health. This happens any time you encoutner any zombie, and although the game likes to make a song and dance about how you're supposed to avoid them, many times this is simply not an option. Zombies can lunge at a huge distance, and the often cramped corridors where they pop up often means there's no way around them other than killing them, or letting them grab you so you can knock them down. I don't know how they made it *harder* to avoid zombies even with the loss of the fixed camera and the tank controls. 

A lot of times, running isn't even an option, especially when you run into stuff like the infected dogs or the Lickers. Those times you *have* to fight, because while the controls are somewhat tolerable now, Leon and Claire both run at about the same pace I do walking to the kitchen. 

And this leads into my second problem: in this remake, the knife is a limited-use item. It basically combines the self-defense weapons from the old gamecube RE1 remake, where you could stab zombies with special knives you found. The problem is those knives were seperate from your actual knife, which you could use even if you run out of ammo.

You know what happens if you run out of ammo here? Game over. You just wasted however many hours got you to that point. You don't have a knife to fall back on, and even if you do, it'll break after using it for an absurdly short amount of time. It's not even that useful, having a shorter range than a zombie's lunge, so you can't even really use it in an offensive capacity. 

Playing this remake also made me remember how much I loathed the inventory system, where a herb and a shotgun take up the same amount of space. I hate having to come back to the RE4 well, but that game did it so much better, where you had limited space, but items all had a different size and took up a different amount of space. Hell, I think in RE4 if you found a health item but your inventory was full, you could still use it, but in this game you can't for some baffling reason. 

I think that's the reason RE4 was so popular and so enduring even now; RE1-3 were just plain bad, and when the fans played an actually good game with its name, everyone was enraptured. 

Enemies are also way too bullet-spongey. This goes back to the toolbooth problem. It's not enough to even headshot a zombie anymore, now you have to do it about 5 or 6 times before they actually go down. A zombie going down quickly from a headshot isn't a reward anymore, it's a damn requirement, because otherwise you're going to expend half your ammo on one enemy. 

So that's my opinion. The Resident Evil 2 remake is a valiant, but ultimately doomed effort to fix what was fundamentally broken. The game isn't scary by any real metric, just frustrating, just like it was in 1998.

I've been a huge fan of the RE series as a hole, I have pretty much all of them par Suvivor on the PS1 and some odd ones here and there. Most of the negative reviews I have seen on here complain about the difficulty of the game.


Now growing up and playing Resident Evil 2 and knowing where to go and what to do, it made the game a cake walk. You chould seriously end the game with over 40 shotgun shells as Leon if you knew what you were doing. Saving ammo by only using custom parts and stuff when you run out of ammo so that you get a free reload essentially. This game is different. No tank controlls, no fixed camera angles and the like. The zombies are tough, yes I admit it is unfair at times but there are ways around it. People think that you have to kill EVERYTHING you come across which just isn't true. The first time I played this game I found it hard and challenging when I played through as Leon but as I played I started to find out some things that made the game easier for myself. Shooting to kill is a only a good option if you NEED to go back into the room. If it looks like it's an important room, usually a good time to kill as much as you can and barricade any windows you see to stop Zombies entering. I do not understand why people are saying that headshots should do more damage when it already has a chance to instantly kill, a chance to stagger and if you follow up with another shot you can just walk right over them. 

The Story seems to be somewhat similiar than the original in the sense that you are still after the G-Virus (L) or the Antivirus (C) for Sherry. Which is good IMO Some characters get more screen time and the like and for people saying that people like Kendo didn't get enough screen time? Well people should really check up on the FREE DLC that is coming out in 3 episodes, one to do with Kendo, One to do with Chief Irons' wife and the other to do with an un-named USS operative, like hunk in a sense.

Another problem that people seem to have with the REmake is that there isn't a 'B' scenario. Yes, this is true, they removed them for something a lot better to be honest. If you want the TRUE ending of the game, the one that is the same as RE2 on the PS1/Gamecube you have to WORK for it, you have to put the time and the effort in to get it. The game ends on a cliff hanger for a reason. Whilst it is a shame that there isn't really any 'b' scenario, look at the RE2, sorry to say but, Leon A and Claire A follow the same sort of deal and the only changes the B scenario's make to it is that Mr X is in some points and you go to different areas, it really didn't change too much.


Mr X in this game however, is a double edged sword, whilst on the one hand you have a tense chase that lasts throught the police station, the problem with that is that he is unkillable. You can knock him down and go on about your day but you can not put him down forever. This is both a good and a bad thing. IT means you need to act FAST. Think on your toes, puts you in the character's shoes and what THEY are going though. They have some monster chasing them that won't quit, if that was you, you'd probably want to get away from him ASAP. Hearing his footsteps across the Police Station or if he is above you? Well, you best watch out and get ready to listen carefully, else you might find yourself getting punched a lot. He's not that hard to dodge if you know how he works and it's really not hard to figure out. Find a wide space that you can run around him, or alternatively, go back to the main hall and use the stairs to manipulate him to go to the one you don't need to be and double back on yourself. There is always two ways out of a wing when you first find X on the first playthrough.



Going back to the weapons people seem to have a problem with the shotgun as well. I personally think they are just flat out using a different weapon. Not once have I had to shoot 3-4 shots into a zombie with a shotgun to kill them or at least put them down. Again, I say this one last time. Killing zombies in this game is NOT what you should be doing unless you KNOW that you will be going back and forth a lot. The zombies in the library for instance. There is no reason to kill them at all. Lure them up the stairs, go down the ladder and then solve the 'puzzle' it's not hard. People just think that everything in this game can be solved with a few bullets, it cannot. Why waste ammo when you have enough room to move around and if you are in a tight spot for ammo, well sadly, that's your own fault for being over zelous with it. I have the game on PS4 and I had to kill the final boss as Leon with a pistol. It took a while but I managed to do it. I didn't know what I was doing at that time, like at all. But when I played through as Claire, well I knew how important ammo actually was. Gunpowder should be used when you are LOW on ammo as well, not when you have a lot of ammo as you can create 3 different types per character. Pistol Shotgun Magnum ammo for Leon or, Pistol Acid Rounds SMG rounds for Claire. In the A scenario it isn't that useful to go with Magnum ammo as the pistol Leon has and the pistol Claire gets just outshine them, not in Damage or stopping power, but in versitility and ammo conservation. I would rather should a zombie 4 times in the head and hopefully get him to fall over and then walk by than waste one precioius magnum round that might bite me in the ass. Shotgun and Acid rounds are a MUST if you are in a B scenario though. The pistols you get. The Revolver for Claire and the M19 for Leon act as your new 'pistol' creating Handgun ammo does not help as it's 45 acp that you need.


All of this knowledge is best learned in the HUNK Mode that you get after beating the game twice sadly. In that mode you REALLY learn how to save ammo as you are ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ tight on it and you NEED to shoot to down and not to kill. Zombies are not a threat if you know what you are doing. Most Zombies in this game can be lured to a corridor that gives you enough time to back up and re aim for those headshots. Lickers are...well fast for one, too fast IMO. If you so much as touch the sprint button they will be on your ass in a heartbeat. I am unsure on how they go about attacking you though. They have 3 and it just seems random. Jumping swipe, swipe or tongue. Jumping swipe has a chance to grab but I am unsure on how this works. Lickers are by far the hardest enemy to kill in the game, Pistols are useless and you should really only use a magnum/shotgun or a G'Nade Launcher to put them down. Most of the licker placements in the Remake are just downright UNFAIR at times. Take Leon's 2nd playthrough for instance, or Claires. The hallway on the left. Lickers and Zombies and it's a LONG corridor as well. I haven't gotten through that room at all without getting hit by anything. You can shoot the zombies sure, but the lickers will hear and come for your throat. Mr X is the next that you will likely encounter and well, I already talked about him. The next would be the enemies in the sewers, these aren't so much of a pain as the lickers are but they are bullet spunges and you should do whatever it takes to kill them without using that much. This gets fixed with the addition of the Flamethrower and the new improved sparkshot which is god tier. These will put those things down relatively quickly and you find them in the sewers. Dogs are unpredictable and the same old trick works, just right from left to right and they will (Hopefully) not hit you. They have two grabs, one from the front and one from the back, the back one you cannot defence your way out of. The zombies are also like this, though if a zombie grabs you on a stair case. You're taking damage no matter what, you will not be able to counter at all. 


Overall, the game is good, very good and worth the money and the time you have to put into it to understand how it works. People who play for 30 mins and give up shouldn't be playing this. AT all.

Before I get into the nitty gritty of the review, allow me to give some backstory of me and my relationship with the series as a whole.
I was brought up surrounded by Nintendo products, I started with the N64 and GameBoy Colour. I loved Nintendo, so one day when a friend brought over his PS1 with Resident Evil 2 and Resident Evil 3, I was curious because my brother and I never played anything other than our N64 and handhelds. My brother seemed to have absolutely no problem what-so-ever with playying something, at the time, very graphic and scary. Myself however, I was easily spooked. 
As some years went on, our friend gave us his PS1 along with all of his games, among them were titles like Tekken 3, Tenchu 1 and 2, Metal Gear. And of course Resident Evil 2 and 3.

Now that I was a bit older, I thought I would give Resident Evil 2 another shot. Oh how I was wrong to even try again. I wasted all of my bullets in the first few rooms alone, had no healing, and continued to die trying to get past the first Licker.
I was too scared to continue, and that is where I left it.

The next Resident Evil game I would go on to 'start' to play would be the first in the series, Resident Evil (remake) for the GameCube. I was still scared by these games, but I got through the starting rooms. Getting nowhere with the puzzles because I wasn't smart enough to them out. I gave up when I saw the Crimson Heads. They were just too scary for me.
Fast forward to 2005, and the launch of Resident Evil 4. My brother jumped for joy when this game came out, buying the special edition for the GameCube. For me, the game looked less scary, something I could actually play and finish. Ha ha, again, I was wrong. The Regenerators were just too much for me to handle, and I had to ask my brother to play through the Regenerator areas for me. I finished the game though, which filled me with joy.
As the years went on, Resident Evil 4 became my all-time favourite in the series, and I would replay it over and over.
In my opinion, 5 and 6 were trash. Only good for coop shenanigans, everything else about the game was not interesting in the slightest for me.
Resident Evil 7 was mixed for me. It looked amazing, the atmosphere and gameplay of the original games were all over it. The story was real good. But I guess the whole 'First Person' aspect just disconnected it for me. 

Seeing the remake for this title gave me joy, something to keep my eyes on. Something to get hype about. 

And I am so glad my 'Hype' was placed in a game that was received with overwhelmingly positive reviews all-round. Usually when I get hyped about a game, it always flops around it's release date. I am glad this game flourished instead of flop dead in the water.

GRAPHICS AND SOUND::

What can I say, the game looks beautiful, and runs amazing on a 970 with most settings on max. The games atmosphere has definately been improved ten-fold thanks to the graphics. Zombies and other enemies look fantastically scary. Leon and Claire both look their age thanks to the graphics. Their voice actors fit the look of the characters. The devs have gone above and beyond with the sound design for this game to make it feel like it looks. Whether it be a zombie bashing at a window or door, or Mr. X busting through a wall, the sound design is mint. 

STORY::

Resident Evil 2 Remake follows the story of the original almost beat for beat. I say almost, because there are changes that were made to cater for the remake. These changes weren't all that big, and took some of the 'campy' qualities out of the original story. 
The beginning of the story starts the same as the original, Leon and Claire meet up and drive into Raccoon City together, only to be seperated by a roadblock and the incoming collision by a truck. Whoever you chose to play as, the beginning is the same. Go through a back alley and reach the police staion (this was one of the first changes I noticed, the fact that you didn't go through the Gunshop before the staion).
For Leon, you meet up with the 'supposed' FBI agent Ada Wong, and for Claire, you meet the young Sherry Birkin on your journey. Both side characters have their own playable segment in the story just like the original game. All throughout the game you are relentlessly pursued by the monstrous Tyrant, a.k.a Mr. X. You will hear his thunderous footsteps pacing through the hallways trying to find you. Bashing open doors and looking inside to hunt you down. He even goes into 'safe' rooms. And just when you think you have lost him, he bursts through ceilings and walls right when you least expect it. Nowehere is safe with him chasing you down. 
It surprised me in a good way when I saw that Marvin felt like an actual person, and not just some guy you talk breifly to. And they gave the Gunshop owner depth as well, you find out his daughter was in the process of turning into a zombie and his wife had been killed prior. To be honest, it was awesome of the devs to put this in the game. The gunshop owner is no longer just some poor shmuck who dies at the start.

CHARACTERS::

Leon Scott Kennedy is a rookie cop with an attitude centred towards helping people in need and determination to complete his quest of stopping the outbreak and saving Raccoon City.

Claire Redfield is a motocycle enthuiest attending university as a mechanic. She learned how to defend herself from one of Chris' friends Barry Burton. Missing her older brother who now lives in Raccoon City with Barry, Claire drives into the fray to find Chris only to be met with a nightmarish outbreak of zombies.

GUNS AND SUB-WEAPONS::

The extra pistols you get from the preorder weren't very helpful in my playthrough. Since you could only find upgrades for your characters starter pistol. 
Both Leon and Claire start with their own pistol. Leon with his 3-burst pistol, the Matilda. and Claire with her Snub-nosed 9mm. Leon also gets the Shotgun, Lightning Hawk Magnum and a Flamethrower. Leon also gets to use the One-shot kill Rocket Launcher at the end. Claire also gets the SLS 60 a 5 shot 9mm pistol that can be upgraded to use .357 rounds like a sudo magnum, another 9mm Pistol the JMB Hp3, a Grenade Launcher, a Mac 10 Sub-machine Gun and the SparkShot.
Sub weapons are mainly used to counter-attack grabbing enemies, all apart from Mr. X. 
HE Grenades, Flash Grenades and Knives will be your best friends to have close if you run out of healing items trying to get through an area.
However, Knives have limited uses just like in Resident Evil 1, they break after a few uses. Grenades can be shoved into the mouths of zombies.
This not only does the original justice, but surpasses it in every which way.

[H1]Introduction:[/h1]
Resident Evil 2 – Remake is, as you can judge by its name, a remake of one of the most iconic horror games, originally released in 1998. Game manages to combine quest and survival horror parts & keeps them very well-balanced. This time Capcom decided to introduce original universe to those people who are still unfamiliar with it, by recreating whole game from scratch and moving it to a decent 3D engine. And so far it seems they made the right choice!

[h1]Storyline:[/h1]
The story takes place in 1998, when unknown virus outbreak hits Raccoon city. Virus itself has 100% death rate for every infected person. People affected by the virus turn mad and try to bite everybody, or even eat them alive. Local police force offers a shelter inside the police station but such decision creates a trap, resulting whole police station building to be besieged by the hordes of the infected. As if not enough, wounded people who found safe haven inside the building also turn zombies and start attacking everyone.

Players’ll take a look on this whole situation from the view of two common people – Leon Kennedy, an outsider police rookie, and Claire Redfield, usual girl, searching for her brother. Both campaigns are interconnected and both characters visit same places every now and then. Game also offers second runs, where some of the events, including the endings, may alternate, depending on which hero reached key places first.

Last but not least, there are 2 additional scenarios, where 2 secondary characters, USS member named Hunk and local meme, TOFU (yes, huge walking human-size piece of cheese) have to reach the extraction point. Each campaign playthrough grants players with various bonuses, such as costumes for characters, or weapon skins. Capcom also promised bringing additional low-poly models straight from original RE2 and yet another additional gamemode, called ‘The Ghost Survivors’, which would tell us what could’ve happened if some secondary characters didn’t die.

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
Gameplay itself presents us a challenging 3rd person old school survival horror, which encourages long, slow and thoughtful area exploration with careful inventory item management. There aren’t many enemies present on the map, but the ones you meet may provide you with quite some challenge. Zombies alone, while being slow and stupid, can crawl over the tables, break doors and windows, for example. Combine that with low amount of ammo and literally tons of health for each monster, and you’ll get a challenge even with such a simple enemy type. So, to put it the right way – sometimes it’s better to avoid the fight, or at least incapacite your enemy by shooting out their limbs, or else you are risking to be left armless while facing yet another pack of enemies.

Game also possesses a lot of riddles. Some of them may confuse a new player at start, but in fact they’re not too hard and usually become rather easy, once you find all the necessary items. Speaking of items – overall you can divide them on 3 main categories: 
[i]-Quest items, that need to be viewed, or placed somewhere; 
-Weaponry, which is… actual guns, weapon upgrades, ammo & powder; 
-Healing items, which include various herbs, sprays e.t.c.[/i]
Sometimes, in order to solve a riddle, or craft useful stuff, you’ll have to combine multiple things in one piece, or gather necessary information, by examining an item closely through the inventory. The last thing worth mentioning here is inventory upgrade. It happens when your character finds empty combat pouches and picks them up.

So, overall gameplay looks like this: you explore the area, while fighting, or avoiding different creatures, find out what blocks your path and solve this riddle. Then you unlock multiple doors, which connect multiple old rooms and open new pass forward. Gameplay slightly changes once (spoiler alert!) a huge immortal boss arrives. He starts hunting for your character, so you’ll have to watch your step carefully and escape as soon as he finds you. This idea, however, falls short on practice, as even though it sounds cool on paper, on practice this boss mostly annoys you. Luckily, you won’t meet him too often.

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
To put it real simple – the graphics looks amazing. You can see that by screenshots, but apart from top notch model quality, Capcom also brought high quality animations, advanced limb system, where you can shoot off various body parts of your enemies, and, of course, advanced gore system. You’ll see a lot of blood and torn off bodies and limbs, so consider that not only as appreciation, but also as a warning, in case you’re a sensitive person.

Overall, game atmosphere feels really apocalyptic, and graphics plays vital role in it – all those rotten bodies, burnt cars and broken lighting inside the building, all of it immerses the player into a cruel unforgiving world, filled with evil and despair.

[h1]The sound:[/h1]
Just the same as with graphics, the sound feels really amazing, be it calm ambient, or some distant roar of yet another zombie woken up. Perhaps, we can say that the graphics in RE2 – Remake serves as driving force of the atmosphere, but it wouldn’t have about half of that atmosphere without the sound of such quality.

[i]Now, as all important points’ve already been covered, it’s time to make some conclusions, so let’s observe good and bad points of the game overall:[/i]

[h1]PRO’s:[/h1][list]
[*][b]High replayability value:[/b]
Game features multiple campaigns which slightly vary, depending on who visited a key place first. Also additional scenarios, secrets, easter eggs and extra costumes. Oh, and different weapons for each character, of course!
[*][b]Advanced gore and limb system:[/b]
Having an ability to disable the enemy by simply dismembering body part adds up some tactical depth to a well-known old school gameplay. It’s not a revolutionary feature, indeed, but it is done on a really decent level.
[*][b]True old school horror atmosphere:[/b]
I wasn’t really scared while playing the game, but all of that attention to small details and work on enemy AI shouldn’t leave average player emotionless. Shooting your last magazine into a zombie and then seeing it stand up and still slowly walking towards you is… impressing, to say the least. Same applies to the cutscenes.[/list]

[h1]CON’s:[/h1][list]
[*][b]Minor holes in game mechanics and plot[/b]:
There are a lot of examples, really, so I’ll only go with 2 of them: Why does one boss hit takes about the same amount of damage as zombie mouth bite, filled with virus bacteria? Or the moment when Leon meets Claire but they’re separated with the locked gate. Couldn’t Claire just climb it over?
[*][b]Annoying boss at the police station[/b]:
Main issue with that guy is his incredible stupidity and slow speed. Things get really annoying, however, when you need to walk from one building wing to another, yet he just stalks you and so you have to make huge detours in order to drop him off your tail.
[*][b]Old school issues:[/b]
All those nasty things like clunky inventory, inability to discharge weapon magazine, e.t.c.
[*][b]Some changes in canon:[/b]
While some of the plot changes were valuable, it still feels awkward, because it strikes on the game lore in general.[/list]

[h1]The conclusion:[/h1]
Overall, it’s rather clear that RE2 – Remake is a really successful remake of an infamous cult classic horror game. All of the key elements and characters are present. Atmosphere feels so old yet so… qualitative. It’s one of those few AAA titles nowadays that fully deserves the money asked.

A brilliantly made remake. I was about 10 years old when I got to play the original RE2, and this is just such a nostalgia trip. But it also prestents the content/story in a fresh new way so it's not the same old game. The game was suprisingly well optimized. I experienced NO glitches at all. Other than some graphics problems with Full Screen (I have an ultra-wide monitor that doesn't seem to play nice with half the games out there), there was no problem adjusting settings and just playing the game glitch free.  The graphics are incredible. The design is excellent. The feel of gunplay and weapons is perfect. 

Cons: 
1) Bullet Sponge Enemies/Lack of ammo
2)Dodge mechanic needed for boss fights
3)Hunk/Tofu modes are too difficult to ever be enjoyable. 

Enemies are bullet sponges, and in-turn, ammo becomes a big problem. There's been plenty of times i've had to reload in boss fights to an earlier save simply because i've had to spend so much ammo on zombies/Lickers. I get that this is a learn-and-adapt kind of challenge, and that you're kind of supposed to Dark Souls it, and play differently the next time around. But for a fresh player, and for casual gamers who may just be rediscovering RE2 or any RE game, they're going to be sitting there saying "I wish the game gave more ammo" or "jees... a zombie needed 10 headshots to die?"  Especially in the case of headshots with pistols, SMG's and even the shotgun - you really should see a zombie get up after that. I get the T-Virus makes things come back to life, but it doesn't harden zombies skin to be bullet proof. This is seen in cinematics where Leon saves Claire with a single headshot to a zombie. So it feels inconsistent.  This isn't a problem for speedrunners, as they've pretty much already figured out how to dodge zombies without spending hardly any bullets. But that's not a playstyle most players want to use. My only other complaint is the lack of a dodge mechanic which is really needed in certain boss fights. As simply sprinting to the sides, or trying to cut the corner on their attack is only successful about half the time. 

The Hunk/Tofu modes, while they are obviously meant to be rage-inducing challenge modes, really do over commit and throw too much at the player. It's just not enjoyable. I'm sure some people will gladly accept the challenge, but it's mostly just frustrating.  I would have liked to see more thought put into how these characters were put into the game, aside from just putting in a rage game.

All that being said - really the game is fantastic. I think it's GOTY worthy, even with Last of Us 2 and many other serious contenders coming out this year. It was just a such a blissful experience to play this game. Genuine horror moments, jump scares, a fresh re-telling of a classic storyline.

The Good:

+Game has excellent visuals and the cut scenes are some of the best I've seen in a while

+The tone of the game is great, really ramps up the fear factor. Dark, but in a good way, you 
  feel the danger

+Great sound, again, adding to a fantastic dark environment

+Inventory management is new, and a lot less restrictive than the original. Tons of inventory 
slots as you progress

+Voice acting is well done. Even though they got rid of the original voice actors  

+No more loading screen doors! 

+Chests for storing loot is back, I've always liked that mechanic

+Runs GREAT even on semi-high graphical settings (I have a Ryzen CPU and a 1060)


The Bad (I wouldn't even call it that, but for the sake of argument):

-Some odd things happen with graphics, but I think that's because I didn't max out. Textures are iffy in spots. (EDIT: Minor settings bumps in textures fixed most of this)

-You move SLOW, but that's by design so I'm ok with it. 

-Mr. X is ANNOYING. Intimidating at first, but easily ran around after the 1st go. He chases you for a long time, up until you leave the RPD. He's chasing you while you're trying to pickup key items, that's the biggest annoyance. Once you trigger the chase, Lickers spawn in a few sections that you must go through, at the same time he's chasing you. Not really challenging to stay away from X, but there's a choice to be made here. Walk and the game takes forever to progress, or run and have X constantly locating you. Nothing good comes from taking either choice as running also alerts the Lickers that spawn. Only thing good that comes from him, is his demise. Was still hoping for Ada to back the swat van up, then hit him again.

-DLC is meh. All the guns are the same, although Wesker's is chromed and Chris' has a blue slide. They all have their strengths, but they're nothing to write home about. Minor attribute boosts such as handling and accuracy. I wouldn't say they're worth buying as the Matilda is more than good enough, plus it has attachments you can find to make it better. There's also a pistol you find in Claire's story that 100% accuracy all the time and a mag attachment, so buying the DLC pistols isn't really worth it. Not a huge fan of the costumes either, but that's subjective. I know some people love the Noire ones.

Overall, this game is great. Everything I mentioned in the bad, is more nit-picky than anything, except for Mr. X. I'm sure after a few playthroughs, my mind will change on Mr. X, but he's exactly like Nemesis was in RE3. Super annoying. He's pretty scary at first, but all that goes away after you've run into him for the 100th time. He goes from "holy **** it's Mr. X!!", to, "omg, not this annoying guy again". He's by no means "hard" to go up against, he's just more of a nuisance especially given the time he shows up. The best method is to walk, as he won't hear you, but that then makes the game very slow and it feels like you can't really play the game at that point. When he's chasing you, you can forget about exploring until you get rid of him, which requires you getting out of the RPD station in both stories. If you want to explore things you've missed because of Mr. X, you're going to have to go through the sewers in order to get back to the station, which takes quite a bit of time.

They brought RE back to its horror routes which is what everyone wanted. Not saying the action installments of the game were bad, RE4 is one of the best games of all-time, but the horror side has been missed for quite a while and this game does a great job of bringing it back. Can tell that the devs of the game took a lot of care with this, everything is polished and done well. It took them a while to remake this game, but I'm glad they did.

Residnet evil 2 is a fantastic modern survival horror that I think any fan of the genre will love. 

Controls:
I've played through the whole game (3 playthroughs) on keyboard and mouse and they work well, of course you'll have some movement issues while using keys over a gamepad stick, overall I feel the issues to be very minor and easily forgotten. 

Aiming
So aiming with the mouse is extreamly easy as it is with many shoorters. 
While aiming you'll have a reticle that starts off large but will get smaller the longer you aim (only take about 2secs to shrink) which increases the tension of any fight, however I noticed the shots don't go randomly inside the giving area of the reticle like some games do, the shots (to me) always land in the middle of the reticle, so if you are good at imagining where that spot is, you'll never have to wait for the reticle to shrink. 

Inventory
Inventory like any good survial horror is limited, you'll be spending lots of time in this menu organising resources and key items. This may be a negative point for some people but I hope they will come to understand it's a necessary element, why? The idea is to plan out what you are going to take, will you take multiple guns, ammo and healing items? Cool but you'll have no space for key items. 
Item management is much easier over the original with multiple upgrades found through the game, also it does pause gameplay while in menus, so don't stress too much. :D 

gameplay
So your basic gameplay will revolve around shooting down zombies and other horrors or trying to avoid them, solving puzzles and backtracking to get better items and resources. 

Shooting
Zombies are very tough to take down, lucky you have many ways to deal with them. 
You could shot the Zombie multiple times in the head which if you are lucky could result in the zombies head exploding (there is a percentage chance of this happen and will change depending on the weapon).
You could also remove limbs by shooting them or cutting them with the knife which will make it so the zombie can't walk or grab you. 
Just keep in mind something are best avoided as you'll need to save up your ammo. 

Puzzles
It's good to see the return of puzzles, I never found any puzzle to hard or frustrating. Just keep an eye open as some codes to safes and other things arn't giving to you in text or files. 
I feel you get a good mixture of puzzles to keep things interesting.

Graphics
A look of a game is always going to be subjective, with that said this game looks great. 
Dynamic lighting and shodow add to the atmosphere and feeling of the game, monsters will get chipped away by your fun fire revealing muscle and bone. 
Overall great attention to detail in both environment and monsters. 

Final thoughts 
Residnet evil 2 I think is a fantastic update and reimagining of the original, I didn't go into much detail about what was diffrent or the layout of the map, i feel that stuff is best left up to you too discover. 
A must buy for anyone interested in this type of game

The main problem with this remake is that it's narratively incompetent. Completely. They cut out several cutscenes from the original game that were key to the plot, but they continued to develop the plot of the remake based on these cutscenes that never happened. It shouldn't take you long to notice the story is literally worse than the original. You'll see what I mean. 

There's no genius of design here. This doesn't elevate game design or the series to any new level.  Literally this is the equivalent of if they put in over the shoulder aiming in REmake 1, except they added silly modern horror mechanics like being chased by an invincible adversary.  It's a tired horror trope at this point which dates back to Nemesis and other games like Silent Hill 2 and Haunting Ground and it's not only overused , but now they've jumped the shark and ruined it for RE3 remake which is the game where Nemesis SHOULD be stalking you all the time. 

The tyrant can pop up at any time, any place, even if makes absolutely no sense. Yet there are also rooms he can't go in besides save rooms. This is especially bad in 4th Survivor where he literally warps in front of you. It makes for an interesting challenge because, in the normal campaigns, all those lickers and zombies you left alive - the Tyrant is going to push you into them. Good luck.

They've cut out tons of content from the original game, not just scenes that were cucial to the narrative but enemies and locations and rooms too. There are no super lickers, no naked lab zombies, very few lab zombies period, no ivy plants (technically), no moth, no spiders. And everyone's favorite sequence - the giant alligator - is a page directly from the "Worst Designs in RE History" playbook. Think RE6 when you are running towards the camera from the Ustanak and can't see what you're running in to.

Despite all of that, REmake 2 is almost good enough to make up for the fact that Capcom ONLY catered this game towards new players and RE4 era fans. With original soundtrack DLC it even brings back the old menu sounds like I asked for. 

Many new puzzles have been added, and older puzzles moved around or changed, but, they're almost too easy. Most of them are too easy I'd say. Gameplay harkens back to the original, with multiple scenarios, arrange mode, Hunk and Tofu, etc, but there is no A/B scenario this itime around. At least it isn't named that way, and what you do in the first playthrough doesn't affect the second. 

Overall I'd say they did a great job of recreating most of the games locations, while making them still interesting, but they've sterilized essentially all of the charm of the real RE2. The intro sequence has been significantly changed, along with some of the best dialog being removed, and in fact they actually made the game MORE cheesy. The game is beautiful with a robust array of graphics options that most PC exclusives don't even have, much less multiplats. You may encounter some massive stuttering - this is caused by enabling RE.net. Either turn it off, or alt tab and disable your internet adapter then go back to the game. Doing it once should fix the game forever, it worked for me anyway. After circumventing the ridiculous RE.net problems it runs buttery smooth.

Ultimately, if you were a fan of the original, this remake is little more than a museum to RE2. It's fun to see what they did but it pales in comparison to playing RE2. If you're a new fan, this is worth it as you're not going to find a new title closer to the original gangster than this besides RE7.,

Now into some of the things I enjoyed a lot about this remake, one is that sets it apart from the other that has been remade and ported to so many consoles is the lack of a fixed camera angle. While I still enjoy the tanky controls of the older games, I fell in love on how this game feels in terms of movement. Now I should say I myself had issues trying to avoid some attacks while also those same attacks at times I could avoid like a champion, and needless to say I felt happy with it overall. I also loved that the combat stayed true to the older games, maybe not on "Assisted", I myself only played on hardcore mode. With that said it still felt fair and rewarding for those landed headshots, even if they did not go down they would stagger and you can run past as if they had fallen. Besides if I had to try to slow one own being able to shoot the legs to bring the zombies down felt even better in some cases, sure it cost a bit more ammo and the zombie would still be alive for later but at least he was less of a threat if left alive and alone. Lastly I want to mention how amazed I was with the atmosphere of the game, it was perfect to me. The lighting felt right maybe not everywhere, but god the Police Station and it's dark blood covered halls, the lightning flashing while undead slamming against the windows.
