Probably the finest remake of a game ever created, and then some.
Filled to the brim with both new moments and homages to the original, even as a 1998 RE2 veteran I was delighted and surprised by plenty of sections, and I adored absolutely every minute of re-exploring the world I first experienced the genre with.

The map is familiar to old RE2 players in a lot of ways, and excitingly changed in others; 
I found myself instinctively knowing where to go at times, only to get turned around on occasion by obstacles and logical alterations to the way the RPD is laid out. Every new area brought back fantastic nostalgia and inspired new fear simultaneously, particularly some surprise changes to boss encounters, creatures and mechanics.

This is survival horror, not terror; if you're expecting jumpscares every few minutes, you'll be sorely disappointed. They're few and far-between, but very tastefully executed. Ammo conservation and puzzle solving are the priorities here, and they certainly live up to the standards of the original 3 games in the series. Tension is offered by the ever-looming threat of a menagerie of mutated monstrosities, topped off by the ultimate trenchcoat-toting-badass, RE3 Nemesis' T-103's older, more chisel-jawed fedora-wearing brother: the Tyrant T-00. 
Two things are certain in this game: he will find you, and you'll wish he bloody hadn't.

Instead of the trouser-browning terror you experience with games like Alien: Isolation, the game instead has a rhythm that keeps you excited to progress while also making you keep a careful eye on your health and ammo. Playing on Normal, I felt like I had just enough of both to get by comfortably; I finished Scenario A with 14 pistol bullets left, a few basic healing items, and nothing else. After learning to conserve ammo and health, Scenario B was slower but I finished with a lot more resources available, leaving me feeling ready to try out Hardcore.

The environmental story-telling is superb, and the game has a fantastic 'show, don't tell' flow to it that echoes the best parts of The Last of Us or Uncharted 4. Documents scattered around fill in little gaps in the over-arcing story, and puzzles need to be solved by paying attention to the environmental clues and using your wits rather than following any thankfully absent objective or map markers. I missed one of the weapons in Scenario A by not figuring out one of the puzzles, which delighted me when I discovered the solution out of curiosity over 5hrs later while exploring more carefully during Scenario B. 

The story tells itself in the same way, with a minimal focus on cutscenes.
Interactions with the few survivors you come across are impactful and brief, and don't take you out of gameplay for more than a moment before tossing you back. Conversations that can take place on the move do so, and one long waiting section from the original release is replaced here with a brief cutscene of dialogue.

The soundtrack is subtle, and echoes the classic music in many ways but leaves the environmental audio to set most of the atmosphere and tension, with music cutting in and out in appropriate areas and moments. I'm looking forward to playing in reverse order with the Classic OST and SFX from the Deluxe Edition!

Replayability is huge here, and while a single first playthrough of both scenarios could take you anywhere from 5 to 8hrs each, replaying them while aiming for an S Rank or while playing on Hardcore offers even more bang for your buck. There are four scenarios in total, two for each character, with the A and B scenarios offering the opposite perspective in each case. The extra unlockable modes are a blast to play too, and offer a great replayable 'time attack' option for people who are fans of challenge runs and speedrunning, and will test your skills and knowledge of the game on an incredible level that isn't afraid to kick your butt.

Graphical options are intuitive and well explained, so I was able to keep a steady 60fps at 1080p on a GTX970 and the game still looked absolutely stunning. The game would stutter to ~50fps briefly for a second or two while loading a new area, nothing massive. Some reflections shimmered in certain areas but that was barely noticeable, and had another review not pointed it out I might never have noticed it at all. Controls are tight and responsive, with plenty of configuration options available for controller or mouse and keyboard players.

For me this game shot right over the head of Resident Evil HD, Nemesis and 7, stealing pride of place as 'Favourite Game in the Series' if not the entire genre. Supreme in quality, a respectful re-imagining of a classic with plenty for everyone.

A must-play, survival horror classic in the making in every way that matters.

Remake? Reimagining? I dunno but what Resident Evil 2 is, is a fantastic game. RE2 manages to walk that very fine line of staying true to the original while being completely fresh and exciting. If you're a fan of the PSX classic you will definitely recognize locations, characters, and story beats but you cannot rely on your memory of the original at all. The puzzles are different, the layouts are different, and the game is much tougher than you remember. All of this to say that it feels like a brand new entry in the series while still flooding your gamer brain with all of the nostalgia you crave. That's a hell of an accomplishment. 

If you've never played RE2 before, don't worry: You don't have to be a fan to enjoy this. Everything has been updated to feel like a current gen game and a damned fine one at that. Certain elements, like the limited inventory space, might seem a bit odd for a modern action shooter but it's balanced exceedingly well so that it rarely if ever becomes cumbersome. And you know what? It's actually scary. Maybe not as scary as RE7 but, when you're running down a corridor and hear the roar of a licker taking a flying leap towards you, your heart will definitely be pounding.

It's absoluttely gorgeous, too, though this was to be expected if you've played RE7. When you first walk into the police station, it's hard to believe that the main hall isn't a prerendered background but a fully 3D, interactable environment. 

When the RE1 remake came out on the Gamecube, my literal first thought was "Okay but when are you doing RE2?" It's been a heck of a long wait but it's so been worth it. While the 1998 version will always hold a special place in my heart, this is without a doubt the best way to experience RE2.

[h1] The Gold Standard For Remasters

A couple of details before I start giving my thoughts on the actual game, in order to give readers a better understanding of why Im writing a review right now.

I completed Leons side of the story in just under 8 hours (7:43:27 for all you sticklers out there who want the actual number) which is about in line for what IGN said a playthrough would take. About 6 of those hours were in one sitting and the only reason I even took a break was because I was starbing to the point where I needed to prioritize my own survival instead of Leons so I could go back to priotizing his survival over mine.

Needless to say I loved just about every single minute of my time with the game thus far. Im not kidding when I say that if this had come out in 2018, this probably would've been my GOTY over the likes of RDR2 and God of War.

Now on to the nitty gritty details.

The biggest comparison I can draw is to Dark Souls. That comparison being the way the "level," is interwoven with itself and that all roads eventually lead to one another. I've always been a fan of that "Open but Linear," game design that has been prevalent in the likes of Dark Souls or Dishonored, and Resident Evil 2 executes that flawlessly here, coupling rewarding exploration with an atmosphere that was tense yet conquerable. 

The graphics in the game are about on par with Resident Evil 7 which I thought was a good looking game when I played it on my PS4 (I didnt have a PC at the time). This game is also phenomenal in the animation department, particularly the facial animations. Take Note Guerilla Studios and Bioware: This is how you do facial animation. 

Gameplay wise this is your standard third person shooter, if you've played a third person shooter you know what you're getting into here. This is my first time playing a Resident Evil game on keyboard and mouse and I have to say I really enjoyed it. Controls transferred over well, especially for a tankier 3rd person shooter like Resident Evil,  and aiming with a mouse was snappy and much easier to nail headshots. Only gripe I had was the ♥♥♥♥+tabbing accidentally into Steam whenever I was trying to sprint and get into my inventory, but you could always just remap the controls like I didnt.

One of the final points Id like to bring up is how well optimized this game was. I have a GTX1080 with an i7-8700k and I was playing with my 144hz monitor with the graphics settings set to high. Now I dont think I hit 144hz consistently, but I never noticed any screen tearing or stuttering, and the game was always buttery smooth to boot with no frame drops around explosions or fire effects or anything of the likes.

In conclusion I have loved my time with this game, I plan on starting my "2nd Run Playthrough," some time after I wake up after writing this review and I anticipate that greatly. This is the Gold Standard for anyone thinking about remastering a past franchise and I woud like to give a shout out to Capcom who had a few rough years but have come back strong with some stellar releases recently. Great job guys, now all you need to do is remaster Resident Evil 3 and 4, maybe 5 and delete 6 from existence and all of your sins shall be forgiven. Thank you for reading this if you got this far, spaghetti and meatballs.

[h1] In A Nutshell [/h1]

🔵 [b] Pros [/b]
+ An incredible remake. Everything was remade from scratch using RE7's engine, delivering top-notch graphics quality.
+ Two parallel stories to play: Claire's and Leon's.
+ Plenty of hidden items, weapons and secrets to find, with exploration rewarding attentive and careful players.
+ True old-school survival horror experience: players need to be extremely conservative with resources and avoid combat when possible.
+ Varied, challenging gameplay situations that keep the experience fresh from start to end.
+ Higher difficulties provide considerable challenge even to veterans of the genre.

🔴 [b] Cons [/b]
- The "Ink" mechanic (enabling game saving only with a certain consumable) on Hardcore difficulty should be optional, as not all players might like it, but still would like the additional challenge compared to Normal.

===

First of all, it has to be said that this is a Remake with capital R, as everything was remade from scratch: models, textures, lighting, even the engine was completely changed to the excellent one used for RE7. As far as looks goes, RE2 delivers astonishing graphical detail, giving a true 2019-worthy look to this great game of old.

For those not knowing it, RE2 is an old-school survival horror, quite a bit different from the more recent chapters. Impersonating either Leon or Claire, players will have to carve their way through zombie infested police stations, putrid sewers, and even worse places. What really changes is how they do this, as RE2 is a "pure" survival horror game, favoring extreme conservation of resources for when they truly matter (boss fights, or unavoidable normal fights), while encouraging players to be creative and avoid as many unnecessary fights as possible, as one would do in a real apocalypse after all.

Exploration is rewarding and satisfying for the attentive players that do want to explore every corner, open every locker, crack every safe, lock they find, and examine items they find to reveal secrets. Not only this is rewarded with ever-needed resources, but aswell weapons and objects, such as additional inventory space, or weapon upgrades. And believe me when i say until the last bullet will be needed to make it through this horror, so better start looking! Combat features detailed dismemberment mechanics such as mutilating an enemy's legs to slow it down, or hitting weak points to stagger it momentarily and run past.

[u] Overall, this remake of RE2 is an excellent survival horror, only quite different than what most players are used to nowadays, and thus needs to be understood to fully enjoy it. Still, to those willing to understand how its mechanic work, it can deliver an unforgettable experience for this genre, as only a few other masterpieces can do. It's actually a game I have been happy to pay full price for. [/u]

[h1] In-depth Feature Analysis [/h1]


🎮 [b] Gameplay [/b]
Gameplay in RE2 is divided into Exploration, Management and Combat.

Exploration is performed with a 3rd person visual, featuring mouse-based aiming, sprint/walk, and plenty of interactions with the environment such as using specific tools to open pathways, barricade windows, or opening lockers and containers to gather loot. Attention to detail and backtracking are fundamental in this game, as many areas will be only accessible as more and more tools and keys are gathered, so going back to already explored places is actually meaningful even if optional, as it often leads to great rewards for those willing to risk it.

Management is a fundamental mechanic in any survival horror, but especially in RE2. Inventory space, especially at the beginning without expansions, is very limited, so either going back often to the Stash to store items, or a wise optimization of resources are needed at all times. Combining herbs, ammo stacks, and decide what to take or leave behind are things players will do often in this title. With the presence of a global stash, however, it's just a matter of storing surplus into it often, when accessible. However, balancing the loadout in ammo, healing items and weapons is important and doing it wrong can lead to not having enough space for critical items.

📖 [b] Story [/b]
The story in RE2 is divided into two parallel campaigns, and its lore is narrated via pieces of information found scattered around, cut-scenes, and dialogues with various characters. The narrative is solid, decently written, and engaging from start to end. Characters have all strong, defined personalities and are interesting aswell. For not being the strong side of these titles, definitely good.

👊 [b] Combat System [/b]
Combat in RE2 is tactical, pretty much slow-paced, and based upon accuracy, preparation, and knowing each enemy's skills and weaknesses. The best offense in this game is... to avoid combat. That's right: try to kill every enemy and soon all ammo will run out, leaving players defenseless and doomed in case of mandatory fights. Instead, careful planning of routes, engagements is vital to save up the spare resources for when they truly matter.

Still, then it comes to it, each weapon has good and diverse feeling to it, while enemies react beautifully to shots, in a shower of gore most of the time. Enemies are considerably tougher than most of nowadays games of the same genres, so beware. This might seem as a CON at first... but once understanding the game's concept, it becomes a good side of it.


💰 [b] Content & Pricing [/b]
Priced at 60€, and lasting (depends on play-style, difficulty and experience GREATLY) around 10-16 hours, this is one of the VERY FEW titles i can recommend getting at FULL PRICE. The quality it delivers is simply too good to be missed. 

🔗 [b] Balance & Challenge [/b]
This is not an easy game by any means, and players can even be forced to restart because of having wasted too many resources. But once understood, it delivers amazing satisfactions. Challenge level is medium/high.


[h1] Technical Analysis [/h1]


🎥 [b] Graphics [/b]
Astonishing. RE7's engine, improved even more, with a plethora of modern effects, filters and settings to tweak, and top-quality textures, models, animations and effects, makes for one gorgeous title. Possibly one of the games with the best graphics around, considering it's a remake.

🔊 [b] Sound [/b]
Excellent ambient sounds, effects, and voice-acting. Directional sounds, also featuring binaural audio for better realism, deliver excellent quality that contributes immensely to immersion.

🔩 [b] Performance & Stability [/b]
The game runs without issues in 1440p with maxed out settings, 3GB textures and 120% quality, on the following config: [i7 4820K, GTX1080, 16GB RAM]. No performance or optimization problems to note.

💻 [b] Artificial Intelligence [/b]
Enemy AI is not that brilliant considering most enemies are mutants or zombies. As expected. The few "intelligent" enemies follow patterns of movement through the maps and chase players on sight.

🏠 [b] Quality of Life [/b]
Good interface and menu handling, without any issue for the genre.

🐛 [b] Bugs & Issues [/b]
Nothing major to report. Great polishing and refinement.


[h1] Conclusion [/h1]
RE2 is really a gem of the old times brought back to life with modern technology. One of the best remade versions I have ever seen on the market, and truly worth every cent.

[h1] Introduction [/h1]
[b] Before starting this review, i would like to say that i don't have any nostalgic connection to Resident Evil 2 since i never played it when it originally came out. [/b]

Resident Evil 2 (2019) is the remake to the original game from 1998. Though calling this game a simple "Remake" would be a disservice as RE2 (2019) is pretty much a whole new game, this makes that they're different enough and so you can still play the original. The only things that are from the original is the plot, setting, and characters, everything else is different. 

The game is now a third-person shooter (for better or worse, personally i like the change in  the perspective), the layout of the police station and the game as a whole is similiar but vastly changed, the story and characters are more fleshed out than in the original, certain events play out differently than in the original and this makes veteran players to stay on their toes, and i could go on and on but it would take too long.

Before you play this game, i highly suggest you to play the Resident Evil 1 Remake, while the gameplay is vastly different from this game, playing it would give you an idea of what a Resident Evil is and what it should be. Plus, it's pretty important to the story for this game and it's definitely one of the best games of all time.

[h1] Story [/h1]
[b] It's kinda hard to not spoil the game while trying to tell the basis of the story so i'll try my best [/b]

Resident Evil 2 takes place a few months after the first game. After a recent zombie breakout in Racoon City, you need to find out what the hell's going on as you explore the police station and beyond. You can play as one of two characters when you start the game. The first one is Leon S. Kennedy, a rookie cop on his first day of the job. And the other one is Claire Redfield, a college student who is looking for his brother Chris Redfield who is one of the playable characters in the first game. Unlike the first game, each of the characters have a totally different story and subplots. As Leon, you'll encounter Ada Wong. While as Claire, you'll encounter Sherry. As i said it's kinda hard to not spoil this game so you might as well play the game and see for yourself. Overall, it's a well written story with likeable characters though i wish leon's campaign had a bit more too it.

[h1] Gameplay [/h1]

While this game is third-person, it's still Resident Evil through and through. Resident Evil 2 is a Survival-Horror game much like it's predecessors. Basically, Survival-Horror is a sub-genre of horror that focuses and puts emphasis on Inventory Management, Puzzle Solving, having a Vulnerable playable character, a somewhat Slow-Paced Combat, and of course backtracking (it may not be in every survival-horror game but it's a huge part of the Resident Evil Series).

[u] Atmosphere [/u]
This game probably has some of the best atmosphere ever in a horror game. It's dark, scary, and has some of the best audio design ever.

[u] Inventory Management [/u]
Having a limited inventory space means you can't pick up everything you see, if your inventory is full and you need to pick up an item, you either need to discard one of your items or backtrack to the last save room so you can store some of your items. This becomes a game in itself as you find out what's best to bring, what to store, and what to discard. 

[u] Backtracking [/u]
Speaking of backtracking, you will be doing it ALOT and trust me it's not as annoying as everybody says, hell i think it's actually done pretty great (just like the old RE games). You need to memorize what room you need to get to and what key you need, if you don't memorize things so well, don't be worried as RE2 probably has the best and most friendly Map Interface in the whole series, rooms you haven't fully explored will be colored red, items you haven't picked up will have a logo, and puzzles you haven't solved will have an exclamation mark.

[u] Movement and Controls [/u]
Movement is very similiar to RE7 only in a Third-Person Perspective, it's kinda slow compared to other games but you still move faster than most of the enemies. Slow doesn't mean it's bad though, more like the opposite, if it was faster it would ruin the game's overall tone and atmosphere so yea i really like it. The game controls really well with mouse and keyboard and you can keybind pretty much every key, my only complaint is that you cant use your mouse in alot of the puzzles though it's probably more of a nitpick since i got used to it pretty quick. 

[u] Combat [/u]
Just like the movement, combat is slow-paced but it's till fun because it has some split second choices and strategy. For example, you need to get to another room but there are a couple of zombies blocking the way, you can kill them and you'll lose some of your ammo but if you backtrack to that room again you wont have to deal with them again, Or you can lead them out of your way and escape but once you go back to that room you will encounter them again. There are alot more examples than this but in a nutshell, that's pretty much it. 

My only complaint with the combat is that killing zombies have some RNG and boy oh boy it's really annoying. Basically because of the game's adaptive difficulty, zombies can take up to 10-20 shots to the head if you rarely die, but at the same time, some of them only take up to 2-5 shots to the head, hopefully they fix this in the future as it might turn new players away. While yes the old games have some really long time to kill as well, it never felt this annoying.

[u] Enemies And Mr.X [/u]
Of couse i can't talk about the game without talking about the enemies and one particular big dude that you'll encounter while playing. First, you have your regular zombies which are surprisingly scary. They might not be that intimidating if you encounter only one of them, but they sure can be a hassle if there's alot of them, they can take alot of damage but they move incredibly slow so my suggestion is to avoid them almost all the time if you can so you don't waste your ammo. Second, one of the most iconic enemies ever introduced in the series, The Lickers. They're basically mutated and more powerful zombies and way scarier, encountering one of them is scary enough and you'll be fu*ked if you meet more than one. There are a few more enemy types but i wont spoil them.

I would like to talk about one more though and that is..... Mister Motherfu*kin X. Some people said that he ruins the game but i beg to differ. He's probably my favorite thing about this game  as he makes you to keep your guard up. I won't spoil where or when you encounter him, so just prepare to be fu*ked.

[h1] Audio and Music [/h1]

Audio design is really great, zombies and lickers sound scary and Mr. X's footsteps sounds terrifying as fu*k. Music on the other hand is a bit hit or miss, this is my personal opinion so yours might be different but IMO the soundtrack is just too subtle. I think it's because they want the game to be more scary with it's fantastic audio design but with less and more subtle music. But after recently completing the RE1 remake, the game can still prove itself to be really scary with more noticable music. Even the save room theme isn't that memorable in this game because i can barely hear it. The best music is probably the Mr. X theme which can be really intimidating when you hear it. This is why i think it's kinda bullsh*t that you have to pay for the original soundtrack because i really prefer it over the new one and like i said before, i don't even have any nostalgic connection with this game.

[h1] Verdict [/h1]

Overall this game is certainly one of the best games to come out this year but there are certainly a few problems that hold it back from being a true masterpiece. I'm glad that capcom is finally bringing Classic Survival-Horror back to the mainstream market and i'm really excited for the future of this series.

Ever since I played REmake, I've been anxiously waiting for Capcom to give the 2nd game the same treatment. About 17 years later, and we finally get it, and it does not disappoint. 

However, this is more of a reimagining than a straight up remake. While the general R.P.D. layout and story beats are the same, the game itself has changed immensely.  The camera perspective has completely changed, the tank controls are gone, and there's new systems in play that radically changes how the game is played. There are now defensive options similar to those found in the first REmake. If you are grabbed, there's a good chance you'll be able to get out of it by using your knife or a grenade. Your knife can be retrieved after doing so, if you can kill the zombie. Knives have durability, so their uses are limited. There's also a gunpowder system, where you can craft ammo using various combinations of gunpowder items. Aiming is now in your full control now, where before you just pointed in the general direction of the enemy and hit it. You can also move while shooting, but this affects your accuracy greatly. 

A gripe of many people a little before the game releases was the lack of enemies. Spiders, Plants, Evolved Lickers, Naked Zombies, and that one moth are all present in the original, but are absent in this game. After completing the game, I have to say I didn't really miss these enemies much. Evolved lickers and naked zombies are basically just reskinned and slightly upgraded (I think? might be misremembering) versions of their counterparts. Spiders are a pretty boring enemy, and there's only about 4 or 5 in the original game. Plants are also not all that interesting of an enemy to fight, with the main thing you have to worry about is not getting hit by the poison they spit. The moth... is ♥♥♥♥ a ♥♥♥♥ enemy in general. There's only one in the original and it's really not worth talking about. 
There's an argument to be had that these enemies added much needed variety to the enemies, even if just aesthetically. While I can agree it can help, I'd say Resident Evil 2 remake provides that in a different way. A new enemy added in remake is a good replacement for the spiders in the sewers. While they are still not the most interesting enemy to fight, they're still more interesting than the spiders. The plants are replaced by an upgraded version of the zombie.
All that leaves in the game in terms of enemy variety is the Zombie, Licker, Zombie Dog, and the new sewer monster.

So with a smaller pool of enemies than the original, and more direct control over your character, something had to be done to make the game challenging. Capcom managed to strike the right balance, I feel. All the enemies in general have been buffed up. Overall, they move faster, take more punishment, and hit harder. Ammo is also scarce. This nullifies the advantages the new systems give you and keeps the feeling that the odds are against you. A lot of this also makes the lack of enemy variety a non-issue. Zombies are the main enemies you'll be up against in the game, and they never really stop feeling scary. While it was easy to juke them in the original, it is now much easier for them to grab you. It is now a lot harder to take them down. This will lead you to either get creative with dodging them, or using a fair bit of your precious ammo to down them, and even then it's usually only temporary. They can pop right back up without much warning at any time. If you're not careful, you'll end up swarmed, with a duo of them grabbing onto you at once. You can shoot their legs and arms off to give you an easier time, however, and there's a chance to crit their head on headshot, causing it to explode and permanently putting them down. 
Lickers seem to be a lot more mobile than before, which makes them a harder target to hit at times. The dogs seem relatively unchanged, and there weren't many that I encountered in the game. 

RE2 REmake follows the same basic story beats as the original did. There's a few surprises mixed in and characters and segments have been expanded, so I won't spoil too much. I feel like the new story flows a lot smoother than the original. and seeing these characters and events with the new writing is a real treat for a long time fan. 

However, there are a few problems I have with the game though. Thankfully, none of them are major, mostly just minor annoyances that weighed on me in certain segments. There are certain rooms which quickly become swarming with enemies whenever you finish a puzzle or grab an item or whatever it is you do to tell the enemies to wake up. Since ammo is scarce as it is, it's really difficult to properly deal with these rooms, as the enemies are usually on top of you before you can really retaliate. There are also some enemy placements that are meant to be jumpscares, but just end up being annoying because you don't have much time to react and they get a free hit on you. 
Another thing is the soundtrack. Or rather, lack thereof. The original Resident Evil 2 had an amazing soundtrack, imo. The save room theme is brilliant. The REMake however, opts for a more silent approach, focusing more on various sound effects than actual music. This is effective and really set me on edge, but I felt like something was missing that the original had, and that was probably the music. The original save room theme is fantastic, and while it is remade in the new game, it's only played once and for about 10 seconds. Thankfully, there's DLC available for the original soundtrack swap, so it doesn't have to affect my enjoyment much. 

Also, the 2nd run portion of the game feels a little rushed. [spoiler] In the original, story beats would change completely depending on whether you picked Leon or Claire, and when you went through the game as the other character things would change depending on the events of the first scenario. This is not the case anymore, as the campaigns are pretty much set in stone and the only difference is the 1st run determines who interacts with Marvin, and the 2nd run determines who fights the final boss. Slightly disappointing, but the campaigns themselves are still very entertaining for it to not be that big of an issue.[/spoiler]

Overall, Resident Evil 2 REmake is an outstanding game and is true to the spirit of the original while offering a game experience that is fresh and more modern. This will probably be a game that I sink a lot of time into replaying multiple times like I did with the original.

[h1]TL;DR - An amazing re-adaptation, re-imagining, full-blown [i]re-make[/i] of an already amazing game brought up to modern standards. Get this game if you were a fan of the original and absolutely [i]miss[/i] proper, Japanese-style survival horror.[/h1]

Tank controls, begone! Many may argue that this was a large part of the charm of the original Resident Evil games - and I agree - but sometimes you need to update your gameplay to appeal to a more modern audience. While the REmake of the original still stands tall as one of the best game remakes of the last thirty-five years, no one can honestly deny with a straight face that REmake 2 (this is how I'm referring to it) isn't a phenomenal achievement.

While still keeping true to the core principles of Resident Evil 2, this version brings its controls up to modern standards. Folks who enjoyed the third-person, over-the-shoulder action controls of RE5 and RE6 (as this game is more like those by gameplay standards) will feel right at home while purist veterans will need some getting used to. Even on PC, though, the controls are very smooth, and responsive. While the original game still had plenty of tension with its tank controls and limited aiming, this game definitely ups the ante by providing a more sinister and anxiety-riddled environment that's sure to bring out your inner six year old - you know, the little kid who couldn't bring themselves to go through this game because of all of the horror elements?

The story has also seen a facelift - along with the acting. With the original game we [strike]suffered[/strike] were graced with the gloriously cheesy and hammy dialog that only the greatest Japanese-to-English Localization talent of 1997/1998 could provide. Now the mood of the characters befits the general tone of the game. The voice actors do a great job with the given material, and the acting itself doesn't cause so much as a cringe. The original has its charm and can never be outmatched, but what we have here is an amazing game with. On the story, it follows the same as the original but it's told in a much more cohesive way.

Parroting what other reviews are already saying; you take control of either rookie cop (and early-2000's gaming heart-throb and cheesy good guy) Leon S. Kennedy or the estranged younger sister of the first game's Chris, Claire Redfield, as they both come upon the spread of the infectious T-Virus unleashed on Raccoon City. The primary focus of the game is on the city's Police Department, where you overcome the hordes of the undead, various creatures unleashed by the T-Virus, and eventually uncover a sinister plot interwoven and enacted by the enigmatic Umbrella Corporation. The characterization in this iteration is vastly different than how we've become familiar with Leon and Claire over the past twenty years. Now, Leon [i]feels[/i] and [i]acts[/i] like a rookie cop, where Claire is just as terrified of everything going down but develops into her own over the course of her campaign. I really like how they remade these characters - we no longer see the snarky confidence of Leon from RE4 and later entries to the series, and we catch a glimpse of Claire's no-holds-barred attitude in the latter stages, after a long and terrible night of facing off against the worst of the worst. 

The puzzles are both back and changed for the most part. RE2, even the original, had done a great job of not leaving you scratching your head trying to figure out how to solve the puzzles presented. Everything has a clue to find, and once those clues are discovered then it's a simple task to get right into solving those puzzles.

Buying the Deluxe Edition gives you access to the original game's soundtrack - and listening to it gives you a wave of heavy nostalgia if you have any memories of the original game. The familiar, hauntingly foreboding music of the RCPD main hall sent chills down my spine as I heard it playing in my [i]modern Resident Evil[/i] game. The sound design, in general, as to be commended. Zombies are sufficiently creepy, Lickers are terrifying, and the slowly approaching thudding of a massive, but familiar foe's footsteps all add to an overall amazing experience.

Seriously, I cannot recommend this game enough. If you are at all fan of the series, or loved the original of this game, then you owe it to yourself to play it. It's very much worth the asking price.

Alright, first things first, I think this remake is ALMOST perfect because it's very faithful to the original, but not 100%... here we go:

WARNING!!!
This review contains "light" spoilers about the enemies, locations and bonuses that are in the game (both original and remake).

Gameplay - 10/10
The gameplay is flawless without a doubt. The new controls, combat, puzzles and boss battles are awesome. It's the best I've ever seen in any Resident Evil game. I liked the fixed cameras in the original RE2, but I think it wouldn't be the best solution to keep them in this modern remake, for today standards. The "over the shoulder" camera lets us explore every detail in every area and it also brings us more fear and tension. This camera gives us the free aim, something I love and it wouldn't be the same with fixed cameras. 

Graphics - 10/10
I don't have much to say, but the game and its effects are very beautiful and detailed. Trust me, you won't regret.

Characters - 10/10
Awesome. They're richer in personality, the faces are so close to the originals and fortunately not like Chris appeared so ugly and different in RE7. Amazing acting, voice and facial expressions. 

Soundtrack - 07/10
The soundtrack is good, but I feel like it didn't do justice to the main hall RPD theme. Not only this, but another iconic track: the save room theme. What happened here? Oh well, at least who bought the deluxe edition or the separate tracks dlc can switch to the original themes.

Enemies - 08/10
I love the enemies. The zombies, the female zombie wearing shorts, lickers, the bosses, the tyrant, every single enemy is scary enough, even the zombies can scare you sometimes (it happened to me). They're perfect, except for: spiders, crows and moths. Why? Because they AREN'T in the game! And why is that, Capcom? Laziness?

Locations - 08/10
Raccoon City is faithful, RPD is faithful and so is the sewer section. But what happened in the labs? The majority of it was changed so abruptly that I can barely recognize some areas from the original. Also, it missed that iconic train yard scenario. 

Bonuses - 07/10
We have Leon and Claire scenarios, both unlocking "2nd run" (like Scenario B) after completion. We have The 4th Survivor, Tofu Survivor... but where is Extreme Battle mode??? That was in the original and it was amazing. I really hope to see this as a DLC in the future, at least. Maybe it's "The Ghost Survivors" capcom announced as a free dlc? Let's hope so, I don't know. Something that isn't necessary, but it would also be cool: some DLC about Ada Wong escaping Raccoon City just like she did in "Death's Door" scenario from Resident Evil: The Umbrella Chronicles. The bonus costumes are cool, just as the files and models that you can unlock in the game.

My conclusion is: this remake was almost perfect. Why would Capcom remove iconic things from the original like enemies, that Sherry section in RPD where you were supposed to run from dogs without anything to defend yourself, solve a puzzle with boxes, etc...? These things were simple, but iconic. And they removed it. For me, removing these classic things was the only flaw in this remake. For example, in the remake of the first game, EVERY SINGLE THING was there. They only added more. And that was what I wanted for RE2 Remake. Overall, an amazing game. I had so much fun playing it and I'm sure I still will for many, many more hours until I get bored of it. 

Resident Evil fan or not, if you like horror games, I highly recommend this one. 

PS: I'm really hoping for a 100% faithful remake of RE3 and Outbreak :)

What a weird experience this game is!

I'm been waiting for this game for 17 years, since 2002 when Capcom made that incredible remake of the first Resident Evil game ("REmake"), and they were planning to remake the whole franchise...until that game bombed and they scrapped the whole thing.
I pre-ordered this game the day it was available, the deluxe edition actually, and now is finally here...

However, while as a survival horror game this is most likely the best you will find, I cant say this is a REMAKE of the legendary Resident Evil 2.
Gameplay is completely different, same goes with the aesthetic, and the whole feeling of the game...this game feels more like an american game than a japanese game.

If I would have to define this game it would be "reimagination" instead of "remake".

Aside from that, the game isnt perfect either.
The game has barely any music in it (music being one of the best things the original RE2 had), and what's in there, is generic as hell...on the other hand, since this game plays like RE6, you can freely aim for zombies' heads, so they made them extremely hard to kill, sometimes needing 10 shots in the head to be put down, and dont be surprised if a few minutes later you see the same zombie still roaming around...

Puzzles are there, and are as "charismatic" as they were in Resident Evil 7, not as "classy" as they were in Resident Evil 2.

In short, is this game good? heck yeah, is an incredible game, a GOTY contender, now, if you are a fan of Resident Evil 2, and you were expecting a REMAKE of said game, you should lower your expectations, this is not "REmake 2".

Edit: ok, I just finished both scenarios, I dont want to give it a bad rating, but I cant believe very few people are mentioning the many flaws this game has...besides the zombies taking 10 headshots to go down, you have lickers who are literally broken, their hit boxes are all over the place, they will ALWAYS hit you no matter what, while you need to put your gun on their "nose" to actually hit them...and speaking of enemies, zombies and lickers are all there is to it, no plants, crows, spiders, you will only have those two enemies...

Visually the police station looks incredible, but it seems all the budget and attention went there, the moment you leave it, the game goes downhill, both visually (it looks like a budget game in some parts) and in level design (you WILL hate sewer levels after playing this game).
I'm starting to think the whole point of 90% of the game being in the dark wasnt a creative decision to make the game scarier, it was to hide how ugly it is in some parts.

Mr X becomes a lot more annoying in scenario B, and btw, aside from cutscenes, both scenarios are identical, you are playing the same game (with minor changes) twice, while 21 years ago, the original game made history by offering a completely new experience in scenario B...on the other hand, this remake tries really hard to be taken seriously unlike the original game which was really cheesy...well, the ending this time around is a lot more cheesy, to the point of almost being stupid...Capcom, make up your mind, either serious or cheesy, you cant have both!

Anyway, this is still a good game, but people saying is a "10/10" or going as far as saying is better than the original, are either lying or are blind by hype...

If you are NOT a fan of the original game, this is a good option, if you have the patience to deal with all I mentioned above, but if you are a fan of the original, either lower your hype, or try the game for more than 2 hours before buying it.

Possibly one of the most fun, yet seriously scary experiences in gaming. Definitely worth the asking price if you want and super atmospheric horror-survival game, that has an interesting story with enjoyable characters, heart racing scares and is super well optimised to boot. The game runs at a perfect 144hz on a 1070 and I7-7800X with no dips in performance (even when streaming). The zombies can be quite spongey but I can give them a free pass on that because of how well detailed and gore-y the damage models are, shoot a zombie in the head, you're going to see chunks flying.

The police station is a labyrinth but not annoying to traverse through, long dark corridors to tight enclosed storage spaces to really kick you in the tension sensors, [spoiler] it ESPECIALLY gets tense when Tyrant starts to hound you down never letting up. [/spoiler]. 

Gunplay is fantastic, not too actiony to take you out of the scare factor but enough to make you feel like you CAN survive this hell.

The scares come from the atmosphere of the game most of the time for me, From creaks in floorboards to the rain bashing onto the windows of the RPD, building tension until you hear the groans of the oncoming dead. The game does feature some jump scares albeit few and far between, they don't rely on them as cheaply as some games do but they're there to get the blood racing and to mess you up when you're trying to collect yourself and your newly filled underpants.

all in all, the game is a really good step in horror gaming and I hope the trend will continue through other genres and make 2019 one of the best years in gaming.

Wow... what can I say... this game lived up to all the hype and more. Being a very avid fan of the Resident Evil Franchise and at one point speedrunning the 1998 version of Resident Evil 2, this is hands down one of the best Remakes of any game I have played. It brough back fear that I haven't experienced in a while, hearing Mr. X stomping around the precinct forcing me to lap around to avoid him was nothing short of butt-clenching every time. The visuals of all the enemies were amazing, especially when Elliot gets half of his torso demolished in front of your own eyes.

But, there are still some negatives to the game overall, the lack of Spiders in the sewers area was surprising, the amount of blue herbs that were thrown at us with next to no use (I wasn't poisoned once) had me looking forward to them. The second was not seeing the evolved and stronger lickers in the Laboratory area. There was just something about those lickers popping out of the vents and taking a beating that instilled fear into me as a child growing up. Although, I guess every enemy tended to absorb a lot of ammo in this remake, and with the lack of such ammo made me actually conserve a lot of it, using the mechanics of lickers to walk by unseen and baiting zombies to run past, and I'm glad I did. The bosses were super tanks! The final Birkin fight on Claire A for me took 400 Minigun Ammo, 30 Acid Round, 10 flame rounds before he would die, which built a whole new aspect on the fights.

Zombies were actually scary and quite unpredictable at times - but like others have said - having to unload 10+ ammo into a zombies head from your handgun seems very overkill. 

Overall I'd rate this remake a 9/10 - very great fan service and well upgraded in the departments it needed to be, but was still lacking a little to give fans the full experience of RE2 and more of the past!

Wow, how intuitive. Now they also have a limited number of uses on your knife, and that includes attack, not just countering a grapple. That's fun... So much for saving ammo. Now speaking of ammo as well, headshots are pointless. Apparently the meta is to shoot legs off and go around zombies. That makes sense considering you are using 9mm hollowpoints at point blank. Supposedly the game does this because of some kind of dynamic difficulty system. The game still has finite ammo points so they should not do that. Keep headshots consistent. If it's 3-4 each zombie then they stay down? Fine. Having to use 8-12+ on ONE zombie? Not acceptable.

Resident Evil 2 Remake is by far the best RE in the series. Resident Evil 2 takes everything that made the orginal games great and made it even better with photorealistic zombies, gore, suspense, horrific and depressing atmosphere, married off to a Resident Evil 4 style camera. While I enjoyed the pre-rendered camera angles of the original titles, Resident Evil 2 remake is essentially the old RE games with a behind the shoulder camera. Everything else is pure classic. You must solve puzzles and riddles in an effort to escape the Undead City / Raccoon City all the while managing your inventory of crucial and story progressing items that provide for some unique gameplay. While some people loath inventory management, I for one enjoy it, as it can provide a challenge. While RE 4 was a great game, it sent the RE franchise down a path that was just not RE. It focused too much on over-the-top action to a point where RE became just another shooter. RE 2 hits the reset button and does it beautifully. 

If you plan on getting this title, then I would recommend adding the original soundtrack swap. It replaces the new soundtrack with the original. Making for a pure nostalgic atmosphere. Not to mention it sounds great and adds more spooky audio to the game.

However, the thing this remake is missing is the short descriptive text that objects display to get the player more immersed in the setting. Also, the game seems to leave out some lore oriented memo's, letters, etc. that the original had. For example, the letter that was faxed in at S.T.A.R.S. HQ upon entering the room with regards to Chris's happenings. Lore that ties in RE 1 & RE 3. And let's not forget the women on the table in the orphanage during Sherry's segment. I also would've apprecited CAPCOM involving both Claire & Leon in each others scenarios a bit more. But the biggest dissappointment is the A & B scenarios. They almost mirror each other and make no sense in the timeline. For example; who destroyed the Ivy monster in the NEST, or who really fought Birkin at certain parts in the game, or how Mr. X really died. The remake scenarios are much different than the 1998 original, and not for the best.

Resident Evil 2 is a really good remake. Hopefully in the event CAPCOM remakes RE 3, they will improve upon it in the way they did RE 2, but add a little more lore immersion to it.

2. This game came in a bundle with my gaming pc.
At first, I was just expecting an OK game that would satisfy my boredom in the first few weeks of having my PC. What I got was a game that has an amazing an impactful story that allows me to empathize with the characters. What would I do in their situation? (Probably run away from it all, but that's not the point) From the first mission, I felt like I have known the characters for a very long time, and I was terrified to see what may happen to the characters. This game is scary, and it makes me hesitate to turn corners at times. It builds tension very well, and the sounds in the game really add to the horror that the player will feel. The "puzzles" in the game are also very thoughtful, and I really enjoy thinking about what I might find when I enter the next room. Honestly, this game actually makes me excited to see the next installment in the series, and if every game i the series is anything like this one, this may just be the best game series.

I never played the original myself. I watched a friend play through some of it when I was little, but I was too scared to take the controller. That said, RE2 was always my favorite of the Resident Evils because I love the setting and characters. I always wanted a remake of this one to come out exactly the way it is so I could experience that AWESOME game with modern graphics and modern mechanics.

The zombies are much more resiliant (like a full mag of 15 rounds to the head to fully kill at times) but that really adds to the more methodical gameplay. You could have the best aim in the universe, but still waste all of your resources on just a few zombies when you could stagger a few and run past the rest. Of course you can still get lucky and get a one shot crit insta kill, but its pretty rare.

Speaking of resources, ammo and other useful items are so rare! You really need to choose your engagements and plan your movements to shoot as little as possible. I made the mistake of not utilizing the wooden planks early on and ended up going through an area I've been through previously. I entered with about 60 something 9mm rounds and came out with 13! Things like that go to show just how careful you need to be in this.

The audio and atmosphere are soooo chilling. Just roaming through the environments keeps you paranoid. If you play with headphones using the 3D audio setting, it feels like the zombies are right on your neck. If you find yourself in an ambush situation, the music changes to a really grim, dreadful tune. The voice acting is soooo good now. I remember the originals being quite hilariously bad.

THIS is how you do a horror game. Only 2.5 hours in, but this is GOTY material right here. The look and feel is perfect. First REmake HD, then RE7 and now this? One of the most iconic survival horror games is back, and let me tell you it raises the bar...
Graphics are gorgeous. The most high-def zombies I've ever seen, and they feel like actual zombies! Lighting is also superb.

Atmosphere? Horrendous, which is exactly what Resident Evil's atmosphere should be. This game is actually scary. Not because of cheap jump scares, but because of what may lurk around the next corner. The zombies can take a lot of bullets to kill, but that adds to the whole tenseness and resource management I think. You're not the Doom Slayer.

If I would have to mention some minor downsides? Leon can sometimes sound a bit dry. Half the city could explode, and all you'd get is a "damnit" in the most bland way possible haha.

Well, they've gone and done it. They remade my favorite Resident Evil game (No RE4 is not my favorite and I think it's overrated). In OG RE2 it was possible to clear out rooms and hallways to make running around easier but in the remake, it's better to run past enemies to save ammo and this really emphasizes fight or flight moments on the regular. The negative to this is enemies seem to be spongier which makes fighting almost a chore. This is especially true during a segment where a certain enemy type from OG RE2 is replaced with a more annoying and bullet spongey enemy. The positive is the dismemberment system which means you can turn a walking zombie into a crawler with some shots to their legs so you can skirt around them easier if you know you'll end up going through that room or hallway again. Puzzles have been redone with some completely removed and new puzzles taking their place. I don't know what they did with the RE engine but it ran like Usain Bolt for me on RE7 and it runs even better for me in this remake so I'm glad they used that engine for this game.

[h1]Resident Evil 2: Remake manages to recreate what made the Original Resident Evil 2 on the PlayStation special, making this one a special and fresh experience as well. It recreates the game while adding new elements to it to modernize the gameplay a bit, and it also makes some nice story changes which are surprisingly fitting to the game.[/h1]


[b]Thats it for the short version. How about we go a little in-depth for anyone with some spare time to read?


[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]This is a Survival Horror game. You cannot go guns blazing and shoot everything you see. Ammo is extremely limited. Same goes for healing items. During a lot of combat moments, you'll have to run away from enemies rather than engage head on. Your character's movement is slow intentionally. You may hate that, but this helps to keep the game balanced and intense at times, instead of turning it into a running simulator, with no need to engage in combat at all.
Aiming also feels a bit stiff and slow. This also helps to balance things out. You are playing as a rookie after all...

[h1]Story:[/h1]The base of the story remains the same from the original game. However, the way this story unfolds has been tweaked a bit. And thats not a bad thing. This is better than copy pasting 100% of the story into the Remake, as veterans who played the Original game, would know exactly what happens at all times. Changing some aspects makes us experience a sorta fresh experience while also having that "familiar" feeling as well.

[h1]Difficulty:[/h1]Folks who played the original Resident Evil games on the Play Station, they are going to feel right at home. The game is fairly difficult, but its possible to get a bit unfair at some rare moments depending on your inventory management.
But if you're new to the Resident Evil games or, god forbid, you only played the games released after Resident Evil 5, you might have some trouble with the difficulty. Zombies don't die by one headshot here...or two...or three...or four! You can also get lost or stuck if you're reckless with your navigation. Don't expect a lot of hand holding.

[h1]Soundtrack:[/h1]This is where it goes a bit downhill. This is all my opinion, mind you! I don't speak for other folks as everyone has different preferences. Remake's Soundtrack just feels "Odd". It has a Resident Evil 7 vibe to it, which I am not a fan of. Most of the time its just too quiet or simply absent. And when I first heard the "Escape From Laboratory" theme of the Remake, I just couldn't enjoy it.
The Original PS1 Soundtrack is available for Deluxe Owners and can be bought as seperate DLC as well. It has been added in the game and it works flawlessly. Its fitting, enjoyable and gives you a great sense of Nostalgia. I definitely enjoyed this game more with the Original PS1 OST enabled.

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]They are great. They are not 2019 cutting edge technology but they still look magnificant when you crank up those Visual Settings. Character models and animations are gorgeously detailed and the facial expressions are insanely good. Shooting zombies and seeing chunks fly outta their face is just satisfying. Exploding stuff with the Grenade Launcher or other explosives looks beautiful as well.

[h1]Optimization/Performance/Port:[/h1]Its done pretty well. I played the game on release day, and it managed to run at a constant 60+ FPS. No crashes so far as well. Optimization is done pretty well on all areas.

[h1]Length:[/h1]At the time of writing this review, I managed to beat only one Scenario, Leon A. It lasted a total of 8 hours. The game features 4 Scenarios plus 2 bonus unlockable minigames. So its safe to say, you get at least 30 hours of playtime. New Scenarios require you visiting most of the areas previously explored in the previous Scenario, albeit with different item placements and sometimes new enemy placements as well. This ain't exactly a bad thing unless you really hate "replaying" the same levels.


[h1]Conclusions:[/h1]Capcom finally decided to make a game about what Resident Evil originally was. A Survival Horror Experience. And they absolutely nailed this one. Everything about this game feels damn fine. Its the Remake that the fans always deserved after all this wait. Its a must have for every Old School Resident Evil fan!
Now if only Capcom manages to keep this up and release some new Resident Evil games like this one instead of those other Resident Evil games we've gotten lately... [/b]

This is truly a masterpiece in three different ways:

1- Technically outstanding. Facial animations, textures, lightning, shadows, ragdolls, dismembers. The engine shines and show off technical features that were never present in any game of the franchise.
2- Old mechanics from the saga were reinvented without removing the feeling of the original. It feels old school, but updated to our modern times. Examining objects serve real purpose. Solving puzzles really make you think twice and interact in different ways with items or objects in the scenario. Shooting feels great, the gameplay itself has a good flow. With some bosses, I felt like I wanted to have an evasive dash or something, but it would have made these fights really easy and unchallenging.
3- The game is a remaster but built from scratch. If you didn't play the original RE2, you will still enjoy this game as ♥♥♥♥; BUT, if you played the original like me, 20 years ago, you won't remember every detail of it, and even though this is not a copy paste of the original, they recreated everything in a way that you'll have intense flashbacks and memories from something "very similar" in the past. It is amazing and very hard to describe that feeling, because it's nostalgia and memories of fun moments, but moments that actually never existed in the way this game shows them now. 

9,90/10. I hope RE3 gets remastered this way.
P.S.: 0,10 were taken away because some boss fights mechanics aren't well developed. I'm not sure how someone would fight some bosses without being hit. There's no much room for movement and I felt like I was punished for defending myself instead of running. I'm sure someone else would master those fights without being hit or tanking an actual fight, but for my first playthrough, I feel like I was missing something...

Perspective 3rd person vs FPS: I personally enjoyed the FPS aspect of Re7 way more, it made you feel there vs your character being the one that reacts. To me it fits better with the these games and was refreshing once it was introduced.

World interest: The level of detail and erie setting in the 7th game immediately sucked me in. I was hooked and felt compelled to beat the game in a single day. It was frightening. This game is a wonderful remake of the 1998 classic survival horror title Resident Evil 2.

It deviates just enough from the original to feel fresh, while also keeping what made the original so great. The change to a more controllable 3rd person camera, free aiming system, and a more dynamic and interact-able world are steps in the right direction in my opinion.

Another negative I have about the game is the removal of the 'zapping' system. If you're not familiar, the original had a system in place where on your A scenario if you did certain things or took certain items the B scenario character would experience different things or not have those particular items in their run. That doesn't exist AT ALL in this remake and it's a little disappointing.

TL;DR below:

Good:
-Graphics
-Music
-Character Design
-Storytelling
-Voice acting
-NPC character development

Bad:
-Removal of zapping system
-A and B scenarios are a little lacking in their interactivity.

Resident Evil 2: Remake is a solid game, I give it a 9/10 simply because I have been craving a good Resident Evil for a while and this is only because I have only played the game on Hardcore. If I were to play it on any other difficulty I feel my rating would be closer to a 8 or even a 7 out of 10 from what I have seen.

Let me explain some of the differences between normal and hardcore.

· Normal has autosaves, meaning dying has less consequence while hardcore has ink ribbons like the classic games. Being a veteran RE player I don't mind this but I can see how some people may not like this but I assure you there are lots of ink ribbons, more than enough in fact and the game is always nice enough to give you one right before something that might kill you. This loss of progress really adds to the survival horror atmosphere because you might be trying to survive just to prevent that loss of progress, and that can get intense.

· On normal, you take I think it is around 3-5 hits depending on adaptive difficulty. On hardcore you always die at two, unless you take a red and blue herb this will give you damage resistance allowing you to take an extra hit or two. Choosing when to use these is another part of the survival horror.

· On hardcore zombies are much faster, and have a longer grab. Good luck cheesing a zombie grab to save ammo in hardcore. They not only apply pressure on you by killing you quickly (i.e. 2 hits) they also have a extended grab animation which you don't want to test.

There are other reasons why I think hardcore is better than normal but basically it comes down to it actually feeling like a game. I am a big believer that a game Should kill you. If you are walking through a game without dying that is a bad sign. Games need to put an wall in your path, and you need to get over it. That being said, you choose the difficulty you would like to play on. Just think about it, and remember nothing will be like your first play through and that first impression will cement your opinion on the game.

This game outside of being too easy on normal and assisted. It has some problems that annoy me. Here are a few; scripted segments that aren't really intense and or try to give off the illusion of intensity (i.e. the start of the game), adaptive difficulty, so so bosses, unfinished b scenario, and indication icons. Let me explain why I have problems with these.
At the start of the game, they throw a tutorial at you. Everyones favorite part of a video game, this teaches you some basic mechanics. Thing is, this tutorial adds nothing to the story really and just gives the illusion of intensity, no matter if you take damage or not doesn't matter in the beginning tutorial since you get all your health back after it's over. The next segment isn't any better. Yes they have all those zombies like the original, the difference being the ones in the original actually posed a threat. In this game they are literally staring at poles and wont really pose any threat to you unless you try to give them a hug. This is super lame because it completely takes away from what the originals opening accomplished.
Once you enter the police station things get better, but one issue I have is indication icons. These are basically little arrows on doors and items that way it ensures you don't miss an item or a door. The problem lies in the fact that not only does this take away from the survival horror aspect, the game already had a good feature to let you know if a room still has items to pick up. The map will show a red room for a room that still needs searching and a blue one for a room that has been searched so all these indicators do is stop you from actually having to look for puzzle items or ammo. 
Adaptive difficulty is another huge issue I have with the game, it doesn't add to it at all. Not because it makes it too hard, but because it can make it too easy. Sometimes if I decide to run around with my infinite ammo weapons I unlocked and just shoot zombies the game will assume I am doing bad, and when I want to do an actual play through, all of a sudden I am one shot their head and it explodes. I don't think it adds much to the game and to be honest static consistent difficulty is just better.
Bosses are kind of lame, but what make them even worse is the B scenario aka the other side of the story that is loaded with plot holes. Did they run out of time or budget? Why would they tack this ♥♥♥♥ on. Now Claire and Leon fight the exact same bosses, which was untrue in the original. All it does is give you some ♥♥♥♥♥♥ new guns with lame animations. No new story or anything. You might as well just play A twice. They shouldn't have even bothered with B Scenario and just made two separate stories. Hell I already know how exactly they could've done it, my assumption is they ran out of budget.

Despite my rants with the game it is a good survival horror game. Not better than the original but good in it's own right. It had the potential but they really screwed the pooch with scenario b and scripted segments. It has good controls for a SH title, and the gameplay is solid. You will have fun playing this and will likely ♥♥♥♥ your pants too. People call me a brick wall when it come to horror and this game even managed to get me panic a few times. If you're a fan of RE games 100% you should pick it up, same goes for survival horror fans. If you are new to the series I recommend start with RE Remake before this one, since it's cheaper and really good if you see this game on sale, for sure pick this one up. Universal and incessant praise over graphics and nostalgia is boring and useless, so even though this game is quite good I want to write a more level-headed review not clouded by hype-glasses

The graphics are, for the most part, very impressive. Capcom did a great job with gore and eviscerations, though some textures and lit surfaces look like they went through a lot of cut corners. I can see why some people find the faces to be "derpy" looking but frankly I got used to them and like them a lot now, they did an excellent job with Marvin, Chief Irons and Ada

Several set pieces are a blast to compare to the PS1 original. Like REmake 1, there's as much old here as there is new. They got the balance right between the vintage and the modern. This more subtle, not in-your-face portrayal is a very tasteful way of having what essentially amounts to fan service

Audio is hit or miss. Some of the songs are decent and welcomed renditions of the original soundtrack. Gunshots and footsteps sound nice. But there is audio (and visual) stuttering a couple times every hour. Plus half of the actors sound a little stilted and almost monotonous despite their cheeky nature, particularly Ada and Leon. As cool as the characters look, they don't sound nearly as attractive

Gameplay is perfectly fine though there doesn't seem to be anything overtly spectacular about it, and it has several minor flaws that more people should be mentioning/noticing. The puzzles were fine, the inventory management was fine, I wasn't bothered by the "short" length of the game since it's about as long as RE2 original. The durability system for the knife is really cool and I don't find the "bullet sponge" zombies to be a big deal at all. Like with RE2 original there's more than enough ammo to get by (on Normal mode). The zombies take longer to kill and now do more damage, which I like. Just like in Code Veronica or RE4, any encounter can go from fine, to complete and utter ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ catastrophe after just one mistake

But it isn't the best Resident Evil, not by a long shot. RE4 and 7 had better bosses. REmake 1 had better puzzles, backtracking and scares. Having to pay for what used to be free in-game unlockables as DLC is a shameless practice, something that Mikami or Kamiya would have never done with (what was once) their beloved franchise. 

REmake 2 commits the dumbest crime that nearly every game inspired by RE4 has made: giving you a center-screen reticle. Aiming a gun in Gears of War, The Last of Us, GTA IV and countless other games just has you moving a rectangular box with a circle in the center. It feels lifeless and homogeneous. Aiming a gun in RE4 has you moving not a square box, but Leon's actual hands, with the laser-sight dot moving all across the screen. I know it sounds like a pedantic gripe but it really is part of what made the combat in that game so tense, visceral and groundbreaking. You'd think Capcom would get this right for their own franchise. It's by far my biggest disappointment with the game and it makes aiming, especially for headshots, feel monotonous and lacking the kind of spacing or dynamics that RE4 brought to the table

On second thought, what might be my biggest personal disappointment with REmake 2 is [spoiler]The Crocodile. It just played out like some boring Uncharted/Tomb Raider obstacle course and was a glorified interactive cutscene[/spoiler]

The game also isn't that scary, I guess? I got mildly spooked more than a few times but you're not gonna see the top-tier, outside-the-box thinking that games like P.T., Eternal Darkness, Fatal Frame, Penumbra or White Day have. But if you're easily spooked then you still should have a thrilling time

First time I have left a review. As a long standing RE fan who fell in love with the original survival horror, this game speaks to me. Finally getting a visit back to what made the series such a fun yet dreadful experience.
The game isn't a 1:1 clone of the original. They added some things or moved some key items to different locations, which makes for an experience that is more unique than just the same old game with better graphics and engine.

The use of lighting and shadows is fantastic. Use of a flashlight in darker areas and the way the light limits your field of vision provides an excellent feeling of claustrophobia and anxiety about what lies around the next corner.
With the exception of the firearms, the audio work is amazing. Walking down a dark corridor, the sound of your every step reverberating off into the darkness whilst the rain beats against the roof and some far off zombie claws at a door, really immerses you into the world.

Zombies are easy to deal with if you want to burn through ammo, but the first few encounters with a fan favorite tongue themed baddie are stressful in the best way possible.
I do miss ink ribbons and having to be more choosy about when to save. I feel like I can afford to be more reckless when I know my last save was 10 minutes ago instead of 3 hours ago.
Health items feel more plentiful than I'd like. I've only been taken to caution health once in almost 2.5 hours of gameplay.
I love having puzzles to do again. Scouring every inch of this place for a USB drive has been a frustratingly fun scavenger hunt.
Anyone who thinks they can Rambo their way through is going to have a bad time. Zombies can take anywhere from 1 (with a lucky crit) to 8 headshots with handguns to put down for good. I have long played games that rewarded killing every enemy you see. This game punishes that school of thought by leaving you ill equipped and completey dry on ammo when you have no choice but to fight.
When a certain fedora wearing trenchcoat shows up, the game changes completely.

Resident Evil is back in the most frightful, dread inducing yet fun and satisfying way.

This is not just a remaster or reskin of the old game, but rather a completely remade game that stays 100% true to the original lore, atmosphere and all round feel of the original. The game looks absolutely gorgeous, both in the cutscenes and general gameplay. The environments are very detailed and the world is scattered with lore to find as always. The sound and voice acting are very well done as well.
The gameplay will feel very familiar to RE veterans and is actually better than what early reviews led me to believe.
I did my first playtrough on normal difficulty and must warn people not familiar with this type of game that it can be very challenging on normal difficulty.
Ammo is scarce and so is health. I often found myself barely clinging to life with no ammo but smart gameplay lets you still pull trough even when you think all is lost.

The puzzles were never overly complicated but still a challenge to overcome. But at no point did it become frustrating or feel unsolveable.

Obviously the game is great, you can read any review for that info, but something more important is that THIS IS A FLAWLESS PC PORT FROM CAPCOM

Theres a wide range of graphics settings, and they detect and benchmark your video memory which makes it super easy to tune the game for maximum preformance + graphical quality.

Too few games actually show you which settings take up what amount of video memory.

Was easily able to tune the game for a completely smooth framerate while pushing my computer to the absolute limit, and I've gotten zero frame drops so far, even in densly packed areas with lots of effects going on at once.

10/10 port.

Hardest difficulty is the way to go, but for gods sake conserve your ammo for the first boss.

♥♥♥♥♥♥ took about 7 shotgun shells and 40 pistol bullets directly in the weak point to go down.

There are not many cases that I can say that things are beautifully created, but this is one case right now, I've not played a huge bunch due to the time of release and such but from what I have done I have really enjoyed sitting here shaking and shivering thanks to the perfectly timed and orchestrated music building up an insane amount of tension in the game, followed by the usual dwindling ammo count and sheer horror from binaural audio giving me chills and upping my heartbeat.

I may update my review later after extended play but for now:-

Graphics - 9.5/10 (Still got a 'solid black' motif, but that might be my monitors)
Game Play - 9/10 (I can't give a remake 10, but it's pushing towards it)
Sound - 10/10 (Spine chillingly horrifying)
Ease of use - 9/10
OVERALL - 9/10

Capcom knocked it out of the park on this one. 

The visual and mechanical storytelling is solid- the game's story has you overcoming the stacked odds to survive and the gameplay really delivers on that. 

Everything from ammo pickups to enemy placement feels really masterfully done; getting a new weapon is a great feeling of "ok, now I am in a good spot" but that quickly disappears when new enemies start appearing that completely eat any ammo you have. 

There are fantastic moments of intense dread that have you whispering to yourself "I can do this, I can do this," which feels totally warranted as the characters themselves occasionally whisper the same thing. 

What items you can carry with you at any time also feels really constraining at times and forces you to make impactful decisions like how many healing items or ammunition you carry on your person or how worthwhile it is to carry a key that you may or may not need. 

If you are a returning fan of the Resident Evil series, you owe it to yourself to pick this up. 
If you are a new fan wanting to try Resident Evil for the first time, this is a fantastic title to do so- the story doesn't rely too heavily on knowing the other games to be enjoyable and the gameplay is some of the best the series has to offer.

A dream come true. A game that takes the best characteristics from the classic games and the modern games, while omitting the more frustrating elements of both. 

Ammo is scarce and healing items are fairly uncommon. You have to make hard decisions over whether to use your precious ammo to navigate a hallway, risk a dangerous dodge, or run. These are the decisions that form the root and core of any survival horror experience. While they have often gone missing from the more action-orientated experiences of RE4, 5 and 6, they are very present here. Even inventory management is a consideration once again, albiet it a lesser concern than the original game.
The combat is much more suited to modern audiences and is rather difficult to master. Enemies are cunning and deadly and will pounce on mistakes, missed shots and recklessness. It feels reminscent of RE7's combat, but with a greater variety of enemies, from shambling zombies to giant mutated bio-weapons. This allows for a challenging, but fair level of difficulty.
As far as horror games go, Resident Evil 2 remake is an terrifying experience. Zombies lurk behind doors, Lickers behave more like a Xenomorph from Alien as they leap from walls and are a constant menace. The game looks and sounds wonderful, especially with the character models and water/fire effects. 
It borrows heavily from the original title, with many areas complete with the smaller details present in the original pre-rendered world. Veterans of the series will suffer from severe bouts of nostalgia, while newcomers will be greeted with a rich and detailed new world to explore. Much has changed however, meaning that RE2 remake will still be a new experience for older fans of the original game.
Capcom have learned from the lessons of their previous titles, both failed and successful, to create a frightening and challenging experience worthy of the franchises grandiose history.
Resident Evil isn't just 'back'; these could very well be brand new heights for the franchise.
